chapters.title: Chapter 565: Chaoter 565
chapters.content:
Chapter 565 - Chaoter 565
<>
<<[Bleach: Why Am I, Kurosaki Ichigo, Not the Harem King?]>>
<<[Naruto Travel Between Worlds Of One Piece]>>
<<[Use your Power Stones on it, and by reaching 1500PS and getting 50 reviews it will be picked up!]>>
"I can bring the dead back to life—but why should I help you?"
The voice echoed across Stark Tower—mysterious, like the truth of the universe itself, yet also chillingly indifferent.
Kingpin, who had been dejected after Spider-Man declared that death was irreversible, froze mid-thought. His expression twisted into shock and disbelief.
The White-Clad Hero... what did he just say?
He... could actually bring the dead back?!
Kingpin was stunned, his mind struggling to comprehend.
And he wasn't the only one—Spider-Man, who had just confidently stated that resurrection was impossible, now stood frozen, his face full of disbelief.
How could something like that be real?
Agent Coulson, the SHIELD operatives, police officers, monks, and even civilians watching the scene through drones—every single one of them was floored.
"Is this real?"
"Can someone actually be brought back to life?"
"Oh God..."
Back in the dark corner of the street, the Avengers Four were in complete shock.
Nebula asked aloud, "Didn't you just say the dead can't come back?"
Every eye turned to Thor.
They all wanted the same answer. Just moments ago, Thor had declared with unwavering certainty that the dead could never be revived—and now the White-Clad Hero, the so-called God of Light Baldr, was saying he could do exactly that?
Thor stared ahead, stunned. "It's impossible... How could anyone return from death?"
"Unless... my brother is lying. Trying to trick that human..."
Tony and the others blinked. That... actually sounded plausible.
Maybe he was giving that man false hope?
While they were entertaining that theory—and while the whole world remained in disbelief—Kingpin, after his initial shock, began to tremble with excitement.
His desperation to bring back his wife and son made him ignore the possibility that the White-Clad Hero might be deceiving him.
This had to be real.
He kept telling himself that.
But soon, doubt and sorrow overtook him again.
After all—why would the White-Clad Hero help someone like him?
Money?
The White-Clad Hero didn't need it. Even if he did, he could just take an entire nation's treasury with ease.
Power?
With a mere flick, he could wipe out all of New York—what need did he have for organizations or criminal empires?
Kingpin couldn't think of a single thing he had that could be of value.
But he couldn't give up. This was his only chance.
After several seconds of agonizing thought, he lowered his head and muttered with despair and uncertainty, "I have nothing... nothing worth trading for this miracle."
Then, more resolutely, he added, "But I'll give everything I have—if there's even the slightest chance."
He lifted his head, looking at the White-Clad Hero with pure devotion in his eyes, silently begging for mercy.
Murmurs spread through the crowd around Stark Tower.
"Does Kingpin really think he can bring people back from the dead?"
"That's ridiculous. There's no such thing."
"And why would the White-Clad Hero even help him?"
But high above, Syd's eyes narrowed slightly.
Kingpin's body... was now giving off threads of faith—he was producing actual divine faith energy.
Not the level of a fanatic, but solidly that of a true believer.
It seemed his longing to bring back his family wasn't just genuine—it was desperate.
Syd's interest was piqued.
He had never actually tried resurrecting someone before. All the methods he'd come up with were still theoretical.
This... could be a perfect test.
More importantly, he had made a promise once—to Kaecilius. He'd promised to bring back his wife and child.
He hadn't had the power at the time, so the matter had been delayed. Kaecilius never pressed him, but Syd could still feel the man's pain and grief beneath his fanatical loyalty.
Now that he had the strength, it was time to fulfill that promise.
Kingpin's case would serve as the experiment.
With a faint smile, Syd said, "I'm in a good mood today. I'll grant your wish."
"But I hope you won't regret it—having a wife and child again will become your weakness."
As he spoke, he cast a brief glance at Coulson and the others—not subtly at all.
Coulson noticed and gave a bitter smile.
Kingpin's expression changed momentarily, but quickly turned resolute.
Seeing that, Syd didn't bother with more words. After a moment of thought, he decided to use Chaos Magic combined with his Creation ability.
First, he would use Chaos Magic to retrieve the souls of Kingpin's wife and son.
Then, he'd use Creation to craft new bodies for them.
In the next instant, under the stunned eyes of people around the world, he raised his right hand and activated his power.
A crimson glow surged to life.
Simultaneously, he used his abstract divine form to sense the location of the two souls.
He reached across heaven, hell, and various dimensions...
Then, with a twist of chaotic reality, he altered their positions.
Red light burst forth.
Under the force of Chaos Magic's reality-warping, two transparent soul forms—one adult and one child—appeared in the air.
The two souls looked confused, unsure of what was happening.
Bathed in red light, their forms were visible to everyone present—including Kingpin.
Before anyone could react, the White-Clad Hero gently blew toward the souls.
His supreme Creation energy spread outward, touching both souls.
And then something truly shocking happened.
The two souls—previously intangible and ghost-like—began to solidify.
It was like watching them come back to life.
No... they were coming back to life.
People stared in utter disbelief.
No matter how hard they looked, they couldn't see the two figures as "spiritual forms" anymore.
They looked real. Alive.
At the same time, without anyone realizing, the deep red glow on Syd's right hand pulsed again.
He twisted reality one more time—altering the fact that the two people had died at all.
Now, they had never been dead.
They'd only been in a state of suspended animation.
This trick was meant to deceive Death herself.
The Creation ability alone was enough to resurrect someone—but if he used it carelessly, Death might immediately sense the anomaly.
So Syd played it smart.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 566
chapters.content:
Chapter 566 - 566
Looking at the woman and child—one tall, one small—floating before him, their faces full of confusion and disbelief, a trace of satisfaction crossed Syd's face.
He couldn't help but admire the overwhelming might of Creation and Chaos Magic.
Creation alone was awe-inspiring—but even just Chaos Magic's ability to twist reality was already absurd.
Syd fell into thought.
In this universe, Doctor Strange had been crippled in a car accident, but in another, his hands were unharmed—yet Christine, his love, had died instead.
To bring her back, Strange used the Time Stone, attempting to forcibly undo her death.
But it was precisely Christine's death that led to the rise of the Sorcerer Supreme.
That created a temporal paradox, a fixed point in time. No matter how many times he reversed time, Christine always died.
Eventually, the corrupted Strange gained overwhelming power, forcibly overturned time, and the entire universe began to collapse.
But if it had been Chaos Magic instead...
What paradox? What fixed point?
Under Chaos Magic, everything makes sense.
All logic is self-consistent.
Collapse? Impossible.
Finishing his thoughts, Syd waved a hand. Kingpin's wife Vanessa and his son gently descended to the ground, returning to Kingpin's side.
Not far off, Spider-Man Peter Parker's jaw dropped. His eyes widened as he stared in disbelief.
"They were really brought back?"
"My God... people can actually come back to life?"
Peter stood there dazed, his worldview cracking apart.
A flicker of desire sparked in his chest.
He too... wanted to bring back his loved ones.
At that moment, Agent Coulson, the officers, the monks, and countless others watching across the globe were in shock.
They had just witnessed a miracle—
No—a divine act.
Someone had actually come back from the dead?
What kind of absurd power was this?
"So this... is the power of a Creator God?" Coulson muttered, barely believing it.
In the shadows nearby—
Nebula, Thor, and the others stared, dumbfounded.
Thor especially looked completely shaken.
His brother—the White-Clad Hero, the God of Light Baldr—hadn't been lying to that mortal?
He actually revived someone?
Thor whispered, dazed, "How... how can this be real..."
Tears welled up in his eyes as faces flashed through his mind—
Father. Mother. Loki. Heimdall...
If only they could come back too...
While Thor was lost in thought, the others were equally overwhelmed.
Then Hawkeye whispered, "Thor... I think I actually believe it now. He really is a Creator God..."
...
Kamar-Taj.
The Ancient One, who had been silently observing from afar—worried that Syd might use the Time Stone to reverse time—showed a rare look of surprise.
Even she felt her worldview shake.
No one knew better than her how difficult it was to bring someone back.
Death in the universe was tied to the force known as Death—a cosmic constant.
Not even magic could undo it.
If resurrection had been so simple, she would've brought back Kaecilius's family long ago. There was no way she would've waited until now.
Meanwhile, not far away, Kaecilius stared at the scene, a mix of shock and excitement in his eyes.
Someone had actually come back to life.
After the initial joy, though, sorrow crept in.
His Lord had once promised to bring back his wife and son...
But it hadn't happened yet...
As he watched, the doubt he had tried so hard to suppress stirred once more.
Could it be... his Lord isn't powerful enough?
Could he be... less powerful than the White-Clad Hero?
Kaecilius's eyes filled with uncertainty.
But far away in New York, Syd sensed his thoughts and silently shook his head.
The next moment, Kaecilius froze.
A mysterious voice echoed in his mind:
"If your heart longs so deeply for their return—then I shall grant it."
As the words faded, Syd began channeling the power of Chaos Magic and Creation once more.
In an instant, Kaecilius's pupils shrank.
Two souls suddenly appeared before him—and a familiar sight followed.
The translucent figures began to rapidly solidify—flesh, bone, breath—becoming real.
"What... what's happening?"
"Are you... daddy?"
The woman and boy blinked, confused and unsure.
Kaecilius was in complete disbelief.
It was almost impossible to believe this was real.
His wife... his child... had truly been brought back?
And this process... it felt eerily familiar, like what had happened with the White-Clad Hero.
Still, Syd had hidden the red Chaos Magic light this time, so Kaecilius couldn't be sure.
He hesitated, then told himself:
Maybe... this is just how all great beings revive people.
He couldn't imagine any other explanation.
Almost simultaneously, a glowing yellow portal appeared nearby.
The Ancient One stepped out in her golden robes, her eyes widening with shock.
Just moments earlier, she had sensed an overwhelming surge of power from this area—and had rushed over to investigate.
What she saw... left her speechless.
Kaecilius saw her, but he paid her no attention—he was too overwhelmed, clutching his wife and son in a tight embrace.
As he held them close, he murmured devoutly, "Oh Supreme Lord... thank you for your mercy upon your humble servant..."
His Lord's power... truly beyond imagination.
And to think he had doubted that his Lord was weaker than the White-Clad Hero?
He felt a pang of guilt.
The Ancient One frowned as she listened, quickly piecing things together.
But confusion still filled her heart.
How could this be happening?
If the White-Clad Hero had revived someone, fine—he was a Creator God. It made sense that he could challenge natural laws and cosmic order.
But this unknown dimensional deity?
How could he possibly do the same?
And even more strangely—
The White-Clad Hero had just performed a resurrection... and then Kaecilius's family was revived too?
Could this unknown god be connected to the White-Clad Hero?
The Ancient One's thoughts swirled with doubt.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 567
chapters.content:
Chapter 567 - 567
At that moment, Kaecilius, still holding his wife and child in his arms, began to undergo a subtle transformation.
The threads of faith connecting him to Syd suddenly thickened—dozens of times over.
Even his soul now shimmered with a faint glow.
To put it simply: Kaecilius's devotion had ascended to an entirely new level—beyond that of even a fanatic.
At this point, his faith was practically unshakable. Even if asked to die, he would do so without question, simply believing it was his Lord's will—and obey gladly.
Back in New York, Syd also sensed this change.
Through the link of divine faith, he even felt as though his consciousness could now descend directly into Kaecilius's body and control it at will.
But he ignored that sensation and shifted his attention back to the scene around Stark Tower.
Kingpin was also embracing his wife and son now, excitedly telling them what had happened.
Meanwhile, murmurs spread among the surrounding crowd.
"Unbelievable... The power of a Creator God. It defies science! But why would the White-Clad Hero bring Kingpin's family back?"
"Where's the justice in that?"
"Why does he get a miracle and not the rest of us? Why would the White-Clad Hero help him?"
With his divine senses, Syd heard the whispers from dozens, even hundreds of meters away—but he didn't react at all.
Why?
Because he wanted to.
He felt like it.
He would do whatever he pleased.
What gave these people the right to question that?
In this world, if it wasn't Kingpin, it would've been someone else.
As long as humans existed, there would always be people competing for the spoils of darkness.
Unless he wiped out all of humanity—like the biblical God's great flood—there would be no end to it.
In some ways, Kingpin's very presence stabilized the underground world.
And if having his wife and child again made him more vulnerable?
That had nothing to do with Syd.
Then, he heard the voices of gratitude.
"Divine One... thank you for bringing back my son... and me," Vanessa said sincerely.
Kingpin and the boy both echoed her gratitude.
After a while, seeing that the White-Clad Hero gave no reply, they respectfully said their farewells, and left in their cars, escorted by Kingpin's men.
The moment they left, Syd heard a wave of desperate pleading from below.
"Oh great Creator God, please... have mercy on me too. Please bring my loved one back!"
"God...!"
Even Coulson and Spider-Man hesitated, as though wanting to speak but not daring to.
Across the world, millions who saw the broadcast via drones were filled with fervent hope. They prayed silently, wishing the White-Clad Hero could grant their desires.
At this point, they had completely forgotten how much they used to scorn mutants, or how hateful their words had once been.
Hearing all of this—seeing the thick crowd swarming beneath Stark Tower—Syd simply closed his eyes.
As if I'd help people like them.
He wasn't some magical wish-granting machine.
If he fulfilled every absurd request, then what—revive every dead human in history?
That would surely enrage not only Mephisto and the Lords of Hell, but even the angels of Heaven might descend to stop him—worse yet, he would certainly alert Death.
Besides, a universe without death... would be terrifying.
Death is what makes new life possible.
And when it came to Heaven—Syd narrowed his eyes.
He couldn't help but think of the God he was now emulating.
According to legend, Heaven was created by God.
Whether that was true or not, no one knew for sure.
Earth, Asgard, Jotunheim—they were all part of the Nine Realms.
But in ancient times, there had actually been Ten Realms. The tenth was Heaven.
Long ago, Heaven suffered a rebellion. The queen of the angels offended Odin. In his rage, Odin severed Heaven from the World Tree itself.
He cursed every angel with eternal banishment—casting them into the endless void.
Thinking of all this, Syd's eyes flickered with doubt.
In Marvel lore, "God" is a vague, undefined figure—and may not even reside in Heaven.
His power was also questionable.
By right, the head gods of every pantheon—Zeus, Odin, etc.—were supposed to be Skyfather-level beings.
But one thing was certain: Marvel doesn't have a true, omniscient, omnipotent "God."
Of this, Syd was absolutely sure.
Otherwise, Marvel's strongest entity wouldn't be the One Above All—it would be God.
He shook his head, thinking back to the divine role he was now emulating.
He was fairly certain he wasn't imitating Marvel's vague "God"...
But the true God—the omnipotent one.
While he pondered this, his closed eyes and aloof demeanor made the crowd go completely silent.
Not even Coulson or the others dared to interrupt him.
Even the whispered discussions began to fade.
Everyone was left wondering...
Why had the White-Clad Hero—this so-called Creator God—appeared here in the first place?
They weren't the only ones puzzled.
Hiding in secret, many aliens who had come to Earth to observe the rumored Creator God were just as confused.
But also thrilled.
The being they'd only heard of in legend... was right in front of them.
And just as Coulson, Spider-Man, and the world watched in confusion—
A new group entered the scene, and gasps rippled through the crowd.
Dressed in specialized suits, Captain America, Natasha, Tony... and others stepped out of the shadows.
The crowd erupted.
"It's the Avengers!"
Coulson, in his black suit, blinked in confusion. "Captain, what are you doing here?"
He wasn't the only one—other SHIELD agents wore the same expression of bewilderment.
They glanced at the uniforms the Avengers were wearing.
"Is this... some kind of new mission gear?"
Could this be an assignment from Director Fury?
Maybe that's why they'd come?
As ordinary people exclaimed in awe and agents puzzled over the situation...
Inside Stark Tower—and across SHIELD and other facilities—some people were reeling in shock.
...
Stark Tower.
Tony stood before the tall windows, watching the scene below with a face full of disbelief.
What was he seeing?
He saw... himself.
A man, identical to him, was standing among the Avengers who had just arrived.
Even JARVIS stuttered.
"Sir... I believe I'm seeing... another you?"
"What is going on?"
Via the security cameras, they had a perfect view of the other Tony Stark standing there in the crowd.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 568
chapters.content:
Chapter 568 - 568
Tony Stark didn't bother answering JARVIS. Without a word, he pressed the arc reactor at his chest.
In the next second, countless nanobots surged across his body, forming a red suit of armor.
With a whoosh, he soared out of Stark Tower.
At the scene—
Coulson and the others were still wondering if Captain and the rest were on some secret mission when suddenly, a familiar red figure burst out of Stark Tower.
Instantly, everyone—on-site and across the world watching through drones—began to shift their eyes between the Iron Man in the sky and the one standing with the Avengers.
"Why are there two Tony Starks?"
"Did Iron Man lend someone his Mark suit?"
They couldn't think of any other explanation.
But the hovering Iron Man quickly dispelled those thoughts.
Hovering in the air, the faceplate of the armor snapped open—revealing Tony Stark's unmistakable face.
In that instant, silence fell.
Everyone stared—mouths agape—at the two Tony Starks.
"God Almighty... two Iron Men?!"
"Am I seeing double?"
"What the hell is going on?"
"Two Mr. Starks?" Spider-Man scratched his head, confused.
The airborne Tony ignored the crowd's stunned faces. His eyes were locked on the "other him" standing with the Avengers.
"Who are you?"
"Why do you look exactly like me?"
"What kind of nonsense is Nick Fury pulling this time?!"
Question after question shot out as a storm of theories raced through his mind.
Then he turned to Captain America. "What's going on here?"
...
Meanwhile, in Asgard—
In the royal palace, watching Earth's projection, Thor and the Warriors Three stood dumbfounded.
"Thor, when Heimdall said he saw another version of you, I didn't believe it," Hogun muttered. "Now I do."
Not far off, Queen Frigga covered her mouth in shock, and even King Odin frowned deeply.
If not for the vast distance and restrictions, they might have already uncovered the truth.
...
Back on Earth—
Coulson's phone rang.
He answered—and heard Nick Fury's urgent voice.
Soon, Coulson learned: not just Tony Stark—Natasha and others with the group were also wrong.
Because right now... Natasha was at SHIELD HQ.
As the call ended, Coulson immediately raised his pistol and aimed it at the Avengers standing in front of him.
His voice was sharp. "Who the hell are you people?! Captain? Natasha? They're in SHIELD headquarters right now—they're not here!"
The crowd erupted into a fresh wave of shock—even the flying Tony Stark looked stunned.
Then, from among the "other" Avengers, Ant-Man Scott Lang raised his hands. "Whoa, calm down—let us explain!"
Coulson hesitated for a moment, then lowered the gun slightly. "Go ahead."
Scott took a deep breath. "Here's the deal. We're from an alternate universe. We're here to find the Infinity Stones."
Without waiting for questions, he continued, "In our universe... Thanos collected all six Infinity Stones and snapped his fingers."
"Half the universe's life... vanished. And then he destroyed the Stones."
He explained how they tried to fix things by traveling into the past using quantum tech to retrieve the Stones and bring everyone back.
When he finished, Tony, Coulson, and everyone on Earth watching through drones were stunned.
"Thanos?"
"Six Infinity Stones?"
"Half the universe just... gone?"
They were shaken to their core.
Could this really be true?
If it was... the implications were terrifying.
Coulson's brow furrowed.
As a SHIELD agent, he knew exactly how dangerous the Infinity Stones were—and he knew who Thanos was.
What these people said... it was plausible.
But there was one problem.
Coulson shook his head. "Impossible. With the existence of the Creator God—the White-Clad Hero—Thanos would never be able to gather the Stones."
"Let alone erase half the universe!"
From above, Tony agreed. "That lie fell apart fast."
"Next time you want to deceive people, try preparing better."
All across the world, viewers watching the broadcast began to agree. The story from these "fake Avengers" was too ridiculous—full of holes.
With a Creator God like the White-Clad Hero around, would someone like Thanos even dare to show up?
Forget that—even the Messiah would be too much for him!
But just as Coulson was about to question them further, Thor from the alternate universe stepped forward, eyes full of sorrow.
"In our universe... the White-Clad Hero doesn't exist."
His gaze instinctively rose to the figure floating above them—dressed in pure white, radiant like a god.
His brother, who in his universe, had only ever been a myth—never once seen in real life.
Coulson and the others were dumbfounded.
What did he just say?
No White-Clad Hero?
Then Thor explained more differences between their two universes.
"Not only do we lack the White-Clad Hero, but the Messiah doesn't exist either."
"Because they're not there, our universe diverged in many ways..."
He paused, then added with grief, "My father... my mother... my brother Loki... they're all gone."
He proceeded to recount the destruction of Asgard—and his own painful journey.
...
Elsewhere in New York—
"Impossible!" Loki muttered in disbelief. "Me? Dead?"
His expression twisted, then suddenly he scoffed.
"Hmph. I'm the future King of Asgard. The brother of the Creator God. Who could possibly kill me?"
"Thanos?"
"He wouldn't dare."
He lifted his chin, pride and confidence radiating from his face.
That other Loki from that other universe? A loser—nothing like him.
Because he... was Loki.
The brother of the Creator God.
Hmph.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 569
chapters.content:
Chapter 569 - 569
Asgard
Listening to the alternate Thor's words, the Warriors Three and others were all stunned—Thor himself was no exception.
His parents... Frigga... Loki... all dead?
Thor didn't want to believe it.
Even just imagining such a scenario filled him with despair.
If merely thinking about it felt this painful, how much worse must it have been for that version of him in the other universe?
"How could something like this happen..." Thor murmured.
At that moment, Odin, frowning deeply, said gravely, "Had your brother Baldr not existed, Ragnarok would have already come to pass..."
He paused and didn't continue.
But though he stopped speaking, Thor and the others clearly understood the unspoken meaning.
Which was to say: what the other Thor had experienced... could very well be true.
Asgard's destruction, Odin, Frigga, Loki, and their people all perishing one after another...
The Warriors Three and Heimdall felt a chill run down their spines.
Thor, shocked and dazed, also couldn't help but accept that such a future was possible.
He whispered with a hint of relief, "Thankfully... my brother exists. Otherwise..."
He couldn't bear to imagine that terrible scene.
And as he thought of that, he cast a look of sympathy toward the Thor from the parallel universe.
...
On Earth, at the scene—
After listening to the alternate Thor's account, Coulson and the others imagined the possibility—and found it hard to deny.
"So... Captain," Coulson asked cautiously, "you all came to our universe to collect the six Infinity Stones and restore the other half of the universe's life?"
Black Widow, Steve, and the rest immediately nodded.
Coulson scratched his head awkwardly. "Well... the problem is, none of the Stones are scattered."
"They're all in the hands of the White-Clad Hero. We have no way of retrieving them for you."
"In fact... there's probably no one in this universe who can take them from him."
"Unless... he's willing to give them to you."
Coulson looked around and added in a more serious tone, "That means, Captain, it's up to your ability to persuade him."
"But I'd strongly suggest not trying to take them by force. That would be... unwise."
Of course, Thor and the rest understood the message loud and clear.
Hawkeye forced a chuckle. "You don't need to say it—we know. We're not crazy enough to try and rob a Creator God."
Though he didn't say it out loud, there was still some skepticism in his heart.
Is the Creator God really as powerful as they say?
Since they hadn't witnessed it firsthand, and given the limited intel, some of them still harbored doubts. Maybe it was all a bit exaggerated?
Even if the White-Clad Hero wasn't as omnipotent as claimed... he was still far beyond their level.
After all, reviving the dead—reversing life and death—was already beyond comprehension.
Captain Steve nodded. "Coulson, we understand."
Then he looked up at the sky.
Floating above, clad in pure white and radiating divine mystery, the White-Clad Hero watched over them in silence.
Steve hesitated, then stepped forward and spoke with solemn respect:
"Unknown Creator God, may we... borrow the Infinity Stones?"
"We'll only use them once. We'll return them immediately after."
Hulk quickly chimed in, "Yeah! We promise—we'll give them back right after we're done!"
Beside them, Natasha and the others looked up with hope, their eyes full of quiet pleading.
Thor shifted awkwardly. "B-brother..."
His face flushed red—he wanted to speak, but didn't know how.
High in the sky, Syd opened his eyes and calmly looked down at them.
A thought crossed his mind, and he summoned the Infinity Gauntlet.
As the six radiant gems glittered in the light, Clint and the others couldn't hide their joy.
Syd's voice rang out—serene, cold, unfathomable:
"You want this?"
"Do you understand the importance these Infinity Stones hold to this universe?"
"If the Stones are removed... this universe loses one of its greatest defenses."
"What if something goes wrong, and you fail to return them?"
His tone was calm—yet it felt like divine judgment itself. The voice of cosmic truth echoed in their ears.
The group froze, stunned.
Then Hulk spoke up hastily, "Nothing will go wrong! We'll return them for sure! Creator God, please believe us!"
Syd didn't respond. He merely curled his lip in secret.
You say that now, Banner...
But he hadn't forgotten what happened in their universe—how the Space Stone was lost when Loki stole it due to their carelessness.
Because of that disruption, the Time Variance Authority ended up arresting Loki.
And the Space Stone? It was never returned.
What if something similar happened with these?
In the multiverse, anything was possible.
That said... for him, the Infinity Stones weren't all that crucial anymore.
As he pondered this, his thoughts turned toward the power of Creation—the divine ability of the God he was emulating.
At that moment—
...
On the ground, near Stark Tower—
A portal of golden sparks opened beside Thor and the others.
Out stepped a woman in yellow robes—the Ancient One.
Everyone blinked.
"Who's this?"
They weren't familiar with her, but the magic circle of golden sparks was something they did recognize.
Magic.
That meant... this woman was likely a powerful sorcerer.
Captain America and the others frowned slightly, already sensing something was off.
Sure enough—
The Ancient One walked forward, bowed respectfully to Syd, and said:
"Greetings, Great Creator God."
Then, pausing, she added,
"Creator God, I must warn that handing over all six Infinity Stones to these outsiders carries great risk."
"What?" Rocket shouted angrily. "What the hell are you saying?!"
"What do you mean it's risky to give them to us?!"
Natasha and the others also frowned—clearly sharing the same sentiment.
The Ancient One turned to them calmly. "Giving you the Infinity Stones may save your reality..."
"But what about ours?"
"If we lose all six Stones, this world will be left defenseless against the forces of darkness."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 570
chapters.content:
Chapter 570 - 570
Banner frowned and said, "We already promised—we'll return the Infinity Stones!"
The Ancient One calmly replied, "That promise is only good if you actually can return them."
There was an undeniable distrust in her tone.
Or perhaps—it wasn't distrust in them, but simply that she didn't want to test the bounds of human nature.
After all, who wouldn't be tempted by six Infinity Stones?
If even a single mishap occurred, the Infinity Stones from their universe could end up lost in another.
And if that happened, recovering them would be a nightmare.
In this moment, not only the Ancient One, but many watching around the world through drone feeds shared the same worry.
Banner and the others were growing frustrated at her distrust, about to argue their case—
But Thor didn't care for the back-and-forth. He looked up at the Creator God—his brother in this universe—and pleaded:
"Is it really... not possible?"
Silence fell. Countless eyes turned toward the White-Clad Hero floating above.
Syd glanced at him, then after a moment of thought, shook his head with a light sigh.
"...Fine. I really can't say no to you."
"Even if you're not the Thor of this world... I can lend a small helping hand."
Of course, more than sympathy, Syd was curious about testing the upper limits of his Creation ability.
Hearing his words, Thor froze in place, and deep in his heart... a complicated mix of envy and longing surfaced.
Why did his universe not have a brother like this?
Or rather—why did his legendary brother never appear in real life?
If he had...
His gaze dimmed with sorrow and unwillingness.
Meanwhile, the Ancient One's expression visibly changed.
Steve and the others, on the other hand, were barely containing their excitement.
Just as everyone thought Syd would hand over the Infinity Gauntlet, the unexpected happened.
He released the gauntlet—letting it float beside him—and simply raised his right hand.
His gaze locked on the Time Stone embedded on the gauntlet.
He was about to recreate it.
Activating the power of Creation, divine energy surged from within him.
Bright green light gathered in his palm—
And in the next second, the energy of time rippled through the air!
Within moments, a luminous green gem coalesced into form.
A perfectly condensed Time Stone—complete.
"...It worked."
Syd looked down at the gem hovering in his palm, impressed by the overwhelming strength of Creation.
To avoid interference, he had crafted this Time Stone using the model brought by Infinity Ultron.
The same task, attempted with Chaos Magic, would've exhausted him just to make a fake version.
But with the ability of God's Creation... it was different.
As Syd admired the glowing gem—
Down below, Coulson, Steve, the Ancient One, and countless people around the world watching the broadcast were stunned.
"What is that?"
"The Time Stone?"
They were dazed, their eyes shifting between the original gem on the Gauntlet and the new one in Syd's hand.
"Two... Time Stones?"
"What's happening?!"
Thor and the others cried out in disbelief. Even the Ancient One's eyes widened—her worldview beginning to collapse.
The Time Stone, one of the cosmic gems said to have been born with the universe itself... had just been created?
And she had witnessed it firsthand.
Time... could be created?
The Ancient One was reeling.
Even knowing he was a Creator God—this level of power still seemed unreal.
Before she could recover, Syd casually flicked the Time Stone into the air. It began orbiting him like a satellite.
Then he opened his hand again.
Red light bloomed...
Then purple...
Then yellow...
Under their astonished gazes, one Infinity Stone after another formed from the void, each glowing with unfathomable power.
Syd's divine ability had produced six new Infinity Stones.
Around the White-Clad Hero, the new Stones spun in orbit.
Everyone watching was silent.
Finally, Rocket muttered, "...I think I'm hallucinating. You?"
Ant-Man nodded slowly. "Same..."
"...So we're both seeing the same hallucination?"
"Which means... this is real?"
He sounded like he was trying to convince himself.
But none of them could deny what they'd just seen.
Not Rocket. Not Thor. Not even Odin watching from Asgard... nor the hidden dimensional beings lurking in the shadows.
Infinity Stones can be created?!
The White-Clad Hero just... did that?
What kind of power is this?!
While the entire world reeled in disbelief, Syd gently waved his hand.
The six new Infinity Stones shot down and floated toward Steve and the others.
Syd's tone remained calm:
"The Infinity Stones of your universe were destroyed."
"These six shall serve as replacements."
Steve and his team stared blankly at the radiant gems.
Though the Creator God spoke so casually, they still felt like they were dreaming.
They had... gotten the Infinity Stones?
And not by fighting, or outsmarting someone, or barely surviving a heist...
But by receiving brand new ones—created before their eyes.
Carefully, reverently, they gathered the six Stones.
Even as relief settled over them, a profound realization dawned:
The power of the White-Clad Hero... might truly be beyond comprehension.
At the very least, his strength exceeded that of the six Infinity Stones combined.
Otherwise—how could he have created them?
Just grasping the power of one Stone was already difficult... let alone all six.
And now someone capable of crafting all six stood before them.
Thor couldn't even begin to imagine it.
Then—
"...Your power is incredible," Steve said quietly, overwhelmed. "Thank you. On behalf of all life in our universe... thank you."
The others followed, bowing and offering sincere thanks.
Afterward, they quietly began to prepare to leave.
"With the six Infinity Stones, we can finally..."
But just as they were about to say goodbye, Syd paused.
Should I... go with them?
When he had unlocked Baldr's full progress, he'd been curious about the other universes.
And now, after hearing their stories—he had guesses... but no certainty.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 571
chapters.content:
Chapter 571 - 571
After thinking it through, Syd made a decision.
Just as Natasha and the others were about to activate the device to return to where they came from, he calmly said, "I'll go with you."
His mysterious voice echoed through the air. Coulson and the others were visibly stunned when they heard him speak.
...
S.H.I.E.L.D.
Fury's eyes narrowed in suspicion. "What does the White-Clothed One want?"
It wasn't just him—at this moment, people across the world were all shocked and puzzled, wondering about the White-Clothed One's intentions.
At the scene.
The core members of the Avengers also looked stunned.
The God of Creation standing before them—was actually going to accompany them back to their universe?
After a brief moment of shock, Ant-Man Scott wore an awkward expression as he offered a slight explanation.
"We use a special type of micro-particle for time travel. The amount we have on us is only enough for a one-way trip."
Captain America and the others beside him also looked apologetic.
Thor, who had looked hopeful when he heard the White-Clothed One wanted to go with them, quickly dimmed again after hearing there weren't any extra Pym Particles. He seemed somewhat disappointed.
Just then, Natasha came up with an idea. She opened her mouth to speak.
However, just as she was about to say it, she recalled how Scott hadn't mentioned the Pym Particles by name, which was probably intentional, so she changed her wording.
She said, "The scientist who created those particles is still alive in this time period. Maybe we can ask him for more. Then we can..."
Captain America and the others froze for a moment.
Just as Natasha was about to continue, something completely unexpected happened.
Syd said calmly, "You can go ahead and travel back. I don't need the thing you're talking about."
Natasha and the others were startled.
They naturally understood what the God of Creation meant.
He didn't need to rely on Pym Particles—he could travel through time and space on his own?
Was this the power of the Creator God?
They found it hard to believe.
Hearing his words, Scott suddenly remembered something—his experience in the Quantum Realm.
That blinding red light...
The memory sent a chill down Scott's spine. He blurted out, "The strange phenomenon we ran into in the Quantum Tunnel... could that have been because of you?"
As his words fell, Captain America and the others were reminded of the terrifying red light they'd encountered on their way here—a memory that still sent a shiver down their spines.
"We ended up at the wrong time and place because of that strange red light..." Banner muttered.
Looking up at the figure in white high in the sky, he asked, "Was that you?"
Amid their shocked expressions, Syd casually nodded.
Seeing him nod, Scott couldn't help but shout, "That was the Quantum Realm! Oh my god!"
"Originally, we were supposed to end up during the Battle of New York in 2012—and you were precise enough to drop us here?"
The more he thought about it, the more terrified he became.
Did this mean the Quantum Realm held no secrets from this being?
Could he freely traverse time and space?
Terrifying!
Captain America and the others, hearing this, also came to the same realization and gasped.
So they hadn't been wrong—this God of Creation appeared over Stark Tower on purpose... waiting for them?
As thoughts whirled through their minds, Coulson and the others nearby were also putting the pieces together.
Even if they didn't understand everything, it was clear that the White-Clothed One had influenced them, causing them to travel to the wrong time and place.
Faced with something beyond comprehension, all they could do was be in awe.
After a while, Captain America and the others calmed down again.
They didn't dare to look at the terrifying figure in the sky anymore. After saying their farewells to Coulson, Natasha and the rest prepared to leave.
In the next moment, they activated their Ant-Man suits.
Whoosh
—in Coulson and the others' eyes, they disappeared in an instant, their whereabouts unknown.
But although Coulson and the rest couldn't see, Syd could clearly see everything from the sky.
He watched as their bodies shrank...
And clearly perceived them entering the Quantum Tunnel.
Syd's vast and abstract conceptual form, fully prepared, sensed where they were going.
It was a universe almost identical to this one!
Or rather, it
was
the same—until his appearance caused a divergence in the timeline, splitting it into a parallel universe.
Syd didn't overthink it.
Now that he had sensed the exact location, everything else was simple.
In the next moment, under the watchful eyes of Coulson, the Ancient One, the aliens, and people all around the world, space rippled.
His figure blurred—and vanished on the spot.
Coulson and the others looked at each other, speechless.
Meanwhile...
Captain America and the others exited the Quantum Tunnel and returned to the platform where they had first left.
"We did it!"
Looking at each other, Hawkeye and the rest beamed with joy.
The mission was a great success!
Just as they were celebrating, Syd's figure appeared above them without warning, briefly surveying the area.
He said, "So this is the divergent universe separated from Earth-616."
The sudden voice gave the Avengers a fright.
Looking up, they were stunned.
"This God of Creation... really followed us?!"
"Incredible... he's not even wearing an Ant-Man suit!"
Scott and the others were in disbelief.
Among them, Thor—with long golden hair and a large body—had a trace of excitement on his face.
Syd then looked toward them and turned his gaze to Natasha, speaking words that stunned the whole team.
"Because of my presence, some of you have deviated from your original path."
"According to the normal timeline, not everyone would've returned. Someone should've remained in our world... forever."
Hearing the mysterious words echo from above, Tony and the others fell into confusion and shock.
Someone would've stayed behind?
Did this being have the power to peer into all futures and destinies?
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 572
chapters.content:
Chapter 572 - 572
After all, what the God of Creation had said really did carry such a meaning.
That's what Ant-Man Scott was thinking.
Then, they couldn't help but find it amusing—were they seriously thinking of such absurd things?
Just as that thought crossed their minds, Nebula's expression shifted slightly.
She looked at Hawkeye and Black Widow with a complicated expression, and said in a low voice, "After my sister and Thanos went to Vormir, they never returned."
Hearing this, Tony and the others' expressions changed as realization dawned upon them.
Then came a wave of relief—followed by shock.
This God of Creation... could even know something like that?
Did he truly possess the power to peer into the fate and future of all beings?
Was it the power of the Time Stone?
Or something else...
At the same time, they couldn't help but grow suspicious—what exactly was this God of Creation's purpose?
"Why did he come to our universe?"
"What does he want?"
As their thoughts grew chaotic and confusion about his motives deepened, Syd ignored their inner turmoil. After casually mentioning the topic, he closed his eyes to sense something.
Relying on his Avatar of Light and the abstract concept body of the 616 Prime Universe, he sensed the presences of Eternity, Death, Infinity, Oblivion, and the Planet Devourer.
This left Syd both surprised and unsurprised.
In every Marvel single universe, there existed an incarnation of Eternity. But the true form of Eternity was unique—only one existed, and it was of the multiversal level.
All the rest were avatars.
Of course, even if they were avatars, they were relatively independent, each possessing their own thoughts and will.
It was the same for the other primordial cosmic entities. They all had multiversal-level true bodies.
With that in mind, Syd's expression grew a bit complicated.
"So... I might be the weakest among the Gods of Creation?"
His body was limited to a single universe—he didn't have a multiversal-level self.
It might've been fine if he didn't know... but now that he did, Syd couldn't help but feel powerless and pressured.
At the same time, a terrifying thought crept into his mind.
"If the multiversal-level Eternity and the others one day sense me... what would they do?"
Frowning deeply, a series of frightening scenarios flashed through his thoughts, making him even more determined to grow stronger.
He had to reach multiversal level as soon as possible!
Otherwise, even if he didn't consider Eternity and the rest, there were already enough threats—like Chthon, the God of Black Magic at multiversal level, and the secret masters behind Kamar-Taj: the Vishanti Trinity.
"Fortunately, the versions of Eternity in the 616 Prime Universe are independent enough. Their multiversal main body probably won't notice me anytime soon."
As long as nothing too outrageous happens...
But Syd wasn't the kind to rely on luck. The best path was to strengthen himself to multiversal level.
The question was—when could he achieve it?
Frowning, he murmured, "Seems like... the only hope is to continue unlocking God's powers."
"Hopefully, I can unlock some special abilities from God soon."
Thinking about his 11% unlock progress on the God template, Syd felt a sense of anticipation.
With those thoughts set aside, he refocused on this divergent universe.
To be honest, while other beings might find it difficult to grow stronger, as a God of Creation, he seemed to have a shortcut.
At this moment, he could clearly feel that as long as he willed it, using his abstract concept body and the Avatar of Light, he could also become a God of Creation in this divergent universe.
At that point, he would possess the power of two universes!
Say what you will—just having the power of two universes would be enough to defeat Eternity in the 616 Prime Universe!
The only question was whether he could beat the five cosmic entities working together.
Syd pondered silently.
Of course, two universes' worth of power was still insignificant compared to the vastness of the multiverse.
Countless single universes made up the multiverse—and new ones were being born every moment!
Under normal circumstances, his Avatar of Light could never cover the entire multiverse.
But that was just theoretical—later on, the combined power of numerous universes could definitely speed up his spread across them all.
At least, that was Syd's guess.
"So this is... yet another path to reach the multiversal level?"
Then, he shook his head.
There were still drawbacks to this method. The more universes he covered, the more anomalies would appear. That would make it easier for other multiversal entities to notice him.
But that was a problem for the future—not now.
Looking at this divergent universe, Syd resisted the urge to spread his presence, deciding instead to wait until he'd handled the Avengers' business first.
With that thought, he turned his gaze to the stunned Tony and the others.
He said, "Have you decided who will snap their fingers?"
At his words, Thor and the others looked at each other.
That finger snap—who would do it? It was a life-threatening issue.
As for the Creator God hovering in the sky, they didn't even consider asking.
The fact that he created the Infinity Stones for them was already generous. They wouldn't dare ask for more.
Likewise, Syd had no intention of snapping for them.
Before they could even decide among themselves, Syd seemed to change his mind.
He said, "Fine. I'll help you just a little more."
As Captain America and the others watched in confusion, he raised his right hand.
In the next moment, divine crafting power belonging to God Himself surged forth!
Then, a red, exquisitely-designed mechanical gauntlet was swiftly created.
"What is that?"
The Avengers were dumbfounded.
Syd explained, "It's a mechanical version of the Infinity Gauntlet. Now, decide who will use it."
With a wave of his hand, the six Infinity Stones embedded in Captain America's gear flew out and instantly slotted into the mechanical gauntlet.
Casually tossing it to Captain America, Syd floated a short distance away, gazing at the beautiful landscape.
Now that he had stepped aside, Tony couldn't resist taking the glove from Captain America and inspecting it. The more he looked at it, the more astonished he became.
"What an intricate design!"
This mechanical Infinity Gauntlet—was it really something that the God of Creation made on a whim?
He even understood technology?
Even in Tony's opinion, this glove was astonishingly sophisticated. He himself would need some time to replicate it.
Then, as he kept studying it, a strange expression began forming on his face.
Tony muttered, "Why does this glove look... kind of familiar?"
It felt like...
Beside him, Rocket the raccoon nodded in agreement. "Yeah, it kind of looks like one of your suits."
Captain America and the others all looked surprised.
Come to think of it... it did resemble his style a bit.
What the hell was going on?
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 573
chapters.content:
Chapter 573 - 573
Staring at the red mechanical gauntlet before them, the Avengers wore strange expressions.
Why did this thing look so much like one of Tony's suits?
They didn't want to admit it, but no matter how they looked at it, the resemblance was undeniable.
Not far away, Syd naturally heard their discussion and glanced at them.
They noticed, huh?
Well, it made sense. After all, this thing was based on the gauntlet Tony would create in the future—of course it shared the same style.
Thinking about it, he couldn't help but once again marvel at the power of divine creation.
Even though he knew nothing about mechanics, as long as he had a clear image in his mind, a basic design and idea, his divine crafting power could bring it into existence.
It was a process that completely disregarded scientific principles—creating something from nothing in the truest sense.
In a way, it carried the very essence of omnipotence and creation from nothing!
God's power of creation was worthy of the name!
Seeing them still stunned over the gauntlet and unable to decide who would wield it, Syd frowned slightly and decided to clarify.
"Stop guessing. I created this based on the gauntlet you'll make in the future," he said, eyes falling directly on Tony.
The mysterious, cosmic-truth-like voice left everyone frozen.
They were all left in disbelief.
Especially Tony—his face was full of shock.
This thing... was made according to the gauntlet he would design in the future?
Even though Syd had said it outright, the implications were still overwhelming.
Not to mention the paradox of creating something from the future—just the technological sophistication of the gauntlet was immense. And yet Syd replicated it?
That meant either Syd's technological understanding was equally advanced...
Or he'd created it purely based on imagination?
The former was acceptable, but if it was the latter...
Tony took a deep breath, feeling his scientific worldview start to crack.
"Are all Gods of Creation this ridiculous...?" he muttered in disbelief.
After a while, everyone gradually calmed down.
Now, they began discussing who should be the one to snap using the mechanical Infinity Gauntlet.
At that moment, the chubby Thor raised his hand. "I'll do it."
The others were startled.
"Hey! Stop right there!"
"Thor, wait!"
Seeing him about to approach the gauntlet, Captain America, Hawkeye, and the others rushed to stop him.
Captain America tried to politely dissuade him. "We haven't decided who's going to use it yet."
"So we just sit here and do nothing?" Thor frowned. "Staring into space isn't going to bring everyone back."
"I'm the strongest Avenger. This responsibility has to fall on me!"
Thor said a lot, but Tony and the others still weren't convinced.
Thor wasn't in the right state right now—he still hadn't pulled himself together. Given his current out-of-shape form, they were genuinely worried that one snap might cost him his life.
As the debate continued, Banner finally spoke up. "Let me do it. You all saw what happened to Thanos—the Stones nearly killed him. None of you can handle that kind of power!"
"How do you know you can?" Captain America frowned.
"I don't." Banner shook his head. "But the radiation these Stones emit is primarily gamma..."
As soon as he said that, realization dawned on everyone.
Banner had transformed because of a gamma radiation experiment—he was, without question, the most resistant to it among them.
At the very least, he could withstand more than anyone else.
Everyone fell silent.
Banner picked up the mechanical Infinity Gauntlet with both hands and said, "Let's do this."
Tony gave a serious reminder. "Remember—everyone Thanos wiped out five years ago, you need to bring them back. Bring them to now, to today!"
"Don't change anything from the past five years!"
"I've got it," Banner nodded firmly.
With that, Tony and the others hurried to prepare.
"Friday, activate containment mode!"
The mechanical voice responded.
"Yes, boss."
Metal plates descended from all around the room, sealing them inside to prevent catastrophic damage if anything went wrong.
Those with suits immediately put them on, ready for anything.
As for Syd, he simply watched with a calm expression, making no move to help.
Even if something went wrong with the Infinity Gauntlet—or if all six Stones activated at once—he could withstand it.
His abstract concept body might reside in another universe, but that didn't mean his level had dropped below that of a single-universe god.
If he wanted, he could instantly call upon the power of his 616 Prime Universe concept body.
There might be a bit of a delay or weakening effect—that much was true.
But no matter how weakened, it would still be far beyond the combined force of the six Infinity Stones.
Most importantly, the six Stones in question were created from his own divine power—not natural ones—so it would be incredibly difficult for them to even scratch him.
Under everyone's watchful eyes, Hulk Banner put on the mechanical Infinity Gauntlet.
"Let everyone come back..."
He muttered to himself, focusing his mind on the thought.
At the same time, as soon as he wore the gauntlet, a massive surge of multicolored energy erupted instantly. Banner dropped to the ground in agony, groaning and writhing in pain.
The colorful rays of light crackled like dense bolts of lightning.
The power of the Stones burned through him. His right arm quickly turned black and charred.
Seeing this, Thor panicked. "Something's wrong! Take it off—now!"
"Wait!" Captain America stopped him. "Banner, can you hold on?"
"Say something, Banner!" Tony urged urgently.
As the group grew nervous and chaotic, Syd off to the side couldn't help but purse his lips and shake his head.
"I should've strengthened that glove a bit..."
This wasn't his fault, really. His divine crafting power had faithfully reproduced Tony's future gauntlet.
At the end of the day, the flaw was in Tony's original design.
It made him appreciate just how skilled the Dwarven King's forge had been.
Tony's version might look like an Infinity Gauntlet—but it was little more than a container for the Stones.
In contrast, the Dwarven-made gauntlet actually protected its user and allowed for much better control over the Stones' power.
You could tell just by the expressions—Banner was in agony, while Thanos, though pained, still had a hint of grim satisfaction when using his gauntlet.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 574
chapters.content:
Chapter 574 - 574
In truth, the difference in physical endurance between Hulk and Thanos wasn't that significant—the real issue lay in the gauntlet itself.
When Thanos snapped his fingers, the main damage was done to the Infinity Gauntlet itself, though he did suffer some injuries.
It was when he used the six Stones to destroy the Infinity Stones that he truly paid the price—losing nearly half his life in the process.
If Tony had used the gauntlet forged by the Dwarven King during the Endgame battle, even as a mortal, he might've actually survived.
As for why Tony didn't show any signs of pain when he snapped during Endgame...
Aside from the fact that his suit absorbed most of the damage, a more likely reason was that his body was simply too fragile. The moment the power surged through him, his pain receptors might've been completely destroyed—like anesthesia, making him unable to even feel the agony.
Otherwise, there's no way he wouldn't have shown any pain.
Though all of this crossed Syd's mind, only a moment had passed in real time.
Looking at the agonized expression on Banner's face, Syd frowned. To avoid these people thinking the gauntlet he created was defective, he finally spoke up.
"You should quiet down."
The mysterious, cold voice—like a universal truth—echoed within the sealed room, making the anxious and panicking Tony and the others freeze.
Quiet down?
Was he talking to them?
Still dazed, they were suddenly stunned by what happened next.
The overflowing energy radiating from the six Infinity Stones suddenly plummeted. In an instant, it dropped off a cliff—only a tiny trickle of energy leaked out now and then.
This small amount of power—Banner could handle it easily. Heck, even Tony could probably take it without much more than a tingling sensation.
Seeing this, not just the suffering Banner, but also Tony and the others were left speechless, staring in disbelief.
"What... just happened?"
"Did the Stones shut down?"
Shocked, their eyes slowly turned upward, locking onto the mysterious white figure above them, filled with confusion and awe.
Seeing their astonished faces, Syd calmly explained, "Did no one ever tell you... the Infinity Stones possess a form of instinct?"
"Among them, the Soul and Mind Stones are the most sentient."
His voice, filled with divine and universal resonance, echoed throughout the chamber.
It was true. The Soul Stone was known to have awareness. The Space Stone had the precision to exile Red Skull. The Mind Stone once gave Vision strange sensations and guidance.
The Reality Stone, as an Aether form, could move around and even possess people.
And while the Power and Time Stones hadn't shown much "will" explicitly, Syd had once clearly sensed—and even personally destroyed—the will within them.
Since these Infinity Stones were created using the Ultron variant of the Stones, this "instinctive flaw" carried over... and even got amplified by Syd unconsciously.
And as their original master and creator, the Stones would, naturally, obey him.
Thus, with just a single command from Syd, the Stones instinctively withdrew their energy and began supporting Banner instead.
Everyone was stunned by this revelation.
"What? The Stones have minds of their own?"
"How is that even possible?"
In an instant, they were filled with both amazement and a strange chill.
Then, it all made sense—the Stones' obedience, their strange behavior—it was all because they were created by this God of Creation.
Once they accepted that fact, the group didn't dwell on it too long.
Their attention shifted again to Banner.
He took a deep breath and then calmly raised his right hand.
With surprising ease, he snapped his fingers.
Snap!
In an instant, the Stones surged again with multi-colored energy, flashing with dazzling brilliance.
But to Banner, the surge was nothing more than a tickle—completely harmless.
"Did it work?"
Banner looked around at the others, unsure.
Nothing seemed to have changed.
As they all exchanged confused glances, Syd's brow furrowed slightly. He looked up, sensing something.
In his eyes, countless grey specks of dust were drifting down and gathering on the ground—gradually forming into human figures.
At the same time, he sensed the Soul Stone connecting to a hidden dimension—and unlocking it.
A vast number of souls were released, each one returning to its original body.
Though this sounded long, it all happened in the blink of an eye, thanks to the Time Stone's manipulation.
If not for his hyper-fast perception, even Syd might've missed it.
He let out a faint sigh—it was pretty much what he expected.
Just then, a phone started ringing.
Hawkeye walked over and picked it up.
His eyes widened when he saw the caller ID—it was his wife, Laura, who had perished five years ago.
He froze in disbelief, then murmured, "We did it..."
He quickly answered the call.
As Hawkeye walked off in a daze, Banner and the others exchanged looks, and realization dawned on them.
Soon, after checking around, everyone's faces lit up with joy.
They had really done it!
And this time, with no interference from Thanos—or perhaps because the Thanos of this divergent 616 universe didn't dare show himself—everything went smoothly and quietly.
At least... it seemed quiet here.
The world outside had already erupted into chaos.
The people who had disappeared five years ago were suddenly returning!
Shouts and cries of disbelief echoed across the globe.
On a lawn outside a villa...
An elderly woman with white hair was watering her plants when she suddenly froze.
She stared in stunned disbelief as her son gradually reformed from the dust.
Her face lit up with shock and joy.
"Oh my God!"
"Joel?!"
"You're alive?!"
"What happened?!"
He even looked so young, like nothing had changed—like it was still five years ago!
Tears welled up in Sammy's eyes.
And scenes like this were unfolding all around the world.
Every global agency and government was scrambling to respond to the return of billions who had vanished.
This event—where half the Earth's population disappeared and then returned five years later—would soon be known as the Reversal.
At that moment, Star-Lord, Spider-Man Peter Parker, Doctor Strange, and the others who had just come back exchanged excited looks.
"We did it!" Strange smiled faintly.
But then, his expression turned somber. He murmured to himself, "Tony will seize that one chance..."
"He..."
A vision of Tony's death flashed through Doctor Strange's mind.
In his eyes, they had won the final battle thanks to Tony—but also because of that, he would...
Not far away—
Peter noticed his expression and asked curiously, "Doctor Strange, are you okay?"
Strange shook his head slightly. "It's nothing."
Just then, Star-Lord grinned. "Hey, cheer up, man! We're back! That means Cap and the others beat Thanos. We won! What's with the long face?"
"He's right!" Drax and Mantis nodded vigorously.
Strange sighed inwardly and didn't speak the harsh truth aloud. Instead, he said, "Let's head back."
He waved his hand.
Sparks flew into a swirling circle—a portal had opened.
Doctor Strange stepped toward it, with Peter and the rest following close behind.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 575
chapters.content:
Chapter 575 - 575
As he stepped through the portal, Doctor Strange paused, startled.
The scene before him didn't match what he had envisioned.
At this moment in time, shouldn't Thanos already be piloting his warship, invading Earth, and blasting the Avengers' headquarters to rubble?
Why was it... that the headquarters remained completely intact?
Even Thanos's warship was nowhere to be seen.
"Where's Thanos...?"
Doctor Strange stood there, dumbfounded.
"Doctor Strange, what's wrong?" Peter Parker asked curiously.
"This isn't what I expected. The future shouldn't look like this. How could the Time Stone be wrong...?" Strange murmured in disbelief.
"What exactly happened...?"
He had already prepared himself. After confirming that the Avengers' base had been destroyed, he planned to head to Kamar-Taj and have Wong gather every available superhero using portals.
They would all charge together, launching an all-out counterattack against Thanos and his army!
He had even pictured the final outcome in his mind—
Tony would seize that one, fleeting opportunity and unleash a blinding snap!
That was the one and only winning chance he had foreseen!
But the current situation was completely beyond his expectations. It didn't match the future he had seen at all.
What had happened?
Hearing Strange's murmured words, Peter and the others also paused in confusion.
"Doctor Strange... you used the Time Stone?"
"The future changed?"
While they were still puzzled, Strange—just to be safe—used a spell to send a message to Wong and the others, instructing them to begin gathering heroes.
After that, he stood quietly in place, waiting, while Peter and the others looked on with concern.
But no matter how long he waited... Thanos and his warship never appeared.
Strange was baffled.
Even if Thanos had a flair for drama, this delay was far too long.
Hesitating, he finally opened a new portal—this one leading directly to the Avengers' headquarters.
He stepped through, followed closely by Peter and the others, all still confused.
...
Avengers Headquarters.
The Hulk and the others were still basking in the joy of the successful snap when a portal opened before them.
Seeing Doctor Strange step through, followed by Spider-Man and the others, the Avengers were filled with joy.
Tony, in particular, strode forward without hesitation and pulled Peter into a huge hug.
"Mister Stark..." Peter was just as emotional.
As they caught up, Strange couldn't hold back anymore and asked, "Where's Thanos?"
The room fell silent.
All eyes turned toward Strange, puzzled.
A second later—
"What do you mean, 'where's Thanos'?"
"Isn't he already dead? Thor chopped off his head with an axe, remember?"
War Machine, puzzled, asked the question aloud.
Thor and the others nodded in agreement, staring at Strange with confusion.
Strange's shock deepened.
He wasn't referring to this Thanos who had died early on.
He meant the Thanos from the past timeline—the one who, through Nebula's interference, had been brought into the present with his warship, catching everyone off-guard.
In the vision he had seen, that past Thanos launched a devastating attack that leveled Avengers HQ with a single blast.
But now...?
Had the future really changed?
How could this be?
After a moment of silence, Strange finally explained, "I'm not talking about our Thanos. I mean the Thanos from the past timeline."
Everyone froze at his words.
The past Thanos?
What was he talking about?
What did the past timeline's Thanos have to do with them?
Strange turned and looked out through the tall windows of the base, scanning the skies—still expecting to see the looming shadow of Thanos's warship.
But no matter how hard he looked, he saw no warship.
Instead, what he did see... was a white figure floating serenely above the rooftop.
Had it not been for his eyes spotting him, Strange wouldn't have even noticed—there had been no sense of presence at all.
He hadn't sensed anything from that person?
Eyes wide in disbelief, Strange asked, "Who is that?"
Star-Lord and the others instinctively looked up as well—and saw Syd, dressed in white, radiating a mysterious presence.
The moment they laid eyes on him, they froze.
Just looking at him, they could tell—this was no ordinary mortal.
He exuded an aura of mystery and awe that was impossible to fake.
It took them a moment to snap out of their daze.
Among them, Drax, bald and broad, his red body covered in ritual-like markings, couldn't help but ask, "Why can he fly?"
Star-Lord glanced at Thor, then back at the mysterious man in white floating overhead. He mumbled, "Why do I feel like this guy is even stronger than Thor..."
He hadn't said a word, yet just standing there, he gave off such an oppressive, divine pressure.
At that moment, Star-Lord made up his mind. He would no longer try to mimic Thor. He wouldn't try to talk like him anymore.
Look at this guy in white—he didn't need to do anything to be cool.
This was who he needed to study and emulate!
As he daydreamed—picturing himself in white, radiating divine energy and stunning everyone—
Thor and the others were just about to explain to them who this being actually was.
But before they could speak, something strange happened outside.
A ripple of yellow sparks appeared—a portal opening.
The first to walk through were three dark-skinned figures, dressed in sleek, black vibranium armor. The one in the center was unmistakable: the Black Panther.
They were people from Wakanda.
Wakanda—a seemingly impoverished, agricultural nation in Africa—was, in truth, the most technologically advanced country on Earth, and the sole possessor of the precious metal vibranium.
Still, they... did kind of look like tribal warriors.
At least, that's how it struck Syd, who watched them through the transparent windows with a slight frown. Something about their appearance felt... off.
Tony and the others inside could also see the portal and the three Wakandans walking through.
Before they could even react, more portals began opening—one after another.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 576
chapters.content:
Chapter 576 - 576
From the portals emerged an endless stream of warriors, soldiers, and high-tech aircraft.
Famous superheroes were among them—Captain America's old friend Bucky, the Winter Soldier, the Scarlet Witch, and even the Valkyrie, one of Asgard's last survivors.
Also arriving were many spellcasters from Kamar-Taj.
Logically, once they passed through these portals, they were supposed to immediately face Thanos and his army.
A fierce, grand-scale battle was supposed to erupt!
But the scene before them was far from what Valkyrie and the others had expected.
There was no sign of Thanos or his army—only calm, quiet peace.
After a long moment of silence, someone finally broke.
"Where's Thanos?"
"What's going on?"
Everyone looked around, completely baffled.
...
Avengers Headquarters.
Through the floor-to-ceiling windows, Captain America and the others clearly saw the overwhelming scene outside.
Besides shock and astonishment, they weren't quite sure how to handle this sudden development.
At that moment, Doctor Strange waved his hand and opened a portal to the outside.
He stepped through.
Seeing this, the others thought for a moment and followed one by one.
Soon, the anti-Thanos army stood face to face with Strange and the Avengers.
Among them, the Scarlet Witch, hands glowing red, couldn't hold back her fury.
"Strange, what is going on here?"
"Where is Thanos?!"
Her eyes flared with hatred.
She loathed Thanos with every fiber of her being—for taking everything from her.
She had sworn to kill him, no matter what.
Not far away, Black Panther also frowned. "Strange, what's the situation?"
Countless questioning eyes fell on Doctor Strange. Even the Avengers beside him looked toward him in confusion.
Realizing there was no longer any way to hide the truth, Strange took a deep breath and began to explain.
"I used the Time Stone to see countless possibilities..."
Strange recounted how he had seen over 14 million futures, and only one where they won.
During his explanation, he laid out the Avengers' original plan in detail.
When he reached the part about how their time-traveling quest to gather the Infinity Stones would also inadvertently attract a past version of Thanos, everyone was stunned.
Their gazes slowly turned toward Nebula.
According to Strange's description, it was due to the past version of Nebula infiltrating the timeline that Thanos and his army had managed to travel to the present.
"Thanos's other adopted daughter, Nebula?"
All eyes turned to the blue-skinned, cybernetically enhanced woman.
Feeling their stares, Nebula instinctively took a step back and gritted her teeth. "That has nothing to do with me. I don't know anything about it!"
She quickly added, "I never split off from the rest of the team!"
At that, the Avengers immediately stepped in to defend her.
"She's right—Nebula never left our side."
"I can vouch for that."
"So can I..."
Natasha and the others spoke up one after another.
With that, the confused gazes turned back to Doctor Strange, waiting for his clarification.
Strange, visibly puzzled, turned to Nebula and the team. "You didn't split up when collecting the Stones?"
Black Panther and the others were just as confused, but Captain America quickly caught on.
He explained, "Originally, that was the plan. Thor and Rocket went for the Aether. Barton and Natasha went for the Soul Stone..."
He paused for a moment, then continued, "According to the original plan, Rhodey and Nebula were supposed to retrieve the Power Stone. Maybe..."
"...something went wrong during that part. Maybe Thanos's people discovered her."
At that, Natasha, Thor, and the others exchanged looks as things started clicking into place.
Even Nebula seemed to realize something.
Black Panther and the rest were momentarily stunned.
Doctor Strange furrowed his brow. "Wait... 'original plan'?"
He instantly realized something had changed—something during the mission to retrieve the Stones had deviated from what he foresaw.
That must be why this unexpected outcome had occurred.
But the more he thought about it, the less it made sense.
In theory, everything should've unfolded as expected. So what had the power to alter the future—even the one predicted by the Time Stone?
Strange was both alarmed and bewildered. He couldn't believe there was something that could interfere with the vision of the Time Stone.
"What exactly did you experience?" he asked gravely.
Scarlet Witch and the others also looked on in confusion.
At that moment, an image appeared in the Avengers' minds—a mysterious white figure.
Captain America thought for a moment and said, "Our original plan was just as you described, Strange. But during the mission, something went wrong. Our travel was disrupted."
"There was... a strange force in the Quantum Realm that interfered."
At that, Strange and the others were visibly stunned.
A mysterious force?
What could do that?
Some people in the crowd didn't know much about the Quantum Realm, but others did.
From among the anti-Thanos army, the newly resurrected Wasp couldn't help but speak up in disbelief, "That's the Quantum Realm. There's no way anything can affect it!"
"Are you sure you didn't make a mistake?"
Captain America and the others shook their heads.
He continued, "Because of that force, the time and location of our arrival were altered. All of us ended up in the same place."
This revelation shocked Wasp and the others.
Doctor Strange frowned and asked, "And then what happened?"
The Avengers glanced at one another.
As Black Panther and the rest began to grow impatient and even more puzzled, Ant-Man Scott had no choice but to speak up.
"What happened next... might be a little beyond what you're expecting. But I swear—it's all true."
That statement stunned everyone.
Beyond their imagination?
What could possibly be beyond their imagination?
They had no idea...
(End of Chapter)
