chapters.title: Chapter 577
chapters.content:
Chapter 577 - 577
Under the watchful gaze of countless curious faces, Captain America slowly began to speak.
"Due to the influence of that mysterious force, we arrived at the wrong time and place. After some investigation... we discovered something."
"The place we arrived at was a parallel universe—almost identical to ours in every way. Events developed similarly, but..."
He paused, hesitating for a moment, carefully choosing how to describe what came next.
While he was mulling over the words, Black Panther and the others were already showing surprise.
"A parallel universe?"
Though this was a bit unexpected, after everything they'd seen, it wasn't enough to shake them too much.
"If it's just a parallel universe, is that really worth such a fuss from Cap and the others?"
"Yeah, seems a bit overblown..."
But just as their confusion grew, they noticed Captain America's expression darken with unusual seriousness—and that look alone made their hearts skip a beat.
What was going on?
The next moment, they heard him say with solemn gravity, "The biggest difference between that world and ours... was a particular presence."
"That being was a God of Creation."
The words dropped—and silence swept the crowd.
Whether it was Black Panther, Scarlet Witch, or Valkyrie from Asgard—everyone looked as if they had just heard something incomprehensible.
"A God of Creation?"
"Cap... are you joking?"
"How could there be something like a God of Creation in the universe?!"
They didn't want to believe what he said—because it shattered everything they thought they knew.
As one astonished gaze after another fell on him, Steve remained composed. After all, he'd been in their shoes not long ago.
With a serious expression, he began to explain. "Legend has it that our universe has five Gods of Creation. Each one embodies an abstract concept of the universe."
"They represent Eternity, Death, Infinity, Oblivion, and the Devourer of Worlds. Together, they form the framework of our universe..."
As they listened, whether it was Black Panther or Scarlet Witch or anyone else, their expressions morphed from doubt to shock and complete bewilderment.
The universe... was built by conceptual gods?
Captain America paused, then continued, "But the being I'm talking about... wasn't one of the five. This one was different."
"He isn't part of the legends, but he is a God of Creation. The sixth one."
"Because of his existence, our two universes diverged drastically."
At those words, everyone was stunned.
By now, they understood—what had split the timeline and caused such differences between universes was this sixth God of Creation.
But... what did that have to do with Cap and the others?
Even if such a being existed, it had nothing to do with them—there's no way the Avengers had direct contact with someone like that.
"So what does that have to do with you?" someone asked.
Captain America replied seriously, "Remember what I told you earlier? That a mysterious force interfered with our travel through the Quantum Realm?"
"That force... came from the God of Creation."
Black Panther and the others widened their eyes in disbelief.
Wasp was completely stunned. "A God of Creation's power...?"
"Incredible. Something actually managed to interfere with the Quantum Realm?"
She wasn't alone—others also began to grasp how extraordinary such power must be.
"So this God of Creation... is the reason your time-travel jump went wrong?" Black Panther asked. "Then what happened next?"
That was the question on everyone's mind.
Under everyone's gaze, Captain America recounted their experience.
When he explained how they discovered the six Infinity Stones were with this God of Creation—and that he just so happened to be on Earth—everyone leaned in, not wanting to miss a word.
"We saw... that white-clothed Creator God... bring two people back to life."
When Captain America described how the Creator God resurrected Kingpin's wife and son, the audience was stunned.
Gasps filled the air.
"Bringing people back to life?!"
"That's impossible, isn't it?!"
Everyone was shaken.
Even among superheroes, the idea of reviving someone who had died years ago was utterly insane.
They didn't even consider the idea that the Infinity Stones could do that—because in their minds, it was completely different.
The Stones were cosmic artifacts. The Creator's act... was divine.
Captain America shook his head. "We saw him create two physical bodies and bring them to life."
Beside him, Black Widow and the others nodded gravely to show they weren't lying.
Even so, Strange and the others still found it all a bit too unbelievable.
Among the crowd, Wanda's dull eyes lit up with a spark of hope.
Then Captain America continued telling how they had asked the Creator God for the Infinity Stones.
As they listened, many of them broke into a cold sweat.
But when they heard that the Creator God casually raised his hand and created the six Infinity Stones, everyone's jaws dropped.
"He created the Infinity Stones?!"
"Cap, are you out of your mind?"
"Those are the Infinity Stones we're talking about!"
Several of those present had interacted with the Stones before—Scarlet Witch, Doctor Strange, and Star-Lord especially were well aware of the power those things held.
"Each Stone contains virtually unlimited energy. How can something like that be created?" Star-Lord exclaimed.
He still remembered how the Power Stone had nearly killed him—and the thought alone made him shiver.
So no—he absolutely refused to believe the Infinity Stones could be created.
Even Doctor Strange, who had wielded the Time Stone often, nodded in agreement.
He knew just how vast the power of time was.
That kind of cosmic authority... how could it be artificially forged?
Looking at their skeptical faces, Captain America and the others couldn't help but sigh.
Telling the truth, and still no one believed them?
That was when Banner raised his right hand, revealing the mechanical gauntlet—with six Infinity Stones embedded in it.
He said earnestly, "These six Infinity Stones were created by that being."
"We saw it with our own eyes."
"Just moments ago, I used them to snap and bring you all back."
"These Stones are real."
As his voice fell, all eyes focused on Banner's right hand.
And the dazzling, multicolored Infinity Stones upon it.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 578
chapters.content:
Chapter 578 - 578
With a serious expression, Black Panther asked, "These Infinity Stones... were really created by that so-called Creator God?"
Banner and the others nodded.
Seeing their solemn, unwavering expressions, completely unlike someone lying or exaggerating, everyone felt a wave of shock.
It took a long moment for the crowd to gather themselves, exchanging glances as they silently came to accept this earth-shattering truth.
After some time, Doctor Strange suddenly spoke, eyes filled with disbelief, "So it was that Creator God who caused the predicted future seen by the Time Stone... to change?"
"If such a being truly exists, then... yeah, even the Time Stone's vision being altered might actually make sense."
Hearing this, Black Panther and the others nodded thoughtfully.
So that was the reason the future he saw had changed?
Just as the crowd began to digest this idea, Valkyrie asked curiously, "So you guys just returned with the six Infinity Stones?"
"And then used them to bring everyone back?"
All eyes again turned to Captain America's team.
Natasha and the others nodded in confirmation.
Black Panther and the others finally understood how everything had unfolded.
But at that moment, Ant-Man suddenly remembered something and quickly said with a grave tone, "Wait—there's one more thing we forgot to mention."
"A very important thing."
At that, Natasha, Steve, and the others immediately realized what he meant. Their expressions turned serious.
Seeing their unusual reactions, Wanda and the others were puzzled.
What could possibly be important enough to shock them like this?
"What are you talking about?"
Just as the questions were about to pile up, a blazing figure streaked down from the sky at incredible speed.
Everyone turned instinctively to look—and saw a woman surrounded by glowing energy and radiant fire, floating above the ground.
She had golden hair, a square-jawed face, and a strong, athletic build.
"Carol?"
Someone in the crowd recognized her.
At the sound of that name, many others looked surprised and began murmuring.
"I've heard of her. That Carol's supposed to be incredibly strong—famous across the galaxy. Stronger than all the Avengers combined, is that true?"
"Is she really that powerful..."
Hearing these comments, Thor looked displeased. He reflexively tightened his grip on Stormbreaker.
Captain Marvel Carol noticed his reaction and looked straight at him.
Their eyes locked. The tension between them instantly thickened.
"What? You wanna go a few rounds?" Carol rolled her wrists, clearly eager.
Seeing that the two of them were about to fight, Star-Lord sighed and said, "Hey! If you're gonna fight, do it later. Let Cap finish what he was saying first!"
At that, both Carol and Thor paused and looked away awkwardly.
The others quickly remembered—Cap's team had mentioned something extremely important just moments ago.
Everyone turned their attention back, curious.
Carol, still floating and surrounded by radiant energy, also looked intrigued. She'd heard some of the earlier conversation, and she was just as curious now.
All eyes locked onto the Avengers.
Ant-Man glanced at the others, and in the end, it was Captain America who stepped forward. He took a deep breath and spoke word by word, seriously:
"The Creator God I spoke of... came here to our universe along with us."
The moment the words left his mouth, the entire area fell into absolute silence.
Those who were already aware of the situation—like Doctor Strange—were instantly stunned, their faces full of disbelief.
Carol, unaware of everything, looked baffled. "What Creator God? What are you even talking about?"
At that moment—
Doctor Strange, deeply shaken, asked uncertainly, "The one who resurrected people... the one who created the six Infinity Stones... that Creator God followed you here?"
"Yes," Steve nodded.
Hissss—
The sound of collective gasps filled the air. Faces all around turned pale with astonishment and disbelief.
No one even knew what words to use to describe their emotions.
It felt like... God Himself was about to appear before their eyes.
While shock rippled through the crowd, Captain Marvel frowned. "What is going on? A Creator God?"
Seeing her confusion, Bruce Banner quickly gave her a rundown of what had happened.
As he spoke, Carol's eyes widened gradually, her shock rising until it matched the rest.
Resurrecting the dead?
Creating six Infinity Stones?
A God of Creation?
Carol had spent years wandering through space and had heard vague tales of Creator Gods. But to her, they were always just legends.
Even then, she'd only ever heard of five such beings. Not once had she heard of this mysterious sixth Creator God the others were describing.
Could such a being really exist?
Even if he came from a different universe... it still sounded far too unbelievable.
Carol couldn't help but doubt.
After thinking for a bit, she looked serious again and asked, "So... where is this Creator God you're talking about?"
The air tensed instantly.
Everyone looked at Steve and the others, waiting for an answer.
Tony and his team exchanged glances, then collectively turned to look behind them—at the Avengers headquarters.
That's when they realized...
The majestic Creator God hadn't followed them out here.
Which could only mean—he was still inside.
Seeing their reaction, Carol and the rest followed their gaze.
"That being is... over there?"
Nervous tension built throughout the group.
There was a moment of silent agreement.
"Should we... go take a look?"
No one objected.
In the next moment, a vast crowd of people, along with several spaceships, moved swiftly toward the headquarters.
Fortunately, the distance wasn't far. It didn't take long for them to arrive.
Inside—
Syd floated peacefully within the building, enjoying the view outside.
Through the glass walls, he calmly observed the sea of people approaching.
Of course, he knew exactly why they were coming.
But he didn't do anything special. He simply floated forward and slowly emerged from the building.
Outside.
Just as the large group arrived, Scarlet Witch and the others looked up—only to see a white figure float out from the building.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 579
chapters.content:
Chapter 579 - 579
As they watched the white-robed figure hovering in midair, exuding an overwhelming sense of mystery and divine presence, Black Panther and the others momentarily froze.
However, none of them immediately believed that this man was the so-called Creator God.
After all, with how Thor and the others had described him—so exaggerated, so awe-inspiring—how could this ordinary-looking person fit that image?
Sure, he looked mysterious. His aura was powerful. But a Creator God shouldn't appear so... normal.
At the very least, he shouldn't look this human.
From the crowd, Star-Lord and Doctor Strange both suddenly blurted out, "It's him?"
Everyone turned in confusion and began to ask.
"Strange, you know this guy?"
"Who is he? Why's he here?"
Facing the questions, Strange shook his head. "We don't know who he is. We just saw him once. If you want to know more, you'll have to ask Cap and the others."
At that, all the curious gazes turned to Captain America and his group again.
Captain America hesitated for a second, then said solemnly and clearly, "He is the Creator God."
The words echoed through the air.
But now, no one had the mood to process the tone or phrasing. Everyone just stared blankly at the white-robed figure floating in the sky.
He... was the Creator God?
Black Panther and the rest couldn't believe it.
Especially Star-Lord, Drax, Doctor Strange, and even Carol Danvers. All of them looked equally stunned.
All of them were thinking the same thing:
A Creator God looks like... that?
Yes, he looked mysterious. Yes, his presence was striking. But... compared to the awe-inspiring title of Creator God, he looked almost too normal.
He just didn't look the part.
For a few moments, no one said a word.
Then, Captain Marvel Carol couldn't hold back. Staring at the man floating in the distance, she said with narrowed eyes:
"This is the 'Creator God' you were talking about?"
"He doesn't look the part to me."
There was deep skepticism in her eyes.
She continued, "I've spent years out in space, and I've heard tales of the Creator Gods too."
"But from everything I've heard, there are only five: Eternity, Death, Oblivion, Infinity, and the World Devourer."
"Each one is said to possess unfathomable power. As for this guy..."
Her gaze landed sharply on the white-robed man.
"You're telling me he is the same as them? That he's on the same level?"
"Are you sure you all haven't been fooled?"
Her words echoed loudly.
And they instantly lit a spark of doubt in many of those present.
Could Captain America and the others really have been deceived...?
Steve and the others frowned immediately, clearly unhappy.
But before they could say anything, Syd—still floating in the air—turned his gaze toward Carol Danvers.
To be honest, he'd never had much fondness for her. Not in this universe, and not in 616 either.
He clearly remembered the time he fought her under the identity of the Messiah.
Carol met his gaze without flinching, even emboldened by the belief that this man might be deceiving her friends. She was itching to test him.
Her eyes showed it—defiance, challenge.
Syd's expression remained calm. He said nothing.
Instead, he simply released the divine pressure he had been suppressing.
Suddenly, the air around him grew heavy and warped. His divine aura intensified.
The mysterious aura around him bloomed into something overwhelming.
Carol's face instantly changed.
Caught off-guard by the terrifying pressure, she dropped from the sky like a stone.
Others were affected too. One by one, they either dropped to a knee or collapsed entirely under the weight of that divine force.
Syd hovered in the air, looking down at them with cold, indifferent eyes. His expression didn't change at all.
He'd expected this.
After all, the divine pressure inherited from Orochi and Baldr was already extremely formidable—he normally kept it sealed for that exact reason.
But ever since ascending to a Creator God, his presence had become something else entirely. His mere aura distorted reality.
And this wasn't even him trying.
If he had tried, it would've been far, far worse.
As he looked down at them, a strange feeling bloomed in everyone's hearts.
It felt like... this being above them was a true god, towering high above the sky, while they—were nothing more than insects. Creatures born to crawl before his feet.
The gap between them was too vast. Unimaginably so.
Doctor Strange felt this even more acutely than the rest.
His face twisted in shock.
Not even Dormammu had ever given him this feeling!
Could it be that...
"He really is... a Creator God?" Strange muttered, still in disbelief.
Spider-Man Peter Parker was pale, sweat running down his entire body.
"M-Mister... he's terrifying. I've never felt anything this terrifying before..."
And he wasn't alone.
Everyone felt the same—except for one person.
Carol Danvers.
Though shaken to her core, humiliation quickly replaced fear.
She'd always been dominant in battle, especially out in space. She had never experienced anything like this before.
Burning with defiance, she lit up in blazing energy, forcing herself to rise back into the air under the crushing pressure.
Teeth clenched, she met the white-robed figure's gaze again.
One look—filled with bitterness and fury.
While his was calm and indifferent, as if nothing had happened.
That dismissiveness only fueled her rage.
Then—she prepared to attack.
But before she could act, a golden spear formed entirely of divine light suddenly pierced through her abdomen.
Her heavily fortified body might as well have been made of paper—no resistance at all.
Thud!
With a cry of pain, Carol was pinned to the ground.
In the next second—four more spears of light appeared.
Shunk—shunk—shunk—shunk!
They stabbed into her wrists and ankles.
Everything had happened in a single second.
By the time everyone reacted, Carol was already nailed to the ground, completely immobilized.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 580
chapters.content:
Chapter 580 - 580
Even as she blazed with energy, radiating intense heat in her Binary mode, it was no use.
Captain Marvel Carol Danvers tried desperately to absorb the energy from the spears of light that pierced her.
But the moment she tried, she failed.
These spears felt as real as solid matter. Their density was unimaginable—completely immune to her absorption. No matter how hard she tried, she couldn't drain even a flicker of power.
Worse yet, a chilling realization struck her:
If she had managed to absorb any of that energy... it might've torn her body apart.
Shaken, Carol quickly tried a different method.
In Binary mode, she could control the entire electromagnetic spectrum—infrared, ultraviolet, X-rays, and more.
But the next second, she froze.
She couldn't manipulate anything. It was as if her connection to the electromagnetic spectrum had been severed entirely.
"What... what is this...?"
Carol stared in disbelief.
At the same time, Black Panther and the others were also stunned.
Even if most of them didn't have a particularly good impression of the arrogant and brash Carol Danvers, no one could deny how powerful she was. Among them, she was one of the strongest by far.
And now, that same powerhouse... was pinned to the ground like an insect, unable to resist in the slightest?
They couldn't believe what they were seeing.
What kind of power is this?
One by one, they lifted their heads with difficulty, staring up at the white-robed figure floating above—filled with awe and shock.
Was this all his doing?
Was this man really a Creator God?
It seemed too absurd to be true.
But as they stared, Syd remained expressionless, unmoved by any of it.
Through his telepathic powers, he could clearly sense the storm of disbelief and denial in Carol's mind.
It almost made him want to laugh.
How naive.
Those spears may have looked small—but the energy they contained was beyond imagination. And with his absolute control, breaking free was impossible for a mortal like her.
As for manipulating the electromagnetic spectrum?
How ridiculous.
Even though Syd had not yet formally become the Creator God of this parallel universe, within the range of his perception, all sources of light, heat, and energy were already under his domain.
Not even beings like Death could take that control from him.
It was his divine authority.
Carol trying to manipulate it in front of him... was just laughable.
Hovering above them, Syd's eyes stayed cold as he looked down at Carol.
Sensing imminent death, a wave of terror surged in Carol's heart.
And for the first time, she truly realized—this being might actually be a Creator God. Someone she should never have provoked.
She braced herself for the end.
But instead of striking, Syd simply looked away.
As if she was no more than a pebble on the roadside, a gnat buzzing in the air—not even worth a glance.
That indifference struck Carol harder than any blow. Her face flushed red with humiliation.
She would've preferred he killed her—anything was better than this condescension.
She was Earth's first Avenger. A warrior feared across the stars. A symbol of power and justice.
And in his eyes, she was nothing?
Her heart twisted in fury and frustration.
But Syd paid her no mind.
Instead, his gaze turned to the others below—to Black Panther and the stunned crowd.
Then, he looked directly at Thor, Valkyrie, and the last remaining Asgardian soldiers.
His voice echoed, deep and resonant, like a cosmic law:
"Come with me. We're returning to Asgard."
The words stunned everyone.
Valkyrie and the remaining Asgardians blinked in disbelief.
Even Black Panther and the others looked utterly confused.
"Return to Asgard? What does he mean?"
Wasn't Asgard destroyed?
They didn't understand what this so-called Creator God meant.
But those who had been to the other universe—Cap and his team—instantly caught on.
Thor's eyes lit up with a glimmer of joy.
Yes, Hulk's snap had brought many people back.
But not his family.
Not his father, Odin.
Not his mother.
Not Loki.
And not Asgard.
He had nothing left.
So when he heard Syd's words, he couldn't help but feel joy spark inside him.
This Creator God—his brother—wanted to go with him?
"Baldr... you're really my brother?" Thor whispered, trembling with joy.
Ever since visiting that alternate universe, he'd been jealous.
Jealous of that version of himself—who had a brother like Baldr.
And now...
Was this Baldr truly accepting him? Acknowledging him?
Did he finally... have family again?
Thor's eyes welled up with tears.
He wasn't alone anymore.
Above them—
Syd watched as Thor's face shifted through sorrow and joy. His expression twitched slightly.
A few seconds passed, and as Thor remained caught in his emotions, Syd prepared to speak.
But then Thor finally composed himself.
"...Brother," he said solemnly, "Asgard is gone. You'll have to come with me to our new home."
Before Syd could reply, the crowd around them erupted in shock.
"Brother?!"
"What did he just say?"
"Did we hear that right?!"
Eyes darted between Thor and the white figure in the sky.
Thor just called him... brother?
The shock rippled across the crowd like a tidal wave.
Even Valkyrie and the remaining Asgardians were dumbfounded.
"His Highness Thor... what is he saying?"
"Another brother? But Loki is gone..."
"When did Odin have another son?!"
They were all stunned and confused.
Meanwhile, Syd remained calm.
Hearing Thor's somber words, he gave the God of Thunder a faint glance.
And then—his voice echoed once more, like a cosmic truth:
"If Asgard is gone... then I will create a new one."
Everyone froze.
Black Panther and the others blinked in confusion.
Create a new Asgard?
What did he mean?
Was he going to designate some land on Earth and call it "New Asgard"?
That was the only thing they could imagine.
Even Valkyrie and the surviving Asgardians thought that was what he meant.
They didn't even consider the other possibility.
Because it was simply... unthinkable.
But Thor—his heart skipped a beat.
Could it be...?
Just as that terrifying thought crossed his mind, Syd raised his hand.
With a wave, space shimmered like rippling water.
A massive, circular portal opened in the air.
It led directly to the remains of the destroyed Asgard.
"Let's go," Syd said calmly.
And with that, he floated toward the portal and entered.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 581
chapters.content:
Chapter 581 - 581
Syd drifted into the spatial tunnel.
But behind him, Thor, Valkyrie, and the rest of the Asgardians stood there dumbfounded.
They weren't particularly surprised by the sudden appearance of the spatial tunnel—but what troubled them was the view on the other side.
Floating stones hovered in the pitch-black void of space, the entire area engulfed in dead silence.
Even now, a massive amount of air was still being sucked into the tunnel from their side.
Seeing this, Thor and the others exchanged glances.
If they stepped through now, even as Asgardians, they'd only be able to hold out for a short while before their lives were endangered.
After all, space—with its absolute cold and total void—wasn't something a regular being could endure.
They instinctively glanced at the white-robed god drifting in the void on the other side of the portal, completely unaffected.
The sight made their expressions twitch.
The others, including Black Panther, also noticed.
Even those among them without much scientific knowledge could guess that stepping through that tunnel meant certain death.
While Thor hesitated, unsure how to proceed, Syd turned around and immediately understood why they were hesitating.
Without any grand gestures, he created something.
A soft glow emanated around him as limitless oxygen began pouring from his body.
In an instant, the entire area was saturated with breathable air.
The vacuum effect that had been pulling air through the tunnel vanished almost immediately.
At the same time, Syd made subtle changes to reality—adjusting the gravity and temperature in that region to match Earth's parameters.
In the blink of an eye, though nothing visually changed, the environment became suitable for survival.
Of course, this was only temporary. Once Syd stopped exerting his power, everything would return to its original state.
On the other side of the portal, Thor and the others seemed to sense the change.
They stared in disbelief at the glowing figure drifting in the darkness—at the divine silhouette that alone lit up this void.
Black Panther and the rest started whispering among themselves.
"That god... did he just do something?"
"Could it be..."
As they speculated, Syd turned to Thor and said calmly, "Come."
Then he turned once more and floated off into the distance.
Still hesitant, Valkyrie and the Asgardians stayed behind—but Thor grit his teeth and stepped forward.
"Thor!" the Asgardians cried out, trying to stop him.
But before they could finish speaking, Thor had already stepped through.
Then he turned around, eyes wide with joy. "I'm fine! Hurry up! There's even solid ground here!"
He bounced a little to prove his point.
Valkyrie and the others watched in astonishment. Though there was nothing beneath his feet, Thor stood as if supported by some invisible force.
"What is this?"
"What did he do?"
Instinctively, they looked at the glowing figure now floating far away.
Not only them—even Black Panther and the others were just as stunned.
A mass of people silently watched as the Asgardians carefully stepped into the tunnel and crossed through—each one managing to stand safely on the other side, eyes wide with joy.
But soon their faces dimmed, their eyes scanning the desolate scene around them.
The surroundings were barren, filled only with countless fragments of rock.
There was little light—so dark it felt suffocating. Only the soft glow from the distant figure brought some measure of brightness.
None of this surprised Thor and his people.
Asgard never had a star of its own—only a glowing orb of light that orbited the realm.
This location was far from that orb, so it was natural that there was no light here.
Just as Black Panther and the rest were about to observe further, the spatial tunnel began to close.
Thor and the others noticed as well, startled.
Before anyone could react, the portal rippled like water and vanished.
The bleak ruins of Asgard and Thor's group disappeared from sight.
Everyone looked at each other in shock.
"What do we do?"
"I wanted to see what that god was going to do next!"
"Same here..."
Truthfully, the idea that this god could "just rebuild Asgard" sounded unbelievable.
At that moment, all eyes turned to Doctor Strange and the gathered sorcerers.
"Strange..."
They wanted to ask him something.
Strange, already knowing what they were going to say, hesitated for a moment. Then he raised his right hand and summoned a portal with sparks of yellow magic.
Soon, a golden portal replaced the vanished spatial tunnel.
On the other side, Thor and the others standing in space spotted the portal immediately.
They understood what was happening.
Still, they didn't mind. If they wanted to come, then let them.
One by one, Black Panther and the rest cautiously walked through the portal and stepped into Asgard's space.
"Huh, we're really okay!" Star-Lord stomped his foot with curiosity. "Seriously, what are we even standing on?"
"There's gravity? And oxygen?"
Others began testing the environment too, and a few reckless ones even tried wandering toward the edges.
"Hey! Are you nuts? Go any farther and you'll die!"
Someone snapped at them.
After a while, the crowd calmed down and turned their attention back to Thor and the mysterious god in the distance.
Thor, gazing at the glowing silhouette floating through the dark, finally called out with hesitation, "Brother, what are you planning to do next?"
The next moment, a voice resonated in their ears—mysterious and majestic, like the very truth of the universe.
"Didn't I say it already? Asgard is gone. So I'll just make another one."
Everyone was dumbfounded.
Then, under their stunned gazes—
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 582
chapters.content:
Chapter 582 - 582
Clad in white, bathed in a soft glow, the mysterious being drifted slowly through the pitch-black void of space, his voice quiet yet resonant.
"Let there be light."
The moment that voice—like the truth of the universe—rang out, a miraculous scene unfolded before Thor and the others.
Endless radiance erupted from the darkness, emerging from the void itself.
Light banished the shadows and illuminated all. Tony and the others, for a moment, were so stunned they thought they had returned to Earth at the break of dawn.
The light of dawn—symbolizing rebirth—bathed everything in brilliance.
A thought surfaced in Tony's mind.
Where... did this light come from?
From where they stood, they could see that the figure in white—this godlike being—was now emitting a blinding radiance.
Then, as if echoing the laws of existence, that cosmic voice once again reverberated.
"Let the waters divide, above and below."
With his words, creation began to flow forth, molding reality.
Brilliant light surged across the heavens.
Within it, water vapor gathered and coalesced overhead, forming clusters of beautiful clouds.
Below them, water pooled and spread, forming lakes and rivers.
The scene became still. Silent.
The vast crowd was completely entranced by the divine spectacle.
As they stood stunned, Syd—wrapped in endless white light—continued weaving the world into being, his expression thoughtful.
Since he was going to rebuild Asgard, it was only right to recreate it exactly as it once was.
Although he only had a general impression of Asgard's appearance, lacking detailed understanding posed no obstacle to him. He instantly thought of a solution.
To see how Asgard had once looked—besides manipulating time to glimpse the past—light also preserved the record of all that had ever existed.
In the next instant, all the information and imagery of Asgard before its destruction surged into his mind, recorded by light itself.
Every tree, every stone of the old realm appeared clearly in his mind.
With those memories and his divine powers of creation, nothing remained difficult.
As the others watched in a daze, he casually waved his hand, rearranging the clouds and the waters below.
Then, creation accelerated.
From the water rose solid ground, quickly expanding across a vast area.
The sight left Tony Stark and the others completely dumbfounded.
In their gaze, the white-clad god floated above, radiating blinding brilliance—while beneath him, a massive continent rapidly formed.
Tony muttered, dazed, "Is this... creation?"
"I think... science just got overturned."
The rest of them weren't doing much better.
Every face was filled with shock.
Especially Doctor Banner and the other learned minds among them—this was utterly incomprehensible.
If physicists and other scientists had been here, their worldviews would likely have collapsed on the spot.
Yet, the act of creation was still not over.
There were clouds in the sky now, and land and water below—but it was all barren, lifeless. A world devoid of vitality.
Syd's divine light surged again, flooding across the new landmass of Asgard.
And then—the miracle deepened.
One by one, plants began to emerge—trees, grass, and flowers—spreading rapidly across the reborn realm.
A moment later, that same voice—divine, as if it were the order of the cosmos—rang out once more.
"Let there be celestial bodies to mark the day and the night."
Under the astonished eyes of Thor and the others, the glowing sphere that had once circled the destroyed Asgard now surged toward them.
Under the authority of light, the stars themselves moved—shifting in mere seconds.
Radiant light flooded the new Asgard.
For a moment, Thor and the others felt as though they had returned to the realm they had lost.
But just as they thought it was all over, something even more astonishing happened.
That luminous figure raised both hands—and birds appeared out of thin air.
They chirped joyously, reluctant to fly away, flocking affectionately around him.
The act of creating life left Black Panther and the others speechless.
If clouds, water, and land were still somehow within the bounds of explanation... this was something else entirely.
Creating life?
This scene was just like the myths. No—this was the myth.
Tony and the others fell into a daze, thoughts drifting back to Earth's origins.
Was Earth really a product of natural evolution?
Or... had it been created?
And just when they thought it couldn't get any more overwhelming, Syd spoke again—his voice absolute.
"Let the earth bring forth living creatures, each according to its kind."
Invisible divine power surged forth, carrying out his will.
Birds, beasts, insects...
Every creature that had once existed in Asgard reappeared—created within seconds.
In the blink of an eye, the once-lifeless land blossomed into a world teeming with life.
Everyone stood there in stunned silence.
Thor and his people were especially overwhelmed.
A vast, flat land floated in the darkness of space. Mist drifted around it like a sacred realm from legend.
The glowing orb illuminated the land, its reflection making the new Asgard appear even more divine and beautiful.
Most incredible of all—the realm was identical to the Asgard they remembered. Not a single detail out of place.
Everything—except the people—was as it had been.
Valkyrie murmured in awe, "A miracle..."
Even if they had once considered themselves gods on Earth, in the presence of this radiant, divine creator, they had no choice but to admit:
This was a true god.
This was a miracle.
While they remained entranced, Black Panther and the rest were equally shaken—and bewildered by one specific detail.
"Asgard... isn't a planet? It's flat?"
This kind of world structure completely defied their understanding.
But what shocked them the most—was still the one who had created it all.
Among the crowd, many were Christians, or at least familiar with the phrases of faith—how often had they exclaimed "Oh my God" in surprise?
But now, having witnessed the act of creation firsthand, their minds couldn't help but recall the Book of Genesis.
In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was without form and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep.
And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light...
How could this scene be so identical to what was written in Scripture?
A man named Frank, wearing a black jacket and sporting a thick beard, stared blankly and whispered:
"...Is he God?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 583
chapters.content:
Chapter 583 - 583
The moment Frank spoke, the people around him all paused.
"God...?"
Countless eyes turned toward the radiant, distant figure cloaked in divine light.
Honestly, this being did resemble God far too much. And with the title of Creator attached to him, it made the thought even harder to dismiss.
Not to mention—they had just witnessed the act of creation. Asgard had been rebuilt before their very eyes!
"Could he really... be God?"
Speculations ran rampant, and the gazes of the crowd grew more reverent by the second.
Among them, some of the faithful couldn't help but mutter devoutly.
"Oh Lord..."
Without realizing it, several believers had emerged from the crowd like blooming flowers of faith.
In that moment, threads of faith energy surged toward Syd from all directions, startling him slightly.
He could clearly sense that this faith wasn't intended for him, but for God. And yet—it was still flowing into him.
After a brief moment of thought, he understood why.
In a sense, to a certain degree... he really was a version of God. An incomplete one.
At the moment, he had unlocked 11% of that potential—still far from complete, but it was enough for him to receive a portion of that directed faith.
Thinking of this, he blinked in realization.
Could he eventually absorb all of the faith meant for God?
There were billions of people in the world who worshipped that name. The sheer amount of faith energy produced every moment was beyond comprehension.
Even for someone like him, it would be a tremendous boon.
Curious, he gave it a try—but soon shook his head.
Beyond this area, he couldn't sense any more faith flowing toward him.
Almost immediately, he figured out the reason.
His current unlock progress was too low—only 11%. That limited the range of faith he could receive.
Once he unlocked more, maybe reached 100%, that might change.
"Although, by then, I probably won't even need faith anymore," Syd murmured with a slight smile.
Pushing those thoughts aside, his attention returned to the newly created Asgard.
It was identical to the old one. Absolutely flawless.
Except... one thing was still missing.
The Asgardians—or rather, the Aesir gods.
Syd's eyes glimmered with thought.
In the distance—
Thor and the others stared at the new Asgard with expressions of bittersweet joy and sorrow.
Black Panther and the others looked on with curiosity and admiration.
By now, everyone—Thor, Valkyrie, the rest of the Asgardians, and the Earth-born guests—assumed the act of creation was finished.
After all, Asgard was complete.
But just as that thought settled in their minds—something even more astonishing began to unfold.
Before their very eyes, the light around the white-robed Creator flared once again. Vast power surged from his being.
In Syd's mind, memories of the old Asgard flashed by—along with the images of its fallen people.
The next moment, particles of dust appeared out of nowhere around him—each gathering, coalescing, until they formed into human shapes.
Almost simultaneously, these dust-formed figures transformed into bodies of flesh and blood.
Clad in plain white robes, they floated in midair with their eyes closed, surrounding Syd like stars around a sun.
Black Panther and the others were stunned.
"Who are they...?"
While they whispered in confusion, Thor, Valkyrie, and the other Asgardians were completely shaken.
"That's Heimdall?"
"And that one—!"
They recognized them all.
Each and every one of them—Asgardians.
"But... didn't they die?"
"What are they doing here...?"
Valkyrie stood speechless, utterly shocked.
Thor, too, was stunned. But then, a thought struck him. His voice trembled as he whispered, "No way..."
His gaze turned to the luminous, divine figure floating in the distance.
Then, under the eyes of all present, Syd—still cloaked in divine light—blew gently toward the newly-formed figures.
Unseen by the others, a blend of chaotic magic and divine creation flowed with that breath—warping reality and infusing it into the bodies.
Meanwhile—
Far away, in a fog-draped land resembling a heavenly realm, was the sanctuary of the dead: Valhalla.
This place, reserved for the honored fallen of Asgard, was warm and radiant, with mountains, rivers, and magnificent halls.
At that moment, within this sacred place, the spirits of the fallen Asgardians—those slain by Thanos and others—suddenly froze.
"What... is happening?"
"I feel... something pulling me—somewhere."
Heimdall, tall and dark-skinned with golden eyes, looked shocked.
Others near him echoed his confusion.
"You too, Heimdall?"
"I feel it too..."
But before they could discuss it further, their expressions suddenly changed.
"What is this power?!"
A red light enveloped them.
The next second, they all vanished—without a trace, as if they had never existed.
Back in Valhalla, Odin, Frigga, and Loki stared in astonishment.
"Where... did they go?" Loki said, gaping.
Frigga looked anxious.
Odin, however, wore a deep, grim expression. He muttered, "Which deity is capable of this?"
Only the highest-tier beings in the cosmos could meddle with the spirits within Valhalla.
And that thought alone filled him with dread—and confusion.
Where had they gone? Why had they been taken?
Even he did not know.
Beside him, Loki frowned. "A deity?"
He wasn't sure what that meant.
Anyone Father called a true deity had to be unimaginably powerful...
Back on the new Asgard—
Under the power of creation and the reality-warping forces, the spirits of Heimdall and the others were drawn from Valhalla and elsewhere, pulled into the newly formed bodies.
As their eyes fluttered open, the first thing they saw was a figure surrounded by radiant light, exuding a pressure as vast as the stars.
"Who... is he?"
"Is he the one who brought us here?"
Heimdall and the others were filled with confusion.
But before they could say more, they heard a wave of shocked voices from afar.
"Oh my God!"
"They're really alive again?!"
"Heavens..."
Black Panther and the others stared at the scene in utter disbelief.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 584
chapters.content:
Chapter 584 - 584
No one was more shocked than Valkyrie and the other Asgardians.
Their faces were filled with awe and disbelief.
The once-dead Asgardians... had actually been resurrected!
Looking at the crowd of Asgardians now filling the sky, they were overwhelmed with emotion and could hardly believe what they were seeing.
At that moment—
Among Black Panther's group, Frank muttered to himself, "Is this... the creation of man?"
Hearing this, those around him paused, especially the believers among them, whose eyes widened.
Truth be told, this scene truly did resemble the biblical tale of creation.
They couldn't help but recall that moment in the Scriptures where God created mankind:
Then God said: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the livestock, and all the creatures that crawl on the earth."
So God created man in His own image...
The scene unfolding before them—first the creation of the world, and now people—was nearly identical to those divine legends.
The more they thought about it, the more fervent and awed their gazes became.
Was this truly God?
Meanwhile, Heimdall and the others turned toward the commotion and spotted Thor and the others in the distance.
"Prince Thor?"
"That's Valkyrie?"
"What are they doing here?"
"Wait... Did they die too? Are they in Valhalla?"
As the resurrected Asgardians muttered in confusion, Thor and the others couldn't help but look at each other, unsure whether to laugh or cry.
Then Thor grinned joyfully and called out, "Hey! Heimdall! This isn't Valhalla—look around you carefully!"
Heimdall and the others blinked in confusion and glanced around.
And then... their expressions froze.
Their eyes widened.
Beneath them lay a vast and familiar land.
"This is... Asgard?"
"How... how is this possible?"
"Didn't Surtur destroy it? We saw it explode!"
Many of them had witnessed the fall of Asgard firsthand—the moment it was engulfed in flames and shattered.
So how... how could Asgard be here again?
Even Heimdall, always composed, stared in disbelief and asked, "What's going on?"
Under the stunned gazes of the resurrected crowd, Thor immediately began explaining what had happened.
As he slowly recounted everything, Heimdall and the others gradually understood.
And when they learned that this Asgard had been newly created, their minds reeled.
And when they were told that they had been brought back to life, they froze completely—stunned and bewildered.
Were they dreaming?
Otherwise, how could something so unbelievable be happening?
The creation of a new Asgard, and the resurrection of every Asgardian?
Then, Thor took the opportunity to explain the identity of the Creator—and turned his gaze toward the divine figure in the distance.
"My brother... the Creator God of the universe. He created this Asgard and brought all of you back."
His words left Heimdall and the others utterly speechless.
They turned to look at the radiant being shining so brightly they could hardly gaze at him directly.
"The Creator God...?"
They trembled inwardly.
What kind of power was this?
Not only to recreate Asgard—but to resurrect the dead, seemingly with ease?
The Creator God of the universe?
As for Thor referring to him as "my brother," that part was either ignored or misunderstood by the others. Most assumed Thor had misspoken or they'd misheard.
Meanwhile, Black Panther's group was just as dazed.
Not long ago, they'd assumed this divine being would simply choose a new place and name it New Asgard.
They never imagined something like this.
Asgard wasn't just rebuilt.
The people were resurrected. The Aesir gods were reborn.
At the same time, in the Realm of Death—
A realm the living could not enter.
Because so many Asgardians were suddenly resurrected—even with chaos magic distorting reality—one of the universe's primordial deities, Death herself, began to sense something amiss.
Back on Asgard—
Syd didn't bother dwelling on what Heimdall and the others were thinking. He simply waved his hand.
In the next moment, space rippled—and in a blink, Heimdall and the rest found themselves standing before Thor.
They stared at each other in silence.
After a moment, Thor blinked and muttered with a hint of sadness, "Where's Father? Mother? And Loki?"
Hearing this, Heimdall and the others also looked around and realized—King Odin, Queen Frigga, and Loki were nowhere in sight.
Confusion filled their faces.
Syd, noticing this, glanced over at them.
Of course, he hadn't forgotten about Odin and the others. But everything had to be done in order of importance.
Their revival... would come last.
Thinking this, he raised his hand once more.
Before everyone's eyes, brilliant golden blood began seeping from his hand.
In the crowd, Scarlet Witch, Doctor Strange, and Spider-Man sensed the energy in that blood and immediately paled.
The power radiating from it was terrifying—beyond comprehension.
Syd ignored their reactions. With a few drops of divine blood, he poured his power into it.
His power of creation surged again—fueling the formation of three divine bodies.
Meanwhile, in Valhalla—
Odin, Frigga, and Loki stood together, uncertain of what was happening.
Suddenly, their faces changed at the same time.
Loki's eyes widened in shock.
Odin's expression turned grim. "Such immense power..."
He could feel it clearly now, and his face grew darker with each passing second.
Before they could react—everything went white.
The next moment, the three of them vanished from Valhalla... and awoke inside the newly-formed divine bodies.
The instant they regained consciousness, they were overwhelmed by the sheer power surging within them.
Loki's jaw dropped. His eyes nearly bulged out of his head.
"This power..."
His gaze grew obsessed.
He swore—he had never felt anything like this.
He didn't even bother looking around. A confident smile spread across his face.
With this power, how could Thor ever hope to surpass him?
"Who am I?" he chuckled.
"The greatest sorcerer of the Nine Realms—Loki!"
But just as he was basking in his newfound might, a familiar voice rang out:
"Father! Mother! Loki!"
Thor?
Loki's entire body jolted. He snapped his eyes open and turned instinctively.
Sure enough—Thor was standing there, waving with joy.
Why was he here?
Had Thor died too?
Loki was stunned.
But beside him, Odin and Frigga were already noticing something strange.
This wasn't Valhalla.
They exchanged glances—
And the next second, Queen Frigga turned toward Thor, frowning slightly.
"Thor... what is going on? Where... are we?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 585
chapters.content:
Chapter 585 - 585
"Thor, what's going on? Where... are we?"
Queen Frigga's voice trembled with uncertainty.
As she spoke, she suddenly noticed something, and froze.
That being in the distance, radiating with blinding light—yes, he was already shocking enough—but what truly caught her attention was what lay beneath them: the vast realm of Asgard.
Then came a cry of disbelief.
"Asgard?!" Loki stared wide-eyed.
Wasn't Asgard destroyed? How could it still exist?
Was he dreaming? Or was this some kind of illusion?
Frigga and Odin were just as stunned. Their hearts raced with a flood of impossible emotions.
As their minds reeled, Thor quickly stepped forward and began explaining, "Father, Mother—here's what happened..."
With his calm recounting, the three slowly began to grasp the situation.
But instead of easing their hearts, the truth shook them even more.
The creation of Asgard? The resurrection of every Asgardian?
The Creator of the universe?
"A god... You mean the 'great deity' you once mentioned is this Creator?" Loki's voice trembled.
He gazed at the luminous figure in the distance, his expression overwhelmed.
Beside him, Odin and Frigga did the same, their eyes filled with awe.
Then Thor dropped a bombshell.
"He's the Creator God of another universe, but also—Balder! The God of Light from Asgardian legend!"
"Father, do you remember the stories you told me when I was young? About my amazing little brother? I thought you made those up... but they were true!"
"I really do have a brother—and he's this powerful! The Creator of the universe!"
"This is unreal! Who could've imagined that Asgard had a Creator God? I never would've believed it if I hadn't seen it with my own eyes!"
Thor grew increasingly excited as he spoke.
But everyone else—Black Panther, Natasha, the Asgardians—were completely stunned.
"Brother?!"
"The Creator God is... Thor's brother?!"
Mouths dropped.
Though they had vaguely heard Thor refer to him that way earlier, none of them had taken it seriously.
Now, it struck them fully.
Asgard... had a Creator God?
Heimdall and the other Asgardians were in disbelief.
Meanwhile, Odin, Frigga, and Loki's emotions were also surging chaotically.
"Balder..." Odin whispered. His expression went distant as he drifted into memory.
A vision surfaced in his mind: a flawless infant bathed in divine light.
That child, the moment he was born, grew swiftly into an adult, possessing godlike wisdom and unimaginable power.
That power... had even made Odin feel suppressed. It had sparked an instinctive wariness in him.
The boy was too perfect—like a true god, without flaw.
But perfection, perhaps, was a curse. It didn't last long before the boy turned into light and vanished—completely and inexplicably.
That moment had been long ago... yet Odin remembered it vividly.
As he stared at the radiant figure in the distance, the two images began to overlap.
"That's... Balder?"
Odin could hardly believe it.
Even if he came from another universe, this was still Balder. And that alone left him shaken.
After a long silence, a question surfaced in his heart.
Where was this universe's Balder?
If the one from another reality still existed, then their own Balder should too.
He sighed and said, "Our Balder disappeared long ago. He turned into light and vanished. Even I don't know where he went."
Thor blinked in surprise. After a moment of reflection, realization dawned.
This Balder was indeed his brother—but from another universe. He wasn't his Balder.
That thought stung.
A faint bitterness rose in his chest, tinged with envy.
Staring at the divine figure floating in the air, Thor muttered defiantly, "I don't care. He's my brother."
Hearing this, Odin and the others were momentarily stunned. But despite their helpless smiles, they couldn't deny it.
In a way, this being was Balder—no different from the one who had once existed here.
Frigga's eyes welled with emotion. Her face flushed with joy, her eyes red, almost on the verge of tears.
Then Loki muttered, "But what about our Balder?"
He wasn't the only one wondering—Thor, Natasha, and the others were asking the same in their hearts.
At that moment, Syd—hovering in the distance—fell into contemplation.
One of his purposes in coming to this universe... was to find out what really happens when Balder reaches 100% progression.
And now, he was starting to understand.
"So this is what happens at 100%..."
In other universes... fragments of himself had appeared?
Wait—no, this wasn't just "fragments of information." Based on what Odin had said, he had actually existed here once.
A trace of doubt flickered in Syd's eyes.
Could it be... their memories were altered? Fabricated?
To confirm it, he quietly activated the Time Stone, rewinding the past.
The power of time surged.
Brilliant light shimmered.
And within that light, he saw it—the birth of an infant bathed in divine radiance.
Syd's eyes widened in shock.
This... wasn't a fake memory?
This had really happened?
As he watched further, more pieces came into focus.
This version of Balder... wasn't truly him. At best, it was an information-based projection—carrying fragments of his consciousness and a sliver of his power.
He watched as the glowing figure vanished into light, confirming his conclusion.
"Not even a proper parallel version... just an echo."
Syd exhaled in relief.
If this had been another full incarnation of himself, things would've been... complicated.
Thankfully, it was just a projection—harmless, just a ripple of his presence across the multiverse.
But just as he was thinking that...
His mind suddenly paused.
A thought struck him.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 586
chapters.content:
Chapter 586 - 586
"Hmm... if I use the Dreamwalking Spell from the Darkhold, would my consciousness be able to travel to other universes?"
Previously, due to the lack of a parallel self, Syd hadn't been able to use dreamwalking to traverse other realities.
But now that this form of information projection had emerged, perhaps it was worth trying again?
Truthfully, Syd still held deep curiosity toward the multiverse.
So far, the universes he had traversed were all diverging branches from the main 616 universe—realities where events developed similarly.
But in truth, within the multiverse, anything was possible.
There were even versions with a female Tony Stark, not to mention countless other divergences.
For instance, Syd remembered one reality quite vividly—an extreme divergence where a zombie virus had transformed nearly all beings into the undead.
And another? The Cancerverse, often dubbed the Cthulhu Universe.
The multiverse... was terrifying.
Far from the calm and order of the main universe—catastrophic annihilation was routine.
As he mulled over this—
A curious voice suddenly broke his thoughts.
"Creator God, do you know what happened to our universe's Balder?"
It was Steve Rogers—Captain America—who asked.
Others, like Tony Stark, also looked on with curiosity and concern.
After all, if this world had possessed such a powerful being all along, perhaps none of their tragedies would've happened.
Thanos? He wouldn't even dare show his face.
They couldn't help but feel a little envious of the other universe.
Syd glanced at them, then calmly replied, "Strictly speaking, the Balder from this universe... was merely my projection. Once a certain point is reached, he naturally dissipates."
Silence fell.
Everyone stared at the radiant figure floating in the air.
"Projection...?"
They couldn't believe it.
Especially Odin and the Asgardians—they were stunned.
They understood what he meant.
He was saying... he was the only real one.
The others were nothing more than fragments. Echoes.
A chill ran down their spines.
Especially Tony and the Earth-born heroes—the thought made their blood run cold.
They'd already encountered parallel universes.
They knew other versions of themselves existed out there.
So the multiverse... was real.
And now—this divine being claimed to be the only version of himself across all universes? That the others were merely projections?
"What kind of power is this?"
"A force beyond the multiverse?"
"A multiversal-tier being?"
They stared at him in awe and fear.
If he was telling the truth... then the power he had displayed so far was only a fraction of his true might.
His real strength? Likely beyond their comprehension.
They were shaken to the core.
From afar, Syd twitched slightly at their expressions. He could tell they'd misunderstood.
If only he was that powerful—it'd be wonderful.
He sighed inwardly.
To meet those expectations, he would have to truly become a multiversal-level entity.
And besides, being "unique" wasn't all that rare. Most multiversal beings were unique—any others were just lesser aspects or avatars.
At that moment, Thor, now filled with envy, suddenly thought of something.
If this Balder was real...
And their Balder was fake...
Then didn't that mean... this one was his true little brother?
A joyful light filled his eyes.
Odin and the others nearby also looked on, their gazes conflicted.
—
While emotions swirled around them, Syd suddenly sensed something.
His gaze shifted toward the distance.
Seeing his movement, Thor and the others instinctively turned to follow his line of sight.
And the next moment—they froze.
In the previously empty space, a shadow had silently appeared.
A figure draped in a pitch-black robe, its hood covering its face.
The parts that were visible chilled the soul.
No flesh.
Only bone.
This skeletal figure stood motionless, its empty eye sockets glinting with eerie light—as if it were gazing at them with curiosity.
Anyone caught in its gaze felt their soul tremble—like death was creeping in.
"A skeleton?"
"Who is that?!"
The crowd murmured in alarm and fear.
A skeleton had just... appeared.
And it was watching them?
But it wasn't just that.
The moment it looked at them, it felt as if something ancient and cold had grabbed their hearts.
Unable to bear the tension, Thor asked aloud, "Who are you?"
The skeletal figure opened its jaw, and the next moment, a chilling voice echoed directly into everyone's mind.
"You may call me... the Goddess of Death."
The crowd blinked in disbelief.
Thor, in particular, scratched his head. "Goddess of Death?"
"Wasn't Hela the Goddess of Death?"
This skeleton... was claiming the same title?
Valkyrie and the others were equally confused.
Then, a cold chuckle spread through the air.
"I am the true Death."
What did that mean?
They were even more confused now.
But Syd was calm.
Unlike the others, he instantly recognized this being.
He spoke in a serene, transcendent tone:
"One of the five Primordial Creator Gods—Death."
He fell briefly into contemplation.
As an abstract cosmic entity, this being had no fixed form.
Like Eternity and the others, Death could appear however it pleased.
This time, she had chosen the form of a robed female skeleton.
Sometimes, she manifested a fleshed form—but more often, she preferred the skeletal visage.
As Syd's voice—like the truth of the cosmos—resonated across the area, everyone froze once again.
"Creator God..."
"Death...?!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 587
chapters.content:
Chapter 587 - 587
As the words echoed in their ears, everyone froze.
Creator God... Death?!
By now, thanks to Thor's earlier explanations, they understood what "Creator Gods" were.
These were cosmic-level entities—literal aspects of the universe itself.
Abstract, absolute concepts incarnate, wielding powers that defied understanding.
And now, this skeletal figure in a black robe...
Was the Creator God of Death?
Tony Stark and the others looked on in disbelief.
At that moment—
Hearing Syd's calm acknowledgment, the Goddess of Death tilted her head in mild surprise.
"You know me?" she asked, her tone curious.
She was genuinely surprised.
Typically, she remained in the Death Realm and only ever manifested before those who caught her interest.
But this radiant being in front of her—she had neither met him nor shown herself to him before.
So... how could he recognize her?
Her hollow eye sockets flickered with doubt.
While she was caught in thought, Tony and the others were furiously trying to guess her intentions.
"Why is one of the Creator Gods—Death—here?"
"What does she want?"
Among the crowd, Doctor Strange had a hunch—and a look of worry crept across his face.
Could it be...?
Then—
Amid the hushed whispers, the Goddess of Death seemed to lose interest in her curiosity and instead gave a cold smile.
A moment later, her gaze locked onto Syd, and she spoke again:
"How did you do it? How did you manage to deceive me?"
"If you hadn't resurrected so many, I wouldn't have sensed the anomaly."
Her voice dropped in tone, colder, heavier:
"Your actions violate the laws of death. You've disturbed the balance of the universe."
"They were not meant to live again."
She glanced toward Odin and the others.
The moment she said that, Doctor Strange's heart sank. So she really is here to pass judgment.
He couldn't deny it—Syd had revived too many people.
If he were in her place, he wouldn't have ignored it either.
The tension in the air thickened.
Tony, Thor, and the others were quick to catch on, and unease flickered in their eyes.
"Are they about to fight...?"
"Who would win?"
None of them were sure.
If anything, they leaned toward the Goddess of Death.
After all, this universe wasn't Syd's home turf. He held no natural advantage here.
Not to mention—she was Death itself. Ancient. Enduring. Absolute.
Just thinking about it made the concern in their hearts deepen.
Then, as if verifying their fears, Death spoke again, eyeing Syd:
"You... who are you? You don't belong to our universe."
Clearly, she had detected something.
Syd replied calmly, "I am Light."
"Light?" Death murmured, clearly puzzled.
She didn't quite grasp what he meant.
As she stared at the divine glow surrounding him, she pondered silently.
Some kind of light god?
That wouldn't be surprising. Many pantheons had their own gods of light.
But to Death, beings like that meant very little.
To mortals and lesser deities, they were powerful. But to her? They were insects—no different from ordinary humans, only larger, slightly harder to crush.
Still, in that silence, someone in the crowd mumbled softly:
"He's a Creator God... from another universe."
That single sentence drew every gaze—including Death's—to the speaker.
The skeletal goddess visibly froze.
A Creator God... from another universe?
She blinked—if a skeleton could blink—visibly confused.
She shook her head.
There were only five Creator Gods in any universe.
Even in parallel ones, that number remained fixed.
A sixth? Impossible.
With that thought, her empty gaze locked back on Syd.
It was time to discipline this imposter.
She began to raise her skeletal hand—
But then paused.
She felt it.
A familiar pressure. Several... presences... watching her.
And she immediately recognized them.
Eternity. Infinity. Oblivion.
Her gaze flickered.
She was surprised—but not entirely.
Still, it was rare for those three to be so nosy.
They really had nothing better to do?
Truth be told—they really didn't.
At that very moment, those three abstract gods were observing the situation.
"Death's out of her realm again. What's she up to this time? Picking a fight with some unknown being?"
"Interesting..."
They watched, amused.
But none of them were particularly worried.
After all, who could beat Death?
She was the embodiment of the end.
She could wield infinite power, command souls, kill or resurrect at will, control entire pantheons.
Even the gods of Asgard or Olympus bowed to her domain.
This glowing figure might be powerful... but the result was inevitable.
As those gods spectated from afar, and the others held their breath, Death prepared to strike—
Only to be stopped by something unexpected.
Syd moved first.
He didn't attack.
He simply surrendered himself to a feeling deep within—to become the Light of this universe.
And in the blink of an eye—before Death could act—
He vanished, dissolving into countless strands of light.
"Hmm?"
The skeletal hand hung in the air.
Death froze.
She sensed... a subtle shift in the laws of this universe—but it had happened too fast for her to fully grasp.
"What did he just do?" she muttered.
Even Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion felt a jolt of confusion.
Not far away—
Thor stared, wide-eyed.
"Where did he go...?"
Black Panther and the others were equally confused.
But then—something impossible occurred.
From the spot where the white-robed god had vanished, an indescribable light burst forth.
In a flash, that strange, sacred brilliance swept over them all—
And in an instant, all of New Asgard was bathed in that divine radiance.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 588
chapters.content:
Chapter 588 - 588
But it didn't stop there—the light was still spreading at an astonishing speed.
"What is this...?"
The Goddess of Death stared in utter shock.
She wasn't the only one. Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion—the other three Creator Gods—also sensed something incomprehensible.
The very laws of the universe... were changing.
The light spread beyond Asgard.
This indescribable brilliance surged across space at an unfathomable speed. In just a blink, the entire universe was bathed in its glow.
Sensing this phenomenon, Death, the other Creator Gods, and even Galactus—who was floating through space in search of a world to devour—all froze in place.
"What... is this?"
"What exactly has he done?!"
Not just the abstract beings—on New Asgard, Black Panther and the rest were also stunned. Before their eyes, the entire sky had turned into a sea of light.
"What's happening?!"
"What did he do?!"
Forcing themselves to endure the overwhelming light, they instinctively looked back to the source.
Meanwhile, on Earth and across the cosmos, all sentient beings were shocked beyond words.
Even when half the universe's population vanished, or when they were resurrected, it hadn't shaken them as deeply as this light did now.
Then—
A strange, indistinct voice began echoing throughout the universe.
It was like a song... or a chorus of praise from countless beings.
"Light..."
"Master of the eternal radiance..."
"The Creator..."
The words were jumbled, scattered, but clearly reverent.
As people listened in awe, the infinite light suddenly began to fade.
The brilliant universe dimmed... and returned to its quiet, lifeless black.
...
New Asgard.
"He... affected the entire universe?"
The Goddess of Death's tone was more serious than ever.
She could feel that light, heat, and other essential forces of the universe had changed.
There was something new—an unfamiliar will—as though part of the universe now belonged to someone else.
She knew this feeling well.
"This guy..."
Death's hollow face filled with disbelief.
"How did he...?"
"He actually..."
Became a Creator God—an abstract concept itself!
He was now like them—an indispensable part of the universe.
If removed, the cosmos would collapse.
As Death reeled, the dark, lifeless universe suddenly lit up once more—no longer frigid, but now warm and radiant.
Then, the boundless light began to shrink rapidly.
Near New Asgard—
Amid the fading chants of praise, the remaining light gathered and formed a humanoid shape.
It was a being made of light.
Radiating sacred brilliance, its face could not be seen. It was blurred, unreachable—divine.
"...What is that?"
Black Panther and the others were still in a daze.
But Death... understood instantly.
"You... what are you?"
Her hollow eyes stared directly at this sacred being.
At the same time, Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion all turned their attention here.
Under their gaze, the glowing figure calmly spoke:
"I already told you. I am Light."
The others fell silent.
They remembered—he had said that before.
Back then, they hadn't taken it seriously.
But now? Now they understood.
He was Light.
The embodiment of radiance and warmth.
The positive force of the universe.
They felt it clearly—just as they could sense their own dominion, they now felt his.
And that was what left them all unsettled.
How... did this happen?
How did he suddenly become one of them?
Then Death narrowed her eyes, as if something finally clicked.
"Are you... truly a Creator God from another universe?"
She had scoffed at the idea when the mortals said it earlier.
But now—she could no longer deny it.
A sudden flash of insight struck her.
Muttering to herself, she said:
"Could it be... when your universe was born, there weren't five of you... but six?"
"And the sixth... was you?"
The more she said it, the more certain she became.
And she wasn't alone—Eternity and the others had come to the same conclusion.
It was possible.
In the multiverse, anything was.
Maybe his universe had birthed six abstract entities instead of five.
He was the sixth.
That would explain why he could seamlessly merge with this universe's rules—why he could become a new Creator God here.
In a sense, he was now one of them.
Or rather... he had always been.
For the Creator Gods, relationships between them were often referred to in familial terms.
And now, as the Light and Warmth of the universe—its positive force—this new being was unmistakably their youngest sibling.
With that realization, Death, Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion all grew quiet.
Even Death, who moments ago was ready to strike, now hesitated.
What was she supposed to do now?
Had this been an ordinary god—violating the natural order, ignoring her domain, recklessly reviving the dead—she would have brought down swift judgment.
She might have punished them cruelly, even toyed with them a little.
But if it was... family?
Then it was different.
Fine. So what if they'd resurrected some gods?
As long as they didn't revive the entire universe, she could turn a blind eye.
Thinking this, her anger began to fade.
And with that—Odin and the resurrected Asgardians vanished from her perception.
She didn't recognize them anyway.
And she didn't care.
But her interest in this new brother only grew.
He had already revived the Aesir and created an entire new Asgard.
What else could he do?
What was his true power?
She wanted to know.
And so did Eternity and the others.
If this new sibling turned out to be weak... they wouldn't do anything about it.
But they certainly wouldn't take him seriously.
Of them all, Galactus was the most excited.
He had long hated being the "weakest" among the cosmic beings—
Now that someone else had joined the circle, maybe he could finally drop that title.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 589
chapters.content:
Chapter 589 - 589
While the Goddess of Death and the other cosmic entities—Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion—were deep in thought, Syd was quietly examining his own state.
After becoming a Creator God of another universe, he could clearly feel that his power ceiling had been greatly elevated. In fact, he could faintly sense that the forces of both universes were overlapping within him.
Of course, although he could now draw upon the energy of the other universe, the separation between universes caused some attenuation. Still, even with that, the boost was tremendous—enough to push him beyond the norm, exceeding the strength of standard Creator Gods.
Just how much stronger he had become, however, was hard to say. He hadn't tested it in combat yet.
And now, he was deeply curious.
What exactly was the power of his current abstract concept body?
Syd focused and began sensing carefully.
Light.
And since light is an electromagnetic wave—he now indirectly controlled one of the fundamental forces of the universe.
In addition, he discovered that he could now govern heat—cosmic warmth itself.
But that wasn't all.
To his surprise, he also began sensing another form of power.
"Emotion?"
More specifically—positive, radiant emotions.
Syd immediately made the connection and murmured to himself,
"So my guess was right. Balder's light doesn't only represent visible light, but the light within people's hearts..."
He suddenly recalled how Eternity had once described him:
"The one who represents light and heat, and... the positive aspect of the universe."
Syd grew thoughtful.
Meanwhile, Tony Stark and the others were nervously speculating from a distance.
Staring at the black-robed skeletal figure—Death—and the white-robed being of divine radiance—Syd, their whispers floated through the air:
"Do you think... the two of them are still going to fight?"
"Maybe not? Balder-sama's power just increased a lot..."
But before anyone could reach a conclusion, Death's skull-like jaw moved, her hollow voice laced with amusement:
"My youngest brother, newly born... I wonder, between us—the indelible powers of the cosmos—who is stronger?"
"I wanted to strike earlier, but didn't expect you to be hiding your identity. Turns out... you're one of us after all."
She paused, her voice growing more playful.
"Well, this is fine. As fellow Creator Gods, it won't look like I'm bullying you."
"I just wonder... will you be able to withstand me? If not, don't forget to yield early."
And before Syd could even frown, she moved.
Without hesitation, the Goddess of Death launched the first blow.
Under the stunned gazes of Thor and the others, twin streams of red flame shot from Death's hollow eye sockets.
BOOM!
In an instant, all they saw was fire—a blazing inferno engulfing the heavens, charging at incredible speed toward Syd.
"...Flames?" Syd frowned slightly.
They looked ordinary. Unremarkable.
Even if they were hellfire, they would mean nothing to his current abstract-form body.
After all, he could feel the transcendence of his new being.
Any attack below the level of a single-universe-class entity would likely be completely ineffective.
So why... was she using flames?
He wasn't the only one confused. Even Thor and the others found it odd.
"Just fire?"
"Even we could block that..."
As the flames surged forward and engulfed him, Syd's expression abruptly changed.
He felt it.
Hidden within those flames... was divine power.
Without question—it was the Goddess of Death's own power.
His mind raced back to the lore he had studied. He remembered—
Any attack from the Goddess of Death is lethal.
Any contact with her power... means death.
Touch = Death.
Even among abstract beings of their level, her abilities were no joke. Getting hit wouldn't kill them outright, but it would hurt—badly.
Even if the flames looked ordinary, they could burn even an abstract concept's essence.
And not just him.
Even Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion would suffer the same if struck.
Death's divine power was unique.
Even a mortal, granted a portion of her strength, could harm abstract gods.
He recalled one infamous case—when Deadpool, empowered by Death, managed to punch Eternity and injure him.
It was absurd.
A mortal... harming a cosmic concept?
Ridiculous—yet real.
So no, Syd had no intention of "testing" those flames.
With a flicker of thought, he dissolved into light—his body disintegrating into strands of brilliance.
Tony and the others saw the flash—then watched in awe as the white-robed being slipped effortlessly through the fire, emerging untouched.
Some were puzzled.
"Why dodge... ordinary fire?"
But the Goddess of Death's chuckle answered them.
"So, you sensed it too?"
"Yes—those flames may look harmless, but they carry my divine power.
Anyone—mortal or divine—who touches them... will die."
The casualness in her voice left Thor and the others stunned.
"Wait... you die just by being touched?!"
"That's... cheating!"
"If anyone can be killed instantly, how do you even fight someone like that?!"
Their gazes turned again to Syd.
How was he supposed to win this?
On the other side, the other Creator Gods began to whisper amongst themselves.
"Death's divine power really is troublesome..."
"I wonder... how will our youngest brother handle this?"
"Besides, that was just a test—she hasn't even gotten serious."
Their eyes glimmered with interest.
Even before Syd became a Creator God, they believed Death could beat him.
Now?
Their opinion hadn't changed.
The real question was—how long could he last?
And in the shadows, Galactus—who had been watching everything—was nearly giddy with excitement.
At last...
He wouldn't be the weakest anymore.
(End of Chapter)
