chapters.title: Chapter 590
chapters.content:
Chapter 590 - 590
It seemed... their youngest brother wasn't so weak after all?
Could it be... that he was no longer the weakest among the Creator Gods?
That thought alone made Galactus visibly excited.
At that moment—
"You better be careful, my dear little brother. Hehehe..."
The Goddess of Death let out a soft chuckle, raising her skeletal hand to cover her mouth playfully.
The sea of flames shifted direction, sweeping back toward Syd once more.
Seeing this, Syd furrowed his brows. The mockery... the toying tone... it irritated him.
The next second, he didn't hold back.
With a single thought, he summoned all the light and heat of this universe, unleashing it upon the chuckling Death.
In an instant, the entire silent, black cosmos became even darker—
As if someone had switched off the universe's lights.
Nearly all light and heat—even those radiated from stars and suns—vanished.
Only what was required to sustain the bare minimum cosmic balance remained.
Everything else gathered into one place—
A kaleidoscopic, multicolored ocean of blinding light.
It surged like a tidal wave straight toward the Goddess of Death.
Radiance beyond imagining.
"Wh—Wha...?"
The skeletal face of the Goddess froze mid-laugh.
Her expression shattered.
"Have you lost your mind, brother?!"
Her skull jaw gaped open so wide, it almost didn't close.
She had just been playing around, lightly testing him.
And now—he'd gone full power?!
Was this even fair?!
Even the hidden onlookers—Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion—were stunned.
"Is he trying to destroy the universe?"
In New Asgard, the people stared, dazed, their eyes flooded by the endless light.
They could see nothing but luminescence.
Within the ocean of prismatic light—
The Goddess of Death invoked the full force of her dominion, the Laws of Death.
A shimmering violet shield of divine law formed around her, resisting the oncoming tidal wave of light and heat.
BOOM!
An unfathomable shockwave exploded outward.
"AHHH—!!"
BANG!
New Asgard, newly reborn... was blown apart in the blast.
And not just New Asgard—Thor, Loki, and the others were caught in the wave too.
They barely had time to react before it hit.
"No! I'm the greatest sorcerer in the Nine Realms—Loki!"
Despite his newfound power, Loki's strength meant nothing in the face of this god-tier clash.
In the next second, he—and Odin, Frigga, and countless others—were obliterated.
BOOM!!!
Under this catastrophic shockwave, even space itself began to melt and distort.
Air, stone, stars—everything was reduced to nothingness.
Within the ocean of light, inside her flickering violet shield, Death was no longer smiling.
She looked... horrified.
Staring out at her glowing little brother—who stood outside the lightstorm, calmly releasing divine laws—she finally cried out:
"Stop! If this continues, the entire universe will break apart!"
She paused, sensing the widespread destabilization.
Then she sighed with awe and reluctance:
"I didn't expect your strength to be this incredible... almost equal to mine."
She added more solemnly,
"Please stop. We're evenly matched—there's no point in dragging this out. If we keep going, the universe itself will collapse."
Just then, several mysterious voices echoed through space.
"Youngest brother... stop this. You mustn't continue."
"If you do..."
Hearing the voices of Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion, Syd narrowed his eyes slightly and checked the state of the universe.
Indeed... the balance had begun to crack.
New Asgard and the others—including Loki—had been wiped out in the blast.
But that was no issue. He could revive them after the fight.
His gaze returned to Death, still shielding herself in the sea of light.
They were evenly matched.
Unless they battled endlessly for eons, no victor would emerge.
But if they did keep going... this universe might not survive the aftermath.
Even if Eternity and Infinity could eventually rebuild it...
Syd frowned slightly.
"Is this really where it ends?"
He didn't want that.
But unless an outside force interfered...
Suddenly, a thought lit up in his mind.
His eyes gleamed.
The other universe.
Without hesitation, he connected to his abstract concept self in the 616 Main Universe.
BOOM—!!!
A surge of titanic force flooded in from across dimensional boundaries.
The full might of the 616 Universe poured into him.
Invisible to all, the two universes trembled.
They began to resonate—like two planets drifting toward each other, pulled by an unknown gravity.
Whatever might happen afterward...
He didn't care.
Right now, with the 616 power fully fusing with him, the prismatic sea of light and divine law erupted.
Within her violet shield, the Goddess of Death sensed it instantly.
Shock overtook her entire form.
BOOM!!
The surging lightstorm and divine force slammed into her shield.
The violet laws of death flickered.
Then—CRACK!
SHATTER!!!
Her protective shield was broken.
She had no time to react.
The divine ocean swallowed her whole.
"IMPOSSIBLE!!!"
She screamed as her skeletal body, her abstract conceptual form, dissolved into the radiance.
"AHHHH—!!"
With a final cry, she vanished into the ocean of light.
And in that moment—
Eternity, Infinity, and Oblivion were left speechless.
"...No way."
"Our youngest brother... just defeated Death?"
"What did he... do?!"
Confusion.
Disbelief.
Awe.
How could the youngest being among them—newly born, barely ascended—
Defeat the embodiment of Death itself?
This shouldn't have happened.
And yet—
It did.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 591
chapters.content:
Chapter 591 - 591
What exactly did this youngest brother do?
Why is he so powerful?
Eternity and the others were filled with questions.
After carefully sensing the situation, they realized that a continuous stream of power was being transmitted to him from a distant place.
At the same time, they noticed that the universe was undergoing some sort of anomaly, being drawn and shifting toward that direction.
Despite their confusion, they turned their attention back to the battlefield.
By now, Death's conceptual avatar had vanished—clearly destroyed by their youngest brother.
"It seems our youngest brother's strength ranks at least in the top three among us."
"I just don't know if he can beat you or Annihilation."
The one who spoke had a black and yellow body, laced with black lines on the surface, seemingly female, and represented the concept of infinity and the boundless nature of space. She glanced at her elder brother Eternity, and the previously youngest and strongest—Annihilation.
As for herself and Galactus, there was no need to even consider it—they definitely couldn't win against this newly emerged sibling.
With that thought, Infinity frowned slightly and murmured in confusion, "Does being the youngest mean being the strongest?"
Of course, raw power was one thing, but it didn't mean there were no weaknesses. Aside from strength, they also valued capabilities.
Among them, Annihilation possessed the most potent abilities, which made him the strongest.
"I wonder... what kind of powers does our youngest brother actually possess?" Eternity whispered with curiosity.
Beside him, Infinity and Annihilation were also quietly speculating.
Of course, they had their guesses—they assumed his powers were all related to light.
But if it was only that, it shouldn't be anything too extraordinary. So how was this brother so powerful?
Did he also possess abilities related to matter?
He could even recreate a new Asgard?
And he had some connection to the concept of life? He could even resurrect the people of Asgard?
Just what other secrets was this brother hiding?
While they were deep in thought, Galactus's face was filled with disbelief, dismay, and confusion.
He had thought this youngest brother wasn't that powerful.
He assumed he was no longer the weakest of the Creator Gods.
He never expected that this newcomer would be even stronger than Death.
If he could defeat Death, he could certainly defeat Galactus as well!
Galactus's excitement completely vanished, replaced by bitterness and disorientation.
"This brother who was just born... is already stronger than me..."
"When will I finally recover the portion of energy I lost?"
Due to a deficiency at his creation and some unforeseen accidents, Galactus had always lacked a portion of his core energy and remained incomplete.
To make up for this, he had to constantly seek planets with life energy to devour.
As a result, his power fluctuated greatly, and he was frequently tormented by hunger caused by his incompleteness.
He clenched his teeth in frustration, continuing to move through the cosmos, determined to find a new life-bearing planet to consume and reclaim what he lacked.
What he didn't know was that once he did recover it, he would attain multiversal-level strength and transform from Galactus the World Devourer into the Bringer of Life.
But when that time came, he would also face judgment from the Living Tribunal.
He represented cosmic balance, the force responsible for consumption in the cycle of matter's gain and loss.
If he became a Bringer of Life—no longer devouring but constantly creating planets capable of supporting life—that kind of power would severely upset the balance of cosmic exchange. Judgment would be inevitable!
Unaware of all this, Galactus continued his tireless search for planets teeming with life.
As for his youngest brother—he no longer paid attention. In his mind, the battle was already settled.
And he wasn't wrong. Although only an avatar was destroyed, in the universe, the power that avatars could exert wasn't much different from their original selves.
If this youngest brother could destroy Death's avatar, then surely he could destroy the real thing. So there was no point in continuing the fight.
At the battlefield—
Syd quietly waited for a moment. When it was clear that the Goddess of Death wouldn't reappear, he turned his gaze to his surroundings.
All around him was a vast void, pitch black and lightless—as if he had stepped into nothingness.
Their battle had not only destroyed the new Asgard, but even the radiant sun had been obliterated in the crossfire.
What's more, Thor and the others had vanished as well.
Seeing this, Syd frowned and raised his right hand.
In the next instant, a golden Infinity Gauntlet appeared on his hand.
The six Infinity Stones shone with an intense brilliance!
But not only that—an overwhelming crimson energy flared up. It was the power of Chaos Magic.
The next second, time began to reverse!
The vanished matter and everything else reappeared in rapid succession, as if the entire process were being rewound.
However, there were some anomalies. For instance, the Goddess of Death and certain other entities did not return.
With Chaos Magic's ability to rewrite reality, everything now made sense and adhered to logic.
Thor and the others reappeared where they had stood, and New Asgard was rebuilt in the blink of an eye.
Even the light and heat that had once been drawn away were restored to the cosmos, and stability returned to the universe!
In a flash, it was as if nothing had ever happened.
"Ugh..."
"We're... still alive?"
Tony and the others stood stunned, exchanging looks of disbelief. When they turned to look at New Asgard, they found it completely intact.
Instinctively, they looked at the white-robed Creator God bathed in light.
There was no need to ask—they knew all of this was his doing.
The realization left them reeling.
They were also confused, unsure who had won the battle between this white-clad Creator and the Goddess of Death.
But as they looked around and saw no sign of her, it became clear.
"The Goddess of Death is gone. Don't tell me..."
Staring at the radiant Creator God, they couldn't help but guess—and feel overwhelming awe.
At that moment—
Syd ignored their thoughts and looked down at the Infinity Gauntlet on his hand.
By now, the golden Gauntlet had turned pitch black—clearly burned out.
For an artifact that was already half-ruined, it wasn't surprising that it couldn't withstand an operation on a universal scale.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 592
chapters.content:
Chapter 592 - 592
In the past, he might not have had a way to deal with this kind of situation—but now, it was a simple matter.
Syd immediately activated his power of creation.
The next second, light surged in all directions, and the previously charred Infinity Gauntlet swiftly recovered, returning to its original golden form.
After restoring the Gauntlet, his gaze turned to Thor and the others.
"I've finished handling things here. If there's nothing else, I'll return to Universe 616," he said, looking at Thor.
The moment he spoke, everyone was stunned.
Universe 616?
It didn't take them long to understand what he meant.
Thor looked a bit flustered and hurriedly said, "Can't you stay here? Our universe is pretty great too!"
Syd gently shook his head.
Because of his presence, Natasha didn't die, Tony Stark survived, Balder's unlocking percentage had been fully discovered, Loki and others were revived, and he had even become the Creator God of this universe.
Everything he needed to do here was already complete. There was no reason to stay any longer.
Just as he was about to dissolve this conceptual divine body—
From within the crowd, the Scarlet Witch gritted her teeth and stepped forward, pleading, "Noble Creator God, could you help me revive Vision?"
Silence instantly fell over the scene.
Tony and the others exchanged complex glances with Wanda.
They were well aware of the history between her and Vision.
Some of them had even witnessed Wanda herself, in agony, destroy Vision in order to stop Thanos from getting the Mind Stone.
Although in the end, Thanos still obtained it.
And once the stone was taken, Vision naturally perished.
Their eyes turned toward the white-robed Creator God. No one knew whether he would revive Vision.
After all, he had no ties to either Wanda or Vision. If he helped, it would be an act of mercy; if he didn't, no one could blame him.
Who would dare command a Creator God?
All they could do was plead.
Hearing Wanda's words, Syd frowned slightly and waved his hand.
In the next instant, his creative power surged, and Vision's vibranium body quickly materialized—complete with the yellow gem on his forehead.
Of course, the yellow gem wasn't the real Mind Stone, but a replica he created casually.
Still, it was enough for Vision's use.
As for his consciousness...
Syd's gaze turned toward Earth. Simultaneously, the Chaos Magic light in his hand and the glow from the six stones on the Infinity Gauntlet flared once more—especially the Time Stone.
The vision before his eyes began to rewind.
In no time, he reached the moment when Thanos tore out the Mind Stone and Vision died.
Syd's eyes lit up, and he immediately used Orochi's soul-extraction technique.
Without alerting Thanos, he pulled Vision's soul from that moment in time.
All of this seemed lengthy, but under the influence of the Time Stone, it all happened in an instant.
To the onlookers, it looked like a flash of light—then the white-robed Creator God reached toward some invisible point in space and suddenly held a glowing yellow sphere.
"What is that?"
While they were still dazed, the sphere was tossed into Vision's head, merging with the fake Mind Stone.
Soon after, Vision slowly opened his eyes in a daze.
Without paying him any mind, Syd casually waved his hand and used Chaos Magic to gently float him to the stunned Wanda.
Having done all this, Syd didn't bother to look at Wanda's shock and joy. He turned to Thor and said, "The light of this universe is also me. If anything happens, you can pray to the Light—I'll know."
And with that, to avoid being pestered for more resurrections, he willed his ineffable divine form to dissolve into countless beams of light.
Before anyone could say a word, the light vanished.
Seeing this, Tony and the others looked at each other in astonishment.
Thor, however, wore a face full of sorrow and reluctance.
But the moment he remembered that the Light of this universe was also his brother, his mood improved significantly.
Looking at the surrounding radiance, he suddenly felt as if his little brother was still by his side—and couldn't help but smile foolishly.
In the shadows—
Having dissolved into light and now ready to withdraw his consciousness, Syd caught sight of Thor's expression and couldn't help but be speechless.
The next second, his divine awareness, along with the dissipated divine body, slipped into the quantum tunnel, following a faint connection to return to Universe 616.
At that moment—
The abstract entities—Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Annihilation—faintly sensed something and grew contemplative.
"Another universe?"
"Perhaps over there, we'll get to see that little brother again... heh."
As they conversed—
Syd's vision blurred, and he found himself once more in Universe 616, standing beneath the sunlight, basking in its familiar warmth.
But just then, as he stood there, he faintly sensed something strange.
As part of the universe itself, he could feel that Universe 616 was being drawn toward something—gradually shifting in that direction.
Syd frowned and pondered. Soon, he had a rough idea.
It was probably because of his influence that this was happening.
"Eternity and Infinity in Universe 616 didn't stop this?"
"Aren't they worried about a multiverse collision?"
While he was puzzled, Eternity, Infinity, and the others within Universe 616 were also struggling to understand this anomaly.
They didn't know what had happened or why this was occurring.
Faintly, they sensed that it might have something to do with their youngest brother—the one who had only recently been born?!
They had originally wanted to get a better sense of this younger brother's strength and abilities, to determine if he was worthy of attention. Now, they had yet another reason to meet him.
They decided to seek him out for answers.
With their power, it didn't take long before they locked onto Earth.
They had sensed their little brother's presence on the planet.
Eternity, Infinity, Annihilation, Death, and even Galactus, all began to move at once.
With their abilities, even Galactus could reach Earth in seconds.
And at that moment, Syd was staring at the unlocking progress of God's Power.
(Unlock Progress: 11%)
"Do I get a new power at 15% or 20%?"
As he checked the progress bar and the rate of energy accumulation, he felt both frustration and anticipation.
While waiting for the energy to accumulate, his attention shifted to the Darkhold and its technique—Dreamwalking.
He was ready to give it a try and see if he could use his consciousness to traverse into a brand-new universe!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 593
chapters.content:
Chapter 593 - 593
Syd's focus shifted to the Dreamwalking spell.
The next second, a ripple in space flickered, and a pitch-black, sinister-looking book appeared before him—the Darkhold.
Now, as a Creator God, looking at this book again didn't bring him any comfort. On the contrary, it made him feel even more wary.
Only after reaching the level of a single-universe god could one truly understand how terrifying a multiversal-level being really was.
Before, he hadn't taken the Darkhold's master—Chthon, the ancient god of chaos—very seriously. Looking back now, that was far too naive.
Syd's expression grew serious as he recalled the faint whispering he'd heard not long after awakening his Chaos Magic.
That voice—it might have come from Chthon himself.
Clearly, his sudden emergence as a Chaos Magic user had already attracted Chthon's attention.
It was just that Chthon remained sealed and unable to manifest yet, which was why trouble hadn't arrived.
But Syd was certain—once Chthon escaped his prison, it wouldn't take long before he came looking for him.
And Chthon would escape. It was just a matter of time.
If Chthon were to break free before Syd's strength reached the multiversal level...
He'd have to deal with the God of Dark Magic Chthon, the vaguely linked Trinity God of White Magic—Vishanti, the looming threat of the Outer Gods' true forms, multiversal beings like Eternity and Infinity...
Even the Time Variance Authority, possibly connected to the remnants of the multiversal variant Kang.
Not to mention Arishem the Judge, who fled and might return with stronger Celestials.
Thinking of all this made Syd's head ache.
Only now did he realize just how deeply entangled he had become with so many multiversal-level beings.
Even if there wasn't deep enmity, that didn't mean they wouldn't act.
Maybe one of them was just having a bad day—and if they noticed him...
Syd didn't dare gamble his life on the whims of such beings.
That thought filled him with a rising sense of crisis and an even more urgent desire to grow stronger.
Reining in his thoughts, he turned his attention back to the Darkhold.
Looking again, he sensed a faint connection between the book and something else.
He immediately suppressed his curiosity and resisted the urge to explore it.
No doubt, that link led to Chthon. It was entirely possible Chthon could transmit his power through the book.
Syd flipped through the pages until he found the Dreamwalking spell.
He compared it to what he remembered from before and, finding no inconsistencies, began to cast the spell.
A radiant white glow burst forth from his body as his internal energy began to deplete.
In an instant, Syd noticed a stark difference from before.
He could faintly sense countless universes—and countless versions of himself.
Of course, these were only projections—not true parallel selves.
"...It actually worked."
A flicker of amazement crossed Syd's eyes.
He could feel that his consciousness could be projected into any of these versions of himself, allowing him to control them—just like the Scarlet Witch had done in Doctor Strange: Multiverse of Madness.
But before he could act, something went wrong.
Even though he hadn't used the Darkhold to cast the spell, he still sensed a dark energy slowly creeping toward him, trying to corrupt him.
Syd immediately sensed it.
That energy twisted minds, corrupted spirits, and altered one's essence to become compatible with a particular entity.
The final goal—body possession and rebirth of that entity.
Of course, this wouldn't work on just anyone. Only those with high compatibility could serve as Chthon's vessel.
Like the Scarlet Witch.
Or... himself.
Syd's brow furrowed. His body flared with light, resisting the encroaching darkness.
On the surface, it seemed he had held it off—but what lay beneath, he couldn't be sure.
He knew far too little about the tricks of multiversal beings.
"Once I finish testing this Dreamwalking spell and understand its principles... I'll make my own version."
Syd's wariness grew stronger.
But once he understood how it worked, he was confident he could create a similar spell on his own.
In traditional mythology, gods were born of the world itself. Magic was just a secondary force. If a god desired to learn it, mastering it was effortless.
As the God of Light, Balder, Syd naturally inherited this trait.
Even from his early days experimenting with various magic types, he could wield them all with ease—proof enough.
In this case, as long as he understood the theory, creating his own version of Dreamwalking should be within reach.
With that thought, he refocused on the projections.
Strangely, he noticed that some projections were brighter while others were dim.
The bright ones gleamed like daylight, the dim ones like dying embers.
Curious, Syd chose the weakest and dimmest one to test.
The next second, he felt part of his consciousness being pulled away.
That part of his awareness traveled into the faint projection.
Just as he began testing Dreamwalking...
Beyond Earth, something else was unfolding.
Five beings descended upon the planet.
One was cloaked in darkness, resembling the starry night sky, with galaxies and stars within his body—Eternity, the embodiment of universal time.
Another was black and yellow, her body traced with black lines, appearing female—Infinity, the embodiment of space itself.
A third, draped in a black robe, had the form of a skeletal woman—Death, the embodiment of the end of all things.
The fourth wore a crimson robe, had gray-black skin, and glowing white eyes, looking terrifying and fierce—Annihilation, the embodiment of destruction.
The fifth wore purple armor and towered like a giant—Galactus, the World Devourer.
Of course, these were not their true forms—only manifestations created for the understanding of lower beings, and shaped according to their own preferences.
Even Galactus, who had a physical form and wasn't an abstract cosmic concept, was currently not showing his true body.
Next to him floated a small silver figure—Silver Surfer, his faithful herald, gliding silently on his silver board.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 594
chapters.content:
Chapter 594 - 594
He was once a man who, to save his homeworld from being devoured by Galactus, voluntarily became his herald. In return, he gained superhuman strength, an indestructible body, and eternal life.
Now, trembling behind Galactus, the Silver Surfer dared not raise his head. Though his body no longer feared cold or heat, he still shivered.
Because he knew all too well what kind of beings had just arrived.
The five most supreme, most powerful entities in the universe—no exception.
The Creator Gods of the cosmos themselves!
Eternity, Infinity, Death, Annihilation—the very embodiments of universal principles and abstract concepts.
Even Galactus, though the only one among them who was a physical being rather than an abstract force, had been born at the same time as Eternity and the others.
"...So this is Earth?"
Staring at the beautiful, blue planet before him, Galactus's eyes flashed with a trace of greed.
From this small world, he sensed an immense surge of life energy!
In just an instant, hunger rose within him. He wanted to devour this world.
To beings like Eternity and Galactus, Earth—even as vast as it seemed to mortals—was insignificantly small. They could destroy it with a mere thought.
Even in his weakened and starved state, Galactus still had the power to consume the planet.
And now, with the five of them manifesting bodies far larger than Earth itself, it was as if the planet was no bigger than a basketball in their palms.
Drawn by the rich life energy, Galactus—clad in purple armor—extended his right hand. He seemed ready to act.
The moment he did, the other four—Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Annihilation—frowned slightly.
At that instant, the trembling Silver Surfer behind Galactus could no longer hold back.
Though he served as Galactus's herald, imbued with the Power Cosmic and possessing immense strength, he was still, at heart, the same man who had once sacrificed himself to protect his homeworld.
His name was Norrin Radd.
And even now, he couldn't bear to watch another inhabited planet with intelligent life be destroyed.
Whenever possible, he guided Galactus toward lifeless planets filled only with energy—no sentient civilizations.
Seeing Galactus reaching for Earth, he quickly stepped forward and said with a trembling voice, "My lord... this planet... it's one that the being cares about. If you devour it, it might ruin your relationship with him."
Galactus's hand froze mid-air. His eyes flickered with clarity as he forcibly suppressed his hunger.
In his mind, he saw that glowing figure—his youngest brother—the one who had radiated divine light and terrifying power.
He paused... and then his voice rumbled through the void.
"You're right. I'll let this planet go."
To him, offending that youngest brother over a single planet simply wasn't worth it.
Suppressing his hunger, he slowly retracted his hand.
The Silver Surfer let out a sigh of relief.
Eternity and the others cast approving glances toward the tiny being.
Those glances only made Norrin Radd tremble harder.
Then—
"Enough. Let's find out where he is," Death said, her voice impatient.
The five gods turned their gazes toward Earth, searching for their hidden younger brother.
But they were surprised to find that Earth was veiled by an abstract divine force that greatly weakened their perception.
If they hadn't been intentionally observing, they might have missed it entirely—like humans overlooking the bacteria on their skin.
After all, the planet's presence was almost too small to notice.
But now that they were focused, the divine concealment quickly lost its effect.
Especially for Eternity and Infinity—in a moment, they had already locked onto a likely target.
While the gods were observing Earth, chaos was erupting on the planet.
Their descent had not been subtle.
Galactus alone had blocked out part of the sun, casting much of the world into sudden shadow.
People looked up and froze, mouths agape.
"Oh my God..."
"What is that?!"
All around the globe, panic swept through the cities.
At major space agencies and research institutions, the satellite feeds clearly showed what was happening: five indescribably massive beings had appeared outside Earth's atmosphere.
"Who are they?"
"Why are they here?"
"Wait... is that Eternity?"
Some staff members recognized the figure among them—Eternity, the embodiment of time.
They had seen him once before, during the incident with the Celestials and the White-Clad Warrior, when Thanos made his infamous wish. Eternity had briefly appeared then—though at a much smaller scale.
But now, with a closer look, they confirmed: that was indeed Eternity.
...
At S.H.I.E.L.D. headquarters—
Nick Fury's face was grim. Panic edged into his thoughts as he muttered, "Those five... don't tell me they're all Creator Gods?"
"What do they want on Earth?"
A thousand terrifying thoughts flashed through his mind, each more suffocating than the last.
While panic and fear gripped the planet, Syd—still on Earth—also sensed the arrival of Death and the others.
He could more or less guess why they were here.
But right now, his attention wasn't on that.
He had just projected a part of his consciousness into one of the weakest projections he had found.
In an instant, his awareness took over the projection—there was no resistance at all.
And then, the previously faint and illusory projection immediately solidified into a tangible existence.
Syd found himself in a pitch-black space, surrounded by a watery substance.
And he was incredibly weak.
A single moment was all he needed to grasp the situation.
"This projection... hasn't even been born yet?"
His eyes widened in surprise.
Carefully sensing the state of this body, he realized how frail and faint it was—without his arrival, it likely would have dissipated naturally.
No wonder it had felt so dim in his perception.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 595
chapters.content:
Chapter 595 - 595
For now, Syd paid no mind to the arrival of Death and the others. His attention was fully focused on the projection of another universe.
In his perception, this projection was extremely weak—still in the embryonic stage of an unborn infant. But for him, resolving such a situation was trivial.
At the moment, he resisted the urge to reconstruct the body and instead turned his attention outward, curious about the surrounding environment.
His powerful mind extended in a subtle wave, sweeping gently beyond.
In an instant, sounds and sights reached him.
He saw a young woman with noble elegance, golden hair cascading down her shoulders, hurrying down a palace corridor.
It wasn't long before she entered a lavish hall.
"Odin, I have good news for you."
Frigga stepped into the room, smiling at the armored man with a broad frame and the Eternal Spear in his hand.
"Frigga, what is it?" asked a slightly younger Odin, a hint of surprise on his face.
Frigga gently placed her hand on her belly, radiating maternal warmth as she said, "There is new life inside me."
Odin was stunned. "Are you serious, Frigga?"
She nodded softly.
Odin quickly extended his senses toward her abdomen—only for his brow to furrow deeply the next moment.
"He's too weak... He won't be a worthy warrior."
Though he was initially excited, once he sensed the child within, disappointment crept into his voice.
To him, the child was too feeble—so fragile it seemed like he could vanish at any moment. Even if born, he would surely remain weak.
"To be a son of Odin... he should at least not be this weak," Odin thought bitterly.
Frigga's expression darkened.
"Odin, is battle all you ever think about? What's wrong with not being a warrior? What if he's weak? As long as he's happy and safe, that's all that matters!"
Then she paused, puzzled. "Wait... I think he's growing... very quickly? It feels like he's about to be born."
Odin blinked, startled. "That's impossible. How could he be born so quickly?"
Even for Asgardians, this speed was unheard of—far beyond anything even Midgard's humans could experience.
But when he focused again, he could clearly sense it: the child's growth was accelerating at an unbelievable rate. He was nearly ready to be born.
"What is going on?!"
Syd, too, sensed it—and though surprised at first, he wasn't too shocked.
After all, this was just a projection of information. Rapid growth was to be expected.
Before long, Frigga clutched her stomach in pain, her body trembling.
"Ahhh..." she cried out.
"What's wrong?" Odin asked, suddenly alarmed.
"I... I'm going into labor!" she groaned.
"What?!"
That quickly?
Odin stood frozen in disbelief.
But there was no time to think. As Frigga doubled over in pain, he rushed to the door and shouted, "Someone! Help!"
Soon after, attendants poured in to assist with the delivery.
Odin, meanwhile, stood outside, waiting nervously. Despite the child's frailty, he was still his child.
As he anxiously stood by, Odin's senses stirred—he could feel the infant nearing birth.
Just as he thought about checking on the child later...
Syd made his move.
He hadn't come to this universe just to look around. His true purpose—aside from observing the 616 universe—was to invade this new universe and become its Creator God, thus stacking and amplifying his divine influence.
Now that he was here, he didn't hesitate.
He followed the pull of destiny and began to merge with this universe's abstract essence—its Creator Deity.
In an instant—before he was even born—a horrifying phenomenon occurred!
An indescribable, radiant brilliance erupted from Frigga's womb, flooding the entire palace.
In the blink of an eye, that strange, sacred light blanketed all of Asgard!
Inside the chamber—
Frigga stared at her belly in disbelief.
The maids were frozen in place.
"What... what's happening?"
"What's that light?!"
Their eyes snapped to the Queen's abdomen, but after barely a glance, the light stung so fiercely they had to look away.
And then they felt it—a terrifying power radiating from Frigga's womb.
Outside, Odin was just as stunned. The light enveloped all of Asgard, and he had no explanation for it.
Throughout the realm, Asgardians stared at the radiant sky in awe and fear.
"What's going on?"
"Where is that light coming from?!"
Cries of confusion echoed everywhere.
Meanwhile—
A young boy, short and golden-haired, resembling a miniature Thor, looked around in astonishment.
At first, it seemed like that was the end of it.
But Odin, Heimdall, and other powerful beings suddenly realized something was very wrong.
The light hadn't stopped—it was still spreading, rushing outward!
The speed—it was impossible to describe.
At the Bifrost, Heimdall, the Gatekeeper of Asgard, stood stunned. His golden eyes, capable of seeing across the Nine Realms, were filled with shock.
"The Nine Realms... the entire universe... it's glowing."
In his eyes, the cosmos had become a sea of blinding light.
Nearby Asgardians gasped at his words.
"The entire universe? Glowing?!"
"Heimdall, are you serious?"
Meanwhile—
Across the universe, various powerful entities sensed the shift.
Something had changed.
A new will had emerged.
What was going on?!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 596
chapters.content:
Chapter 596 - 596
At that moment, the brilliance that lit up the entire universe suddenly contracted, converging toward a single point.
Asgard.
An infinite radiance now gathered in Frigga's womb, and in the next instant, a baby cloaked in divine light—hazy and indistinct, as if he were light itself—descended into the world.
Faintly, it seemed that the entire universe began to echo with praises and hymns.
"Great Light..."
"Master of Ten Billion Rays..."
"O Creator..."
These voices resonated not only in Frigga's and Odin's ears, nor just among the people of Asgard—but throughout all of existence, every sentient being in the universe paused in stunned reverence.
Suspended in the palace air, Syd hovered, cloaked in a boundless glow, utterly indescribable.
The next moment, Odin burst into the palace and froze at the sight.
"Is this... my child?"
He murmured in a daze, instinctively reaching out with his senses.
And in that moment, his expression turned to pure shock.
What he sensed was not a frail newborn—but boundless light... an entire universe.
The immense energy concentrated within the child frightened him just by its presence. He staggered a step back.
"How... how can he be this powerful?!"
The very presence of this seemingly fragile child filled Odin with suffocating fear and disbelief.
Before he could gather his thoughts, the infant—shrouded in immaculate brilliance—gently descended to the ground.
Under the astonished gazes of Odin, Frigga, and the attending maids, the baby began to grow.
His body elongated, and his facial features matured from soft and childish to sharp and dignified.
In mere moments, he transformed from a newborn into a radiant youth of seventeen or eighteen.
The holy light surrounding him solidified into a pure-white divine robe, faintly glowing with every movement.
As the brilliance gradually retracted, his full appearance was revealed.
He was flawless.
So perfect, it was as though the universe had crafted him as its most refined creation.
A radiance of warmth, majesty, and divine mystery cloaked his entire being, declaring him the most exalted existence in the cosmos.
The moment Odin and the others laid eyes on him, they were overwhelmed with an inexplicable joy.
Joy that surged from the soul.
Irresistible and pure.
Fortunately, this strange emotional influence faded quickly—otherwise, even Odin would have feared for his sanity.
Syd opened his golden eyes, gazing calmly at the stunned crowd before him.
Then, in a voice as mysterious and profound as universal truth itself, he declared:
"I am the God of Light across the Cosmos—Balder."
His voice echoed across the palace...
And not only there.
It rang across the entire universe.
Every living being—mortal and divine—heard the celestial proclamation.
Those who heard it froze.
Regardless of species or language, all instantly understood the meaning, even if the words weren't in their native tongue.
And then—shock, awe, and uproar.
"God of Light?"
"Where did this deity come from?"
"Was that earlier cosmic anomaly because of him?"
"How terrifying... When did the universe gain such a powerful god?!"
Across the cosmos, every technological power and pantheon began fervently discussing what had just occurred.
Meanwhile...
On Earth, still in its medieval age, humans were utterly stunned.
"There really are gods?"
"Balder... Is that the name of this god?"
"God of Light?"
"Is this... the Second Coming?"
In this age of fervent belief, countless followers in the West were overcome with joy and awe.
It was common knowledge that the true name of "the Lord" was a mystery—every name across religious texts was a stand-in.
Now, they began to wonder if this Balder, the God of Light, was in fact the one true God.
While humans on Earth reeled in disbelief, back in Asgard, Odin stared blankly at the being before him.
This child, this impossibly perfect being who radiated divinity from every pore—was supposed to be his son?
And yet, deep within his heart, a sense of unease began to bloom.
This divine being was far too powerful.
Just brushing against his energy earlier had sent shudders down Odin's spine.
Even as his father, Odin couldn't help but feel dread.
Just then, a weary voice broke the silence.
"Balder?"
Frigga, pale and drenched in sweat, called out weakly.
Syd turned his golden gaze toward her. Seeing her state, he gently raised his right hand.
In an instant, the power of creation surged forth.
Frigga felt a mysterious force flow through her, and all fatigue, all discomfort vanished in an instant. It was as if her very essence had been restored.
She blinked in disbelief.
"What kind of power is this...?"
Odin, too, had sensed what happened. His face only grew more shocked and tense.
Syd ignored their reactions, his gaze drifting beyond the palace to the entirety of Asgard.
"How is this universe different from Earth-616? What unique features does it hold?"
Curiosity stirred within him.
He was just about to activate his abstract conceptual form to begin analyzing the universe...
When the sound of footsteps echoed from outside.
Syd's gaze easily pierced through the palace walls, seeing the group rushing toward them.
Heimdall, a younger Thor... and others.
Odin and Frigga also turned to look.
Soon, Heimdall and the group arrived outside the palace. With Odin's permission, they stepped inside.
Their eyes immediately scanned the grand hall.
They spotted King Odin, of course.
They also saw Queen Frigga, standing neatly, no trace of childbirth left on her.
But what caught all of their attention—what utterly stunned them—was a stranger.
He wore a robe of immaculate white that glowed faintly, his very body emanating radiant light.
His features were strikingly handsome.
And his presence...
Unfathomable.
Who... was this being?
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 597
chapters.content:
Chapter 597 - 597
Staring at the unfamiliar figure before them, Heimdall and the others were momentarily stunned, confusion filling their eyes.
"Your Majesty, who is this?" Heimdall asked curiously.
Odin hesitated for a moment, then began to explain.
As the truth came out, the expressions of those present gradually shifted from confusion to utter shock.
The youngest son of King Odin?
Thor's brother?
It had only been a short while, and suddenly the Allfather had another son?
Heimdall and the others exchanged bewildered glances, disbelief thick in the air.
Especially among them, young Thor stood frozen in place, eyes wide.
What shocked them even more wasn't just the sudden appearance of another prince—it was his name and presence.
According to Odin, this prince had only just been born, and yet here he stood, fully grown and named Balder?
Their minds echoed with the voice that had earlier proclaimed across the universe.
"Could this prince be... the God of Light, Balder?"
Heimdall asked, his voice uncertain.
Odin and Frigga both nodded.
Seeing the Allfather and Queen confirm it, the group's disbelief only grew deeper.
They all remembered it clearly—the light that had filled the cosmos, a divine proclamation that had stunned gods and mortals alike. If that being was now standing right in front of them...
Just how terrifying was this new prince's power?
As such thoughts circled their minds, Heimdall and the others looked at Balder with hesitation, doubt, and awe.
At this moment—
A short, golden-haired boy stepped forward from the crowd: young Thor.
He tilted his head back to look up at the taller, regal presence before him, struggling to accept what he saw.
Not only was this "brother" suddenly added to his family, but the guy even looked older—more like a big brother.
It was infuriating.
And in Thor's young heart, defiance burned.
"He doesn't believe any of it—this whole 'lighting up the universe' stuff. That's just impossible!"
"No way someone from Asgard is that powerful!"
His childish voice rang out, and Heimdall and the others instinctively looked over at the little prince.
Truth be told, even they couldn't help but feel the same. It was just too unbelievable.
But then Thor's eyes lit up as an idea struck him.
"If you're so powerful, then tell me about my future! Will I become a great warrior?"
"That's called a prophecy, right? Only great gods can do that!"
Everyone went silent.
A prophecy?
Even for Asgardians, prophecy was considered both a miracle and a taboo.
One by one, all eyes turned toward Balder, radiant in divine robes, surrounded by soft glowing light, exuding divine mystery and nobility.
Could he really do it?
Even Odin was curious.
Frigga, meanwhile, opened her mouth to speak—wanting to step in, to shield her newborn son from impossible expectations.
After all, he had just been born. How could he possibly make a prophecy?
Wasn't this too much?
Feeling all their gazes, including Frigga's worry and hesitation, Syd glanced at young Thor.
Prophecy? That was easy enough for him. He could casually state anything from the future.
But... that only applied to normal circumstances. This universe might not be the same as Earth-616. Who knew how things would unfold here?
If he gave a fake prophecy and it later turned out wrong—it would be bad.
Which meant, in this situation, the best course was a real prophecy.
And for him, even that wasn't difficult.
Even though this was just a projection body—just a fragment of his consciousness—he was still a Creator God. He could connect with his true body and borrow its power.
And truthfully, he was just as curious about how this universe differed from 616.
"Balder, don't mind your brother's words. You're still young, and a prophecy..."
Frigga smiled, trying to diffuse the moment.
But before she could finish, under everyone's gaze, the divine figure of Syd raised his right hand.
In that instant, crimson energy pulsed through the air.
Everyone, including Thor, paused, minds racing with possibilities.
"Is that... divine power? Or magic?"
As they watched, Syd activated the power of chaos magic.
Immediately, the red energy transformed into green.
It was the power of the Time Stone.
Within the shifting energies, a translucent stone flickered in and out of existence—though it never fully materialized.
He didn't bother forging a real Time Stone.
All of this—hidden under the mingling glow of red chaos and green time—went unnoticed by Odin and the rest.
Syd's mind brought up the ancient spells related to the Time Stone stored in Kamar-Taj.
Naturally, these spells were sourced from the minds of Kaecilius, Doctor Strange, and others.
With a casual gesture, the combined powers of chaos magic and the phantom Time Stone conjured the most probable future—one without his direct involvement.
"That's... the power of time?"
"The Time Stone?!"
"Impossible!"
Odin's face turned pale with shock.
He could feel something familiar in the energy Balder was wielding—something he'd once sensed from Earth's Sorcerer Supreme.
"Is he... using the Time Stone?" Odin whispered.
Then quickly shook his head.
"That's impossible!"
Balder had just been born. How could he have gotten the Time Stone?
Besides, it was still with the Sorcerer Supreme on Earth. There was no way it could be here in Asgard.
Which left only one terrifying possibility.
"He can freely wield the power of time... He was born with the ability to control it?"
Odin's voice trembled as he spoke, the realization leaving him shaken.
Those nearby—Heimdall, the others—were equally stunned.
At that moment, Syd gave a gentle wave of his hand.
The image of the most probable future appeared in the air, projecting itself for all to see.
Everyone stared at the vision—Odin included.
Even Syd himself looked on with curiosity.
He hadn't previewed it beforehand, so this was his first time seeing this universe's future as well.
The sky in the image was gray and heavy, a world of ice and snow unfolding before them.
With just one glance, Odin immediately recognized where it was.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 598
chapters.content:
Chapter 598 - 598
"Jotunheim?"
Odin frowned deeply, as did the others.
The realm of the Frost Giants—one of the Nine Realms?
Why would the vision show Jotunheim?
The next moment, in the snowy landscape, they saw the towering figure of King Laufey wielding his ice hammer, locked in fierce combat with Odin, who held his spear.
"His Majesty Odin is fighting Laufey?"
Heimdall and the others were surprised at first, but didn't think much of it.
In their eyes, Odin's victory was all but certain. How could Laufey, a Frost Giant, possibly defeat him?
But then—they saw the unthinkable.
Laufey's hammer pierced through Odin's abdomen. Blood exploded across the snow.
Impossible!
In shock, Heimdall and the rest watched Odin fall to the frozen ground.
Syd's golden eyes glimmered as he whispered softly.
A cold, mysterious voice—like a cosmic truth—resonated in their minds:
"Though it may seem a fair fight, fate leans toward Odin."
"In myths, the noble hero always defeats the monster..."
"But... what if this time is not like the stories?"
A heavy silence fell upon the hall.
Then—
"This must be fake!" young Thor shouted, shaking his head furiously. "There's no way that Frost Giant could beat Father! It's fake!"
He glared at Syd with defiance.
But the vision continued.
After Odin's death, Laufey invaded Asgard. In the midst of the terrified crowds, his gaze landed on the child—Thor.
He narrowed his eyes... scheming.
To Heimdall and the others' shock, the Frost Giant King adopted young Thor—and imprisoned Queen Frigga.
Thor, now Laufey's ward, vowed that one day he would destroy Jotunheim.
Time passed.
Then, Laufey's true son—Loki—appeared. After certain events, he and Thor formed a deep bond.
Thor grew into a powerful warrior, defeating many formidable enemies. The Frost Giants, who revered strength, came to favor him—especially Laufey, who began to treat Thor like his own son, even naming him heir to the throne.
Meanwhile, Loki, being cunning but not a warrior, was increasingly neglected.
Lonely and desperate, Loki formed a bond with the imprisoned Frigga. He longed for Midgard, the "realm of stories" Frigga spoke of.
Time passed again.
Thor eventually inherited the royal weapon—a hammer named Icebreaker—and became heir to the throne. Loki, by contrast, remained in the shadows.
Still, Thor treated Loki like a brother.
One day, Thor revealed that Laufey wanted them both to help conquer Muspelheim, the land of fire giants ruled by Surtur. But Loki refused.
Instead, he knocked out the guards, freed Frigga, and used her magic to summon the Bifröst to escape to Midgard.
But just as they reached the bridge, Laufey and Thor appeared.
Thor's skin had already turned the characteristic icy blue of the Frost Giants.
Laufey had known all along. He had let them get this far—just to kill them here.
As Laufey raised his weapon toward Loki, Thor pleaded with him to stop. In the chaos, Loki struck first—killing Laufey.
Furious, Thor turned on Loki.
"No, no, no—what have you done?!" Thor screamed, wielding Icebreaker as a storm of frost raged around him.
A deadly surge of cold exploded from the hammer.
Loki, terrified, would have been struck down—if not for Frigga.
"Loki! Look out!" she cried, hurling herself into him.
"No!"
The frost engulfed her. A large part of her body froze over.
Loki scrambled to her side, holding her in panic.
"Thor... what have you done?!"
Frigga, now mostly frozen, murmured weakly,
"Thor... was that really you?"
She turned toward him, trying to see him clearly... but the frost spread over her completely.
In Loki's arms, her body shattered into a pile of glistening ice.
"What... did my father and his cursed hammer do to you..."
"You don't even recognize..."
"...your own mother..."
Before he could finish, Frigga had crumbled away in his embrace.
Loki screamed in agony and attacked Thor.
But he was no match.
Thor, now the God of Winter, defeated him easily.
Yet in the end, Thor relented and let Loki escape across the Bifröst to Midgard.
They never saw each other again.
Loki lived a peaceful life on Earth.
Thor remained in Jotunheim—king and guardian of the realm, the cold sovereign of winter.
Image after image played before their eyes.
No one could believe what they were seeing.
Especially the part with Frigga and Thor.
Little Thor clutched his head and backed away in terror, screaming:
"The prophecy's fake! It's fake! I'd never hurt Mother!"
"I don't want to see it anymore! I don't!"
His face twisted in fear and dread. He no longer dared look at Balder—the terrifying god who conjured the vision.
Then he screamed and fled the palace.
"Thor!" Frigga called out, chasing after him.
As she left, the prophecy vanished from above.
But no one's heart had calmed.
Their expressions were heavy with turmoil.
"Was that real?" Heimdall asked suddenly.
Syd answered calmly,
"What do you think?"
He didn't say yes. But everyone, especially Odin, understood—it could be real.
Yet emotionally, they couldn't accept it.
Then Heimdall's eyes lit up, noticing something.
"Balder-sama... you weren't in the vision. Could that mean it's inaccurate?"
Odin blinked. His heart lightened slightly.
That's right. Maybe it's changeable...
His eyes turned toward Syd with hope.
Syd said flatly,
"Time cannot predict me."
The crowd went still.
Time... can't predict him?
Impossible.
And yet, here he stood.
If it were true... then Balder's existence was more terrifying than they imagined.
Feeling their eyes on him, Syd fell silent for a moment.
Then he spoke:
"What I showed you was merely the most probable future. It's not set in stone."
"With my arrival, the future has already changed. Aside from Ragnarok, which is destined... you needn't worry. Just act as if you never saw this prophecy."
As he spoke, he floated calmly out of the palace, lost in thought, experimenting with a new chaos magic technique similar to dream-walking.
Crimson light shimmered from his fingertips as he worked.
Odin and the others let out a collective sigh—then froze again.
"Ragnarok?" Odin murmured. "He even knows about Ragnarok...?"
He was stunned.
A child just born—and he already knew of the twilight of the gods?
Meanwhile, far beyond the multiverse...
Tentacles began to emerge.
A massive, unknowable, and utterly terrifying presence drifted closer.
The true body of the Old One.
Its voice echoed across the void—
"Insect... You dare destroy my avatar..."
"I warned you... It's far from over..."
"When I descend, it will be your end..."
"You will be my puppet..."
"The power you wield... will be my dessert..."
"Insect..."
A creature not even on the level of a single-universe god, a crawling bug, dared defy Him?
He would crush that ant.
Now.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 599
chapters.content:
Chapter 599 - 599
The true body of the unnameable Old One brimmed with malice, its thoughts consumed with how it would crush that defiant insect who dared challenge its will.
A being so insignificant... how dare he provoke It?
"Soon... very soon..."
"It won't be long..."
It began imagining whether it would annihilate that wretch with a glance—or obliterate him with a single syllable.
...
While the Old One's true body surged toward the 616 Main Universe, Syd's consciousness projection was still calmly studying the spell of Dreamwalking.
Suspended in the air, deep crimson light pulsed from his palms as he continued experimenting and refining the technique.
"This part is used to separate consciousness... and this part..."
With his divine-level talent as Balder, he swiftly broke down the spell's inner workings. In no time at all, he fully grasped its core principles.
And once the underlying mechanics were understood, replicating and improving the spell became far easier.
To accelerate the process, Syd's abstract conceptual consciousness enveloped all of Asgard's libraries, absorbing all their magical knowledge.
He didn't stop there—even Earth's Kamar-Taj was not spared.
In an instant, his vast will spread over the ancient sanctum.
"Who—!?"
"This presence... It's terrifying!"
The current Sorcerer Supreme on Earth was filled with shock.
Just sensing the tip of this will filled him with fear and a reverent awe.
"What kind of god... is this...?"
He fell silent in dread.
But Syd ignored him.
In the blink of an eye, he had absorbed all the magical knowledge hidden in Kamar-Taj.
As his consciousness swept across, countless arcane texts and forbidden tomes were scanned and rapidly understood.
...
Asgard.
Ten minutes later.
Syd opened his golden eyes, shimmering with strange brilliance. Ancient runes occasionally flickered across his irises.
With the divine superiority granted to him by nature, and having absorbed nearly all magical knowledge from Asgard and Kamar-Taj, it had only taken ten minutes for him to develop a new Dreamwalking-like spell.
Of course, having the original technique as a reference made this even easier.
And on top of that—he improved it, adapting the spell to fit his divine nature.
"Now, it's not just projection. As long as any universe contains my information, I can send my consciousness—or even my body—there."
Syd understood very well: though projection and body travel might sound similar, the difference was vast.
Some universes didn't have Asgard. Which meant no Odin, no Frigga... and thus, no Balder.
But while Asgard might not physically exist in those timelines—it didn't mean Asgardian mythology didn't.
Almost every universe had tales of Asgard and Norse mythology.
Even in those where they didn't exist originally, now that Balder's progression was at 100%, fragments of his identity had already spread into those realms.
Syd's gaze gleamed.
Using his new Dreamwalking spell, he could detect the traces of himself in various universes—allowing him to descend into them.
With those universe coordinates, crossing over wasn't limited to consciousness—his body could follow as well.
"It's time to leave," he murmured.
He had completed what he came for.
Of course, it was only his consciousness departing. A portion of this universe's Light now belonged to him, and from 616, he would still be able to monitor it.
In the next moment, before the eyes of countless Asgardians, his figure blurred—and in a flash, scattered into radiant strands of divine light.
Brilliant rays shimmered in the sky—
Then slowly faded.
As if he had never existed.
Everyone—Heimdall, Odin, and others—stared, dumbfounded.
Thankfully, just before departing, Syd remembered that this Asgard was still relatively fragile. A thought crossed his mind—
And in an instant, the power of creation surged across the entire realm.
To Odin and the others' shock and awe, they felt their bodies undergoing immense transformation.
Within seconds, bathed in white light, the ordinary citizens of Asgard gained physical strength that surpassed even Hulk and Thanos.
As for Odin, Frigga, and the royal family—radiant golden blood now coursed through their veins.
Boundless abstract conceptual divine power flowed into them.
In an instant, their auras surged to astonishing levels.
With these powers, it wasn't an exaggeration to say their strength now rivaled the Celestials.
Odin's strength, in particular, had grown even more terrifying.
And with that final act, Syd's consciousness withdrew from the universe and returned to his true body in the 616 Universe.
...
But his departure left Asgard in uproar.
"This power...?"
Heimdall clenched his fist, marveling at the overwhelming strength in his body, shock still etched across his face.
The rest of the realm was equally stunned.
"What happened?"
"How is this possible?"
Even Odin looked dumbfounded.
The upheaval lasted for some time before Odin stepped forward to calm everyone down.
But the question remained: what exactly had happened?
It didn't take long before they all reached the same conclusion:
"It must've been Balder-sama..."
"Incredible..."
No one else could've possibly done this.
Yet, to their dismay, Balder-sama had vanished.
No matter how they searched, he could not be found.
While they scoured for him, Eternity and other cosmic beings also silently descended upon Asgard.
But no one noticed.
They had only one thought:
Where is he...?
...
616 Main Universe.
Syd opened his eyes.
"Now I hold power from three universes... but I still need to move faster."
Fortunately, with the new Dreamwalking spell, universe conquest would accelerate greatly.
"And I can't neglect the God Unlock Progress either. That's still the top priority..."
His gaze turned toward the system's interface.
[Unlock Progress: 11%]
Then he glanced at his energy points... and shook his head.
Still not enough to push the progress to 15%.
He needed to accumulate more.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 600
chapters.content:
Chapter 600 - 600
As Syd pondered, he suddenly sensed something.
He faintly detected several gazes observing him.
Looking up, his eyes met with the massive shadow hanging in the sky—an unspoken exchange occurred through space itself.
"Galactus and the others... have they found my location?"
He was a little surprised.
Still, he wasn't too concerned.
After all, now that he possessed the power of three universes, not even Annihilus at his peak would be a match for him.
With that thought, he temporarily dismissed the looming presences of the cosmic entities. His attention shifted back to the Dreamwalking spell.
In the next moment, he activated it.
Brilliant light flared from his body as a portion of his consciousness separated, vanishing like a streak of starlight.
The sensation was similar to Chthon's Dreamwalking spell—except this time, there was no darkness, no threat of corruption or invasion.
His consciousness blinked and arrived in a new universe.
And immediately, he frowned in surprise.
In this universe, his previous projection had already naturally dissipated. In other words, he no longer had a vessel to anchor to.
Fortunately, even just a fragment of his will could access his main body's power. If needed, he could craft a new vessel on the spot.
But this time... it wasn't necessary.
Without delay, Syd began radiating his divine Light across the universe.
In an instant, endless brilliance flooded the void. The entire universe was lit up once more, triggering shock and awe across countless worlds.
After a while, the phenomenon receded. The infinite light converged into a single form—his abstract conceptual body.
Syd was about to depart again, preparing for his next Dreamwalk—
But then he sensed something... wrong with this universe's Earth.
His attention was instantly drawn to it, and what he saw made his eyes narrow.
...
New York City.
Wails and howls echoed through the streets. Countless grey-skinned zombies roamed the ruins.
"Zombies?"
Syd raised a brow.
A moment later, his body dissolved into pure light and vanished from the sky.
Then, in the blink of an eye, he appeared above a tall building in New York.
At the same time, red Chaos Magic shimmered in his hand, overlapping with green light—the power of the Time Stone.
In his golden eyes, the recent past began to unfold.
He quickly understood what had happened.
Hank Pym, the creator of the Pym Particles and the original Ant-Man, had ventured into the Quantum Realm in search of his wife, Janet van Dyne, the Wasp—who had been lost in that dimension.
But what he didn't know was... Janet had been infected by a Quantum Zombie Virus.
When Hank reached her, he embraced her without hesitation—and was bitten.
Both returned to the real world as zombies.
From that point, the virus spread rapidly. In just a few days, New York was overrun.
The vision continued to play.
The Avengers fell.
Tony Stark, Captain America, even the Scarlet Witch—all infected.
And the worst part?
Even though they had become zombies, they had not lost their powers—or even all of their intelligence.
They could still fight. Still wield armor and magic.
Only a handful of heroes and civilians managed to survive.
As Syd reviewed the timeline, a roar echoed across the city.
On a nearby rooftop, a zombie leaped toward him.
"Look out!"
A voice rang from the distance.
A red-suited figure swung through the air, shouting in warning.
Peter Parker—Spider-Man—desperately tried to reach him.
But he was too far.
All he could do was hope this glowing being noticed in time and evaded the zombie attack.
If that being gets infected... what kind of nightmare would that be?
A moment later—
Before the zombie even came close, it was vaporized in a flash of light.
Gone without a trace.
Syd turned his gaze toward Spider-Man, finally acknowledging him.
The zombies? Not even worth a glance.
Peter landed nearby, still shaken.
"Oh my god... you're amazing!"
In the blink of an eye, that thing had just vanished!
But—
More howls erupted nearby.
Drawn by the noise, a swarm of zombies approached.
"We've got to go! Now!" Peter waved anxiously. "There's too many of them!"
Syd looked at him.
And in the next second—Peter froze.
A blinding white light swept across the streets.
In the span of a breath, all nearby zombies vaporized into nothingness. Silence returned to the ruined city.
Peter stared, jaw slack.
"You... you..."
He could barely form words.
Syd ignored him and scanned the planet once more, his expression darkening.
He knew a fair bit about zombie viruses.
And this wasn't the only universe plagued by such outbreaks.
In Earth-2149, tensions between humans and mutants had reached their peak. In a desperate move to empower mutants, Magneto had retrieved a virus from another dimension—one supposedly harmless to mutants.
But upon arrival in that dimension... the virus mutated.
Not only did it infect humans—it infected mutants too.
The outbreak was catastrophic.
Even Hulk, Wolverine, and Jean Grey, wielding the Phoenix Force, were infected.
Even the corporeal form of Galactus became a zombie.
"Ridiculous... totally broken," Syd muttered.
His gaze drifted over the decaying Earth.
At the rate the virus was spreading, if Spider-Man and the remaining survivors couldn't stop it—it would soon consume the entire universe.
"If this universe turns into a zombie realm... and I've become part of it..."
"Would I... be affected too?"
He was curious.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 601
chapters.content:
Chapter 601 - 601
Syd pondered what might happen if this universe completely turned into a zombie universe.
At the current rate of virus spread, if the little Spider and the others couldn't stop it, it really could spread across the cosmos.
He was curious—if the universe became a zombie universe, what would happen to him, as a part of it?
After a moment of thought, Syd shook his head. "Most likely, nothing will happen to me."
"Except for the planet-devourers who have physical forms, abstract concepts like myself and the others—Eternity, Infinity, Oblivion, Death—don't meet the conditions to be infected."
In the end, once this universe turned into a zombie universe, those zombie superheroes would begin heading toward other universes.
Thinking about this, he couldn't help but sigh. Eternity, Infinity, Oblivion, Death—those guys really don't care about anything.
Unless the matter involves the destruction of the universe, they rarely appear. Even with something as serious as a zombie outbreak, none of them had shown up to stop it.
After finishing his thoughts, in order to prevent the zombie virus from spreading to the 616 main universe, Syd extended his right hand.
Crimson light from Chaos Magic shimmered, interwoven with the green glow of the Time Stone.
Next to him, Peter Parker—Spider-Man—was completely dumbfounded, having no idea what was happening.
Then, Peter felt like he was dreaming.
Everything around him began to rewind?
Buildings that had collapsed reassembled in reverse, and even the dead stood up, restored to life.
In Peter's stunned expression, in the blink of an eye, everything had returned to normal.
The streets bustled with life, people were laughing and talking as if nothing had ever happened.
Under the power of Chaos Magic and Time, it all seemed so natural, so logical.
Peter could hardly believe his eyes. He felt like he was hallucinating—how could something this surreal be real?
"Y-You... what did you just do?"
After a long pause, he turned stiffly to look at the glowing figure hovering mid-air, surrounded by radiant light.
Syd glanced at him and said casually, "I reversed time. Everything has returned to the beginning. You'd better go stop Dr. Hank Pym while you can."
"If the zombie virus breaks out again, I won't intervene."
As he spoke, his form shimmered and began to fade.
In Peter's eyes, streams of light flowed out from this incomprehensible being.
Then, with a blink, Syd disappeared—only a few scattered strands of light remained, gently glowing in the air.
"Holy crap..."
Peter Parker was completely dazed.
For a long while, a bold thought popped into his mind: "That guy... was he a god?"
Because aside from a god, he couldn't think of anyone who could reverse time like that.
Lost in a daze, Peter finally snapped out of it—he had to stop Hank Pym.
With no time to think more, he fired his webs and sped toward Dr. Hank Pym's house, simultaneously contacting Tony Stark and the others to report everything he'd just witnessed.
A while later, after hearing Peter's full explanation, Tony and the others were in utter shock.
"The zombie virus?"
"A god who reversed time?"
Was this for real?
Iron Man, Tony Stark, and the rest could hardly believe it.
Half skeptical, they went to Hank Pym's place, and after questioning him, they found out that Hank was indeed preparing to enter the Quantum Realm to rescue the Wasp, Janet.
Realizing this, Tony and the others were shaken.
They proceeded into the Quantum Realm and, just as Peter had warned, discovered that Janet had been infected with the zombie virus.
At Hank Pym's pleading, they didn't kill her, but instead detained her, hoping to research a cure for the virus.
Thus, the zombie crisis was temporarily averted.
It was only then that they truly believed Peter's words—and were profoundly shaken.
A god who could reverse time?
Unbelievable!
While they were still stunned, on the other side, in the 616 main universe, Syd had already reabsorbed the consciousness fragment he had sent out.
Sensing the faint connections forming with four different universes, he felt quite pleased. "With power from four universes now... within the single-universe tier, no one is my match."
At this point, only multiversal-level beings were still a threat to him.
With that in mind, Syd muttered, "I have to speed up the assimilation of the multiverse."
Only by truly becoming a multiversal-level being could he finally be at ease.
With that thought, he immediately began using Dreamwalking again and again.
In an instant, parts of his consciousness detached and flowed into unknown universes.
At that moment, he discovered a universe belonging to the X-Men—and it piqued his curiosity.
But just as his attention shifted slightly in that direction, a mysterious voice echoed in the minds of everyone on Earth.
"Our youngest brother... we need to speak with you."
The ethereal voice of Eternity reverberated across the planet.
Everyone was stunned.
Soon, people realized that Eternity and the others were talking to just one person—
The White-Clad Hero!
Curious, they wondered what the five cosmic beings wanted from him.
While the world speculated, Syd, standing alone in a deserted corner, thought for a moment and decided to meet them.
In the next second, his body rose into the sky, flying beyond Earth's atmosphere to converse with the cosmic entities.
At the same time, quietly, his power surged.
Five universes...
Six universes...
One after another, universes formed a connection with him, slowly assimilated into his being.
During this process, he spared some attention to the X-Men universe.
Just one glance, and he showed a surprised expression.
"The timeline's still early? Xavier and Magneto are still young?"
It seemed like the X-Men prequel era.
At this stage, there was only one individual worth noting—Sebastian Shaw, the Black King, a mutant with energy absorption abilities.
His ability to absorb energy made him nearly invincible. He could even absorb the energy of a nuclear reactor, making him a pseudo-Omega-level mutant.
"I used to compare my early-stage energy absorption—when it was only level 2—to his..."
Syd shook his head with a smile.
They both had energy absorption, but in the beginning, the difference between them was vast. Shaw was leagues ahead in power.
If not for his ability evolving recently...
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 602
chapters.content:
Chapter 602 - 602
Thinking about it, Syd grew curious. "I wonder—does my current energy absorption ability count as a pseudo-Omega-level, or is it already Omega-level? Between me and the Black King, who's stronger now?"
At the same time, he was also curious about the younger versions of Professor X and Magneto.
With that, he decided to go check things out—not just with his consciousness, but in person.
The next second, Syd activated a combination of spatial shift and portal magic.
A golden spatial gate appeared before him. As he stepped through it, his figure vanished instantly.
Beyond Earth.
Eternity and the others, who were patiently waiting for their youngest brother, fell silent as they stared at the strange move he had just pulled.
Wasn't he supposed to meet with them? Where did he vanish to all of a sudden?
Fortunately, streaks of divine light began to shimmer in front of them, and an indescribable abstract conceptual form slowly emerged, which eased their curiosity for the time being.
While controlling his abstract divine form in that realm, Syd's attention turned toward the X-Men prequel universe.
There, his godly body appeared high above Earth, in the cloud layer tens of thousands of meters up, observing below with curiosity.
But as he observed the Earth's surface, satellites quickly picked up his presence.
The American authorities were stunned by the sight of a glowing figure floating in the clouds, gazing down at them.
"Who is this guy?"
"Is he a mutant?"
Unease spread through them.
Soon, the incident was reported to the top brass of the United States and garnered immediate attention.
Above the clouds.
Syd had only been observing for a short while before three fighter jets were dispatched and came flying his way.
Without a word, the jets opened fire.
Multiple small missiles streaked through the sky, heading straight for him.
Hearing the commotion, Syd glanced at the incoming missiles. He was about to erase them outright—but then paused.
He suddenly remembered he hadn't tested his energy absorption ability in actual combat yet. Curiosity sparked.
So, he simply let them come.
Moments later, thunderous explosions rang out as his figure was engulfed in fire.
Inside the cockpits, the pilots radioed back excitedly:
"Target hit! Target down!"
But just as they made their reports, they all froze.
The explosions were rapidly shrinking in size.
Looking closely, they witnessed a terrifying sight—this white-clad figure extended his right hand, drawing all the explosive energy into it.
In just a few seconds, the energy of all the missiles was gone. The man remained untouched, completely unharmed.
"Monster..."
That was the only word that flashed through the pilots' minds, fear written all over their faces.
And it wasn't just them—the U.S. high command and military officers watching were equally dumbfounded.
"This mutant can fly—and absorb energy too?"
They felt fear rising—and a killing intent. They wanted this threat eliminated.
Immediately, they issued an order to the fighter pilots: eliminate him at all costs.
Though the pilots were afraid, they steeled themselves to obey.
But just as they made that decision, ready to die for their country, Syd glanced their way.
In the next instant, three golden beams of light descended from the sky, piercing the jets in an instant.
BOOM!
Explosions erupted.
The three fighter jets became nothing more than fireworks above the clouds. As for the pilots' dreams of "dying for their country," that was simply laughable.
Even if this hadn't been his abstract divine body, even with just his physical god body, those jets wouldn't have been able to scratch him—even if he just stood there doing nothing.
Ignoring the explosions behind him, Syd floated leisurely toward the Black King's location, planning to observe his energy absorption ability and see if there was anything worth studying.
"Maybe... the energy absorption X-gene in the Black King's body could help further perfect my own ability?"
Syd pondered this.
If so, the gains from this trip would be tremendous.
After all, energy absorption determined the upper limit of energy point accumulation—and if that could be improved, then the progress of unlocking Godhood would skyrocket!
Syd felt a wave of anticipation.
While admiring the scenery, he drifted slowly through American airspace. His carefree attitude and relaxed pace were like a taunt to the American upper echelon.
Arrogant!
A mutant who dared to ignore the authority of the United States?
Who did this guy think he was?
They were the number one country in the world—how dare a mutant act so blatantly?
Drifting slowly, as if sightseeing, without a trace of fear?
The higher-ups scoffed coldly, deciding to teach this mutant a harsh lesson.
In the next moment, nearby military bases sprang into action.
More fighter jets and missiles were launched toward the flying Syd.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Thunderous roars echoed across the sky.
Wherever Syd's gaze landed, golden beams shot out, vaporizing the incoming jets and missiles one by one.
Throughout the entire process, he remained untouched.
U.S. High Command.
A middle-aged white man sneered. "I don't believe he can use his mutant power forever. He'll burn out eventually!"
His words drew immediate agreement.
"He's just showing off."
"He thinks having mutant powers makes him untouchable?"
"That mutant is too full of himself. Let's see how long he lasts."
The U.S. officials sneered with disdain.
These days, who still believed having mutant powers made one invincible?
To defy the U.S.? Even the strongest mutants never dared pull such stunts.
They figured this guy had probably just awakened his powers and didn't know the rules yet.
As they watched with mocking grins, waiting to see him fall, the battle's chaos grew increasingly obvious to the world.
The noise was overwhelming—jets, missiles, explosions—hard to ignore.
Even ordinary citizens could hear the blasts.
Before long, American news networks began reporting on the event.
Countless civilians and mutants alike learned that a mutant was facing off against the U.S. military in open sky combat.
(End of Chapter)
