chapters.title: Chapter 603
chapters.content:
Chapter 603 - 603
With the news coverage of the event, countless ordinary Americans believed the mutant in question had gone insane—how could someone so arrogant think they could challenge the military?
Even the mutants watching the broadcast had the same thought.
Inside Professor X's mansion—
At this point in time, the young Magneto, Professor X, Beast, Mystique, and the others had not yet parted ways over ideology. They watched the news together, wearing expressions of helplessness.
They all thought the mutant in question was far too young—completely ignorant of the military's true power, and reckless for showing himself like that.
This was bad—really bad!
"Charles, can you locate that mutant kid?" the young Erik—Magneto—asked with a frown.
"I can try," Charles replied calmly.
With that, he led the group into the Cerebro room and activated the recently developed Cerebro device.
As the machine powered on, Mystique and the others watched curiously while Charles closed his eyes, beginning his search for the mutant currently under military attack.
He focused his mental scan on the skies.
It didn't take long before he sensed a few presences at high altitude.
However, much to his confusion, all of them were ordinary humans—there didn't seem to be any mutants among them?
"What's going on...?"
Unable to sense Syd, Charles wore a baffled expression.
Meanwhile, tens of thousands of meters high in the sky—
Syd was still casually playing around with fighter jets as he flew toward the Black King's location, planning to extract his X-gene.
At that moment, he felt a wave of psionic energy sweeping through the skies—a familiar kind of mind wave.
Syd recognized it instantly.
BOOM!
The air warped around him.
A vast wave of psionic power burst from his consciousness, coming into contact with Charles' scan.
In an instant, the mental field of Professor X—amplified by Cerebro and enough to qualify him as a level-five mutant—was completely overwhelmed and invaded.
In that brief connection, Syd saw everything Charles was seeing—and understood his goal.
With a knowing look, Syd gently withdrew his psionic presence.
Back in the mansion—
Mystique and the others watched in confusion as Charles' face suddenly turned pale. He opened his eyes in shock and gasped for breath.
"Huff... Huff..."
"What happened?" Erik asked, frowning.
Charles took a moment before speaking through labored breaths. "I found the mutant."
"That's great news, isn't it?" Hank asked, confused.
Magneto and Mystique both nodded.
But Charles gave a bitter smile.
If only it were that simple.
At first, when his scan failed to detect the mutant, he assumed there was a problem with Cerebro—or maybe the mutant wasn't in the area.
But just as he was shifting focus elsewhere, a terrifying wave of psychic energy exploded from the very area where he had detected nothing.
The force of it completely crushed him. Even with Cerebro's amplification, he was no match at all.
As he explained, Magneto and the others looked at each other in disbelief.
Charles had always been the most powerful psychic they knew. Was there really someone out there stronger than him?
How could that be possible?
Then Charles grew solemn. "That psychic energy... it definitely belonged to the one we were searching for."
"And it wasn't just the mind. I sensed something else in his body—some terrifying form of energy. I've never encountered a mutant like this before..."
He paused, then added gravely, "He might be an Omega-Level mutant."
His words left everyone stunned and wide-eyed.
Omega-Level?
Charles had never sensed a mutant this powerful before?
"Charles, don't you think that's a bit exaggerated?" Erik asked, still in disbelief.
Mystique and Beast nodded—they, too, thought Charles might be overreacting.
After some quick discussion, they decided they couldn't just sit back and watch. They had to try contacting or helping this mutant.
Meanwhile, the young mutants they had recently brought in had also heard about the incident—and were eager to join.
"Professor, is that mutant really that strong?"
"Professor Charles, aren't you exaggerating a little?"
Considering they had undergone training and gained some combat ability, Charles ultimately decided to bring them along.
Soon, they boarded the black X-Jet, heading straight for the battlefield.
While they moved out—
Syd had already reached the skies above a city.
From his divine observation, he could tell that the Black King, Sebastian Shaw, was inside a large mansion at the city center.
Without hesitation, he flew straight for it.
At the same time, several fighter jets had locked onto him and opened fire again.
Syd glanced at them casually.
BOOM BOOM BOOM...
Golden beams rained from the sky, obliterating six more jets in seconds. The surroundings fell quiet again.
After clearing out the pesky flies, Syd continued his slow flight toward the city center.
But while he had moved on, the American high command—who had been watching—were left seething.
Murmurs and complaints echoed.
"Damn mutant... why is he still standing?"
"This is ridiculous..."
Seeing him enter city airspace, they were filled with unwilling rage and resentment.
Now that he was above a civilian area, they could no longer launch missiles—and for the moment, they had no way of dealing with him.
That was when a white-haired senator suddenly brightened, chuckling coldly.
"He's flying into the city to take shelter. That means he's running out of power!"
"This bastard's about to burn out!"
His confident assertion made the other officials' eyes light up.
The more they thought about it, the more it made sense.
Confidence returned to them—and along with it, disdain.
So much for that earlier arrogance—now he was forced into retreat, hiding in a city to escape?
Hmph!
They sneered with satisfaction.
After a brief discussion, they decided to send ten more fighter jets.
As for missiles—they held off for now.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 604
chapters.content:
Chapter 604 - 604
After issuing their orders, the American high command began closely monitoring the white-clad mutant using satellites and surveillance footage from within the city, eager to see what he would do next.
Under their watch, the white-clad figure flew toward the center of the city and hovered over a luxurious villa—complete with a pool and other lavish amenities.
At the same time, the explosions from the earlier aerial combat had caught the attention of civilians below.
With the deafening noise echoing through the city, it was impossible not to notice.
Very quickly, the people realized—the mutant making headlines across every major news station had come to their city.
Panic and confusion rippled through the population.
Many looked up and saw the white figure floating above a villa.
"What is he doing here?"
Whispers filled the streets.
Just then, under everyone's watchful eyes, four people emerged from the lavish mansion.
Leading the group was a man in his forties, dressed in a sleek black suit—Sebastian Shaw, the Black King, a mutant with the power of energy absorption.
Next to him stood a woman dressed in all white, her wavy platinum hair cascading down—Emma Frost, the White Queen, with psychic abilities and a secondary mutation allowing her to transform her body into diamond.
The other two: one was red-skinned and devilish in appearance—Azazel, the Red Devil, known for his teleportation abilities. The last was a man in his thirties capable of manipulating storms—Riptide.
All of them lifted their heads to gaze at the white figure hovering above.
Emma, Azazel, and Riptide wore wary expressions, clearly on alert.
But Shaw?
He appeared utterly relaxed, smiling as he calmly observed the powerful mutant making waves across the nation.
From afar—
Civilians and American officials watching the feed furrowed their brows.
"More mutants?"
Azazel's inhuman appearance made it clear. There was no hiding what he was.
So what was the white mutant doing here?
While everyone speculated, Syd, hovering in the sky, also turned his attention toward Shaw and the others.
More precisely—his focus zeroed in on Sebastian Shaw.
"Level four, possibly pseudo-level five energy absorption... Let's see what secrets your body holds."
Without anyone noticing, a wave of psychic energy flowed from Syd and enveloped Shaw.
Simultaneously, detection spells from Kamar-Taj and Asgard formed in his mind.
Mystic runes flickered through Syd's eyes as he began probing Shaw's body.
Within seconds, the data of Shaw's X-gene unfolded in his mind.
He rapidly absorbed the information on Shaw's energy absorption ability.
Before long, he had parsed through much of it.
"This part can refine my own absorption... This one is useless..."
Quickly, Syd discarded the irrelevant data and retained the beneficial portions.
The more he analyzed, the more satisfied he became.
Sebastian Shaw's X-gene, despite its flaws, held some value.
Most importantly, by integrating this refined genetic data using his chaos magic and creative powers, Syd could enhance his own energy absorption ability.
This meant faster collection of energy points—and an accelerated progression toward mimicking the divine.
He could hardly wait to upgrade himself and push the pace of his divine unlocking process.
But—there were still loose ends to tie up.
Syd glanced at the circling fighter jets above the city, and at Shaw's group below.
Just as he was about to speak, Sebastian Shaw beat him to it.
With a smile, Shaw looked up and said, "So, you're the one bold enough to challenge the military?"
"Are you here for me? Ready to join my ranks?"
After a moment's thought, Shaw nodded and commented confidently, "You've got potential. If you become my subordinate, I'll help you deal with the military."
He then cast a dismissive glance at the fighter jets in the sky, his expression full of contempt.
Emma and the others beside him remained composed, clearly thinking the same.
Truthfully, with his pseudo-level five energy absorption ability, Shaw was nearly invincible.
Whether bullets, missiles, or heat shockwaves—he could absorb them all and redirect them.
If his ability were completely passive, he'd be nearly unkillable short of continuous nuclear bombardment.
Unfortunately, Shaw's power was subject to his own will—and therein lay his fatal flaw.
Without his helmet to block psychic interference, he could be mind-controlled, and that's exactly what happened in the future—controlled by Xavier, and then killed by Magneto with a coin through the head.
A shameful and anticlimactic death, one that never even let him use his power to fight back.
While Syd pondered this, a new sound came from the sky.
Everyone turned—and saw a black jet approaching at high speed.
The X-Jet.
Inside, Erik—Magneto—immediately saw Sebastian Shaw and a flash of hatred surged in his eyes.
It was Shaw who had caused his mother's death. Erik wanted nothing more than to grind him to dust.
Charles, noticing his change, quickly placed a hand on Erik's shoulder. "Stay calm, Erik!"
Charles knew full well how powerful Shaw was. Even together, he and Erik likely wouldn't stand a chance.
With Shaw wearing his helmet to block mental attacks, Charles' psychic powers were useless. And Erik alone? Not enough.
Erik gritted his teeth but nodded, holding back—for now.
Outside the villa—
Shaw gave the incoming X-Jet a cursory glance, unimpressed. His attention returned to the white-clad figure above.
"Well? Have you made your decision?" Shaw asked with a smile.
His tone was full of confidence.
In his mind, if the white-clad mutant wanted to survive, he'd have no reason to refuse his offer.
Emma and the others smiled as well—they were sure how this would go.
But just then, Syd looked down at them and said coolly:
"I refuse."
The moment the words fell, Shaw, Emma, and the others froze—staring up in disbelief, stunned by what they'd just heard.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 605
chapters.content:
Chapter 605 - 605
Sebastian Shaw had been absolutely confident that this white-clad mutant—who looked like he had nowhere else to go—would eagerly accept his offer. He wasn't alone; Emma Frost and the others shared the same expectation.
Who would've thought, just as he asked for a response, he'd get an answer no one expected?
Rejection.
The mutant actually refused?!
And not just that—his tone was so indifferent, so dismissive, as if none of them were even worthy of his attention.
Shaw, Emma, and the rest of the Hellfire Club stood there in disbelief.
Then, dressed in black, Riptide stepped forward. "You're way too arrogant. Don't think fighting the military for a while makes you invincible. Let me teach you a lesson."
A cold grin stretched across his face as he extended his hands, summoning his power.
Moments later, a massive ten-meter-wide tornado formed with a roar, swirling violently under his control. With a wave of his hand, it surged toward the floating white-clad mutant.
Emma smiled at the scene. "Riptide, make sure to teach this arrogant fool a lesson."
Azazel nodded in agreement.
Shaw's eyes gleamed with interest.
This white-clad mutant was strong, sure, but he was clearly too full of himself. Let's see how he handles Riptide's power. A little pain might humble him.
From afar, civilians and U.S. military officials saw this scene and brightened.
Let the dogs bite each other. Best case? They both end up wounded.
The U.S. officials watched with anticipation.
On the X-Jet—
Seeing the tornado, Beast—piloting the aircraft—quickly banked hard to avoid the blast radius.
Inside, Professor X, Magneto, and the others watched the whirlwind closely.
Could this mysterious mutant withstand that?
Charles' heart was tense. For some reason, he felt a strange familiarity with the white-clad boy—and didn't want anything bad to happen to him.
Under everyone's gaze, the storm closed in fast, while the mutant in white floated in place, unmoving.
What?
Even Riptide was confused when he saw the mutant make no attempt to dodge.
The tornado engulfed him completely.
This...
How could someone just stand there and take it? Even if he were weak, he should've at least tried to avoid it!
Shaw frowned, disappointed.
Riptide, on the other hand, smiled triumphantly.
No matter how strong someone was, getting hit by one of his storms was going to hurt. That guy would definitely come out bleeding.
Back on the X-Jet, Charles, Erik, Hank, and the younger mutants' faces shifted dramatically.
Charles immediately placed two fingers to his temple, preparing to psionically control Riptide to prevent him from using his powers again.
Magneto raised a hand as well, ready to manipulate nearby metals to block the storm.
He didn't know why, but he liked this white-clad mutant—he didn't want to see him die like this.
Meanwhile, the U.S. officials weren't buying into the hype.
They had little hope the tornado would do much.
Sure enough, the next moment, everyone watched as the storm began to shrink—from the inside out.
"What's happening?"
Riptide was stunned. He didn't understand what was going on.
Emma and the others were just as confused.
As the tornado thinned and dissipated, they finally saw the figure at its core: the white-clad mutant, completely unharmed.
With each rotation of the storm, it shrank further—as if the wind itself was being devoured by him.
What the hell was going on?
Their eyes widened in disbelief.
Then they saw him raise his right hand.
Syd calmly absorbed the kinetic energy of the storm. Then, he looked straight at Riptide—and pointed his hand at him.
In the blink of an eye, he released all that energy, using terrifying control to compress and launch it like a cannon blast.
BOOM!
A thunderous sonic boom cracked the air.
The condensed energy rocketed through the remnants of the storm and slammed into Riptide before he could react.
BAM!
He was sent flying, smashing hard into the villa's outer wall. Bones cracked loudly as he collapsed to the ground, bloodied and unconscious—like a broken doll, no trace of his former arrogance left.
Emma shuddered, instinctively transforming into diamond form. She stared in shock.
"What kind of power is that?!"
In just a heartbeat, Riptide had been destroyed?
Azazel's face darkened. He became visibly tense, prepared to teleport away at the first sign of danger.
On the X-Jet, Charles and the others watched in awe.
The U.S. military officials, meanwhile, just nodded, their faces calm.
They'd expected this.
While emotions swirled through the crowd, Shaw's expression suddenly changed.
He had sensed something.
His face darkened. "You... absorbed kinetic energy?"
"That's your mutant power?"
"How many abilities do you have?!"
The words hung in the air.
Emma and the others looked startled. They knew exactly what Shaw's ability was: energy absorption. It was what made him so formidable.
But now Shaw claimed this white-clad mutant had the same ability?
They couldn't believe it.
Back on the X-Jet, Beast had deployed a surveillance drone to listen in—and picked up Shaw's words.
"A mutant with the same power as Shaw?"
"This mysterious kid... has that ability too?"
Charles and the others were stunned.
Back on the ground—
Syd calmly responded to Shaw's question.
"You're talking about mutant abilities?"
"I have many. Which one are you asking about?"
Silence fell.
Shaw and his group stared in disbelief. Then, they couldn't help but laugh.
What kind of nonsense was this mutant spouting?
Even Charles and the X-Men didn't fully believe it. They assumed he was just joking.
But then—
"Many abilities?" Shaw repeated, shaking his head, eyes now cold.
"Young man, let me tell you—there's a gap between mutants and mutants."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 606
chapters.content:
Chapter 606 - 606
"Even if you do have energy absorption, that doesn't mean you can defeat me."
"If you surrender now and become one of my subordinates, I can spare your life."
"Young man, my ability is not something you can compare to."
Sebastian Shaw's calm voice echoed throughout the area.
Emma Frost and the others, hearing this, began to relax again.
Aboard the X-Jet—
Magneto's expression grew darker. No one understood the strength of Sebastian Shaw's power better than he did.
What Shaw said wasn't wrong—two people may have the same power on the surface, but that didn't mean they were equal. Shaw's energy absorption was absolutely among the most powerful.
Syd, hearing Shaw's words, replied with a calm tone: "Is that so?"
As Shaw prepared to make a move, Syd casually raised his right hand.
In an instant, a deep crimson glow of Chaos Magic erupted.
Before Emma and the others could even react, whoosh—Sebastian Shaw was blasted away by the energy.
BOOM!
The villa's wall was shattered as Shaw was flung through it, crashing into the ground on the other side.
Dust filled the air.
Emma and Azazel stared in disbelief.
Sebastian Shaw was sent flying in an instant?
From the ground, Shaw slowly got up, wiping off dust and asking in shock, "What kind of power is this?"
"Telekinesis? You have that ability too?"
The disbelief on his face deepened.
How could one person have so many mutant powers?
But a moment later, both Shaw and his allies eased up again.
Patting the dust from his clothes, Shaw stood there completely unscathed and shook his head. "Don't waste your strength. Whether it's telekinesis or any other power, you can't hurt me."
Syd tilted his head. "Really?"
The next moment, something happened that left not only Shaw but also Magneto and everyone else completely stunned.
A crimson glow radiated from the mysterious white-clad mutant—then in the blink of an eye...
Sebastian Shaw's black suit turned into a clown outfit.
Even his face changed—a big red nose appeared, and the helmet that protected him from psychic intrusion twisted into a colorful explosion wig.
In an instant, he looked utterly ridiculous.
Emma, Azazel, and the others were frozen in place, staring blankly at Shaw's clown appearance.
On the X-Jet—
Magneto and the others were speechless.
The American officials monitoring the scene stood up abruptly, stunned.
Shaw instinctively reached for his head and felt only a puff of fluffy clown hair. His hand moved to his nose and then to the ridiculous outfit he now wore.
His calm demeanor vanished. His face was full of disbelief.
How did this happen in the blink of an eye?
Shaw raised his head and glared furiously at the white-clad mutant hovering above. "What did you do to me?!"
Everyone's eyes were now locked on the figure floating in the sky.
Syd looked around casually, clearly dissatisfied with the environment.
Suddenly, a sweep of deep crimson light surged across the ground—
And an entire amusement park appeared out of nowhere: merry-go-rounds, roller coasters, pirate ships...
Even the grand villa behind Emma and the others turned into a Ferris wheel.
Their clothes? Clown suits.
The once-elegant Emma Frost now looked like a complete joke.
She stared at herself in disbelief.
Not just her—the entire crew aboard the X-Jet watched in stunned silence.
Then—
A voice, mysterious and resonating with the weight of cosmic truth, echoed in everyone's ears.
No, not just theirs.
The entire population of Earth heard it.
"Oh, I forgot to mention... I also have the ability to rewrite reality. If I want to, I can change anything—or anyone—into whatever I wish."
On Earth, billions of people froze in place, their eyes wide with shock as the words rang in their minds.
At the scene—
Shaw, Magneto, Charles, and the others stood frozen, their expressions blank.
"Reality manipulation?"
"What kind of power is that?"
"How could something like that even exist?"
Professor X shouted in disbelief.
Magneto and the rest were visibly shaken.
Meanwhile, the clownified Shaw stood still for a moment, then cried out, "That's impossible!"
"Is it?" Syd tilted his head again.
The next moment, a far more terrifying scene unfolded—
A torrent of crimson light flooded the sky and earth.
In the horrified eyes of the American command and those watching:
The entire United States—no, all of North America—was swept in a wave of red.
People in every country across the continent stared, stupefied.
Clouds in the sky turned into colorful cotton candy, forming into animals—elephants, lions, tigers...
As far as the eye could see, everything was transformed.
The ground turned into a cartoonish amusement park.
Buildings became rides. People's clothes morphed into clown costumes—everything looked absurd.
Even bridges, vehicles—everything had become animated, cartoon-like jokes.
What they saw was only the beginning. U.S. officials saw even more through satellite feeds.
All of North America had become a circus.
The entire world seemed to fall silent, stunned at what had just happened.
At the scene—
A man in a black suit, looking like a government agent, had been covertly observing the area.
Suddenly receiving an urgent message, he turned pale and exclaimed:
"You turned all of North America into this?!"
"How did you do it?!"
"Do you even realize what you've done?!"
At that moment, whether it was Shaw, Professor X, or anyone else—their faces were blank with shock.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 607
chapters.content:
Chapter 607 - 607
All of North America... turned into that?
Sebastian Shaw, Professor X, and the others were left completely dumbfounded.
Before the white-clad figure spoke, they hadn't really thought about it. They assumed the changes were limited to a small area.
But then, he said it casually—all of North America had been transformed?
That was an entire continent.
With multiple countries and massive landmass.
How is that even possible?!
Emma Frost stared in disbelief. "You're not joking, right? All of North America? Changed like that?"
"How could there be a mutant this powerful?!"
All eyes shifted to the agent who had broken the news.
Under their gaze, Agent Dean stared up at the glowing figure floating in the sky, his face grim and serious.
"It's true. I just received confirmation moments ago!"
"Senators and other officials saw the change with their own eyes via satellite surveillance. There's no mistaking it!"
His heavy words dropped like bombs, plunging the entire scene into silence again. One by one, everyone turned their eyes back to the white figure in the sky.
This kind of mutant ability actually exists?
How could that be possible?!
While everyone reeled in disbelief, Agent Dean forced down his fear and questioned, "Do you even know what you've done? North America is paralyzed! Every nation has suffered catastrophic losses!"
"How could you do this?! How is something like this even possible?!"
Faced with his interrogation and the others' horrified expressions, Syd remained calm and indifferent.
Before anyone could react further, his divine body suddenly dissolved into countless strands of glowing light, vanishing on the spot.
Everyone was stunned.
Then—
A blinding surge of white light burst forth!
It engulfed the entire United States... then spread outward to envelop the entire Earth... and then the entire solar system.
"What's that light?"
"Ahhh—!"
Countless people felt the overwhelming brilliance erase everything in their view, unable to comprehend what was happening.
But soon, they noticed the white light was converging—spiraling outward into space.
Sebastian Shaw, Emma Frost, Azazel, Professor X, and billions of people across Earth all looked up in dazed wonder.
And then... they saw it.
Bathed in a hazy, divine radiance, they beheld a colossal figure, so immense it dwarfed the Earth itself.
In reverent whispers of praise and awe echoing across the stars, they watched as this indescribable, glowing form gently cupped the Earth in two vast hands—like one might hold a basketball.
Thanks to Syd's power, everyone saw it clearly.
And then, a cosmic voice, mysterious and vast like the laws of the universe itself, rang out through the solar system:
"It's just North America. If I want... even the entire Earth can become what I desire—a toy in my hands."
The sacred tone of the voice echoed.
Hearing it, Shaw, Emma, Azazel, Charles—all were utterly paralyzed, faces blank.
Agent Dean stared skyward, his lips trembling as he muttered:
"This... this has to be fake... this can't be real..."
The reality shattered his mind.
Turning the Earth into a toy?
What kind of mutant could do that?
"How can a mutant be this powerful...?"
His sapphire eyes had lost their focus.
And it wasn't just him.
Aboard the X-Jet—
Magneto sat frozen in his seat.
He muttered in disbelief, "Charles... this is the mutant you said had a powerful presence?"
Then, after a pause, his voice cracked with disbelief.
"This isn't just powerful... this is too much!"
The young mutants behind them echoed in confusion:
"Professor, this is the powerful mutant you mentioned?"
"Professor Charles, did you underestimate just a little?"
They all stared at the divine being in the sky and questioned everything they had ever known.
Charles himself was no exception—his eyes filled with utter disbelief.
He had never imagined a mutant could be this powerful.
At the scene—
Emma, who had just questioned everything a moment ago, stood frozen.
Turning all of North America into a cartoon theme park had already shattered her understanding of reality.
But now—
Watching Earth being held like a toy in massive divine hands—
She began to wonder if she was dreaming.
"This... this can't be real..." she murmured.
Azazel was similarly stunned.
And Shaw—who had prided himself on his power and calm demeanor—could no longer maintain his composure.
His face betrayed true fear.
He didn't want to believe it either.
But the truth was undeniable. It stood before him.
He began recalling the things he had said earlier—
"There's a gap between mutants..."
But that gap?
Was nothing like what he had imagined.
How could the gap be this enormous?!
His heart filled with bitterness, jealousy, disbelief.
But none were more terrified than the high-ranking U.S. officials.
Thanks to Syd's power—and satellite footage—they had seen everything.
They saw the glowing, divine form.
They saw it hold the Earth like a toy.
Their expressions twisted with confusion, terror, dread, and—regret.
They suddenly remembered all those missiles they had launched earlier...
Why had this being not retaliated?
Why had he just floated toward the city?
Because he was exhausted?
No.
It was painfully clear now.
He was never tired. His power was never depleted.
He was just toying with them.
The white-haired senator who first suggested Syd was weakening—Senator Dagger—began to tremble.
The rest of the officials weren't much better—shaken and full of terrified hope.
"He's so powerful... maybe he won't notice us, right?"
"We're probably fine... right?"
They could only pray.
Across the globe, billions of humans stared at the sky in stunned silence.
"My god..."
"God...?"
Murmurs of fear and awe echoed worldwide.
As emotions surged, Syd calmly looked down at Earth, eyes coldly focused on Sebastian Shaw.
This was the first time he had taken on such a massive form.
Oddly enough, it wasn't uncomfortable.
For beings like Galactus who possess physical form, size has meaning.
But for abstract conceptual beings—like the Creator Gods—they are, in truth, part of the universe itself.
To Eternity and Infinity, all life exists within them.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 608
chapters.content:
Chapter 608 - 608
After his thoughts settled, Syd's focus returned to the stunned Sebastian Shaw.
Then came a voice—mysterious, echoing like the truth of the universe itself. It resounded across the entire Earth:
"Sebastian Shaw, didn't you say nothing can harm you? Then let me test that."
As the shocked Professor X and the wide-eyed Shaw looked up, a pale golden beam shot down from the clouds, linking heaven and earth—locking directly onto Shaw.
Scorching, terrifying energy waves rippled outward!
Emma Frost, in her diamond form, scrambled to flee in panic. Azazel vanished instantly with a teleport.
BOOM!
The heat was so intense, even the water in a nearby swimming pool began to steam.
Within the golden beam, Shaw grunted in pain, body trembling under the assault of solar energy.
At first, he managed to absorb the heat and smiled grimly. But very soon—his expression twisted. He staggered and tried to escape.
But no matter where he ran, the beam followed, leaving a blackened, flaming trail behind.
"Ahhhh—!"
He screamed in agony.
Watching from a distance, Emma, Azazel, and Professor X all showed signs of disbelief.
"What's going on?"
This was the first time Emma had ever seen Shaw look like this.
No matter what he had faced in the past, Shaw always appeared calm and untouched. He never wore expressions of pain—until now.
They were confused. But Syd wasn't surprised.
After all, while Shaw's mutant power allowed him to absorb and redirect all forms of energy—there was a limit. Once he exceeded his internal energy storage cap, it would start to damage him.
At that moment, under everyone's gaze, Shaw realized something was terribly wrong.
He used the solar energy he had absorbed to enhance his body, boosting his speed and narrowly escaping the beam temporarily.
Then, he thrust out both arms and unleashed all the energy inside him.
A blinding golden flash erupted from his hands.
BOOM!
The descending golden beam froze momentarily as Shaw's solar-powered energy clashed against it.
Shaw finally smiled.
In the distance, Emma Frost and Azazel smiled too.
That was the Black King they knew—unshakable.
Aboard the X-Jet—
Magneto's face darkened again. He muttered, "Even a mutant this terrifying can't deal with Shaw?"
Charles' expression also turned grave.
If that were true—this was bad. Very bad.
But far above Earth, Syd remained calm.
That beam?
It was just a speck of solar energy he had drawn from the sun. Compared to what he used against Death, it was barely a grain of dust.
And then, the voice of the cosmic truth returned, echoing across the globe:
"Not bad. But let's increase the energy now."
What?!
Everyone—Shaw, Emma, the X-Men—froze in alarm.
BOOM!!
The golden beam intensified in an instant—richer, heavier, more divine.
The solar energy Shaw had released was instantly blown away, and the ground beneath his feet turned to molten lava.
"No—!"
"Stop—!"
Shaw shouted—but before the words even left his lips, he was consumed by the golden light.
The energy surged—brighter, holier than before.
Even without anyone knowing, Syd had just laced the beam with a trace of conceptual divine power—power from a Creator-level abstract god.
The pain was unbearable.
Shaw's face twisted in terror, disbelief, and agony.
"Aaaaah—!"
In the next instant, his body was completely swallowed by the beam—gone.
The golden light faded slowly...
And what remained in Emma's and Charles' eyes was a deep crimson crater.
Shaw—was nowhere to be seen.
He was just... gone.
Emma and the others stood frozen.
"He's... really dead?" Emma whispered, trembling.
But she knew—
This wasn't because Shaw was weak.
It was because that being in space was too terrifying.
And more importantly—this was barely even a fraction of his true power.
She looked up at that massive, divine figure—larger than the Earth itself.
There was no way this was all he could do.
In fact, she suspected...
If he wanted, he could destroy the planet with ease.
The possibility? Nearly 100%.
Anyone with basic common sense could see that—just from his size alone.
Inside the X-Jet—
Magneto sat in stunned silence.
Shaw... was really dead?
Part of him felt the satisfaction of revenge.
But another part—was lost, uncertain.
Behind him, the younger mutants murmured in awe.
"That power is insane... we're all mutants, but how is the gap this big?"
"I'd be happy just having one-tenth of his power."
"No, one percent would be enough!"
While they marveled, Syd's attention shifted to the American high command.
He had been bombarded with missiles earlier. He hadn't retaliated at the time—
But that didn't mean he had forgotten.
A pulse of psychic energy swept the Earth.
Every human who had shown hostility toward him—stood revealed.
And under the scorching sunlight—they began to scream.
"No... no—what's happening?!"
They had been noticed.
They screamed in pain, in fear, in disbelief.
And under the burning solar light—and the screams of those around them—
They all turned to ash.
Outside Earth—
After cleansing the high command, Syd turned his gaze back to Charles, the X-Men, and...
His next objective: the energy absorption ability.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 609
chapters.content:
Chapter 609 - 609
Syd's objective in coming to this X-Men prequel universe was essentially fulfilled.
But since he had already run into this universe's Professor X and others, he figured—might as well leave them something useful, so they wouldn't be killed by some new American government scheme in the future.
Raising his right hand, a shimmering, platinum-white, wriggling liquid appeared—clearly a spawn of Venom.
The next moment, he casually flicked it toward Professor X and his group, then stopped paying attention.
Even though it was a spawn restricted by the original Venom, it still had a basic intelligence. The moment it touched Charles, Wolverine, Magneto, and the others, it would automatically bond with them.
With a Venom spawn on their side, they'd no longer die so easily. Even if Sentinels showed up—they'd survive.
And under Syd's current power, even this spawn's strength had grown far beyond what most could imagine.
Having done that, Syd ignored the stunned expressions of the X-Men and directly dispersed his abstract conceptual form.
On Earth, somewhere remote in the United States—
Streaks of divine light coalesced as Syd's physical body reappeared.
"Let's see how much the energy absorption ability can improve."
There was a flicker of curiosity in his eyes.
With the complete X-gene blueprint of Sebastian Shaw in hand, his own energy absorption ability was about to get a major upgrade.
His energy point absorption speed, and more importantly, the progress of mimicking God, would both be boosted.
[Light Energy +103]
[Light Energy +103]
...
(God Progress: 11%)
As the system's voice chimed in with the light energy gains, Syd's eyes shone with anticipation. He extended his right hand.
The next moment, Creation Power activated.
A transparent glass test tube rapidly formed from bottom to top.
Now came the key part: crafting a gene-enhancing serum to optimize his energy absorption X-gene.
Syd recalled every detail of Sebastian Shaw's energy absorption ability.
Following his thoughts, a clear liquid formed inside the vial—designed to perfectly suit his own body's structure.
Terrifying energy radiated from the serum, warping the surrounding air with its pressure.
Syd stared at the vial with intense anticipation.
Compared to the last version crafted with Chaos Magic, this one—made with his full Creation Power—was flawless.
A serum tailor-made for him.
One that would maximize his energy absorption capacity.
He raised the vial and drank it down.
Litchi flavor.
Naturally—he'd set the flavor himself. No way he was leaving that to random chance.
As the clear fluid hit his stomach, it transformed into a warm current, rushing through his limbs and bones.
Syd could clearly feel his X-gene mutating—refining under the serum's effect.
And he didn't stop there.
One vial... three vials...
He continued producing and consuming more—until his body no longer reacted. At that point, drinking the serum felt no different than drinking water.
Finally, he stopped.
And then—
He felt it.
Massive changes.
His energy absorption capacity had multiplied—at least dozens of times over!
Even more surprising—
His ability could now absorb psychic energy, and convert absorbed energy into permanent cellular enhancements.
His eyes lit up with shock and excitement.
This meant—
The energy absorption ability was now truly perfected.
"If Shaw had this version of the ability, he would've been nearly invincible among mutants."
"At the very least, no normal person could kill him."
"Even Jean's Phoenix Force—he might've been able to absorb a fragment."
Of course, only fragments. A complete Phoenix Force would be something else entirely.
After all, the Phoenix Force was said to be the embodiment of life and psychic power from the origin of the universe.
It represented the spiritual connection to all existence in the multiverse—past, present, and future. It was the source and creator of all psychic energy, the vessel and ruler of all emotional and life-based power.
That said, a complete Phoenix Force had never once appeared—only fragments had ever been seen.
Even so, Syd now felt confident.
Maybe he couldn't go toe-to-toe with the Phoenix Force itself, but his energy absorption ability was no longer weak.
Previously, he wasn't even sure if his ability was truly level 4 or 5.
But now?
There was no doubt—his energy absorption ability had reached full Omega-level Tier 5.
More than that—because the absorbed energy could now permanently enhance his body, this power had effectively no ceiling.
Done with his thoughts, Syd closed his eyes and focused on absorbing energy.
High-frequency light rays surged into his body.
His mimic ability triggered—rapidly transforming absorbed energy into energy points.
[Light Energy +5157]
[Light Energy +5157]
Just like that—his efficiency had multiplied nearly fifty times.
He did a quick mental calculation—then his eyes lit up:
"If before I could accumulate 2% of God Mimic progress in a day, now... I can max it out in one day!"
Even Syd himself had to take a sharp breath at that realization.
Omega-level abilities were on a whole different scale.
Feeling satisfied, Syd looked around at the world of the X-Men prequel universe and prepared to leave.
But then—he paused.
"Wait... that black stone artifact that predicts death... I haven't used that in a while, have I?"
Ever since solving the last crisis with it, he'd completely forgotten.
That was careless.
"Still not cautious enough. What if something had happened and I wasn't even ready?"
With a serious look, Syd summoned the black stone artifact from his dimensional ring.
Holding it in his hand, he began channeling light energy into it.
Soon, the black stone began to radiate a dense black light, and strange, familiar energy began to ripple outward.
But then—
Something unexpected happened.
He didn't feel the usual pulling sensation.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 610
chapters.content:
Chapter 610 - 610
Or rather—it wasn't that the pull wasn't there. It was that the pulling force was now too weak to draw in his consciousness.
Syd frowned.
He immediately understood why.
His strength had grown too much—making the black stone artifact ineffective.
The thought filled him with frustration.
This black stone artifact had always been extremely useful. If it could no longer function...
But the next moment, an idea sparked in his mind.
He extended his will—and invoked his Creation power.
A mysterious energy surged forth and wrapped around the black stone, rapidly enhancing it.
A terrifying wave of energy spread outward, while eerie black light began to flicker from the stone.
After several seconds, the process ended.
Syd examined the now-altered black stone artifact. Then, he channeled his divine power into it again.
The familiar tug returned.
"It worked."
Without resisting, he let himself be pulled in.
In a flash of light, the world spun—and Syd found himself within a new, unfamiliar scene.
What he saw immediately triggered a sense of unease.
Outside a pitch-black universe, a figure emerged—an unfathomable being, shrouded in thick black mist.
It was massive, with most of its form hidden. But even the small portion exposed dwarfed the universe nearby—making it look like a mere marble.
A single tentacle of this entity coiled around the "marble"—a broken and collapsing universe.
Syd recognized them instantly:
Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and Galactus.
They were there—but they were being destroyed. The universe itself was collapsing.
"Insolent insect... this is the end that awaits you."
"To become my puppet is your only fate."
A twisted, mocking voice echoed in all directions.
One of the monstrous tentacles pierced a glowing cosmic figure in the chest. The light surrounding that being began to dim, as though it were the twilight of the gods.
Even an abstract conceptual body was succumbing to terrifying mutation.
Syd felt it—that was himself, in that future. And his consciousness was being erased.
Before he could process more—
The vision froze.
And in a blink—he returned to reality.
"That's it?"
Syd muttered.
It had ended so quickly. The entire death scene lasted only a few seconds—far shorter than any prediction he'd seen before.
"Was it because that being was too powerful, and the artifact couldn't handle it?"
That was the only explanation he could think of.
Even with the artifact enhanced by Creation power, it had only been able to glimpse a few seconds?
Or... perhaps the problem wasn't the artifact—but his own level of power.
He hadn't unlocked enough of God's power to fully use Creation.
After all, Creation was a divine ability granted by God. He had only mimicked 11% of God's total capability.
Without unlocking more, he couldn't bring out the full potential of the artifact.
That realization left his mood heavy.
And yet—there was no mistaking it:
The entity from the black mist and tentacles... was an Outer God. The original.
"So that's the true body of the Old One...?"
"What level is that thing—Multiversal?"
Its body was massive beyond measure. It hadn't even been scratched—yet it casually annihilated the universe, even turned conceptual gods like Eternity and Infinity into puppets.
A wave of dread filled him.
"To think... the first enemy to arrive is the true body of an Outer God. And its power..."
"What am I supposed to do against that?"
He had no answer.
Against an existence at that level, no amount of struggle would matter.
It seemed like he was doomed to die—to be turned into a puppet.
Then—his eyes shifted.
"Wait..."
His gaze landed on the God Mimic progress bar.
That was the only way forward.
Only by unlocking more of God's power could he hope to overcome this looming catastrophe.
It was his only hope.
He remembered: the black stone artifact could only predict death based on his current strength.
It couldn't foresee what would happen after more of God's power was unlocked.
So as long as he increased his God Mimic progress—the future could still change.
That thought gave him a small sense of relief.
"There's still a chance."
He shook his head, no longer thinking about it.
With a wave of his hand, he activated Space Shift and Portal Magic.
A swirling yellow gate opened before him—its other side revealed a familiar scene: the black void of outer space, just beyond Earth.
Syd's figure glided forward and stepped through.
The next moment, he returned to the 616 main universe, floating above Earth.
Immediately, his attention was drawn to a nearby gathering.
Six indescribable figures stood in space, radiating abstract divinity.
They were:
Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, Galactus... and his own abstract conceptual form.
As Syd arrived, the cosmic entities turned their attention to him—eyes flashing with surprise.
A moment later, they turned their gaze back toward his radiant form hovering nearby.
Infinity tilted her head.
"That's your material body?"
She looked curious, then added:
"Wait... I'm sensing the rules of another universe on you..."
The others—Eternity, Death, Oblivion—also noticed it.
But before they could fully analyze it, the yellow portal behind Syd closed.
Their attention shifted back to him.
Earlier, they had descended to Earth and requested a meeting with their youngest brother.
But shortly after, Syd's material form entered a portal and vanished, and his abstract body appeared in its place.
He had only said, "wait"—and then vanished.
So they had waited—silently.
And now, finally, his material form had returned.
"He really went to another universe during that time?"
They were all astonished.
Nearby, Syd said nothing at first.
His material body glowed, then merged into his conceptual body, becoming one.
Then, at last, he turned to face the five beings before him.
He looked at their indescribable forms, shimmering in the void.
"This is the first time we've met... in the 616 main universe."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 611
chapters.content:
Chapter 611 - 611
[200PS!]
At the moment when Syd and the Five Eternals were facing off, countless people on Earth were feeling nervous and fearful.
It wasn't just that the six beings in their Creator God forms looked bizarre and terrifying—their sheer size, each larger than Earth itself, was enough to inspire deep dread.
Everyone feared that if even one of these six Creator Gods accidentally brushed against Earth, they would all be caught up in the ensuing disaster.
At this moment—
Syd's physical body had fully merged into his abstract conceptual form. Facing the Five Eternals before him, his voice, mysterious and echoing like the truths of the universe, resonated:
"What do you want from me?"
As soon as he spoke, the Five Eternals exchanged glances. Infinity, the one representing Space, stepped forward and spoke:
"Not long ago, we sensed an anomaly in the universe. It seems related to you..."
They wanted to ask what was going on. Why would the universe suddenly face a problem like this?
Hearing Infinity's words, Syd wasn't surprised at all. Under their watchful gazes, he calmly replied:
"Because of me, our universe has been attracted to another one. You don't need to worry about it—I'll handle the matter."
Syd truly didn't see this as a major concern. Ever since gaining the power of multiple universes, he had absolute confidence in dealing with cosmic collisions.
Moreover, the universes being attracted were linked to him—resolving it would be even easier.
Upon hearing the youngest brother's casual statement, the Five Eternals were stunned.
The universe was being attracted elsewhere?
And he could resolve it?
They were filled with doubt and astonishment.
However, since he said it so plainly, they could only reluctantly believe him.
At that moment, the weakest among the Five, Galactus, couldn't suppress his curiosity and asked:
"Would you let me witness your strength and abilities?"
As he spoke, an expectant look appeared in his eyes.
After all, without testing each other's strength, no one would know who was truly stronger.
And as the weakest among the Five, he had long wished to shake off that humiliating title.
The other four also shared the same thought—curious about their youngest brother's true strength and whether he truly deserved to be called a Creator God.
If he turned out to be too weak, even if they wouldn't act against him, they would hardly regard him with much importance.
Seeing their expressions, Syd raised his eyebrow, immediately understanding their intentions.
"So they want to test my strength... maybe even give me a little 'lesson' to help me recognize my place?"
Syd contemplated silently.
In the next second, he turned his senses inward to evaluate his current strength.
During this period, although his material body had traveled to other universes, his abstract conceptual form had not been idle. Using his Dreamwalking technique, he had traversed many universes, becoming their Creator God.
Through his senses, he immediately connected to seventy-one universes, including the X-Men prequel universe—each linked faintly to him, a clear indication that they had become part of him.
Syd could clearly feel that, after becoming the Creator God of seventy-one universes, his upper limit of power had skyrocketed to a terrifying level.
And that was without actively channeling and merging the power of those universes into himself.
If he did summon and combine all that power... even he wasn't sure how strong he would become.
"Could I easily destroy a universe?" Syd pondered with a bit of hesitation.
Even though the vast distances between universes would weaken the transmitted power, it would still be far beyond the limits of a single universe's standards.
Probably somewhere between the power of a single universe and that of a multiverse—maybe what could be called a "super-large universe-level" power.
Of course, even without actively summoning dozens of universes' powers, Syd estimated that his normal state was already strong enough to easily destroy the main 616 Universe.
Having thought through this, he turned his gaze toward the Five Eternals.
As the two sides prepared for battle with growing anticipation, countless people on Earth were thrown into shock and panic.
Since neither Infinity nor Galactus had made any effort to hide their conversation, all of Earth now knew:
—they intended to fight.
The first reaction among people was fear.
One after another, voices of panic and speculation rose up:
"We're doomed! If these Creator Gods start fighting, won't Earth be destroyed?!"
"Be a little more confident. Remove the word 'won't'—not just Earth, the entire Solar System could vanish!"
"Damn it! I just finished paying off my mortgage—I don't want to die yet!"
Besides the widespread panic and fear, governments across the world also began heated discussions about who would come out on top.
Inside S.H.I.E.L.D., Nick Fury frowned deeply, falling into serious thought.
The White-Robed Hero... probably wasn't a match for the Five Eternals.
Although the White-Robed Hero had always displayed terrifying might on Earth, facing the Five Eternals was an entirely different matter.
Recently, Fury had asked Carol about the Creator Gods and also obtained information from one of Thanos' former followers.
He now had a clear understanding of the situation: the Five Eternals had been born alongside the universe itself—they
were
the universe's gods.
Meanwhile, the White-Robed Hero's emergence as a Creator God was a recent event.
Given these facts, it wasn't hard to guess who would be stronger.
A newly born Creator God against five ancient ones? It was obvious.
And it wasn't just him thinking this—inside the Stark Tower, Iron Man Tony Stark and the rest of the Avengers were coming to similar conclusions.
Across the dimensions, countless eyes turned toward the Solar System.
Mephisto, Lucifer, Dormammu—those hiding in the shadows—all focused intently.
To be honest, some of them had never even seen all Five Eternals together before.
After all, aside from Galactus, the other four almost never manifested unless a universe faced true annihilation.
Thus, seeing the Five gathered here—along with the mysterious White-Robed Hero—was an event too big to ignore.
Hearing the Eternals' conversation, some dimensional demon gods began muttering darkly to themselves:
"The White-Robed Hero's defeat is certain!"
"Is that even a question?"
"Maybe he could beat Galactus, but the other four? Forget it."
Those who had witnessed the Eternals' true power couldn't help but feel a chill in their hearts.
Meanwhile, Dormammu and the others, who had longstanding grudges against Syd, were gloating in secret.
Hopefully, the White-Robed Hero would finally be taught a proper lesson, so he would understand true strength.
While they were thinking these malicious thoughts—
Facing the Five Eternals, Syd nodded calmly and agreed to their challenge.
Without wasting any more words, he began drawing upon the power and laws within his being.
In the next second, an overwhelming aura burst from his form—a boundless sea of light surged forth, engulfing the Five Eternals standing before him.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 612
chapters.content:
Chapter 612 - 612
The originally dark universe grew even darker, with even the stars ceasing to shine.
Light and heat were instantly drawn away.
While attacking, Syd also spared a thought to protect Earth and the Solar System.
Boom!
Infinity and the other four had just been smiling, about to say something, when their expressions abruptly changed at the sight before them.
Good heavens—he had gone all out from the very start!
"Daring to strike at all five of us at once, isn't our youngest brother being a bit too arrogant and reckless?"
"Exactly. He's insane!"
The good impression they had just formed of him instantly plummeted, replaced by a sense that he was being wildly overconfident and looking down on them.
Who were they?
The original Creator Gods of the universe!
This youngest brother, who had only recently been born, actually dared think he could handle all five of them at once?
How arrogant and mad must he be?
Even among them, the strongest—Oblivion—would never dare take on all five at once!
And yet this newly born brother dared?
With that thought, the Five shared a telepathic exchange, preparing to give their youngest sibling a painful lesson.
Eternity and Infinity raised their hands.
Death, Oblivion, and Galactus all moved to unleash their powers.
But then, something utterly unexpected happened.
Whether it was Eternity's or Infinity's power, or Death's, Oblivion's, and Galactus's attacks, all of them were instantly overwhelmed and shattered by the sea of light.
The terrifying light engulfed their abstract entities.
In an instant, they were swallowed by the radiance.
"Impossible!"
"This power..."
At that moment, all five of the Eternals were filled with shock and disbelief.
Their attacks—broken in an instant?
The infinite light pressed down on them, leaving them unable to move.
Although they realized they could theoretically struggle free, the moment they tried, they understood something critical:
Their youngest brother's power had completely surpassed their expectations!
By an overwhelming margin.
Even if they managed to escape temporarily, it would only delay the inevitable—they would still lose in the end.
No matter how many tricks they pulled, against such overwhelming force, it was meaningless.
Worse yet, they faintly sensed that this youngest brother was holding back, deliberately restraining his strength.
Was he afraid that too much power would damage the universe?
How could that even be possible?!
The Five Eternals stared in stunned silence.
Noticing that they had lost the will to continue fighting, Syd withdrew his attack.
In an instant, the brilliant light dispersed, and the surroundings returned to their original state, as if nothing had happened.
However, despite the restoration, the atmosphere was incredibly silent.
The Five Eternals exchanged glances, looking at their youngest brother, who still radiated divine light, their hearts filled with shock and bewilderment.
After a long silence, the skeletal Death Goddess spoke first:
"You win. You defeated all five of us..."
Unable to suppress her astonishment, she blurted out:
"Why is your power so strong?"
"How can you be so much stronger than us?!"
She could hardly believe it.
This sibling, who had only recently been born, was already vastly more powerful than they were?
He dared face all five of them—not out of madness or arrogance—but because he truly had the power!
The other four stood beside her, similarly filled with disbelief and confusion.
They simply couldn't understand why this newly born brother was so strong—so strong that he could utterly crush them with ease!
"Could it be... the younger you are, the stronger you are?"
Death thought dazedly.
And it wasn't just the Five Eternals who were stunned—the dimensional demon gods secretly observing the battle were also left speechless.
"The White-Robed Hero actually won?"
"How is this possible?!"
"His strength... it's completely beyond reason!"
Sensing the vast, endless power emanating from the figure wrapped in divine light, the demon gods were filled with fear and uncertainty.
In the Dark Dimension—
Dormammu, seeing the scene unfold, felt his heart fill with panic, muttering:
"How has the White-Robed Hero become this powerful?"
On Earth, countless people were equally stunned.
They had clearly heard Death's words, and, through satellite footage, had witnessed the battle themselves.
In such a short time, the White-Robed Hero had defeated five Creator Gods?
Inside S.H.I.E.L.D., Nick Fury was left dumbfounded.
This outcome was far beyond anything he had imagined.
Five Creator Gods who had existed since the dawn of the universe, defeated by the White-Robed Hero alone?
Nick Fury was both shaken and utterly bewildered.
At the same time, Tony Stark and the others in Stark Tower were filled with turbulent emotions.
Outside of Earth—
Hearing Death's questioning, Syd chose not to answer.
Seeing his silence, Death and the other four had no choice but to suppress their curiosity for now.
At this moment—
Galactus let out a deep sigh, muttering to himself:
"I guess I'll always be the weakest..."
He sighed again, full of unwillingness.
Suddenly, he thought of something, his eyes lighting up.
The next second, pretending to be curious, he asked:
"Our youngest brother, aside from mastering the light of the universe, do you have any special abilities?"
At these words, the other four Eternals froze briefly—then their eyes lit up with interest as well.
Maybe they could salvage a little pride here!
Having overwhelming strength was one thing, but it didn't necessarily mean he had strong abilities too.
As Creator Gods, each of the Five had areas of specialty—abilities that transcended the imagination of normal beings.
Among them, Oblivion possessed the most special and powerful abilities, which was partly why he was so strong.
From what they had seen, their youngest brother hadn't seemed to use any particularly special abilities yet.
It had been pure, overwhelming abstract divine power—light, heat, laws and rules—nothing more.
The more they thought about it, the better they felt.
Maybe this youngest brother was mighty, but when it came to unique abilities, he surely couldn't compare!
Facing the Five Eternals' expectant gazes, Syd fell into brief thought.
In his mind, a list of abilities appeared:
Chaos Magic, Creation, Embodiment of Light, Solar Radiance, Black Particles, Divine Finger...
After thinking for a moment, Syd calmly said:
"I haven't fully mastered the abilities of a Creator God yet. Give me a few more days—I'll show you then. You'll understand."
As for when?
Naturally, it would be when his God's Mimicry Progress reached 100%.
He just hoped that by then, they would still have the curiosity and daring to ask.
As his words fell—
"A few days?"
The Five Eternals were startled but quickly exchanged glances and thoughts, secretly growing excited.
They figured the little brother must be stalling because he was embarrassed, having nothing impressive to show.
But that was fine.
In a few days, they would definitely return!
And then—they would truly get to see what he was capable of!
The Five shared secret smiles and anticipation as they waited.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 613
chapters.content:
Chapter 613 - 613
Faced with the Five Eternals' obvious desire to see his abilities, Syd felt a little speechless.
He casually found an excuse to delay for a few days, planning to wait until his God's Mimicry progress reached 100%.
He said,
"We'll talk about it in a few days. I have something to attend to."
In the next instant, his abstract conceptual body turned into threads of light, disappearing from the sight of the Eternals and countless people on Earth.
Seeing him vanish, Eternity, Death, Oblivion, Infinity, and Galactus couldn't help but show looks of anticipation.
Infinity smiled and said,
"Then we'll wait. In a few days, we'll come see your abilities, little brother."
As he spoke, there was a lightheartedness in his heart, and the other four shared similar smiles.
The way their youngest brother had hurried away only confirmed, in their minds, that he was making excuses.
Perhaps his strength was great—but surely his abilities couldn't compare to theirs.
Otherwise, why delay?
The Five Eternals became even more determined:
In a few days, they would return to Earth to see just what kind of abilities this little brother could display.
The Five Gods shared this thought with inner amusement.
The next moment, except for Galactus, the abstract conceptual bodies of Eternity, Death, Oblivion, and Infinity dispersed, disappearing who knew where.
As for Galactus, he flew out of the Solar System, planning to search for a life-rich planet to consume.
On Earth—
Seeing that even Galactus had begun to withdraw, people all over the world who had been watching couldn't help but start talking.
"Is it over?"
"Thank God... I thought I'd be dead by this time next year!"
Relaxed and joking on the surface, inwardly, they were still filled with wonder.
They had clearly heard the last exchange between the Creator Gods.
Many began to speculate:
Was the White-Robed Hero deliberately stalling, or did he realize that his abilities couldn't match up to the Five Eternals, so he was delaying?
Across the globe, curiosity grew.
Regardless, they would have an answer in just a few days!
While they were speculating and wondering—
In a city somewhere in the United States, beams of light began to appear.
Through the use of his Light Incarnation ability, the beams of light converged, forming a material divine body—Syd's physical form.
As soon as he arrived, he fell into deep thought.
[Light Energy +5157]
[Light Energy +5157]
(Unlock Progress 11%)
Hearing the constant notifications and seeing the unlocking progress for God's Mimicry, Syd's eyes were full of anticipation.
At the current rate of energy collection, it wouldn't be long before his God's Mimicry progress reached 100%!
As he was thinking—
Suddenly, Syd paused, sensing something, and turned his gaze into the distance, picking up on a familiar aura.
"The Power of the Phoenix?"
His golden pupils swept the surroundings, and he realized the place seemed familiar—it was where he had once fought against Dark Phoenix Jean.
Syd suddenly understood.
When he had been in the X-Men prequel universe, while enhancing his energy absorption abilities, he had naturally thought about the Phoenix Force.
When he randomly chose this location earlier, he hadn't thought much about it.
By pure coincidence, he had selected this familiar place.
Now, with his golden pupils piercing across vast distances, he saw the old battlefield.
It was right here where Jean Grey, the Phoenix, had disappeared.
Even at the time, he had sensed something was wrong—he had felt that Jean might not have truly died.
But back then, his strength was too low, and he couldn't confirm it.
Now, he closed his eyes, and the consciousness of his abstract conceptual form swept toward that location.
Following the lingering aura, he sensed a special space where Jean Grey was sleeping with her eyes closed.
Syd was a bit surprised.
Phoenix Jean was indeed still alive!
Her body was even perfectly intact?
Then again, he wasn't particularly concerned—after all, the Phoenix Force itself was the embodiment of destruction and rebirth, so this outcome was perfectly reasonable.
Sensing the probing presence, a sharp bird cry suddenly erupted from Jean's sleeping form.
A roaring flame blazed to life, forming a massive fiery bird that gazed toward Syd across layers of space.
Sensing this, Syd frowned slightly.
"The Phoenix Force?"
Luckily, it was only a fragment of a fragment—not a full manifestation.
Moreover, with Jean Grey herself as a "burden," it couldn't unleash its full power.
Thus, Syd wasn't particularly afraid.
Sweeping his golden eyes over the sleeping Jean Grey, he grew a little curious—was she still in her normal state, or had she already fallen into darkness?
The Phoenix Force was the embodiment of life and the emotional spirit of the universe.
Any host it possessed would have their inner emotions stirred up—and if reason failed to suppress desire, Dark Phoenix would be born.
Of course, it wasn't the Phoenix Force itself that turned dark, but the host.
Modern humans, bound by countless rules suppressing their desires, were particularly vulnerable—once unleashed, blackening was almost inevitable.
Thus, Syd wasn't surprised that Jean Grey might have fallen to the Dark Phoenix.
"Come to think of it... I'm probably also suitable for hosting the Phoenix Force, aren't I?"
Syd mused with curiosity.
The Phoenix Force preferred hosts with incredibly strong spiritual and mental power.
And his current mind and spirit far surpassed Jean Grey's.
Of course, Syd was just thinking aloud—he had no real interest in merging with the Phoenix Force.
After all, the Phoenix Force wasn't a dead thing—it had its own consciousness and preferences!
Plus, its full power was far too massive.
Syd was genuinely concerned that absorbing even a fragment might cause trouble later when encountering a more complete Phoenix Force.
Glancing once more at the still-sleeping Jean Grey, Syd considered whether to wake her.
"Forget it. With my current strength, Jean Grey isn't much of a threat.
I might as well wake her up. She could even help protect Logan, Professor X, and the others."
The next second, he waved his hand forward, using space transfer and portal magic.
Beneath the sleeping Jean Grey, in that mysterious space, a golden portal opened.
Moments later, the portal swallowed her.
At the same time, Phoenix Jean Grey appeared in the real world—falling out of the portal, almost crashing to the ground.
However, the raging Phoenix Force around her caught and supported her.
Looking at the Phoenix Force so close at hand, Syd's expression didn't change in the slightest.
With his Omega-level energy absorption ability, he wasn't even slightly intimidated.
Even without it, he wouldn't have been overly concerned.
At that moment, relying on his abstract conceptual body, he faintly sensed something unusual.
He frowned.
He could sense a subtle connection between his material divine body and the Phoenix Force—a link so faint that without his conceptual form's strength, he wouldn't have noticed it at all.
"What is this?"
Syd's frown deepened.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 614
chapters.content:
Chapter 614 - 614
Suddenly, a thought struck Syd, and his face turned grim.
"Could it be..."
Staring at the Phoenix Force that was continuously destroying the land before him, Syd fell into deep thought, recalling the descriptions of the Phoenix Force.
The Phoenix Force was the manifestation of the original universe's life energy and emotional energy, linking the life and spirit of all things.
It was both the storage and the ruler of life and spirit!
In simple terms, life and spirit were both part of it.
It was just like how light was a part of Syd—connected intrinsically to him.
Syd's brows furrowed tightly.
Given that kind of connection, he seriously suspected that this fragment of the Phoenix Force could potentially draw out the life energy and spiritual energy from his own body!
While he was frowning and pondering—
Suddenly, Phoenix Jean Grey opened her eyes, her gaze filled with confusion.
"Where is this?" she asked, looking around bewilderedly, before locking eyes on the white-robed figure standing before her.
Hearing her voice, Syd snapped back to reality and glanced at her, confirming a previous doubt.
The Jean Grey before him was her normal persona—not the darkened one.
"So the dark personality is still hiding?"
Thinking that, Syd didn't pay it much mind.
After all, it wasn't his problem—whether Jean's potential dark personality awakened or not could be left for Logan and the others to handle.
Right now, his main concern was how to deal with the connection between his divine body and the Phoenix Force.
The next second—
In Phoenix Jean's astonished gaze, the space around Syd rippled—and he vanished without a trace.
Leaving behind a completely confused Jean Grey.
After a long while, she finally collected herself and hurried away, intending to contact Professor X and the others.
Meanwhile, elsewhere—
Space rippled, and Syd reappeared in another city.
As he walked forward, his brow remained tightly furrowed, his mind weighed down with serious thought.
"If the Phoenix Force fragment can casually draw out life energy and spirit energy... then..."
Suddenly, he stopped walking, his expression growing even more serious.
Because of the Phoenix Force matter, he realized something even worse:
His divine body might not only be linked to the Phoenix Force, but also to beings like Eternity and Infinity!
After all, the true forms of Eternity and Infinity could be said to be the universe itself.
And everything existing in the universe was naturally connected to them—part of their being.
Thinking of this, Syd's brows knitted even tighter.
"Troublesome!"
"How do I sever this connection?"
After a long time of contemplation, he still couldn't come up with a good solution.
"I'll have to try things one by one..."
If he didn't resolve this hidden danger, it would definitely cost him dearly in the future!
At that moment, Syd thought of something else.
His focus shifted to the progress of God's Mimicry, and fragments of descriptions about "God" surfaced in his mind.
He had a strong premonition—this matter might ultimately depend on the progress of his mimicry of God.
Moreover, the true bodies of the Old Ones would soon descend—and that too would require God's power to deal with.
Thinking of this, Syd turned his attention to the energy points he was gathering and quietly began waiting.
[Light Energy +5157]
[Light Energy +5157]
...
Thanks to his extremely efficient absorption of light energy, the panel showed his energy points rapidly increasing—soon enough to push his unlocking progress from 11% to 15%.
Syd focused on the panel:
[Name: Syd]
[Age: 17 (Normal lifespan: ∞ days)]
[Mutant Abilities: Mimicry, Energy Absorption]
[Current Mimic Target: God (Titles: Creator, Maker of Worlds, Omniscient and Omnipotent One)]
(Unlock Progress: 11%)
[Abilities: Creation (Max/Max) Level 5 (Unlocked)]
[Energy Points: 5,420,000]
Glancing at the energy points, Syd didn't hesitate.
With a single thought, he poured all the points into unlocking progress.
[Energy Points: 0]
The unlock progress fluctuated slightly:
(Unlock Progress: 15%)
Syd's eyes were filled with expectation.
But even after a long wait, no new notification appeared.
"Looks like... 15% isn't enough..." Syd sighed quietly, muttering:
"Maybe it's 20%... or 25%?"
Fortunately, the rate at which he was gathering energy now was extremely fast—otherwise, he would be far more anxious.
Time passed slowly.
After several hours, the progress continued to rise.
(Unlock Progress: 20%)
(Unlock Progress: 25%)
Under Syd's intense anticipation—
The unlock progress shifted once again:
(Unlock Progress: 30%)
And then, a joyful notification rang out in his mind.
"What will it be?"
Full of expectation, Syd eagerly awaited the result.
Soon, a new ability appeared:
[Ability: Self-Existence (Unlocked)]
[Ability: Self-Existence (0/100) Level 1]
"This ability is...?"
Syd froze, his face filled with astonishment.
Immediately, a description flashed through his mind.
Legend had it that God was "Self-Existent."
Existing because He willed it so—relying on nothing external for His birth or survival.
He existed purely because He chose to exist.
There was no beginning and no end—He was the origin of all matter and life.
"This ability..."
Syd grew even more astonished.
However, a strange realization quickly followed:
Although he had obtained the ability "Self-Existence," he felt no noticeable changes in himself.
Even using the power of his abstract conceptual body, he could sense no difference.
It was as if... nothing had happened?
Syd's expression turned puzzled.
Moreover, he had another concern:
How exactly was he supposed to level up this "Self-Existence" ability?
He was momentarily baffled.
During all this mental scrambling, only a few seconds had passed in the real world.
Then, a notification suddenly sounded:
[Self-Existence Experience +1]
[Ability: Self-Existence (1/100) Level 1]
Hearing this, Syd's eyes widened.
"I didn't do anything, did I?"
"And yet... it improved?"
He hurriedly checked himself, confirming that he hadn't performed any action whatsoever.
To be sure, he even shielded himself from external influences like light and matter.
Yet the next second—
Another notification came, just as calmly:
[Self-Existence Experience +1]
"Is it... leveling up on its own?"
"And at such a fast speed?"
Syd was stunned.
Then, he couldn't help but grow excited and curious.
What would happen when Self-Existence evolved?
Would it change him?
Would it alter the outside world?
Would this ability eliminate the hidden risks from things like the Phoenix Force?
Under Syd's eager and curious gaze, the "Self-Existence" trait continued to upgrade automatically and rapidly—like a true god-tier perpetual motion machine.
It was absolutely absurd.
(End of Chapter)
