chapters.title: Chapter 615
chapters.content:
Chapter 615 - 615
<<[400PS!]>>
[Self-Existence Experience +1]
[Self-Existence Experience +1]...
Under Syd's watchful gaze, this newly obtained divine trait of God continued to level up rapidly.
Soon, a notification sounded.
[Ability: Self-Existence (0/500) Level 2]
As Self-Existence advanced to Level 2, Syd, who had been closely monitoring himself, immediately noticed a difference.
Faintly, he could feel his body connected to countless things—an overwhelming sensation of interconnectedness spread through him.
These connections, like a vast spiderweb, seemed to entangle him.
"What is this?"
Syd's eyes showed confusion.
He carefully channeled his power to sense more clearly.
Using the might of his abstract conceptual body, he faintly realized that these countless invisible connections were somehow tied to the laws of the universe.
A moment later, some clarity dawned on him.
Although his divine body had been heavily modified and enhanced, its essence was still formed from the matter of Earth, meaning it naturally had ties to all things—to the universe itself.
Now, with Self-Existence reaching Level 2, the endless web of connections binding him to all things had significantly thinned out—some links had even completely snapped.
However, because there had been so many, the change wasn't yet dramatic.
"Level 2 isn't enough, huh?"
Syd instantly grasped the situation.
He then relaxed, smiling to himself.
"Luckily, this God-tier perpetual motion machine called Self-Existence is extremely powerful. The leveling speed is insane—I won't have to wait long at all."
With that thought, he quietly waited.
[Self-Existence Experience +1]
[Self-Existence Experience +1]...
About half an hour later, another familiar notification echoed in his mind.
[Ability: Self-Existence (0/1000) Level 3]
As Self-Existence reached Level 3, Syd's abstract conceptual senses picked up dramatic changes.
The countless threads binding him were severed in an instant!
His perception of the surrounding world suddenly became far clearer and more expansive.
However, Syd's brow furrowed slightly as he carefully sensed his surroundings.
While the dense network of connections had vanished, a few immensely powerful and stubborn links still remained—now clearly visible to his perception.
Among them, Syd sensed his ties to the Phoenix Force, to the universe itself, and to Time.
These few remaining connections were incredibly resilient.
Even the divine trait of Self-Existence, at Level 3, hadn't broken them.
Syd frowned again but didn't dwell too much on it.
After all, Level 5 was supposed to be when the ability reached full perfection.
It was normal for Level 1–3 to still struggle against such massive cosmic forces.
Compared to beings like the Phoenix Force, his Level 3 ability was still far too weak.
As he waited patiently—
Nearly another hour passed.
[Ability: Self-Existence (0/2000) Level 4]
Upon reaching Level 4, those stubborn links weakened significantly—so much that without careful observation, they were almost invisible.
Seeing this, Syd was somewhat surprised.
"Even Level 4 can't completely sever them?"
"It'll have to be Level 5 then!"
He wondered:
What kind of transformation would occur once Self-Existence reached its maximum?
With a sense of eager anticipation, Syd kept his eyes on the panel.
Time continued to slip by.
About two more hours later, the progress was approaching its final breakthrough.
[Ability: Self-Existence (1999/2000) Level 4]
[Self-Existence Experience +1]
With the final notification, the data on the panel changed.
[Ability: Self-Existence (Max/Max) Level 5]
In an instant—something extraordinary happened!
Mysterious fluctuations surged through Syd's body.
Those lingering, stubborn connections snapped completely.
In that moment, Syd felt an incredible shift:
His body, his soul, his mind—every part of him—was no longer linked to anything.
He was no longer the product of any biological or material origin.
His existence was tied to nothing but himself.
He existed solely because he willed himself to exist.
And if he no longer wished to exist—he had the faint sense that he would simply vanish into absolute nothingness.
This feeling was indescribable—impossible to put into words.
"If I decided not to exist anymore... what would happen?"
The thought flashed through Syd's mind, and he was momentarily curious.
However, after sensing the nature of his new ability carefully, he wisely abandoned that suicidal idea.
Instinctively, he could tell that if he truly willed himself to cease existing, he would completely disappear—not even leaving behind a void—true annihilation.
It was terrifying.
Syd dared not experiment lightly.
He couldn't even be sure he could return afterward.
If he couldn't—that would be the ultimate, irreversible death.
Of course, it was possible he could return...
Aside from that, Syd realized Self-Existence wasn't as simple as it appeared.
After reaching Level 5, although on the surface nothing seemed to change, the reality was drastically different.
Following a subtle intuition, Syd raised his right hand.
A golden Infinity Gauntlet appeared, fitted securely onto his arm.
The next second, the Time Stone on the gauntlet lit up with a green glow.
Instantly, the power of the Time Stone enveloped him.
Syd tried to slow down the flow of time around him.
But then—
Something unexpected happened.
The Time Stone's power brushed past him—without causing any effect at all.
Recalling the severed connection to Time he had sensed earlier, Syd muttered:
"So it's true..."
Self-Existence might have appeared unremarkable outwardly—but internally, the changes were massive beyond imagination!
Now, he was no longer affected by the flow of time!
To put it more vividly:
Any influence of time had absolutely no effect on him anymore.
Syd even suspected that if someone tried to travel back to the past to assassinate his younger self—it would fail completely.
In simple terms, he had transcended the timeline!
Syd's golden eyes gleamed brightly.
This was an extremely crucial power.
At his current level, the beings he had to face were all terrifying entities.
Take the Phoenix Force, for example—
On the surface, it only seemed capable of destruction.
But in truth, it could also resurrect, reverse causality, alter timelines, rewrite history, or even annihilate historical existence altogether.
Syd wasn't sure whether the fragment of the Phoenix Force he was dealing with could wield such abilities.
Jean Grey, while using the Phoenix Force, had only displayed destructive power, rapid healing, and occasional glimpses into the future.
The deeper, scarier abilities hadn't been shown.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 616
chapters.content:
Chapter 616 - 616
It wasn't just the Phoenix Force—after reaching the single-universe level, many powerful beings possessed abilities related to time.
For instance, Kang the Conqueror, the hidden mastermind behind the Time Variance Authority, had the ability to prune timelines.
Even Eternity, who appeared to have lost when facing Kang in direct combat, hadn't actually unleashed the full extent of his time-related powers.
He should have been capable of doing similar things.
After all, he was the personification of Time itself.
In short, time-based powers were extremely common once you reached the single-universe level and beyond.
If one wasn't careful, it was easy to fall victim to them.
But now, with Self-Existence—none of that could touch him!
Time could no longer influence him!
"This ability is such a cheat... or rather, God Himself is kind of a cheat," Syd sighed.
At this point, he even felt confident enough to enter the Time Variance Authority!
Kang's greatest strength lay in manipulating time.
Now that time-based attacks were ineffective against him, Kang's threat level had dropped by several tiers.
Aside from time, recalling the other stubborn connections he'd sensed earlier, Syd thought:
"Abilities related to causality should also be useless against me now."
After all, he was no longer entangled in any karma or causal threads.
After marveling at how powerful Self-Existence was, just as Syd thought all the changes had settled—
His consciousness suddenly wavered.
He found himself at the very beginning—before the universe had even been born.
A pitch-black void, devoid of any life, stretched infinitely.
Only he existed there, alone.
His whole body radiated light, illuminating the endless darkness around him.
Syd felt a profound sense of boredom.
He had no idea how long he drifted there.
Suddenly, apart from himself, another point of light appeared.
Within the dark emptiness, a singularity—or what could be called a cosmic egg—exploded in a blinding flash.
The Big Bang had occurred!
With the Big Bang came the birth of the four abstract conceptual beings: Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion.
And also—the sole survivor from the previous universe, absorbed into the cosmic egg and now reborn alongside them—Galactus.
As the Big Bang expanded, Syd's indescribable form also began influencing this new universe.
His being, alongside the others, became one of the foundations and pillars of the cosmos.
The universe evolved...
Heat, light, energy—all things began to fill the expanding universe.
Syd personally witnessed the entire process of cosmic evolution.
After a time, Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and Galactus each became aware of his presence.
They sensed him—and realized what he was.
A Creator God, just like themselves—part of the universe, embodying aspects like light, heat, and positivity.
Without him, there would be no light, no warmth, no positive forces within the universe.
Sensing a being of equal standing, they naturally felt a deep goodwill toward him.
Yet at the same time, an odd feeling stirred within them.
"You seem to have been born even earlier than us?"
Infinity, the goddess representing Space, conveyed her thoughts telepathically, filled with disbelief.
Hearing her words, Eternity, representing Time, also froze.
He felt the same.
He spoke:
"You feel it too?"
The Five Creator Gods of the universe all exchanged shocked and confused thoughts.
"How could you have been born before us?"
Their perceptions couldn't possibly be wrong.
Maybe one could make a mistake—but not all of them at once.
They each sensed it—clearly, unmistakably.
Thus, it had to be true.
A deep sense of awe and reverence naturally rose in their hearts.
This mysterious existence—they instinctively respected him.
More ancient than them.
Stronger, perhaps, than them.
Initially, they had perceived him as embodying light, heat, and positivity—core aspects of the universe.
But now, they weren't so sure.
After all, if he existed before even they were born—then those assumptions might not be entirely accurate.
What was he, truly?
Faced with their questioning thoughts, Syd pondered briefly.
Then, he chose not to answer.
In the next moment, he vanished.
His consciousness returned to reality.
"Huu..."
Syd opened his eyes, a flicker of astonishment flashing through them.
He had appeared before Eternity and the others—even earlier than they did?
No doubt about it—it had to be the effect of the Self-Existence trait.
Still, he couldn't help wondering whether what he'd just experienced was real or some kind of illusion.
As he was deep in thought—
Meanwhile, in the realm of Death, and in other hidden corners of the universe where Eternity, Infinity, Oblivion, and Galactus dwelled—
All of them suddenly froze.
Their expressions turned distant, as a new memory surfaced in their minds.
Suddenly—they recalled something.
At the dawn of the universe, they had indeed seen that younger brother of theirs!
Although he hadn't appeared afterward, their memories of that ancient presence—of the one who embodied light, heat, and positivity—remained vivid and unmistakable.
Most importantly—
He had existed even before them.
Such a mysterious being—how could they possibly forget?
As they thought about it, the Five Eternals' faces grew increasingly strange.
Now, they each possessed two conflicting sets of memories.
One memory saw Syd as their younger brother.
The other saw him as an ancient elder, a figure older and greater than themselves.
For a moment, their minds were in complete turmoil—unsure which memory was real.
Even Eternity—the personification of Time—carefully examined reality but found no flaws.
No sign that anything had been tampered with.
Confused and uneasy, the others turned to Eternity:
"Eternity, what's going on?"
Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and Galactus all reached out to him telepathically, seeking answers.
But—
The next second, they heard Eternity's own confused voice:
"I don't know either..."
Even as he answered them, Eternity's consciousness returned to the birth of the universe, searching for clues.
After careful examination, he was stunned to discover that—
Syd had indeed existed at the dawn of time!
Yet this conflicted with all their previous memories!
Could it be that their memories had been wrong?
Or perhaps... tampered with?
But that was impossible.
At that moment—
Infinity, full of doubt, couldn't help but voice her thought:
"Could it be... our little brother traveled back through time and altered the past?"
Hearing this, Galactus, Oblivion, and Death all felt a jolt of realization—maybe that was the answer?
Yet surprisingly—Eternity did not agree.
After a moment of deep thought, he shook his head and said:
"You all know—I am Time itself.
If our little brother had traveled back and altered the past... there's no way I wouldn't have noticed."
At those words, the other four fell silent.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 617
chapters.content:
Chapter 617 - 617
The Four—Death, Oblivion, Infinity, and Galactus—had just been wondering whether their little brother had used time-travel abilities to go back to the beginning of the universe.
But just as they voiced this suspicion, Eternity immediately denied it, leaving them all stunned.
At that moment—
The Goddess of Death pondered aloud:
"That's true. If our youngest brother had really used time powers, Eternity, you would have sensed it."
"But if he didn't use time powers... how could he have existed at the birth of the universe?"
This question left even Eternity at a loss.
Yes—if no time-travel had been involved, how had their little brother existed at the universe's beginning?
Surely it couldn't be that their memories were wrong?
The Five Creator Gods thought in amazement.
After a while, Galactus suddenly said:
"Why don't we just go ask him directly?"
At his suggestion, the other four immediately agreed.
Very soon, each of them used their own means to contact their youngest brother, who was still on Earth.
Meanwhile—
Not just the Five—countless beings across the universe were also left dazed and confused.
In their minds, two different memories had surfaced.
In one memory, there had always been Five Creator Gods.
In the other, there had always been six Creator Gods, including a mysterious one representing light, heat, and positivity.
This mysterious Creator God had never appeared publicly.
Few even knew of him—only those who had closely interacted with the Five might have heard whispers of his existence.
He had never shown himself.
No one had seen him.
Among the Six, he was the most enigmatic.
He had long been the subject of speculation and discussion across the cosmos.
Many had debated why this Creator God had never revealed himself.
Now, sensing the two conflicting memories, beings all over the universe were left stunned.
What was happening?
How could there be an alternate memory?
Had there really always been six Creator Gods?
Countless individuals were plunged into confusion.
...
Earth.
At that moment, Syd was still pondering whether what he had experienced earlier had been real or not—
When the voices of Eternity and the others reached his ears.
"Our youngest brother... there's something we wish to ask you..."
Hearing their explanation, Syd's eyes flickered strangely.
That memory—even the Five Creator Gods possessed it?
And it wasn't just them.
Apparently, throughout the universe, there were legends of a sixth Creator God?
Even more, Eternity had firmly confirmed that this phenomenon had nothing to do with the manipulation of time.
That's why they had come to ask him directly.
Listening to them, Syd was increasingly astonished.
He thought to himself:
"Self-Existence... could it really have nothing to do with time?"
He had assumed it was a temporal manipulation.
But clearly, it wasn't.
Under the Five's watchful gazes, Syd fell into deep thought.
After a while, a new idea struck him:
"Could this be related to causality?"
After all—while the Big Bang theory explained the origin of the universe, it didn't explain the cause of the singularity—the cosmic egg's existence.
Many theologians and philosophers had long argued for the concept of a "First Cause" or an "Ultimate Cause."
This concept was meant to explain the origin and reason for the existence of everything, emphasizing that every effect must have a cause—and that cause must ultimately trace back to something that itself had no cause.
Otherwise, there would be an infinite regress of causes, which is illogical.
Thus—there must be a First Cause.
And traditionally—that First Cause was God!
He occupied the position of the First Cause and Ultimate Reason.
Syd speculated:
"So... maybe Self-Existence connects me to the First Cause?"
"Is that why I appeared before the birth of the universe?"
The more he thought about it, the more plausible it seemed.
Yet he also felt it couldn't be explained so simply.
After all, God Himself was a literal 'bug'—and causality alone probably only explained part of it.
More likely, deeper divine forces were involved.
As he continued pondering, Syd suddenly noticed something strange:
"It seems... I haven't claimed the First Cause of the multiverse—only that of this universe?"
He immediately tried sensing it carefully.
And sure enough—he discovered that in the other universes he'd visited, such as the X-Men prequel universe, he had indeed appeared before their Big Bangs.
The next moment, he casually used Dreamwalking, sending part of his consciousness to a brand-new parallel universe.
A few seconds later, after becoming that universe's Creator God, he confirmed one thing:
Only in universes he had visited could he occupy the position of First Cause.
In universes he hadn't visited—Self-Existence had no effect.
In other words—
Self-Existence, for now, only operated at the single-universe level.
It had not yet reached the multiversal level—or beyond.
It hadn't even influenced the earlier history of the 616 main universe!
Syd hadn't forgotten what Galactus truly was.
Unlike the four abstract beings—Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion—Galactus had once been a mortal being.
He was the sole survivor of the previous universe, absorbed into the cosmic egg and reborn.
Strictly speaking, Galactus was not so much a Creator God as he was holding a cosmic position.
Every time a universe was destroyed, the last living being would become the next Galactus.
That's why Galactus was so different.
He had a physical body rather than being a purely conceptual existence.
It was also why he was often weaker—and why he could be defeated or even killed without the universe collapsing.
Whenever great cosmic disasters struck, Galactus was usually the first to fall.
Whereas Eternity and the others rarely encountered real danger.
Simply put:
Poor Uncle Galactus—defeated again and again.
"616's main universe was born after the destruction of the previous one..."
Syd frowned, feeling a wave of disappointment.
Self-Existence seemed powerful—but it hadn't allowed him to seize the First Cause of the multiverse.
Nor even the First Cause of the earliest history of 616.
The more he thought about it, the deeper his disappointment grew.
But then—
He suddenly realized something, freezing in place.
"Wait... this might not be a problem with Self-Existence itself—it's my problem."
While he had obtained the Self-Existence trait—
its effectiveness clearly depended on his own strength.
"After all, I'm not even at the multiversal level yet.
Naturally, Self-Existence can't touch the multiverse."
Realizing this, Syd finally understood.
The issue wasn't the ability itself.
It was that he lacked the full "Godhood" necessary to unleash its true effects.
He was missing the true components needed to claim the ultimate First Cause.
Similarly, he recalled that Chaos Magic's reality-warping ability also depended heavily on strength and completeness.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 618
chapters.content:
Chapter 618 - 618
The level of Chaos Magic could theoretically reach beyond the multiverse, but due to the lack of a true source for it—without an energy supply—the casting of Chaos Magic relied entirely on the light energy stored within Syd's own body.
This led to the problem that, unless he went into a berserk, out-of-control state, he was fundamentally unable to unleash the true power of Chaos Magic!
Thinking of this, Syd couldn't help but sigh inwardly.
Ultimately, it was still a matter of lacking strength.
He had tons of bugged abilities, but no power to support them.
Fortunately, this problem was easy to solve!
"As long as I keep progressing in imitating the Almighty and obtain a true portion of the Almighty's power, then..."
An expectant emotion welled up inside Syd.
While he was both looking forward and sighing, unbeknownst to everyone, tremendous upheavals were taking place in countless unfamiliar universes.
Without anyone realizing it, creators and cosmic beings across different universes began to discover that there was suddenly a new Creator recorded within their universe's existence.
If one could rewind time, they would even see that from the very beginning of those universes, a figure shining with radiant light had been projected into their foundations.
No one knew who this figure was. They only knew that a new memory had suddenly been implanted into their minds—an existence that was among the creators, and one of the most mysterious ones at that.
Even before the birth of the 616 Main Universe, Syd's presence and past projections were slowly extending backward through increasingly ancient times and higher realms.
All of these changes occurred silently, without much disturbance, and because the multiverse was so vast, Syd did not immediately notice.
Had he discovered it, he truly would have been astonished—astonished that the trait of self-existence and eternal being was far more powerful and broken (bugged) than he had imagined.
Relying solely on self-existence and eternal being, he could slowly ascend to become a multiversal-level entity!
Shortly after these changes began, Syd suddenly sensed that his own power had inexplicably strengthened.
Just as he was about to investigate this oddity, he heard Eternity's confused voice asking, "What exactly is happening?"
Hearing Eternity's question, Syd remembered that the others were still present. He thought for a moment, then replied vaguely, "I'm not sure either."
The words had barely left his mouth when Eternity and the others twitched internally, clearly not believing him.
However, since their youngest sibling was unwilling to explain, they had no choice but to drop it.
After a brief discussion, the Five Abstract Entities decided to change the subject.
Galactus laughed and said, "Our youngest brother, don't forget—you'll need to show us your Creator abilities in a few days."
As he spoke, there was a look of expectation in his eyes. Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion all shared similar feelings, their hearts carrying faint traces of amusement.
Their little brother's strength had exceeded their expectations; however, in terms of abilities, they were still confident they could regain the upper hand.
They were eagerly awaiting the moment when their little brother would run out of tricks, when he would be exposed!
Syd showed a strange expression.
As the five abstract beings laughed and spoke a few more words, they withdrew their attention from Earth.
Just as they were about to disperse and handle their own affairs, Infinity suddenly spoke with a hint of confusion, "Have any of you noticed? It seems like our universe has been growing stronger lately?"
Or rather, it felt as if their own powers had mysteriously increased by some unknown influence.
Upon hearing her words, the four who were about to leave froze.
"It does seem that way."
"But maybe it's just an illusion?"
Hearing this, Infinity also dismissed it, thinking she must be overthinking it—that's why she had imagined their powers had grown.
Meanwhile, on Earth—
As the abstract entities conversed, Syd's conceptual form also heard their discussion, causing him to freeze slightly.
Very quickly, he figured out the cause and muttered helplessly to himself,
"Looks like... I grew too strong too fast, and the 616 Main Universe was dragged along with me?"
After all, he was now part of the universe itself, part of its foundation. If he grew stronger, the universe would naturally grow stronger as well.
After sorting through these thoughts, Syd shifted his attention back to himself.
Just now, because Eternity and the others had interrupted, he hadn't had the chance to check the cause of his sudden strengthening. Now he finally had time.
In the next second, he began to examine his condition carefully.
It didn't take long before he truly discovered something.
While casting his Dreamwalking technique, Syd sensed countless universes shining as brightly as daylight.
Normally, the brighter a universe appeared to him, the stronger his information projection in that universe.
Yet now, suddenly, a massive number of universes were shining with a daylight-like brilliance?
Some of them even approached the intensity of those like the X-Men prequel universes—the ones he had already conquered!
What was happening?
Syd blinked in astonishment.
Even as he watched, a few more previously dim universes began to light up brightly in his perception.
The scene before him left him thoroughly confused.
Realizing the urgency, he immediately began checking the situation.
The next moment, he activated Dreamwalking, detaching a portion of his consciousness toward one of the bright universes.
As soon as his consciousness approached, the universe's light became even more dazzling.
At the same time, within that universe, the once-vague projection that had seized the First Cause and claimed the sixth Creator position abruptly became solid and real.
This scene shocked not only Syd but also the creators and cosmic beings of that universe, who were left utterly dumbfounded.
The mysterious, illusory Creator had become real?
While they were still reeling, Syd quickly figured out the truth.
"So that's it..." Syd marveled.
He hadn't expected that self-existence and eternal being would be so ridiculously strong—far stronger than he'd initially thought.
After a moment of astonishment, Syd's mood improved significantly.
Because he realized that with self-existence and eternal being, his speed in conquering universes had skyrocketed!
Originally, Dreamwalking limited him: he couldn't separate too much of his consciousness at once, so conquering universes was slow.
Now, thanks to this trait, everything seemed easy.
He no longer needed to physically enter those universes.
He only needed to drift near the light points representing universes where he had seized the First Cause, and the projections within would immediately solidify into reality.
Naturally, those universes would then become part of him, feeding him massive power.
Moreover, Syd wasn't sure if it was just his imagination, but it felt like the speed at which self-existence and eternal being conquered universes was increasing.
The brightening of the light points seemed to be accelerating.
Although puzzled, Syd didn't dwell on it. Instead, he focused on the universes that had already lit up.
The next second—
Syd's consciousness swept across over a hundred shining light points.
In an instant, he sensed more than a hundred universes.
A terrifying, overwhelming torrent of power surged toward him!
At the same time—
The Five Abstract Entities, who had just parted ways, were startled to find that the universe was rapidly growing stronger!
"What is happening?!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 619: Chpater 619
chapters.content:
Chapter 619 - Chpater 619
Feeling the universe rapidly growing stronger for no apparent reason, Eternity and the others were filled with astonishment and confusion, unable to comprehend what was happening.
Suddenly, they sensed something.
They realized that the portion of the universe representing light, warmth, positivity—belonging to their youngest brother—was rapidly becoming stronger.
Because that portion had grown too powerful, the rest of the universe was being affected, and was strengthening alongside it.
"What did our youngest brother do?"
Sensing this phenomenon, they were filled with disbelief.
What had he done to cause the part of the universe associated with him to suddenly become so overwhelmingly powerful?
And even more unbelievable, it was dragging the rest of the universe along, making it stronger too?!
While they were bewildered, on the other side, Syd was also feeling the surge of power flooding in from those hundred or so universes.
At this moment, he had the sensation that with just a flick of his hand, he could easily destroy the 616 Main Universe—or even several universes.
In short, he could feel that he had completely transcended the single-universe level.
After soaking in this feeling for a while, Syd quickly pulled himself back together, his expression turning serious.
"I've only conquered about a hundred universes, and I already have this much strength. What about those multiversal-level beings like the true Eternity and others?"
He had never forgotten that the Eternity in the 616 Main Universe was merely an avatar—the true Eternity was at the multiversal level!
And their strength...
To put it figuratively, the 616 Universe was like a single cell, and countless such cells made up the multiverse, forming the true multiversal Eternity and others!
Thinking about this, Syd felt a heavy weight settle on his heart. He murmured to himself,
"Compared to the multiversal Eternity, I'm still far too weak."
"I wonder when I'll truly reach the multiversal level?"
Suddenly, he noticed that the speed at which self-existence and eternal being was lighting up universes was indeed accelerating with time.
Realizing it wasn't just his imagination, Syd immediately formed a guess:
"The more universes that get lit up, the stronger self-existence and eternal being becomes, and the faster its efficiency?"
He recalled how at the first level, self-existence and eternal being had upgraded itself automatically.
Now, even at level five, it still functioned like a divine perpetual motion machine!
His eyes lit up.
This meant that as time passed, he would continue to grow stronger!
Eventually, he might even become multiversal!
However...
There might not be enough time left for him to fully grow.
Syd pondered grimly, recalling the death scene he had glimpsed when he used the black stone artifact not long ago.
Facing that true body of an Old One, he might not have enough time to reach the multiversal level before dying!
Syd's gaze shifted back to his panel, focusing on the God Imitation Progress.
(Unlock Progress: 30%)
The next moment, he poured all the energy points he had accumulated recently into the unlock progress.
Instantly, the progress value changed.
(Unlock Progress: 39%)
Syd frowned slightly, doing a quick calculation in his mind.
"The consumption rate increased?" he muttered to himself.
Normally, his progress should have reached over forty percent by now—not just 39%!
However, he quickly composed himself and wasn't too surprised.
When he had previously unlocked the powers of the Great Serpent, Scarlet Witch, and Baldr, he had encountered similar situations. It was within expectations.
Besides, things were different now—he was accumulating energy points at an absurdly fast rate, so higher consumption didn't matter much!
After organizing his thoughts, he focused again on the 39% unlock progress.
"I wonder... will I gain a new ability from God at 40%?"
"Or will it be at 45%, or even 50%?"
"And will God's omniscience and omnipotence finally appear?"
Syd's eyes were filled with anticipation.
"It won't take long at the current speed of energy accumulation!"
Just then, he heard the astonished voices of Eternity and the others.
"The universe is suddenly getting stronger—what's happening?"
Hearing their questions, Syd was momentarily stunned.
He really didn't know how to answer them.
He couldn't very well tell them that he had just gained the power of over a hundred universes, indirectly strengthening the 616 Main Universe, could he?
For this situation, he could only continue to vaguely reply, "I'm not sure."
While he was casually dealing with the Five, elsewhere at Xavier's Academy—
On the school's open grounds—
Professor X, Logan, Iceman, and other mutant students looked up at the sky, watching as a red-haired woman floated down.
As she landed, Logan and the others immediately rushed toward her.
"Jean? Is it really you?" Cyclops asked, his voice trembling.
"Jean, you're alive?"
"What happened?"
Logan and the others were overwhelmed with emotion as they stared at her.
Jean smiled warmly and quickly explained.
Hearing that a mysterious figure in white had saved her, Professor X and the others instantly thought of a particular figure.
"The White-Clothed Hero?!"
They exchanged glances, shocked, but also understanding.
It had to be the Creator-level White-Clothed Hero. Who else could have the ability to revive Jean?
They each filled in the blanks in their minds, picturing the scene.
...
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]...
Having shaken off the Five's questioning, Syd continued to wait as his energy points grew and self-existence and eternal being lit up more universes.
Suddenly, he remembered something and took out the black stone artifact.
"With my current strength, could I hold out against that Old One's true body?"
With that thought, he immediately poured energy into the artifact.
The familiar pulling sensation appeared, and Syd's vision blurred.
Outside the pitch-black universe, a nameless, formless being cloaked in dark mist emerged.
However, what followed was almost no different from before.
The Old One's tentacle still pierced through his chest effortlessly; he couldn't even put up the slightest resistance.
The familiar contemptuous voice sounded:
"A feeble ant who dares to offend me—this is your fate..."
"...Becoming my puppet will be your final destiny..."
Suddenly, the vision froze and he was pulled back to reality.
"Even after gaining the power of over a hundred universes, I'm still no match for that Old One's true body?"
"The gap is still this vast?"
Syd frowned deeply.
Feeling the crushing difference, he dared not idle any longer.
While self-existence and eternal being automatically lit up more universes, he frantically began casting Dreamwalking.
One by one, his consciousness fragments entered different unfamiliar universes.
Each time he became a Creator within a universe, his consciousness would quickly return, repeating the process in a cycle.
With the combined effort of himself and self-existence and eternal being, the speed at which universes were conquered increased dramatically, and his strength soared.
One universe after another became part of him...
Just as he was growing stronger, after about an hour, something abnormal happened outside Earth.
A massive space fluctuation appeared!
The sudden wave jolted Syd awake. He immediately turned his gaze toward outer space, silently on alert.
"Is the Old One's true body arriving?"
Making the worst-case assumption, Syd prepared to flee the 616 Main Universe if necessary—though he knew that if the being was as strong as the death vision had shown, his chances of escape were slim.
While he observed, the Sorcerer Supreme, the Ancient One, and some other sorcerers at Kamar-Taj also sensed the anomaly.
"A massive spatial fluctuation!"
"Who could it be?"
The Ancient One and others hastily cast spells to investigate.
Under their and Syd's watchful eyes, a colossal spatial rift appeared in outer space.
Then, one after another, giant beings exuding vast auras appeared.
The moment they descended, their overwhelming presence surged outward, pressing down on Earth and causing countless hearts to tremble.
"It's the Celestials!"
Seeing the colorful giants, the Ancient One and the others' faces grew grave and shocked.
And not just them—countless people across the globe noticed the abnormality. Government agencies scrambled to redirect satellites.
When they saw the Celestials, they were stunned.
"Celestials?!"
Hundreds of Celestials floated densely around Earth, eyeing the planet like predators surrounding prey.
And what they intended seemed obvious.
Most likely, they were here for the White-Clothed Hero!
At that moment, a familiar red-armored Celestial stepped forward.
Glaring down at Earth, his gaze ice-cold, he declared,
"White-Clothed Hero, I told you—I would return!"
The voice of Arishem the Judge echoed across Earth, reaching everyone's ears.
Many who had witnessed previous events immediately realized who he was—the Celestial who had once been defeated by the White-Clothed Hero and barely escaped.
At the same time—
Syd was also observing the Celestials.
His gaze swept across the five strongest Celestials at the front.
These five felt overwhelmingly powerful to his senses—comparable even to the earlier strength of the Abstract Entities!
Of course, the Abstract Entities had grown stronger recently thanks to him—
well, all except Galactus...
At that moment—
Among the five powerful Celestials, a fully purple one frowned and said,
"Arishem, are you sure this White-Clothed Hero is really on this planet?"
"Is he truly as powerful as you claim?"
Even as he spoke, there was visible skepticism in his eyes.
The other four elite Celestials, and indeed most of the Celestials present, also harbored doubts.
How could a single being on one planet possibly be so powerful?
And even be acknowledged as the sixth Creator?
There were supposed to be only five Creators.
How could there be six?
What was going on?!
While the hundreds of Celestials watched, Arishem solemnly nodded.
Meanwhile—
On Earth—
Staring at the surrounding Celestials, Syd's brow furrowed slightly.
In the next moment, he activated his space-shifting ability.
Under the watching eyes of Arishem and the Celestials, his figure instantly appeared outside Earth.
The moment they saw him, Arishem's gaze turned even colder.
Nearly two hundred Celestials stared intently at the man in white.
The tension thickened rapidly.
On Earth, governments nervously monitored the situation.
Even dimensional demon gods sensed the disturbance across the Solar System.
...
In Asgard—
Heimdall, observing the Nine Realms, immediately reported the situation to Odin.
Soon, Thor and the others also turned their attention toward the Solar System.
...
At Omnipotence City—also known as the Pantheon—
Zeus and other gods, who had been keeping an eye on Earth, now focused their full attention.
All the god pantheons were secretly watching.
...
At the same time, as part of the universe itself, Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and even Galactus all sensed the turmoil within the Solar System.
Since this was the home of their youngest brother, they couldn't ignore it.
The moment the anomaly erupted, they immediately noticed.
Seeing nearly two hundred Celestials, Eternity simmered with anger.
"What is Arishem trying to do?!"
Most of these Celestials weren't even Eternity's creations—they were foreign invaders.
Especially those five strongest Celestials—
they nearly matched his previous strength and posed a true threat back then.
Though surprised by their strength, he wasn't entirely shocked.
Most of the Celestials within the universe were originally created to maintain balance, but because of their divided duties, the majority weren't particularly powerful.
Hence, Celestials occasionally dying wasn't rare.
They weren't supposed to be stronger than him.
However, some Celestials from beyond the universe were exceptions.
They were relics of earlier cosmic epochs—some of them were even stronger than him!
Now, the attention of the Five Abstract Entities turned toward their youngest brother.
Could he handle the Celestials?
Would they need to intervene?
While they watched—
In the Solar System—
Facing the army of Celestials, Syd's brow furrowed slightly.
He, too, had sensed everything—
and he understood even more than Eternity did.
He knew full well:
among the Celestials from beyond the universe, some possessed terrifying strength.
It wasn't just the colorful Celestials—there were also the dark ones.
Before the Marvel Multiverse even existed, there was only a single universe, its sentient being known as the First Firmament.
Feeling lonely, the First Firmament created the earliest Celestials—the Black Celestials.
Later, the Black Celestials, modeling themselves after their creator, created the colorful Celestials.
As time passed, ideological rifts developed between the two types, eventually culminating in a war.
The battle was so intense that it even damaged the First Firmament itself—
its shattered fragments later formed the multiverse.
Thus, the early Celestials were unimaginably powerful—
they had torn apart the First Firmament's body, after all!
Thinking of this, Syd's brow furrowed tighter.
While he was deep in thought—
From afar, Arishem saw his expression and sneered inwardly.
"Now you're afraid?"
"Where's all your arrogance from before?"
"Today will be your death!" he declared coldly.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 620
chapters.content:
Chapter 620 - 620
[700PS!]
Under the gaze of countless people on Earth, dimensional demon gods, gods from Asgard and other pantheons, and even the Five Abstract Entities, the Celestial Judge Arishem spoke.
Facing the white-clothed figure floating outside Earth, he said coldly,
"Today is your day of death!"
His tone was utterly firm, without a hint of hesitation, filled with confidence that his words would become reality.
Hearing his words, nearly two hundred Celestials present—whether it was the five strongest or the others—held the same belief.
This white-clothed Creator was indeed strong, but against five beings of comparable level plus the aid of countless Celestials, how could he possibly win?
He would inevitably fall!
They were filled with absolute confidence.
As Arishem's words fell, the leaders of nations across Earth were shaken.
"That guy... really thinks he can defeat the White-Clothed Hero?"
"Could the White-Clothed Hero actually lose?"
The thought left them stunned.
And it wasn't just them—even the hidden dimensional demon gods were startled.
Were the Celestials really that confident?
Sensing the terrifying pressure released by the five strongest among the nearly two hundred Celestials, even the demon gods had to admit—Arishem might indeed have some basis for his confidence.
So what would happen to the White-Clothed Hero?
At that moment, the gods of the various pantheons shared the same uneasy feeling.
Under the watchful eyes of all these beings, the white-clothed existence they focused on spoke calmly,
"Is that so?"
His voice was mysterious, like the very truth of the universe, echoing through space.
Hearing him, many Celestials sneered.
Still boasting even at the edge of death!
Arishem exchanged glances with the others and ordered coldly,
"Attack together. Don't give him a chance to escape!"
The Celestials all nodded.
The next second, multicolored beams of energy erupted from their hands, along with psychic powers and other abilities.
A multicolored ocean of energy surged toward Syd at astonishing speed.
Watching the tidal wave of energy approach, Syd remained indifferent.
With a mere thought, he drew upon gamma-ray bursts occurring across the universe.
He even actively created more gamma-ray bursts, imbuing them with his divine conceptual power.
Boom!
Invisible gamma-ray bursts swept across the entire Solar System!
Of course, under Syd's control, they caused no harm to anything within the Solar System, only targeting the Celestials.
Boom!
The gamma-ray bursts, moving at unimaginable speeds, collided head-on with the Celestials' energy attacks.
In an instant, a terrifying shockwave spread across space!
Seeing this, Arishem and the others were stunned.
This guy... actually blocked the combined attack of the Celestials alone?!
Before they could process it, Syd, who had casually unleashed gamma-ray bursts, slowly raised his right hand.
A deep crimson light of Chaos Magic flared up.
He closed his hand into a fist toward the gathered Celestials.
In a flash—agonized screams erupted!
Countless witnesses were stunned to see seventy-one Celestials enveloped by the crimson light, compressed into tiny masses.
Their armor twisted, their bones shattered, and blood splattered across space.
In the blink of an eye, these seventy-one Celestials were crushed to death by Chaos Magic!
Seeing the White-Clothed Creator casually obliterate seventy-one Celestials with a single gesture, even Arishem and the five strongest Celestials showed utter disbelief.
How could it be so effortless?!
Just like that—seventy-one of them gone?!
Vaguely, they began to realize something was wrong about this White-Clothed Creator's strength.
While they were reeling in shock, everyone on Earth—governments, demon gods, and pantheon gods alike—were left speechless.
At the same time, Syd didn't wait for them to react. He wasn't interested in playing around anymore. Slowly, he closed his eyes.
In the next moment, infinite light gathered around him, and for an instant, the entire universe was illuminated.
Outside the Solar System—
A colossal being shining with radiant, indescribable, and unbearable brilliance manifested.
The being stretched out a hand—
In the palm of its hand, the entire Solar System sat!
Syd looked down indifferently at the tiny Celestials scattered across the Solar System.
The next second—
The power of over a hundred universes surged forward like an ocean of light, enveloping the five strongest Celestials and Arishem along with the others.
Boom!
Under the disbelieving gazes of Arishem and the others, their bodies froze entirely.
They were like insects trapped in amber—fragile and pitiful.
They looked upward and saw the White-Clothed Creator, who now seemed larger than the entire Solar System itself.
But what truly terrified them wasn't the size—
It was the overwhelming power blanketing them.
No matter how they struggled or resisted, they couldn't move at all.
Simultaneously, a deep crimson light of Chaos Magic shrouded them, twisting and altering reality.
Their special abilities were completely disabled—sealed off and silenced.
This absolute, crushing force left even Arishem and the Celestials in a state of disbelief.
"How... how can your power be this strong?"
"How could such power even exist?!"
Arishem murmured in stunned disbelief.
At the same time, the five strongest Celestials, each comparable to the earlier Abstract Entities, were also completely dumbfounded.
Among them, a blue Celestial named Damien exclaimed in panic,
"Even if you're the Creator of this universe, you shouldn't be this powerful! This isn't normal!"
"Each of us five is close to the strength of Eternity and the others—how could you possibly..."
His furious and terrified voice echoed through the void.
Hearing these words, many Earthlings, who had assumed the Celestials were just weaklings, froze in shock.
The five strongest Celestials' power was close to that of the Abstract Entities?
Then how could the White-Clothed Hero crush them so effortlessly?!
Surely it couldn't be that the White-Clothed Hero could also easily suppress Eternity and the others?!
They found it hard to believe.
Meanwhile, the demon gods across various dimensions were equally stunned.
Compared to humans, they could sense far more.
They clearly felt the vast power radiating from the five Celestials and realized—they weren't lying.
What shocked them now was the White-Clothed Hero's own power.
The level of this strength...
In Asgard—
Odin, Thor, and the others were dumbfounded.
In other pantheons like Omnipotence City, Zeus and the other gods felt much the same.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 621
chapters.content:
Chapter 621 - 621
[800PS!!]
At this moment—
Feeling the radiant light that enveloped and imprisoned them, along with the deep crimson energy that suppressed their powers, another Celestial named Tuolt muttered in disbelief, "This power... far surpasses the level of a single universe!"
"Could it be... that you're a multiverse-level being?"
"No, that's impossible!"
Just as his shocked words fell, ordinary people on Earth like Tony weren't too fazed—they didn't really understand what it meant.
But at Kamar-Taj, the Ancient One and Doctor Strange exchanged glances and gasped sharply.
Multiverse-level?!
In their eyes, only the Vishanti—the Triad who backed Kamar-Taj—could ever reach that realm.
The Vishanti were known as guardians of the multiverse.
Besides them, there was also Cyttorak and a few other entities they knew of who transcended single-universe boundaries.
These beings were unimaginably rare. Each of them was incomprehensibly powerful—terrifying, even.
Yet now, a Celestial had declared that this man in white had exceeded the single-universe level and stepped into the multiverse realm?
How could that be?
As everyone grappled with shock and disbelief, the demon gods across various dimensions were no less stunned.
"Multiverse-level?"
Dormammu, the ruler of the Dark Dimension, was utterly dumbfounded.
This kind of power utterly eclipsed his own!
How could this white-robed man possess such might?
Not just him—Mephisto, Lucifer, and other great beings shared the same feeling in their hearts.
In the Omnipotence City, gods like Zeus all gasped in horror.
Meanwhile—
Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and the World Devourer were all dumbfounded.
"Multiverse-level?"
They were nearly frozen in disbelief.
No one understood more than they did what it truly meant to be multiverse-level.
But now, their youngest brother... had reached that level?
While they were still reeling, the Celestial Judge Arishem was overcome with despair.
"A proper Creator God should never grow in strength this fast!"
His hopelessness deepened, and he shouted, "You're a monster!"
...
Outside the solar system—
Looking down upon the solar system from afar, the white-robed figure, Syd, was eerily calm.
A voice echoed—mysterious, as if it were the truth of the cosmos.
"Looks like today is your day to die."
Hearing the very words he himself had once uttered, Arishem's heart filled with bitter resentment.
Syd, still gazing at the Celestials' pitiful state—sensing their unwillingness, terror, despair, and hatred—didn't say a word.
He simply ended it.
In the next instant, golden beams composed of light, heat, and abstract concepts surged forth and pierced through the Celestials.
"No!"
"Spare us!"
Arishem and the others screamed in agony.
As their bodies rapidly dissolved under the golden light, their hearts were consumed with hatred and despair.
But no matter how much they screamed or resented it, the result was the same: they faded into nothingness.
Soon, silence returned to the solar system.
All the Celestials that had appeared were now gone.
With the Celestials dealt with, Syd had no intention of lingering. His abstract form dissolved into beams of light and disappeared beyond the solar system.
Watching him vanish—whether it was the countless humans on Earth, the dimension gods, or the divine pantheons, or even beings like Eternity—they were all left in stunned silence.
That was it?
That fast?
Back in the Dark Dimension—
"The Celestials were actually killed off just like that?"
"That white-robed freak is a monster!" Dormammu growled, fear gripping his heart. He immediately shrank back and did everything he could to hide, terrified that the white-robed one might notice him.
He didn't even dare to respond to his own worshippers on Earth anymore.
As countless beings were discussing the event—
In a quiet corner of New York, Syd reappeared.
After glancing around, he fell into thought and muttered to himself, "Finally took care of that nuisance."
That Celestial Judge Arishem was finally dead!
But...
"I just don't know if the deaths of these Celestials will attract attention from others outside this universe..."
After pondering a while, he didn't dwell on it.
Whatever came, he would face it.
The most important thing now—was to keep getting stronger.
As long as his strength kept rising, what could the Celestials do to him?
With that in mind, Syd immediately began using his Dreamwalking Technique.
His consciousness split apart and traveled to countless unknown universes, gathering experiences and then returning.
At the same time, Self-Born Eternal was at work, lighting up universe after universe like tiny points of light.
Syd noticed the efficiency of Self-Born Eternal growing at a remarkable rate.
Realizing this, his anticipation surged.
Before long, the speed at which Self-Born Eternal lit up universes would reach a staggering level—spreading like a virus!
And when that time came—
"That will be when I truly become multiverse-level!"
Syd whispered to himself.
Of course, imitating God might also help him reach that step even faster.
(Unlock Progress: 39%)
With great anticipation, Syd continued lighting up universes while silently accumulating energy points.
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]...
Three hours passed, and his energy point count shifted.
[Energy Points: 21.53 million]
Unable to resist, Syd dumped them all into unlocking progress.
The next moment, the progress bar changed.
(Unlock Progress: 48%)
Syd's eyes gleamed with hope.
But to his disappointment, the expected system notification didn't come.
"Does it need 50% or more?"
He sighed and could only continue stockpiling energy points and sending his consciousness across universes, supporting Self-Born Eternal's mission to ignite more worlds.
1,100 universes...
1,200 universes...
As Self-Born Eternal grew stronger, its universe-ignition speed increased dramatically.
The torrent of energy from over a thousand universes surged into him, making him vastly more powerful than before.
At the same time, Universe-616, being anchored to him, also grew several times stronger.
By now, Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and the World Devourer had grown completely numb.
Feeling the strengthening of the universe, they had initially felt discomfort. Now, they were almost used to it.
Of course, they could tell what was causing it—the sheer abundance of light, heat, and positivity had grown overwhelming.
No matter how much they asked, their youngest brother never answered.
They could only continue to observe with suspicion and awe as the universe grew ever stronger.
Still, it wasn't all bad. Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion were pleasantly surprised to find their powers also increasing significantly.
As for the one exception—
The World Devourer was consumed with envy, practically wishing he could take Syd's place.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 622
chapters.content:
Chapter 622 - 622
As Syd continued gathering energy and lighting up universes—while countless beings were still discussing recent events...
Inside the Time Variance Authority—
Mobius and the others had also just witnessed the fall of Arishem and the rest of the Celestials.
Beyond feeling pity for Arishem and his kind, they were utterly shaken by the power displayed by the man in white.
"He's getting stronger?!"
"How is this happening?"
"How is he doing this?"
Whether it was Agent Mobius or the others, all were equally horrified and stunned as they watched the demise of so many powerful Celestials.
They had heard Tuolt's final words before his death too—
The man in white had possibly reached multiverse-level?
Their archives certainly contained records of such terrifying beings.
And just thinking about such entities made their scalps tingle and filled them with dread.
At that moment, a black-suited man in his thirties, named Patrick, said anxiously, "We can't let this white-clad man continue growing stronger—otherwise, the consequences will be unimaginable!"
As soon as he said this, a series of frightening images flashed through everyone's mind.
Syd's current strength had already surpassed the single-universe level and was suspected to have reached multiverse tier. If allowed to continue, there would be no more doubt—he would become multiversal.
And when that happened, the Time Variance Authority would definitely be in trouble.
They hadn't forgotten how many times they had offended him before. Once he became a true multiverse-level being, they might be the first target he'd eliminate.
That thought made Mobius and the others deeply uneasy.
Patrick scanned everyone's expression and suddenly said, "Let's prune the timeline of Universe 616."
"It's the only way to truly get rid of him."
Silence fell.
Mobius, Judge Renslayer, and the others exchanged looks.
Finally, they made their decision.
Even though the 616 universe was tied into the Sacred Timeline, they had no other choice now—they had to prune it.
Compared to preserving the 616 timeline, erasing this anomaly—the white-robed being—was far more important.
Once decided, they immediately ran to the timeline-pruning console and began operating it.
This time, they didn't even notify the Time Keepers.
A short while later, all eyes were fixed on a monitor.
A glowing thread representing the 616 timeline was slowly fading from existence.
Seeing this, they began to smile.
"It worked!"
"We finally got rid of that white-robed freak!"
They were ecstatic.
With the erasure of the 616 timeline, its entire universe would vanish. No matter how powerful that man was—once the timeline ceased, so would he.
As they stared at the screen in excitement and anticipation...
Meanwhile, in Universe 616—
On a remote, uninhabited part of Earth, Syd was seated with his eyes closed, performing Dreamwalking and assisting Self-Born Eternal in lighting more universes.
Suddenly, an inexplicable feeling surged in his heart, and his eyes snapped open.
"What's this?"
He sensed that something was wrong with the universe. It was... collapsing?
It was a familiar sensation—he had felt the same in Universe 838 when he seized the Darkhold, exploring the remnants of a shattered universe.
Immediately, his vast, abstract consciousness swept across the entire universe to probe deeper.
And the next second, he found it.
"The timeline?"
Someone was trying to erase the timeline of Universe 616?!
He instantly knew who was behind it.
The Time Variance Authority!
"I haven't even gone after you yet—and you dare come after me?"
Syd's gaze turned icy.
Ever since he had gained Self-Born Eternal, he had lost all fear of time-related powers. Even if the 616 timeline collapsed, he would remain unaffected.
At most, the rest of Universe 616 would fall apart—but the part that belonged to him would remain intact.
In a sense, he had already transcended time itself.
The TVA's threat level had dropped several tiers in his eyes. If not for the sake of caution, and needing to gather more power, he would have long since obliterated their entire headquarters with a single blow.
As he pondered this, he frowned.
Even though he wouldn't be harmed, Odin, Thor, Frigga, Tony, Logan—everyone he knew—would be doomed.
Everything familiar to him would disappear.
He would never allow the TVA to succeed.
Besides, something like this was... simple to deal with.
Syd muttered, "TVA... do you really think that if the timeline breaks, the universe must collapse?"
"Yes, under normal logic that's true. But..."
In the next instant, light erupted throughout the universe. Outside Earth, Syd's abstract concept body materialized.
Simultaneously, his material divine body on Earth dissolved into beams of light and merged with the abstract form.
His appearance stunned everyone on Earth.
They were bewildered not only by the strange change in their surroundings—but also by the sudden appearance of the white-robed man.
At the same time, Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and the World Devourer sensed something was wrong.
In the starry void—
The Silver Surfer stared in surprise as he saw the World Devourer's face contort in shock.
A second later, the devourer whispered in disbelief, "The universe is collapsing... what's going on?"
He tried to halt the process—only to realize, to his horror, that he couldn't.
The collapse felt... inevitable.
As panic set in, he too noticed the anomaly manifesting outside Earth—the arrival of his youngest brother.
"He's noticed it too?"
"Can he stop this?"
The World Devourer muttered anxiously.
Meanwhile, inside the TVA—
Mobius and the others were still monitoring 616 and had also seen the spectacle outside Earth.
Seeing the white-robed figure appear, Patrick and the others sneered, shaking their heads.
It was obvious that the man had noticed something was wrong and had come to intervene.
But would it work?
"The timeline's been erased. The collapse of 616 is guaranteed. No one can stop it."
"Not even you, White-Clad One!"
They spoke with smug certainty, waiting eagerly for the look of despair to appear on his face.
Unfortunately for them, his abstract concept face was cloaked in divine radiance—they couldn't see a thing.
Just as they were lamenting that—
They saw him slowly raise his right hand.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 623
chapters.content:
Chapter 623 - 623
Syd extended his right hand, and in that instant, a deep crimson glow of Chaos Magic lit up around it.
Boom!
Amidst the stunned gazes of countless beings, a terrifying surge of Chaos Magic erupted!
The next second, even the panicking World Devourer and other cosmic entities couldn't help but freeze in astonishment.
They could feel it—the universe's collapse... was stopping!
Inside the Time Variance Authority—
Patrick and the others, who had been excitedly awaiting the 616 universe's destruction, suddenly froze. Their expectant expressions turned stiff, their faces filled with disbelief.
"How is this possible?!"
They were completely stunned.
The collapse of the universe had actually stopped?
What did that white-robed man do? How could this happen?
They refused to believe it. The timeline had already been erased—how could the universe remain unaffected?
Then, all eyes locked onto Syd's right hand, and the crimson energy radiating outward.
"That's..."
"Did he rewrite the universe's reality?"
"He changed the logic that says: if the timeline collapses, the universe must collapse?"
How could something like this be possible?!
Mobius and the rest were utterly shaken.
Just then, they noticed something on their display screen: the time thread of the 616 universe—which had nearly vanished—was rapidly recovering!
This scene shocked them to the core.
They immediately began frantically operating the controls, trying to erase the 616 timeline again.
But to their horror, they discovered that their commands were no longer affecting the timeline at all.
"What... what's going on...?"
While panic and disbelief overtook them—
Back in the 616 Universe—
Drifting through the cosmos, the World Devourer sensed the universe's collapse halting, and couldn't help but exhale in relief.
Then, as he looked toward Earth and the dazzling white-robed figure hovering outside it, his face filled with wonder.
He could feel it clearly now—some of the universe's core logic had been altered.
This youngest brother of theirs... had rewritten reality?
"So this is his ability as a Creator God?"
"This kind of power... it's truly remarkable!"
The World Devourer was stunned.
He had once thought his little brother's powers were limited to controlling light—nothing too special. But now he saw that Syd could distort and rewrite the very fabric of reality itself?
That kind of power... was no joke!
"Was he trying to give us a surprise?"
"To think he hid such a terrifying ability from us?"
"If we hadn't found out now, we really would've been shocked when we met in a few days!"
The World Devourer smiled faintly to himself.
When they met up again, he planned to have Syd demonstrate this power for them in detail—just to see it firsthand.
But clearly, Syd's surprise had been spoiled.
The other four cosmic entities—Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion—were thinking the same.
Thankfully, they had found out in advance. Otherwise, they'd truly have been floored.
Syd's planned surprise had completely backfired.
The four laughed to themselves.
Outside Earth—
Looking over the now-stabilized universe, Syd withdrew his Chaos Magic-imbued right hand, without much surprise.
After all, when it came to altering reality, Chaos Magic had no issue handling this kind of situation.
Even if the logic was completely broken, Chaos Magic could simply rewrite it.
Now, thanks to the spell, the 616 universe's timeline had become... a mutation.
With the collapse crisis resolved, Syd turned his attention toward the Time Variance Authority.
"In a few hours... I'll deal with you."
Once he made further progress on mimicking God's abilities and unlocked another skill—gaining one more trump card—he would invade the TVA directly.
He was getting seriously fed up with those troublesome people. If not for Kang the Conqueror still being a wild variable, he'd have already crushed them long ago.
"Just as well... I'll use this time to visit Asgard."
Syd had made up his mind to head to Asgard—to help Thor and the others improve their strength.
After all, if they were too weak, they'd die at the drop of a hat, which would be troublesome to deal with.
If the TVA came knocking again, Thor and the rest wouldn't stand a chance.
With that thought, Syd's abstract divine body transformed into threads of light and vanished. A moment later, his physical divine body reappeared.
He waved his hand—and a golden portal to Asgard opened.
With a flicker, his figure drifted through and appeared in the skies above the realm of the gods.
He hadn't tried to hide his presence, so Heimdall sensed him immediately.
After Heimdall's notification, Thor and the others quickly got the message.
Soon, they emerged from the palace and gathered in Asgard's grand plaza.
Gazing up at the white-robed figure in the sky, Thor shouted joyfully, "Brother, you've finally returned to Asgard!"
Beside him, Odin frowned slightly. "What's going on?"
Under everyone's watchful gaze, Syd slowly descended and calmly said, "I've come to enhance your powers."
Surprise spread across their faces.
"Enhance our powers?"
"How?"
Both Odin and Thor looked confused and curious.
Without explaining, Syd simply extended his right hand and activated his Creation Power.
Instantly, mysterious divine energy spread and flowed toward Odin.
The aging All-Father—with white hair and a massive frame that had grown weak—suddenly felt a divine, incomprehensible energy envelop him.
Under this divine power, every flaw and hidden wound in his body was healed, and his decaying flesh was replenished with vitality.
Odin's eyes widened in disbelief as he removed his golden eyepatch.
Thor and the others were stunned as they saw a new eye rapidly grow in Odin's left socket.
Even his once-white hair darkened into a rich black, and the wrinkles on his face faded away—leaving behind a strong, youthful face.
In just a blink, he looked like a man in his early thirties again.
Seeing Odin's familiar, younger appearance, Frigga gasped in shock, her face filled with disbelief.
"Father?" Thor stood frozen beside her, completely dumbfounded.
Just moments ago, their father had been frail and aged—and now he was young again?
How was this even possible?
Thor turned to stare in awe at his floating, white-robed brother.
Then—
An overwhelming aura burst from Odin's rejuvenated body.
Now free of physical limitations, his power surged—surpassing even what it had been in his prime.
The godlike power of old... in the body of youth...
Feeling the divine strength coursing through him, Odin whispered in shock, "Such tremendous power..."
And just when he thought it was over, strands of familiar golden divine blood began to emerge inside his body.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 624
chapters.content:
Chapter 624 - 624
Strands of golden divine blood carrying a familiar aura surged into Odin's body, initiating a complete transformation—his Asgardian physiology was evolving into that of a true god.
"These blood traces... they carry Baldur's presence..."
Odin could feel his power soaring, and more astonishingly, he could no longer sense the limitation of mortality.
It felt as though... he had become immortal.
Realizing this, Odin stood there in stunned silence.
And at that moment, from the golden divine blood, a unique golden divine energy was born—its strength vastly superior to Odinforce itself.
With the birth of this divine power, Odin sensed that he had formed a connection to a great being—he could draw strength from it, just like the sorcerers of Kamar-Taj drew their magic from the Vishanti.
In that instant, Odin felt stronger than he had ever known. The Celestials he once fought in ancient times now seemed... insignificant.
He was utterly astonished.
Lifting his gaze toward the white-robed figure floating in the sky, Odin understood that it was all the work of Baldur—his youngest son.
Beside him, Thor asked curiously, "Father, how are you feeling?"
Everyone around turned their attention to Odin.
Sensing the tremendous power within himself, Odin said with reverence, "I feel like I could destroy the Celestials... with ease."
Thor and the others froze.
They all knew what the Celestials were.
Yet their father, Odin—no, now someone vastly beyond his former self—had just claimed he could kill them easily?
How strong had he become?
While they were still caught in shock and disbelief, Syd clenched his right hand, releasing a vast wave of Creation Power that washed over all of Asgard.
In an instant, all Asgardians began undergoing transformation.
The regular citizens gained incredible strength, with physicality on par with the Hulk or Thanos. Their lifespans were altered—they would now live forever, unless slain.
With just one move, Syd had elevated them from an alien race... into true gods.
As for Thor, Frigga, and the others—their bodies were transformed into divine forms, and they too received the same borrowed divine energy as Odin.
Even if the Dark Elves were to attack now, Frigga alone could annihilate them.
She wouldn't even have to move—their attacks couldn't pierce her defenses.
Simply releasing her divine aura would obliterate them all.
And she wasn't just physically empowered—Frigga had deep mastery of magic. Previously, she was limited by energy sources, but now, her magical prowess rivaled Agatha Harkness or even Doctor Strange.
It was just like Loki's case—once known as the Nine Realms' greatest sorcerer, he had become an assassin due to circumstance.
But in his true form, even a mere projection of Loki could overpower Doctor Strange, truly making him the Nine Realms' top mage.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Suddenly, golden lightning crackled across Thor's body. His eyes lit up, crackling with divine thunder.
Above Asgard, the sky turned dark—storm clouds gathered and roared.
Heimdall and the others, now more powerful than ever, looked at Thor in awe as an overwhelming aura pulsed from his body.
"Thor's power..."
"Why does it feel... terrifying?" said Fandral, one of the Warriors Three, his heart trembling with reverence.
"Hahaha! I'm invincible now!" Thor roared, golden lightning surging from his form. "Anyone want a fight? I feel like I could crush the world!"
"Uh—except for my brother, of course," he quickly added with a grin as he blurred forward.
BOOM!
A flash of thunder and he vanished, reappearing several hundred meters away in an instant.
Everyone gasped in disbelief at his display.
While they were still absorbing what had happened, Syd spoke again, "Your powers have all been enhanced. I'll return to Earth now. If anything happens, just pray to the light—I'll hear you."
He lifted his right hand.
A golden portal opened to Earth, and before anyone could say a word, Syd stepped through and vanished.
Thor froze. "Ah..."
He wanted to say something, but by the time the words formed, his brother was already gone.
His eyes were filled with a sense of loss.
The others—who had just moments ago been filled with excitement—suddenly fell quiet. As they stared at the portal closing, they couldn't shake the awe from their hearts.
In just a short while... they had become incredibly powerful.
All of it, every miraculous change, had been granted by their great Creator God—Baldur.
"His divine power is unimaginable... I can't even think of something He can't do."
"Unbelievable..."
Meanwhile, back on Earth—
In a quiet, uninhabited corner of America, Syd reappeared.
He fell into deep thought.
After a while, he murmured, "Alright... since I've helped Thor and the others, I might as well upgrade Magneto and Professor X too."
"But first... I should change outfits."
With a thought, his appearance shifted—the white robe darkened into black, taking the shape of the Messiah's attire.
The next second, an image of Xavier's School surfaced in his mind—and he activated spatial teleportation.
A spatial ripple emerged—and in the blink of an eye, he appeared above the Xavier Institute.
Before long, students from the school noticed him.
"Is that the Messiah?"
"Why is he here?"
"It's been ages since he last appeared—what is he doing here now?"
Iceman Bobby and others were shocked.
Even while still processing it, they quickly began calling for the others.
Soon, Professor X, Wolverine, Cyclops, Jean Grey, and even Rogue—who had recently escaped from a lab—all emerged and gathered in the courtyard, gazing up at the black-clad figure floating above.
"Syd?" Wolverine shouted with a grin. "Where've you been? No word from you for ages!"
Beside him, Chris—the first mutant Syd had met—added, "Yeah, where did you go? You didn't run into any trouble, did you?"
"What brings you to the school?" Professor X asked, eyeing him curiously.
Syd shook his head and said plainly, "I'm here to upgrade Professor X's powers."
Hearing this, Charles and everyone else looked confused.
Syd didn't bother explaining.
Instead, he focused his attention squarely on Professor X... staring for a few moments at that famously bald head.
(End of Chapter)
