chapters.title: Chapter 625
chapters.content:
Chapter 625 - 625
[900PS!!]
Syd remained thoughtful.
Come to think of it, both the main universe's Professor X and the one from Universe 838 had had their powers nerfed.
In the comics, the Cerebro amplifier had already been transformed into a portable model.
That meant that when Professor X traveled, he would wear the cerebral amplifier as a kind of helmet—essentially making him a Level 5 mutant at all times.
But in the movie universes, that portable helmet version simply didn't exist.
If the Professor X from Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (the 838 universe) had access to that helmet, then Wanda likely wouldn't have been able to massacre the Illuminati so easily.
The Professor with Cerebro and the one without it—were two completely different beings in terms of power.
As he thought, Syd slowly raised his right hand and activated his Creation Power.
Under the gaze of Professor X and the others, a blue helmet marked with an X symbol gradually formed in his hand.
Seeing the helmet, everyone around showed surprise and confusion.
"What's that?"
"A helmet?"
"The Messiah just created a helmet?"
"Since when could he do that?!"
They were full of bewilderment and curiosity. What exactly had the Messiah gone through during his absence? Where had this new ability come from?
For a while now, many had believed the white-clad man had surpassed the Messiah—but now they weren't so sure.
The Messiah still exuded a mysterious aura—shrouded in fog, impossible to fully understand.
Facing their puzzled gazes, Syd calmly explained, "This is a portable Cerebro. You can wear it at all times. It doesn't require a Cerebro chamber."
Everyone went silent.
A moment later, they understood the weight of his words.
Iceman Bobby and the other students immediately gasped.
"A Cerebro... you can wear all the time?"
"That's so broken!"
"Oh my god..."
They all knew just how terrifying Professor X's powers were with Cerebro. Now that he could have that power anytime?
Syd's thoughts stirred again—he activated spatial transfer.
In front of everyone's eyes, the helmet in his hand flashed, and in the next moment, it appeared in Professor X's hands.
Seeing this, Wolverine grinned, "C'mon, Charles. Try it on!"
The students around him all nodded wildly.
Taking a deep breath, Professor X placed the blue X-helmet onto his head under everyone's watchful gaze.
The next instant, he was stunned. His mind expanded infinitely, and he could feel... everything.
Every mutant and human mind across Earth became visible to his mental senses.
But more than that—Professor X felt something different.
His psychic power had... evolved. He had gained new abilities.
"I think... I have new powers?" Charles said, stunned.
Everyone froze.
Floating above them, Syd's expression grew contemplative.
He had created the helmet based on its comic version, even adding enhancements of his own.
So the Professor's new power made sense.
A moment later, Syd's voice echoed in their minds.
"Your current psychic ability should allow you to peer into a person's soul—to copy their memories, thoughts, and essence."
"If you find a way to create physical bodies, you could embed souls into those shells—bringing back deceased mutants with their memories intact."
In the comics, a few powerful mutants had created self-sustaining bodies, while Professor X copied souls and minds to resurrect countless mutants.
Of course, this wasn't the comics universe. Here, no such mutant team existed—so creating bodies would likely rely on cloning technology. Only then could Professor X achieve resurrection.
Whether or not those clones would have problems—or if the resurrection was truly a resurrection—was still unclear.
It might just be... recreating someone from scratch.
The moment he finished speaking, Professor X and the others were stunned.
"Bringing back the dead?"
"That's something only a god could do..."
Now, Professor X had that power?
Even if just a portion—it was enough to leave them breathless.
"This helmet... is way too powerful..."
Their gazes turned from the helmet... to the figure floating in black above them.
They hadn't forgotten—this device was created by the Messiah.
Even Professor X looked up in shock at the being in the sky.
Without responding, Syd simply extended his right hand again—silently modifying Professor X's body.
In a flash, Charles felt his entire body lighten.
And for good reason—Syd had altered his lifespan using Creation Power.
Though his appearance remained unchanged, his body had been freed from decay.
Ignoring the Professor's stunned expression, Syd turned his attention to Wolverine.
As one of the few familiar faces, he certainly hadn't forgotten Logan.
Since he was helping Professor X, he might as well help Wolverine too.
Seeing the Messiah's gaze fall on him, Logan tensed instinctively and tried to speak. "Syd—"
But before he could finish, Syd activated his Creation Power.
A surge of divine energy wrapped around the adamantium in Logan's body.
Instantly, the adamantium began to transform—from metal... into bone cells.
But despite becoming cellular in nature, the adamantium retained all of its original properties—remaining indestructible.
Even more, these cells now carried regeneration factors.
As a bonus, Syd used Creation Power to enhance Wolverine's healing factor.
And it worked—perfectly.
Based on his assessment, Syd concluded that with this level of regeneration, even if only a single cell remained, Logan could eventually regenerate completely.
More importantly, the adamantium bone-cells were nearly impossible to destroy.
This essentially made him... immortal.
As the transformation finished, everyone around could sense the change. Logan even looked visibly younger.
"Logan, you..." Scott narrowed his eyes. The more he looked, the more he saw the change.
"I..." Logan clenched his fist. His entire body felt lighter. The burden he'd always carried—gone.
He bounced on his feet a few times and was shocked.
His once-heavy adamantium body... now weighed nothing at all?
"Syd... this was you?"
"What did you do to me?"
Logan stared up at the floating man in black, awe and disbelief in his eyes.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 626
chapters.content:
Chapter 626 - 626
[1000PS!]
"My body..."
"Syd, what did you do?"
Logan asked in shock.
Syd shook his head without answering, his gaze shifting to Chris, who stood beside Logan.
Chris was the first mutant he met after escaping from the lab—naturally, he hadn't forgotten him.
On his right hand, the power of Creation surged forth.
In Syd's mind, the X-gene profile of the Black King surfaced.
The next moment, Chris's X-gene began to transform—shifting toward the gene structure of the Black King.
Chris felt a warm sensation flood through his body, as if something had changed, though he couldn't quite explain what.
Noticing Syd's gaze, Chris quickly realized that this change must be Syd's doing.
Before he could even ask, the transformation completed.
Syd calmly said, "I need to go to Magneto next—strengthen his abilities."
"I'm off."
With that, he manipulated the abstract conceptual divine body and marked both Professor X and Chris.
As long as they were in mortal danger, the divine body would pour divine power into them and provide assistance.
Once everything was in place, spatial ripples appeared and Syd vanished from the skies above Xavier's School.
Watching his swift departure, Professor X and the others were left stunned.
Especially Logan and Chris—they hadn't even had time to ask Syd what he had done to them.
"How do you guys feel?" Cyclops Scott asked curiously.
Chris and Logan exchanged a glance and saw the same look of confusion in each other's eyes.
Both of them shook their heads.
Seeing this, Hank—covered in blue fur and towering like a beast—rubbed his chin thoughtfully and said, "Let's head to the lab. I'll run a few tests."
Logan and Chris agreed without hesitation and followed him.
Jean Grey and the others, driven by curiosity, also tagged along to see what changes had occurred in the two.
A few minutes later, they arrived at the lab.
Under Hank's arrangement, Logan and Chris stood beneath a series of diagnostic machines.
Once all the scans were complete, Chris asked eagerly, "Well? What did you find?"
Everyone turned their eyes toward Hank.
He stared at the monitor, stunned, his expression growing more and more shocked by the second.
"Messiah... he..." Hank muttered in disbelief.
He couldn't help but explain, "Logan, the adamantium in your body has mutated. And Chris, your X-gene has undergone significant changes!"
As he spoke, he brought up a series of data and began explaining the transformations they had undergone.
Everyone was dumbfounded by his report.
After several rounds of testing, they finally figured out what had happened.
The adamantium in Logan's body had mutated into a form of osseous cells, and his healing factor had grown unimaginably powerful.
As for Chris, his transformation was just as startling.
In addition to his original mutant powers, he had now acquired a second ability—
The energy absorption power of the Black King!
Professor X, who had personally experienced the Black King's power, understood better than anyone just how terrifying it was.
Unknowingly, the lab fell into silence.
"How did the Messiah do this?" Cyclops Scott muttered in shock. "He actually has such a power?"
"This kind of matter and gene-altering ability..."
"Doesn't that mean he can casually create mutants? And even wield countless mutant abilities himself?"
"How is that any different from being a god?"
Until just now, he had always thought that compared to the White-Clad Hero, the Messiah—despite being a super Omega-level mutant—was far inferior.
After all, one had become a Creator God, and the other was just a super Omega mutant. How could the two be placed on equal footing?
But now, Scott suddenly realized he may have completely underestimated the Messiah and never truly seen the extent of his power.
This ability to alter matter and genes could fully qualify as a super Omega-level power!
Not to mention, Syd still had many other unknown abilities.
Messiah was like a figure wrapped in layers of mist—mysterious and impossible to see through.
Scott even began to feel the illusion that Messiah might be as powerful as the White-Clad Hero.
As he sat stunned, Logan and the others were also overwhelmed with emotion.
At that moment, Iceman Bobby muttered the thought lingering in everyone's hearts.
"Could it be that the Messiah is no weaker than the White-Clad Hero? Maybe even on par with a Creator God?"
With those words, silence once again fell upon the room as everyone looked at each other in disbelief.
"No way... right?"
"That's a bit much!"
They were filled with doubt and anxiety.
Even after a long discussion, they couldn't come to a conclusion—only that the Messiah was cloaked in mystery, impossible to decipher.
There was, however, one more thing that concerned them.
"When he left, didn't he say he was going to find Magneto to enhance his powers?"
The thought sent chills down their spines. They couldn't even imagine what Magneto would become after his powers were strengthened.
Magneto had always been regarded as a dangerous extremist among mutants—X-Men had clashed with him more than once.
Still, they had to admit one thing—Magneto only targeted humans. He rarely harmed fellow mutants, and even when provoked by other mutants, he usually just taught them a lesson.
Otherwise, the X-Men would have been wiped out long ago...
Now, they were torn between fear and curiosity—what would Magneto become with Messiah's enhancement?
To what extent could the Messiah transform him?
At this moment—
Chris, surrounded by the others, seemed to recall something. A hesitant expression appeared on his face as he said, "There's something I need to tell you all... about the Messiah."
His voice echoed in the lab, catching Professor X and the others off guard.
What could he be so serious about?
Something regarding the Messiah?
...
While Scott and the others were full of curiosity and confusion—
Syd, guided by his abstract divine body, located the Brotherhood of Mutants' base.
Spatial ripples formed, and he activated his teleportation.
In the blink of an eye, he appeared in the skies above the Brotherhood's stronghold.
Before long, his presence was noticed by the Brotherhood members—Toad and the other mutants.
They looked up in unison.
"That's... Messiah?!"
"What's he doing here?"
"Quick, alert Magneto!"
Toad and the others only needed one glance to recognize him. Their scalps went numb, and it felt like their souls were about to leave their bodies.
No matter who it was, no matter how stubborn before—none of them dared to act rashly. They quickly scrambled into the base to find Magneto.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 627
chapters.content:
Chapter 627 - 627
A few minutes later, Magneto—helmeted and cloaked—walked out from the Brotherhood base.
Standing among the crowd, he looked up at the figure in black floating in the sky and exclaimed with emotion, "Child, have you come to see me?"
"Are you ready to join the Brotherhood of Mutants?"
"Come, child. Only with us—the Brotherhood—will you find your true home!"
Hearing Magneto's impassioned words, Syd twitched at the corner of his mouth and shook his head.
"I didn't come here to join the Brotherhood of Mutants."
Magneto's face subtly changed, a hint of disappointment flickering across his features. "Then... what for?"
Toad, Sabretooth, and the others nearby looked just as puzzled.
Instead of answering, Syd descended slowly and began walking in circles around Magneto, carefully observing him.
Toad and the others instantly tensed, suspecting Syd might be planning something hostile.
But Magneto waved them off. "Relax," he said, puzzled. "Is there something wrong with me?"
As he continued his circling, Syd calmly asked, "Your ability is to control metal, right?"
Magneto blinked, confused by the question. "Yes... is there a problem?"
Toad and the others were just as baffled. Wasn't this common knowledge?
Under their watchful gazes, Syd continued circling him and said in a calm tone, "Your power should be to control magnetic fields—one of the four fundamental forces of the universe: electromagnetism. So why are you limited to just controlling metal?"
Magneto froze, momentarily stunned.
At that moment, information about Magneto surfaced in Syd's mind, and the reason became clear.
As he pieced it together, Syd explained, "There's a kind of invisible restraint in your mind—subconscious programming, if you will—that convinces you you can only control metal."
"This subconscious limit restricts your power, making it so you can only manipulate magnetic forces through metal."
Magneto stared at Syd, stunned.
In his understanding, Messiah was known for his overwhelming power—but he hadn't expected the man to understand his ability in such depth.
What Syd said next left them even more shocked.
"If you can break through that restraint," Syd said slowly, "you'll undergo a secondary mutation. Your power will truly awaken—and no longer be limited to just metal..."
Syd recalled that mutants could undergo secondary mutations—a phenomenon where their powers evolved or amplified significantly.
It could be triggered by external stimulation, such as drugs, or simply by further mutation of the X-gene.
This could lead to anything from new powers to massive boosts in existing ones—or even physical transformations.
For instance, Beast—originally just a mutant with incredible speed and agility—underwent a secondary mutation that made him regress into a blue-furred, muscular creature with claws and fangs.
Kitty Pryde may have experienced similar changes, gaining the ability to phase people's consciousness through objects.
Even the Black King experienced this—after his secondary mutation, he could absorb not just energy, but even psychic powers, making him nearly invincible in all aspects.
Unfortunately, he died too early.
Syd reflected, "My own energy absorption ability... could that count as a secondary mutation too?"
It was a subtle concept—he might've overlooked it altogether if not for Magneto's issue.
As he pondered, Magneto and the others looked at him with shock.
"Not limited to metal?" Magneto muttered, stunned.
He had always believed that controlling metal was the extent of his power—but now, he realized there might be more?
Controlling magnetic fields?
With trembling breath and a look of longing in his eyes, Magneto instinctively tried activating his power.
A distant piece of metal floated into the air...
He clenched his fists, focusing with all his strength to control something other than metal.
But no matter how hard he tried—no matter how he willed or convinced himself—he could only manipulate metal. He simply couldn't achieve what Messiah described: control of the magnetic field itself.
Toad, Sabretooth, and the others watched with growing doubt.
"Is Messiah really telling the truth?"
"Could he be messing with Magneto?"
Syd heard their whispers clearly and gave them a sidelong glance.
Magneto, now visibly disheartened, stopped trying. With a sigh of disappointment, he said, "I can't do it..."
Syd wasn't surprised.
If it were that easy, Magneto would've figured it out by now—and become unstoppable.
Secondary mutations were extremely difficult to achieve and typically required external help. In X-Men: Apocalypse, for example, Magneto only achieved it after being enhanced by Apocalypse.
At that time, his powers changed drastically. The environment around him would distort under his influence—clear signs of magnetic field manipulation.
Whole cities crumbled under his power. Matter disintegrated and floated into the sky—he was a true force of nature.
But aside from that one encounter with Apocalypse, he was never able to replicate that feat.
If he had been able to, even a plastic prison wouldn't have been able to hold him. Nothing would've.
With these thoughts swirling, Syd looked at the dispirited Magneto and calmly said, "I can help you."
Magneto, looking like he had aged several years in mere moments, paused—stunned. His eyes widened as he looked up at the floating Messiah. "Help me? You can help me undergo secondary mutation?"
His voice was filled with disbelief.
Could Messiah really do that?
Not only Magneto—Toad and the others were equally shocked.
Without saying more, Syd raised both hands.
On his right hand, the power of Creation activated.
A mysterious force enveloped Magneto, strengthening the X-gene within him.
On his left, red-shrouded Chaos Magic activated—targeting Magneto's mind, twisting and rewriting his subconscious.
A silent hum echoed.
In that moment, the mental restraints holding Magneto back shattered.
Magneto's expression turned dazed as he felt something change within—both physically and mentally.
"I..."
He lifted his hands, staring blankly at them.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 628
chapters.content:
Chapter 628 - 628
Under the power of Creation, Magneto's X-gene was rapidly enhanced, and with the influence of Chaos Magic, the invisible restraints in his mind were utterly shattered.
Syd even used his Creation ability to discreetly extend Magneto's lifespan.
"I... right now..."
Watched closely by Toad and the others, Magneto slowly raised his hands and stared at them in a daze.
A moment later, he tentatively activated his mutant ability.
Under the astonished gazes of Toad and the others, he floated into the air, ripples like waves forming around his body.
In the next instant, countless materials on the ground rose into the air, and nearby buildings began to disassemble inch by inch.
In a blink, a wide swath of structures was heavily damaged, and a massive amount of debris floated in the sky, blocking out the sun.
Even worse, an unintentional electromagnetic pulse released during Magneto's manipulation of the magnetic field swept across the city—paralyzing countless electronic devices.
"Oh my God!"
"What's going on?!"
Cries of alarm echoed across the city.
Fortunately, Magneto snapped out of it just in time and hurriedly deactivated his power. Otherwise, the entire city might have collapsed within minutes.
Staring at the buildings he had inadvertently destroyed and the masses of floating debris still suspended in the air, Magneto muttered in shock, "This... this is my power?"
Feeling this almost omnipotent strength, even he couldn't help but feel intoxicated.
"I think I could destroy a city with ease now..." he whispered to himself.
While Magneto was lost in thought, Toad, Sabretooth, and the others were completely dumbfounded.
"Lord Magneto?!"
"What terrifying power..."
The sight before them filled their hearts with dread. It was now painfully clear how powerful Magneto had become after being transformed by Messiah.
It was simply unbelievable.
Their eyes flickered between Magneto and Messiah, their hearts shaken.
Never mind Magneto—Messiah actually had the ability to grant such power to others?
Suddenly, their gazes toward Messiah became heated with desire.
"If only Messiah could help us too..."
Just imagining it made their hearts pound with anticipation.
Meanwhile, Syd ignored the blazing stares of Toad and the others, keeping his eyes on Magneto and the floating debris overhead.
He wasn't surprised at Magneto's display of city-destroying power.
After all, even Apocalypse's enhancement had allowed Magneto to do something similar. With both Creation and Chaos Magic involved, it was expected that the result would be even more terrifying.
And this was just the beginning of Magneto's secondary mutation. He hadn't even fully mastered his new powers yet.
Once he did...
Syd hesitated slightly. Did I just unleash a monster?
With his current strength, Magneto might very well be capable of establishing an entire nation for mutants.
But he quickly shook his head, brushing the thought aside.
"Not my problem. If there's trouble, it's the American government's mess to clean up."
He didn't care what happened to the U.S.
Besides, with Professor X and the others around, Magneto probably wouldn't do anything too crazy.
...Hopefully.
Not thinking further on it, Syd turned his attention back to Magneto and said, "Now that your secondary mutation is complete, I'll be leaving."
He was about to depart when Magneto suddenly called out, "Wait!"
Syd paused and turned to look at him, curious to hear what he wanted to say.
Magneto's expression was incredibly complicated.
Staring at Messiah not far away, and feeling the immense power now coursing through his body, he couldn't help but ask, "Why did you help me?"
Toad, Sabretooth, Mystique, and the others were also filled with confusion.
Under their expectant gazes, Syd answered calmly, "No reason. I just felt like it."
That left them all speechless.
Just felt like it? Was it really that casual?
As they stood there dumbfounded, Syd added, "Anyway, I'm leaving now."
With matters concerning both Professor X and Magneto taken care of, it was time for him to return and continue using Dreamwalking to light up the universe and gather energy points to accelerate his path to the multiverse level.
In the next second, he activated spatial transference. As the ripples spread, he vanished from sight right before their eyes.
Staring at the spot where he disappeared, Magneto's gaze grew even more conflicted.
Sigh... if only he'd agreed to join the Brotherhood.
He felt a pang of regret.
At the same time, he couldn't help but marvel at Messiah's ability.
To grant someone a secondary mutation at will?
In just a brief moment, his power had skyrocketed to the point of being able to annihilate a city. The boost was simply unimaginable.
So then... how powerful was Messiah himself?
While Magneto was deep in thought, Mystique—Raven—rushed over and warned, "Erik, the government's definitely detected the anomaly here. We need to leave!"
Magneto blinked.
The massive commotion surely alerted government agencies. In fact, they'd probably already pinpointed their location.
Out of instinct, and following his old habits, his first thought was to evacuate.
After all, they weren't like Messiah or the White-Clad Hero—who could fly boldly over cities without fear of retaliation from the American government.
Every mutant in the Brotherhood was precious and couldn't be risked unnecessarily.
But then... Magneto paused.
He suddenly realized something.
After Messiah's transformation, he wasn't the same anymore.
A wicked grin crept onto his face.
"Why should we run?"
Raven and the others were stunned.
...
While Magneto and his group were still discussing, back at Xavier's School, Professor X and the others were frozen in disbelief.
Moments earlier, after Messiah left, Chris had said he had something to tell them about him.
At first, no one took it seriously—but once Chris hesitated and then spoke up, they were left completely dumbfounded.
"Chris, what did you say? Syd is the child of Professor X and Magneto?" Logan asked, stunned.
"Chris, man, that's not even funny!"
Logan was speechless. His first reaction was to think Chris was joking.
After all—what sane person would believe something that absurd?
Messiah is the child of Professor X and Magneto?
Hah...
Even Professor X himself, Charles, couldn't help but chuckle helplessly. "Chris, that's quite the joke..."
Everyone was expecting Chris to admit he was just kidding.
But instead, Chris shook his head solemnly and said with great seriousness, "I'm not joking. It's true."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 629
chapters.content:
Chapter 629 - 629
[1100PS!]
Chris began explaining slowly.
As he spoke, Logan and the others were left in a daze—especially Professor X, Charles, who was completely dumbfounded.
"Messiah... has both my and Erik's genes?"
His thoughts spiraled into confusion.
Even though his relationship with Erik was quite close, the idea that the two of them had somehow produced a child together left him stunned.
And that child was none other than Messiah—the terrifying super Omega-level mutant who had shocked and awed him so many times!
How could this be?
It took the group a long while before they finally recovered.
"If this is true," Cyclops Scott asked hesitantly, "should we tell Magneto?"
Uhh...
Everyone looked at each other, uncertain.
Professor X's face flushed slightly, and he stammered, "Let's... let's wait. We'll tell Erik after we've investigated it more thoroughly."
Just as he was about to say more, a mutant student burst into the lab, panting as he called out, "Professor, check the latest news!"
Startled, the group turned toward the tablet the student was holding.
On the news feed, a section of a city was shown—buildings collapsing, debris floating in the air.
The terrifying footage stunned them all.
"What's going on?"
"What happened?"
The student hesitated and then said, "It... it seems to be Magneto."
As he spoke, he adjusted the video feed, revealing the figure of Magneto, Erik.
He hovered in midair, ripples of energy surging around him, with an enormous field of floating debris—stones, building fragments, and more—circling him like a storm.
"Magneto did this?"
Staring at the footage, Professor X and the others couldn't believe their eyes.
When did Magneto become this powerful?
He could control so much at once?
Most importantly, they could clearly see that it wasn't just metal he was manipulating. Stones, rubble, entire sections of buildings—all of it hovered in the air under his influence.
How was that possible?
"Wasn't Magneto only able to control metal? How is he manipulating all this?"
They even watched, frame by frame, as an entire building disintegrated and floated upward.
The concrete debris, bricks, and non-metallic materials were also suspended.
As confusion set in, Scott suddenly remembered something.
"Didn't Messiah say earlier that he was going to enhance Magneto's abilities?"
That line snapped everyone to attention. Realization dawned.
"Messiah enhanced Magneto?"
Because of Messiah?
Looking again at the overwhelming force Magneto displayed in the footage, they could hardly believe it.
What kind of power was this?
A mere enhancement from Messiah... and Magneto had become this terrifying?
At that moment—
Looking at Professor X, Scott asked, "What should we do, Professor?"
All eyes turned toward Charles.
He hesitated, then said, "We're going to meet Magneto. I need to speak with him."
Logan and the others nodded in agreement, unsurprised by the decision.
Soon, they arrived at the X-Jet hangar. Jean Grey, Logan, Scott, Hank, Chris, and Professor X all boarded the black X-Jet.
The jet streaked across the sky.
...
While Logan and the others were en route, the American authorities were also mobilizing.
Teams of agents were dispatched toward Magneto's location.
Satellites locked onto the floating figure of Magneto, feeding live footage to military officials.
The U.S. military and intelligence agencies stared at the images in disbelief.
Was Magneto always this powerful?
Soon, a convoy of armored vehicles and field agents arrived at the scene.
On one vehicle, a middle-aged officer lifted a megaphone and shouted, "Magneto! What are you doing?"
"Stand down immediately!"
As he barked the order, the agents and soldiers beside him raised their plastic firearms, discreetly aiming at the figure floating in the sky.
Hovering above, Magneto fixed a cold gaze on them.
Their so-called threats meant nothing to him now.
If it had been before, he might've exercised caution. But after Messiah's enhancement, he had no need to fear them.
Just as he was about to act—
He suddenly sensed something and turned his gaze to the horizon.
A familiar aircraft was swiftly approaching.
The X-Jet?
"Charles?"
Frowning slightly, Magneto held back from striking the approaching military forces.
Meanwhile, the U.S. troops also noticed the new aircraft.
Uncertain of its origin, they held their fire.
Moments later, the X-Jet landed on a nearby open field.
The ramp descended, and Logan and the others—clad in their black X-suits—stepped out.
"Hmm?"
Magneto, still floating in midair, immediately noticed something strange.
That was... Charles?
Charles isn't in his wheelchair?
And... what's that he's wearing on his head?
As he watched Charles walk down from the X-Jet alongside Logan and the others, Magneto's mind reeled.
Without waiting for a response from the military, he floated over and looked down at Charles.
"Charles, your legs... they're healed?"
"How did that happen?"
Logan and the others tensed as Magneto approached.
But Professor X wasn't alarmed. Instead, he looked up at him and smiled gently.
"Messiah healed me."
Messiah?
Magneto blinked, stunned.
As the two spoke, more military vehicles rolled into position, surrounding them.
The dozens of agents, soldiers, and officers at the scene had also heard what Charles said.
"Messiah?"
These people... had dealings with Messiah?
They were stunned.
Among them, a thirty-something major named Pedro quickly pulled out a communicator and reported the situation to command.
On the other end, a stern male voice replied at once.
"Do not engage for now. Let's hear what they have to say."
Pedro's expression showed that he had expected as much. He wasn't surprised.
Both the White-Clad Hero and Messiah were taboo subjects to the military. If they could avoid provoking them, they would.
Putting away the communicator, Major Pedro fixed his gaze on Magneto and the others, ready to listen in on their conversation.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 630
chapters.content:
Chapter 630 - 630
[1200PS!]
"What are you doing here?"
Magneto frowned as he looked at Professor X and the others approaching from the X-Jet.
At his words, over a hundred agents, soldiers, and officers stationed in the distance tensed up, their eyes filled with curiosity and caution. No one knew what these newcomers intended.
All eyes shifted to Professor X's group, waiting to see how they would respond.
But instead of answering directly, Charles—wearing his cerebral amplifier helmet—countered with a question. "Erik, as I recall, your powers never reached this level before. What happened to you?"
He glanced up at the sky, at the countless objects swirling through the air under the influence of Magneto's magnetic field.
Magneto narrowed his eyes and didn't answer right away.
But before he could change the subject, Charles suddenly said something that froze him in place.
"Was it Messiah?"
"Did Messiah enhance your abilities?" Charles asked cautiously.
The moment the words left his mouth, Magneto's expression visibly changed. He frowned deeply. "Charles... how do you know about that?"
Everyone in the group stiffened.
"So it really was Messiah?"
"That power... I can't believe it. He really strengthened you to this extent?"
Even though they had guessed as much, hearing it confirmed still sent shockwaves through Cyclops and the others. They were amazed at both Magneto's sudden surge in power and Messiah's frightening ability to cause it.
Their reactions weren't the only ones.
The surrounding military officers, agents, and even the hidden government officials watching the situation from afar were equally stunned.
"Messiah?"
"Magneto suddenly became this powerful... because of Messiah?"
"Messiah enhanced Magneto's abilities?"
"How the hell is that even possible?!"
They all knew Magneto's prior power level well—yes, he was dangerous, but nothing like this. This was a whole different league.
And now, just from a single enhancement by Messiah, Magneto had become a monster of unimaginable might?
They didn't want to believe it.
Messiah had already been terrifying enough on his own—now he could give others that level of power?
Back on the scene, Magneto frowned again. "Charles, you still haven't answered my question."
"Messiah helped me too," Professor X said with a small smile, tapping the cerebral helmet on his head.
"That helmet?" Magneto asked, looking puzzled.
He had noticed it when Charles stepped off the X-Jet and had wondered why Charles would be wearing something like that.
Now, seeing Charles's expression, it was clear—this device had something to do with Messiah.
Charles nodded. "Messiah made it for me. It enhances my mental powers."
He cast a brief glance at the government agents nearby and decided not to say more. If he revealed everything, those people might panic.
Magneto nodded slightly. He was curious, but didn't press further. Instead, he shifted topics. "Then why are you here?"
"Erik, the damage you've done to this city is serious. Try not to hurt innocent people," Charles urged.
Lately, his outlook had changed. If Erik took action against the government or the military in defense of mutant rights, Charles could almost turn a blind eye.
But when innocent civilians were caught in the crossfire, he couldn't help but feel uneasy.
"Hmph. You're still too soft, Charles," Magneto replied coldly.
Charles didn't argue. He simply sighed and, after a moment's hesitation, said, "Erik, there's something important I need to tell you. It's about Messiah."
Magneto blinked. "What is it?"
Charles scanned the surroundings, noting the nearby agents. Then he released a powerful surge of psychic energy.
In an instant, over a hundred agents and soldiers were enveloped by it. Their eyes glazed over, and they stood motionless, their resistance completely suppressed.
Magneto's curiosity deepened. What could Charles possibly have to say that requires this level of secrecy?
Something about Messiah?
What?
Under his watchful gaze, Charles began slowly.
"Erik, Messiah... he..."
As the explanation continued, the curious expression on Magneto's face faded, replaced by shock and disbelief.
"Messiah is our child?" Magneto asked stiffly, his face rigid. "You're not joking?"
Charles nodded solemnly.
Seeing that, Magneto's eyes went wide. For a moment, he wasn't sure if he was hallucinating.
This is insane.
He and Charles... had a child?
And that child was Messiah?
The being who was practically a mutant god... was his son?
His mind went blank. He almost forgot how to think.
It took a while before he came back to himself. His heart raced, and after the initial shock passed, a sense of joy and realization began to settle in.
"So that's why Messiah helped me..."
Suddenly, everything made sense.
Magneto's expression shifted to one of deep regret. He was now kicking himself for not stopping Messiah from leaving.
At the same time, he wasn't sure how to face Messiah... or even Charles.
Seeing that Erik had come back to his senses, Charles silently released the agents from his psychic hold.
Major Pedro and the others blinked, momentarily dazed—but none of them noticed anything had happened.
Magneto noticed too—but at this point, he had no interest in those people.
In fact, his earlier desire to unleash his power and teach them a lesson had completely vanished.
He said in a low voice, "Charles, I need to go somewhere to clear my head."
And with that, he turned and flew off, intending to leave the area.
But just as he took off, Major Pedro called out loudly, "Wait, Magneto!"
"You haven't given us an explanation! You activated your powers without warning and caused major damage to the city—!"
As he started to deliver a threat, Magneto suddenly stopped in mid-air and turned his icy gaze toward them.
Then he slowly raised his right hand.
Seeing this, Major Pedro's heart sank. A terrible feeling crept over him, and he shouted, "Open fire, now!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 631
chapters.content:
Chapter 631 - 631
Agents and soldiers all raised their plastic guns, preparing to shoot at Magneto.
However, they were already too late—and even if they had plastic guns, it was useless.
Erik, had discovered that he could not only control magnetic fields but also generate magnetic fields in any object.
That meant, even plastic, or things that typically had no magnetic field, could now be controlled by him!
He even vaguely sensed that through magnetism, he was touching upon the Grand Unified Theory—possibly even influencing gravity itself.
Feeling this power surge, Erik couldn't help but marvel at the strength granted by the Messiah ability.
From the ground near Major Pedro and the others, chunks of stone suddenly floated into the air and then shot forward like lightning.
It all happened so quickly that Pedro and the others had no time to react. In an instant, the stone bullets pierced straight through their chests.
"Ahhh—!"
Blood splattered as screams filled the air.
And it didn't stop there. Countless objects floating in the sky suddenly shifted direction and launched toward them like a storm.
Before Professor X and the others could react, Pedro and his men were swallowed by the barrage.
The whole thing took only two or three seconds—then everything fell silent.
As dust settled over the corpses of Pedro and his team, Professor X and the others stood stunned.
Too fast. Far too fast. They had no time to stop it. Pedro and the rest were dead just like that.
"Erik, you..." Professor X began, shocked, trying to speak.
Magneto coldly cut him off. "Charles, stop being so merciful. Only by showing strength will they respect and take us seriously."
With that, he disappeared into the horizon.
Watching him vanish, Professor X sighed deeply. With no other choice, he and Logan returned to the X-Mansion.
But though they left, the incident's consequences had only just begun.
News stations everywhere began reporting on it, triggering intense public backlash among ordinary people.
...
Elsewhere—
Syd was still using Dreamwalking, splitting his consciousness and traveling across universes. Thanks to the Eternal Attribute, he became a primordial creator god in every universe he entered.
As for what happened with Magneto—that wasn't his concern.
With the attention of abstract conceptual deities on them, neither Professor X nor Magneto could die. As for the soldiers and agents of the American military? He simply didn't care.
Ever since he escaped the lab, he had been hunted. No one except mutants ever helped him. If he didn't hold back his rage, he could have crushed the entire solar system. The fact he hadn't was already mercy.
Feeling the ever-growing power of his Eternal Attribute, Syd smiled. "Almost there... Multiversal level!"
Time passed slowly. Another three hours went by...
(Unlock Progress: 48%)
Unable to resist, Syd poured all his stored energy points into his progression.
As he watched with anticipation, the system prompt changed:
(Unlock Progress: 55%)
Seeing it reach 55%, Syd felt a twinge of disappointment—there was no prompt announcing a new power.
"Is it at 60% or 70%?"
Frowning, he sighed. He had to keep accumulating more.
Just as he was about to resume his efforts, something unexpected happened only half an hour later.
Syd sensed another anomaly in the universe.
He looked beyond Earth.
And he wasn't the only one. At that moment, Eternity, Infinity, Oblivion, Death, and Galactus also noticed something strange.
Even Earth's various space agencies, equipped with satellites and telescopes, gradually detected the anomaly.
"Oh my God!"
"What is that?!"
Astronomers and technicians were horrified to discover a massive new planet outside of Earth... slowly approaching!
The sight terrified nations across the world.
A new planet suddenly appeared in the solar system?
What was happening?!
And then came the shock.
After observing and analyzing the data, they realized that the approaching planet looked very familiar.
After cross-checking repeatedly, with increasing dread, they found the probability was over 90%...
It looked exactly like Earth!
...
S.H.I.E.L.D.
"How can another Earth just appear out of nowhere?"
Staring at the image on the monitor, Nick Fury's brow furrowed deeply. A deep unease churned inside him.
The strange new Earth was drawing closer. He couldn't even begin to imagine what might happen when it arrived.
His gut told him—this was bad. Very bad.
He immediately reached for the pager to contact Captain Marvel, requesting her assistance.
While chaos spread across every department on Earth, in a quiet corner, Syd already knew what was happening.
Staring at the approaching Earth, he muttered:
"A Universe Collision Event?!"
He had actually anticipated this.
As for why a duplicate Earth appeared in such an event—he understood that too.
The root cause of the Universe Collision Event was the imprint he left in another universe, which created an attractive force between the two.
Or rather, their timelines were being drawn together and overlapping.
Timelines exist in higher dimensions. When they intersect, it's nearly impossible for a universe to remain stable.
It was highly likely that both universes would be destroyed due to this overlap!
Worse yet, the collisions might trigger a chain reaction across other universes as well!
Syd pondered.
A Universe Collision Event was bound to be something the Avengers would face down the line.
In fact, the ending of Doctor Strange 2 already hinted at it.
As for why this kind of event always involved another Earth?
It was due to Earth's unique nature.
Because of various extraordinary factors, Earth could be considered the center of the universe. When problems arose, the first place where timelines collided was always Earth.
During such collision events, there was usually a short window—several hours—where the two Earths would briefly appear in each other's skies.
To resolve the situation, there were only two options:
Destroy the other Earth.
Or use the Infinity Stones.
In Universe 838, the Illuminati seemingly used all six Infinity Stones to forcibly push the other Earth and universe away, preserving their own reality.
However, the displaced universe wasn't so lucky. That universe lost trillions of lives.
Worse still, five of the six Infinity Stones shattered. The Time Stone vanished completely.
That was also why the Illuminati in Universe 838 eventually executed their version of Doctor Strange.
To defeat Thanos, he had studied the Darkhold and used Dreamwalking to travel across universes, leaving his mark and triggering a universe collision event. He had to be held accountable for the trillions who died.
Now, watching this approaching Earth, Syd fell into deep thought.
If he wasn't mistaken, this Earth belonged to the same universe the Avengers had recently traveled from.
In that universe, to defeat the Goddess of Death, he had actively summoned help from the main 616 universe—creating a link between the two, drawing them together.
"So... how should I deal with this?"
Syd pondered in silence.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 632
chapters.content:
Chapter 632 - 632
Syd pondered deeply on how to resolve the impending Universe Collision Event.
Use the Infinity Stones?
No—that wouldn't work. Using them would cause them to shatter, and he'd have to spend time recreating them...
Besides, even if the Infinity Stones were used, the universe where the Avengers from Endgame resided wouldn't escape unscathed.
That universe was still contributing power to him—destroying it would be a waste.
Shaking his head, Syd dismissed that option along with other shortcuts.
"Forget it. I'll just use the power of the Abstract Conceptual Deity Body to forcibly separate the two universes."
Just as he made that decision, the Earth in the universe of the Endgame Avengers also discovered the presence of Earth from Universe 616.
As they saw the slowly approaching Earth, Tony and the others were visibly shocked.
A vague sense of danger crept into their minds, and they quickly gathered the Avengers to discuss the situation.
"This Earth looks dangerous. What should we do about it?"
Tony and the rest exchanged glances before turning to Thor in the crowd.
"Thor, do you have any way to deal with this?" Natasha asked.
Caught off guard by the sudden attention, Thor shook his head, indicating he didn't have a solution.
Then, something came to mind. He hesitated for a moment, then said, "This might be something only my brother Balder can deal with..."
Hearing that, Tony and the others froze, recalling that incredible being who had recreated Asgard and resurrected its people.
Yes—only someone like that could possibly stop the Earth from colliding.
As the Endgame Avengers were still discussing it, and Nick Fury and others from Universe 616 were also weighing their options, something shocking occurred between the two Earths.
A brilliant light suddenly flared between them.
In the next instant, the two universes radiated with divine brilliance. Every shadowed place was illuminated.
The light then began to converge toward a single point.
A being of radiance—immense, unfathomable—appeared between the two Earths.
Compared to his colossal form, Earth itself seemed tiny. With his outstretched hands, it felt like he could cradle both planets.
Seeing the figure, shock spread across the faces of both Nick Fury from Universe 616 and Tony from the Endgame universe.
"Is that... the Creator God Balder?"
Floating between the Earths, Syd clearly sensed the two universes nearing complete overlap.
Once fully overlapped—when their timelines merged—it would spell disaster for both realities!
Under the gazes of both Earths and even the abstract entities like Eternity, a radiant light suddenly burst from Syd's body.
Bathed in that brilliance, the two Earths ceased their collision.
Or rather—both universes were forcibly halted by his overwhelming power.
The Eternal beings sensed this clearly.
"So powerful?"
They were left awestruck.
Then, a terrifying crimson energy surfaced around their youngest sibling—and suddenly exploded outward.
Under the reality-warping influence of Chaos Magic, even in higher-dimensional layers, the two timelines—on the verge of convergence—froze and slowly began to pull apart.
Eternity and the others could only watch in amazement as the universes rapidly separated.
The Avengers on both Earths saw the other Earth vanish from view at an incredible speed.
In the blink of an eye, it was gone.
Watching this, Nick Fury of Universe 616 grew solemn and murmured,
"The White-robed Man's power... still terrifying..."
Meanwhile, in the Endgame universe, Thor and the others were similarly in awe.
While they each processed their thoughts, Syd was already addressing the deeper issue—the timeline of Universe 616.
The Endgame universe had been the first to approach—but it wouldn't be the last!
The universes he'd visited with Dreamwalking... and those lit up by the Eternal Attribute... would all eventually converge.
Syd wasn't about to show up every time to manually stop a collision—that would be maddening.
So, he began applying the reality-warping power of Chaos Magic to erect a repulsion barrier outside the timeline of Universe 616.
This barrier would automatically repel any approaching timelines!
That way, Universe Collision Events would no longer occur.
Scarlet energy from Chaos Magic burst from his body.
A crimson glow surrounded the timeline of Universe 616 like a shell.
Even after this was done, Syd didn't feel completely at ease.
While 616 was now safe, the Endgame universe might still be in danger.
Because of his influence, the universes were all now interlinked and bound to crash into one another eventually.
With no better solution in sight, he went one step further: he placed repulsion barriers on every universe he had touched.
Not only that—these barriers were contagious.
Any timeline approaching another would be repelled, and that repulsion would spread—making it impossible for timelines to overlap again!
Only after finishing all this did Syd stop, allowing his vast, unfathomable Abstract Concept Body to dissipate.
Earth.
On a tranquil, sunlit beach with no one around, Syd's material godly body reappeared.
He conjured a lounge chair, lay down, and summoned a chilled coconut, sipping from it leisurely.
As he prepared to close his eyes, he suddenly sensed something and looked toward Asgard.
Earlier, during the Universe Collision Event, he hadn't paid attention to much else. But now he clearly felt a fluctuation of spacetime energy coming from Asgard.
And that fluctuation... was familiar.
He recognized it in an instant.
"Time Variance Authority?"
Syd's expression darkened.
He hadn't even gone looking for them yet, and they dared to show up?
And they chose the moment he was busy handling the Universe Collision?
"Can't take me on directly, so they're targeting Thor and the others instead?"
He had actually expected something like this to happen—that's why he had strengthened Thor and his allies beforehand.
In the next moment, he rose from the chair and space rippled around him.
With a spatial shift, Syd vanished from the beach...
...And instantly appeared in Asgard.
The moment he arrived—he heard a startled scream.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 633
chapters.content:
Chapter 633 - 633
[1300PS!!]
"Thor!"
Frigga cried out in alarm.
In the distance stood a few panicked Time Variance Authority (TVA) agents. On the ground lay over a dozen charred corpses—clearly dead.
Golden lightning crackled over Thor's body as a yellow, rectangular Time Door opened beneath his feet.
"Ahhh!"
Caught off guard, Thor fell straight into it.
The Time Door closed instantly.
Syd's gaze flicked over, immediately spotting a TVA agent pressing buttons on a time controller. His hands were still on it—obviously the one responsible for activating the portal that caused Thor to fall in.
Frigga was relieved to see Syd appear, while the surviving TVA agents—including a man named Colin—froze in terror, their faces pale with dread.
Seeing the situation, Syd frowned. His eyes lit up with a deep crimson glow—the light of Chaos Magic.
In the next second, the glow shifted to green—the power of the Time Stone.
Using Chaos Magic to tap into the Time Stone, Syd began reviewing what had happened just moments earlier.
One image after another flashed before his eyes.
Not long ago, near Frigga and Thor in Asgard, a yellow Time Door had opened, and a dozen TVA agents stepped out.
They had come with the intent of forcefully capturing Thor and Frigga.
What they didn't expect—what left them shocked—was how powerful Thor had become.
He didn't even use Stormbreaker. Golden lightning surged out from him, and within moments, ten agents were down—burned black and killed instantly.
This left the remaining agents in a state of total panic.
In his panic, the middle-aged Colin had slammed both hands frantically against the time controller—likely not even knowing what he was pressing.
A yellow Time Door suddenly opened beneath Thor's feet, and off-balance, he fell in—just as Syd arrived on the scene.
Fully understanding the situation, Syd turned his gaze to the five surviving TVA agents.
"Wh-White Robed Man..."
"Easy! Let's talk this out!"
The five were terrified—no thought of resisting. Even with their advanced technology, they knew they weren't a match for this monster.
Syd frowned deeper.
These persistent gnats who kept pestering him again and again—he was truly fed up.
He didn't even want to hear another word.
With a flicker of crimson light from his Chaos Magic—
Colin and the others froze, faces twisting in fear and disbelief.
Their bodies began turning to paper from the limbs up.
"No, please—!"
As their terrified, regretful screams rang out, the paper fragments scattered—and they were gone.
"Thor..." Frigga said, worried.
Syd shook his head. "That wasn't the TVA on the other side. He should be fine."
"The Time Variance Authority?" Frigga repeated, confused.
Syd didn't answer right away. Instead, he focused on sensing the energy of the yellow Time Door Thor had fallen into.
From his perspective, the portal didn't lead to the TVA.
It felt like a completely different universe.
But where exactly—it was unclear.
Still, he wasn't overly worried.
After being reforged by him and infused with his divine power, Thor's strength now rivaled, even surpassed, many Celestials.
In this state, it was nearly impossible for anyone to harm him—more likely he'd be the one causing trouble.
Syd's curiosity began to stir.
"I wonder which universe he fell into..."
Driven by curiosity, he started preparing to open a portal to this unfamiliar universe.
While he was deep in thought and Frigga still seemed concerned...
Elsewhere—
Above a peaceful, sun-drenched, heavenly version of Asgard, Thor came tumbling down.
He was screaming loudly during the fall—
Until, after a second or two, he suddenly paused and muttered, "Uh... why am I screaming?"
"Didn't I already learn to fly?"
With that realization, his fall abruptly stopped midair.
Hovering in place, Thor grinned.
Standing midair like this had once been impossible for him. He used to need Mjolnir or Stormbreaker to fly.
But now?
After being remade by his brother Balder, not only had his body become truly immortal, he also carried Balder's divine blood and the power of an abstract concept god.
Such power naturally granted him the ability to fly.
Of course, after over a thousand years of being grounded, old habits died hard. In the moment of panic, he simply forgot.
Now enjoying the sensation, Thor began surveying his surroundings.
Golden sunlight, radiant palaces...
"This is... Asgard?"
One glance was enough for confusion and awe to appear on his face.
He had fallen from that yellow portal—yet somehow ended up in another Asgard?
Thor was stunned. But deep down, he sensed something was off.
For some reason, this version of Asgard felt strange—different from the one he knew.
As he took it all in, others in this mysterious Asgard noticed him too—thanks to all his yelling.
People began emerging from the palaces, looking up at the floating Thor in surprise.
"Prince Thor?"
"What's he doing?"
Confusion spread across the crowd.
Then—
From the throne room, King Odin and Queen Frigga appeared.
Seeing Thor hovering midair, Odin narrowed his eyes. His sharp gaze gleamed, sensing something unusual about this version of his son.
Before long, a voice shouted from afar:
"Who are you?! How dare you impersonate me?!"
Everyone turned—
To see another Thor approaching.
The crowd fell into a daze.
Two Prince Thors?!
Was this... an impersonator?
Just as questions began forming, Odin locked eyes on the Thor in the sky. His tone turned sharp:
"Who are you?!"
At the same time, a terrifying aura erupted from him.
Feeling that pressure, the floating Thor was visibly startled.
He now understood—this was a parallel Asgard.
"But... what's going on with this Father? Why is he so much stronger than mine?!"
Compared to the Odin from his own universe, this one was immensely more powerful—shockingly so.
And even the other Thor approaching him—he too was much stronger than Thor had been before Balder's transformation.
"What the hell is going on here...?"
Thor muttered in disbelief.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 634
chapters.content:
Chapter 634 - 634
[1400PS!]
Thor speculated that this parallel universe must be quite special—otherwise, how could this version of his father and the other him be so overwhelmingly strong?
Of course, he didn't want to admit that it was his universe that was weak.
Still, even though the Odin and Thor of this universe were powerful, he wasn't fazed.
Ever since he was enhanced by his brother Balder, Thor had become incredibly powerful—he genuinely believed that no one could defeat him now.
So, faced with these stronger versions of his father and himself, Thor didn't back down at all.
When Odin asked who he was, Thor thought there was no need to hide anything and boldly said,
"I come from another universe. I am the Thor of Asgard in that world!"
As soon as he said it, astonishment flashed in the eyes of the Asgardians present—King Odin, Frigga, and the other Thor.
"Another universe?"
"A divergent reality?" Odin muttered, eyes gleaming with insight.
With his level of power, Odin could sense many things—and he more or less believed this Thor's claim.
He could clearly tell that the man before him was of Asgardian royal blood.
Still, there was something odd—maybe it was the influence of being from a parallel universe, but this Thor's aura felt both familiar and foreign. He seemed to possess a power none of them had.
While Odin contemplated, the other Thor—his golden hair shining, a silver winged helm on his head—stepped forward, shouting:
"What nonsense are you spewing? Another universe? You think I'd believe that?"
"Tell the truth! Who are you really?! Why are you impersonating me?"
"Or... are you Loki in disguise?!"
He stretched out his thick right arm.
In a flash, the silver Mjolnir flew into his hand.
The parallel Thor scoffed. "Let's see what you really are!"
A clap of thunder burst forth as lightning surged over his hammer.
With a mighty leap, the parallel Thor rocketed into the sky.
BOOM!
A sonic boom exploded as he shot toward the other Thor at supersonic speed.
Odin and the others showed no surprise—they watched the unfolding clash with full focus.
Who would win?
In the sky, the alternate Thor's eyes widened.
"What kind of speed is this?!"
Even a sonic boom? Was this for real?
If it weren't for the enhancements from his brother Balder and his divine-level reflexes, he might not have reacted in time!
But now...
A smirk curled on Thor's lips.
BOOM!
Golden lightning erupted across his body and then blasted forward—straight at the charging parallel Thor.
"ARGHHH!"
The parallel Thor screamed as the golden lightning struck him, launching him across the sky and slamming him hard into the ground.
BOOM!
The earth cracked under the impact, a massive crater forming where he landed. The parallel Thor, charred and paralyzed, lay motionless inside.
"You..."
His body was numb, his head spinning. He couldn't believe it.
He couldn't believe how badly he'd been struck by lightning—or how strong this "fake Thor" actually was.
One attack.
And he was almost completely out of the fight.
How could that be?!
When had Asgardian blood become so weak?
"What kind of lightning was that? How could it be so powerful?"
He shouted in disbelief.
Then he noticed something else—his eyes widened in shock.
"You summoned that lightning... without your hammer?!"
Even he, the so-called God of Thunder, couldn't produce such lightning without Mjolnir's aid.
How had this guy done it?
The onlookers—Odin, Frigga, and the others—were just as stunned.
Their Thor had... lost?
And in just one strike?
How could there be such a massive difference between two Thors?
And... why was this one's lightning golden?
While the others looked on in shock, the victorious Thor floated proudly above them, beaming.
"Of course! I don't need Mjolnir or Stormbreaker to unleash lightning like that!"
Ever since Balder transformed his body and granted him divine blood and abstract god-force, those weapons had become almost irrelevant.
Even when carrying them, they barely enhanced him anymore. In fact, he sometimes forgot to bring Stormbreaker at all.
*(Stormbreaker: "...") *
Thor grinned as he looked down at the defeated version of himself and declared smugly,
"I'm not like you—clinging to some hammer. You're the God of Hammers—I'm the true God of Thunder!"
"You—!!" the parallel Thor roared, glancing at Mjolnir in his hand and nearly suffering a brain aneurysm.
"God of Hammers?! What the Hel does that even mean?!"
Fuming, he shouted,
"If you really are another universe's me, how could you be so much stronger?!"
That made Odin frown. The others, too, were puzzled.
Thor just smirked again.
"Well, of course I'm stronger. I was reforged by my brother Balder. His divine blood and abstract god-power flow through me. You think you can compete with that?"
"Forget you—if a Celestial showed up right now, I'd smash them flat with a single blow!"
As he boasted, the others were dumbfounded.
Celestials?
One blow to kill a Celestial?!
Their first instinct was disbelief.
But one name stuck with them:
Balder.
The image of a broad-shouldered man appeared in their minds.
The parallel Thor quickly shook his head.
"No way! Balder doesn't have that kind of power! There's no way he gave you anything close to that!"
"If you're gonna lie, at least make it believable!"
Thor's eyes widened in shock.
"What—my brother's here too?!"
Moments later, a figure walked toward them—an unimpressive-looking man with a bland appearance that didn't match his own Balder at all.
Thor's mouth twitched.
He mumbled, "My universe's Balder is the real deal."
"There's no way this guy is my brother."
"No way my brother would be this weak."
As he spoke, he cast a sidelong glance at the parallel Balder, his eyes unconsciously filled with puzzlement—and even a bit of contempt.
Hearing that, this universe's Balder flushed with anger and shame.
"You—!"
Outraged, he prepared to rush forward and challenge the alternate Thor.
But Odin stepped in, stopping him.
He stared intently at the newcomer, his eyes flickering with a calculating gleam.
In just this short time, he'd already begun to piece a few things together...
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 635
chapters.content:
Chapter 635 - 635
The Thor before them was incredibly powerful—perhaps even...
At the level of a self-contained universe.
And then there was his brother, Balder. According to this Thor, his Balder was vastly different from the one they knew—supposedly unimaginably powerful.
Could he also be at a universe-level tier?
Perhaps even stronger?
Odin couldn't be sure, but his curiosity was certainly piqued.
Not just Odin—everyone, including the parallel Thor, was now intrigued by this alternate-universe Balder.
As Odin studied the mighty Thor before him, a flicker of hope emerged in his heart.
Though he appeared calm on the surface, Odin was anything but. Deep inside, he was filled with urgency and dread.
Because he had discovered a terrifying secret—
The secret of Ragnarok.
In the vision of Ragnarok he had seen, the gods would perish alongside Surtur, Fenrir, and other great enemies.
Thor, Loki, himself, and the rest of the Asgardian gods—and even Asgard itself—would ultimately be destroyed.
But that wasn't the end.
A while later, Asgard and its gods would be reborn—their memories erased, doomed to repeat everything from the beginning... until Ragnarok came again... and again... in an endless loop.
This cycle had repeated countless times. And no one but Odin had noticed.
Only he knew the truth.
He was filled with bitterness and fury.
Asgard and Ragnarok—were just a dish.
Somewhere deep behind the scenes, **higher gods—gods above gods—**were pulling the strings. They orchestrated everything, guiding each Ragnarok from the shadows.
The Asgardian gods were nothing but seeds. These gods above gods scattered them, let them grow strong, and then harvested them at the end of their life cycles through Ragnarok.
All the power and energy the gods accumulated over a lifetime was devoured in death by these higher beings.
Ragnarok was just their meal.
A recurring, carefully paced feast...
Although Odin had uncovered this truth, he stood no chance against the gods above gods. All he could do was follow the fate laid out for him.
Until now.
Looking at this alternate-universe Thor, Odin saw hope—a chance to finally break the cycle.
This Thor was overwhelmingly powerful. Perhaps he could resist the gods above gods?
With that thought, Odin hesitated only a moment before saying,
"I need your help with something."
The parallel Thor and others were stunned, while Thor himself was confused.
"What is it?" he asked.
"Come with me."
Odin led him to a palace chamber. After shielding the area from all prying eyes and ears, he revealed everything he knew about Ragnarok.
As the story ended, the room fell into dead silence.
Thor's face was frozen with shock and disbelief.
Ragnarok?
Gods above gods?
What kind of nightmare was this?
His skin crawled just thinking about it. For a moment, he wondered—was his own Asgard also being controlled by such entities?
But... they hadn't shown up during his Ragnarok, right?
Balder had rewritten their fate...
Maybe those higher gods were afraid of Balder? So they never appeared?
Or maybe... his Asgard simply didn't have those gods above gods?
Was it a difference between universes?
One guess after another ran through his mind.
At the same time, he felt troubled by his other father's request.
Sure, Balder had made him feel near-invincible, but going up against those things? Gods above gods?
He wasn't sure he could win.
Coming back to his senses, Thor said cautiously,
"This... might be something only my brother Balder can help with. I'm not sure I can handle it myself..."
Odin blinked in surprise.
Balder again?
He was puzzled.
Could Balder really be that strong?
And Thor's refusal disappointed him.
He was about to try persuading Thor again when—
Both Odin and Thor sensed it.
They simultaneously looked up, staring beyond the palace walls.
A massive, armored female figure wearing silver battle armor and a long cloak was suddenly standing above Asgard, floating in the sky.
Her head was lowered, her gaze locked directly on their location.
Both men's faces changed instantly.
They knew.
She was one of them.
A god above gods.
She must have noticed something—possibly even heard their conversation.
Odin's face twisted with regret and dread.
Then—
The towering goddess extended her hand. In full view of the stunned Asgardians below, she reached directly for Odin and Thor's palace.
Thor instantly felt a life-threatening danger.
He didn't hesitate.
Drawing on the divine power gifted to him by Balder—the power of an abstract concept god—he lashed out!
BOOM!
Golden lightning roared from his body, blasting through the roof and smashing straight into the giant silver hand.
The towering goddess showed no reaction at first. Her expression was cold and emotionless.
After all, a mere Asgardian god couldn't possibly harm her...
Or so she thought.
But in the next instant—
"AHHH!!"
She cried out in pain.
Her eyes widened in disbelief as she looked at her injured hand.
"You... how did you hurt me?!"
She—Cleo, one of the gods above gods—couldn't believe it.
A Thor from Asgard had wounded her?!
Even if she had been caught off guard and unprepared, it still shouldn't have been possible!
As she reeled in shock...
Back inside the wrecked palace, Odin stared wide-eyed.
He glanced at the wincing Cleo, then turned to Thor—who was crackling with golden lightning and radiating an overwhelming aura.
He noticed something unusual.
The golden lightning wasn't just powerful—it tore tiny rifts through space wherever it passed.
And it carried... something else.
A mysterious aura that made Odin's heart tremble.
"This... this feels like a divine aura..."
He muttered, unsure.
Up above, Cleo had also sensed it and exclaimed in disbelief,
"What... what divine power is this?! How is it so powerful?!"
Born of this divine energy... or perhaps infused by it...
This lightning had actually wounded a god above gods.
What the hell was going on?!
Cleo stood in the air, stunned, her eyes locked on Thor with utter confusion.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 636
chapters.content:
Chapter 636 - 636
Cleo couldn't understand what kind of divine power this was—how could it hurt her?
Down below.
Thor, upon seeing this, immediately relaxed a bit and muttered in surprise, "My little brother's divine power really is useful. This woman couldn't withstand it either!"
Odin, standing beside him, caught the faint muttering and looked slightly stunned.
That power came from Baldur?
Was it really that strong... that unique?
While Odin was still reeling from the thought, he quickly warned, "Be careful. This one's not so easy to beat."
Almost as if to confirm his fears, the very next second, a terrifying aura burst from the female Supreme God, blanketing all of Asgard. The skies of Asgard darkened instantly.
Many Asgardians were gasping for air under the pressure.
Odin gripped Gungnir tightly, ready to leap into battle.
Thor, feeling the overwhelming pressure as well, prepared to go all out in a fight with the Supreme Goddess.
But then, suddenly, two more enormous figures appeared in Asgard's sky.
They were dressed similarly to the first Supreme Goddess. Thor and Odin instantly understood who they were.
Gazing at the three Supreme Gods above, Thor's expression darkened. The pressure grew heavier.
He wasn't sure he could win against these so-called Supreme Gods.
Odin beside him couldn't help but feel despair creeping in.
So many Supreme Gods were watching this place. This wasn't good!
As the three Supreme Gods sneered with contempt and Thor and Odin tensed, ready to fight, a spark of golden light suddenly flared in the sky above Asgard.
Its abrupt appearance, especially at such a tense moment, drew the attention of the three Supreme Gods, the hidden ones spying from the shadows, as well as the Asgardians and Odin and Thor.
What was that?
They were stunned.
Very quickly, the golden spark expanded into a complete, round portal.
Through it, one could clearly see the scene on the other side.
A figure draped in white, shrouded in mysterious energy, slowly floated out of the portal.
Seeing this figure, everyone reacted differently.
The Supreme Gods, Asgardians, and Odin all wore puzzled expressions—they had no idea who this person was. But Thor's eyes lit up with joy as he shouted, "Hey! Brother, over here!"
Just entering this universe, Syd turned his head in response.
Hearing Thor's call, the others were shocked.
Asgardians started murmuring in surprise.
"He's the brother of Thor from another universe?"
"Baldur?"
Everyone was curious and puzzled about him.
Thor from another universe had mentioned before that his changes and powers came from this person—was he really that strong?
Odin too was filled with uncertainty and curiosity.
The three Supreme Gods present, as well as the hidden ones, had heard Thor mention this person earlier, so they naturally knew who he was.
They were wary, but not truly concerned. After all, with so many Supreme Gods here, could they not handle just one person?
At that moment, Supreme Goddess Cleo furrowed her brow and questioned, "That power on him, did it come from you?"
Syd turned his head and looked at the towering female Supreme God.
By now, he had roughly figured out what kind of universe this was.
"No wonder this universe feels so powerful. It's a comic book universe..." he murmured to himself.
Compared to the movie universe, the comic universe had absurd power scaling and some truly ridiculous beings.
Not just universal-level beings—there were multiversal ones too!
As for the three figures not far off, he had naturally guessed who they were: the Supreme Gods hiding in Asgard, weaving the threads of fate, controlling the gods, and orchestrating Ragnarok.
In essence, these Supreme Gods were to the Asgardians what the gods were to humans—beings of a higher order.
Their power was immense. In the end, it was Thor who became Rune King Thor and broke free from fate.
But the ones who truly dealt with these Supreme Gods weren't Rune King Thor, but Loki—or more accurately, the God of Stories Loki.
The comic book version of the God of Stories was incredibly powerful, even stronger than the TV version. His level was multiversal or beyond, just below the Phoenix Force.
In the comics, he couldn't defeat the pure Phoenix Force.
Even so, his abilities were still tremendous.
Thinking of this, Syd felt a tinge of apprehension.
"As I conquer more and more universes, I knew I'd eventually run into ones that are hard to deal with..."
If luck wasn't on his side, he might encounter enemies that were truly problematic!
As for these Supreme Gods—since he hadn't fought them directly, he wasn't sure how strong they were.
But, seeing how they needed to consume Asgardians' energy, they probably weren't that outrageous in strength.
Casting a glance at Cleo and the other Supreme Gods, Syd decided to err on the side of caution. He activated his Avatar of Light ability.
In an instant, endless light poured from his body, causing Cleo and the other Supreme Gods to instinctively raise their hands to shield their eyes.
Soon, the blinding light enveloped all of Asgard and began to spread outward beyond it.
Moments later, the entire universe was bathed in light.
Before anyone could react, that boundless radiance gathered back toward Asgard.
In a blink, above Asgard—
A vast, indescribable abstract conceptual divine form appeared.
Cleo and the other Supreme Gods stared, dumbfounded.
"An Abstract Cosmic Entity?!"
They couldn't believe their eyes.
And then, they felt their memories become hazy. New memories were forming in their minds.
As Syd became this universe's Primordial God of Creation, his self-existent and eternal abilities kicked in.
He had directly become the God of Creation from the very birth of this universe—or even earlier.
His ancient myths and records began to appear across the cosmos and within the memories of all beings.
Cleo and the other Supreme Gods were lost in confusion, not understanding what had just happened.
While they were still in shock, Syd himself was a bit surprised.
Now that he had become the Creator God of this comic universe, he felt his power surge explosively.
Still, facing these Supreme Gods, he didn't dare to lower his guard. After all, this was a comic book universe—who knew what ridiculous powers they might have? He didn't want to fall victim to some unexpected trick.
The next second, he activated Chaos Magic. The holy brilliance of his abstract divine form instantly turned a deep crimson.
But just as Syd was about to activate his reality-warping ability, something unexpected happened.
The Chaos Magic radiating from him expanded, and under its blood-red glow, the surrounding space turned into flickering mosaics—as if everything could be twisted and transformed into anything at any moment.
(End of Chapter)
