chapters.title: Chapter 637
chapters.content:
Chapter 637 - 637
[100PS!!]
Syd felt a strange familiarity wash over him—he had encountered this before.
It was the occasional loss of control that came with Chaos Magic.
Back before his Chaos Magic had reached level five, it would sometimes trigger this reality-altering state spontaneously.
Of course, it wasn't a full meltdown—more of a minor destabilization.
Feeling the current state and gazing at the three Supreme Gods in the distance, a trace of pity arose in his heart.
If this had happened earlier—back when he was just getting used to the comic universe—he might have stumbled or been ambushed. But now, in this runaway Chaos Magic state, there was basically no chance of that.
The truth was simple: the Supreme Gods were just unlucky.
The next second, Syd's voice echoed across all of Asgard—a mysterious sound, as if it came from the cosmic truth itself.
"There shall no longer be Supreme Gods of Asgard."
As his words fell, the three distant Supreme Gods froze, confused by the meaning of what this mysterious deity had just said.
They weren't the only ones puzzled. Odin and the rest of the Asgardians below were equally bewildered.
At that moment, Thor's eyes lit up. He muttered, "It's here—my brother's reality-warping ability!"
"What?" Odin blinked, not immediately understanding.
Up in the sky, the three Supreme Gods furrowed their brows.
"You..." Cleo started to speak, but then suddenly noticed something strange about her body—and stopped in her tracks.
Their forms were starting to turn translucent and illusory, as though a giant eraser were slowly rubbing them out of existence.
"What have you done to us?!"
"What is this power?!"
The three Supreme Gods, including Cleo, were filled with shock and terror.
They could sense it—a power of fundamental superiority was erasing them.
The worst part?
They couldn't resist it.
"How is this possible?! We are Supreme Gods! How can a force exist that we can't fight against?!"
"No!"
The three were consumed by panic and disbelief, trying to speak—
But the very next moment, their figures vanished completely.
From the shadows of Asgard, faint wails could be heard echoing.
In a flash, the entire realm of Asgard fell silent.
All of its Supreme Gods had been erased by just a single sentence from Syd.
Witnessing this, the Asgardians below were stunned speechless.
Just one sentence—and those terrifying beings were gone?
What kind of power was this?
Inside the ruined palace...
Odin looked up, having witnessed what had just taken place.
"This..." he was frozen in place.
Suddenly, a realization struck him. He turned to Thor and murmured, "Reality-warping?"
Now he finally understood what Thor had meant earlier by that term.
Though he understood now, it didn't make it any less awe-inspiring or terrifying.
Reality-warping?!
Thor, noticing Odin's gaze, couldn't help but puff out his chest proudly. "My brother is a great Primordial God of Creation. Of course those so-called Supreme Gods were no match for him!"
"Primordial God of Creation?" Odin repeated, stunned. Suddenly, a different set of memories flooded his mind.
In this new memory, the figure in the sky was the sixth Primordial Creator who had existed since the dawn of the universe!
Odin's mind was spinning. He couldn't tell which memory was real anymore—the ones he always had, or these new ones that had just emerged.
At the same time, a wave of envy—and even jealousy—began to swell in his heart.
Why did the Thor and Asgard of another universe get such a powerful god?
Why wasn't he here?
Odin's heart soured, and he looked at the divine figure in the sky with a mix of complexity and bitterness.
Then, the sky suddenly darkened.
Having resolved the Supreme Gods' threat, Syd dispelled his abstract divine form and floated down toward the ruined palace where Thor stood.
He spoke simply, "Let's go. Back to Universe 616."
This comic universe was full of unknown dangers—even now, as its Creator God, he didn't want to linger any longer than necessary.
Thor hesitated, glancing at Odin, then at the ruined remnants of Asgard. A trace of reluctance flashed across his face. "Can I still come back here?"
Syd gave it a thought, glanced at Thor, and in an instant, golden light surged over Thor's body.
Thor's eyes widened in shock—he could feel a new, unique ability had been added to his body.
Syd had granted him temporary control over space transfer, linking it to his own power.
As a bonus, Syd also sent the complete knowledge of portal magic into Thor's mind.
Whether Thor could master or use it—that would be up to him.
Thor was elated.
With a wave of his hand, Syd opened a new portal leading back to Universe 616.
The next moment, he floated through it.
As he did, Odin looked on with a complicated expression. He wanted to say something, but in the end, remained silent.
Far away, this universe's versions of Thor and Baldur watched the white-clad figure disappear with equally conflicted emotions.
"That guy... was he telling the truth all along?"
Looking at that Thor, Baldur muttered, stunned, "Could it be that he is the real Baldur, and I'm the fake one?"
If not, why was he so strong... and he himself so weak?
His mind reeled.
The parallel Thor felt the same—and even more so. Emotions like shock, envy, and disbelief roiled in his heart.
...
Universe 616
Syd didn't care when Thor would return—his attention was entirely focused on his Dreamwalking Technique, Self-Existence trait, and the accumulated energy points and God unlock progress.
This journey to the comic universe had only deepened his sense of urgency.
He had to reach the multiversal level as soon as possible—otherwise, he might not even have the strength to resist what's coming!
Forget the overpowered beings in the comic universe—just take the God of Dark Magic Chthon or the Trinity of Vishanti, for example.
Even more terrifying was the real body of that Great Old One that would soon arrive.
There was no way he could deal with any of them in his current state.
Syd sighed to himself.
Not long after, Thor returned from the comic universe.
Time flowed quickly—and before long, a whole day had passed.
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]...
(Unlock Progress: 55%)
Hearing the familiar system prompts in his ears and seeing the accumulated energy, Syd's eyes filled with anticipation.
The next second, he dumped all the energy points into his unlock progress.
Instantly, the percentage changed—
(Unlock Progress: 78%)
But after a while, no new system notification came.
"No new ability?"
"And only 78%?"
Seeing this, Syd froze for a moment, disappointment welling up in his heart.
He was already at 78%, and still no new ability?
"Don't tell me it'll only appear at 80%... or 85%, 90%—maybe even 100%?"
He was speechless.
Also, when exactly would the core ability of God be unlocked?
Syd furrowed his brows in deep thought.
After a moment, he shook his head and sighed.
"Forget it. No point in overthinking. Just keep grinding."
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]...
The prompts continued to ring in his ears.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 638
chapters.content:
Chapter 638 - 638
[200PS!!]
While continuously illuminating the universe, Syd kept collecting energy points without pause.
An hour passed...
Suddenly, his attention shifted to a certain dimension within the 616 main universe.
As he conquered more and more universes, his power grew rapidly, edging ever closer to multiversal level.
Naturally, his perception and exploration capabilities expanded exponentially as well.
Just moments ago, he had faintly sensed a dimension emanating a very familiar aura.
Without hesitation, Syd projected his awareness into that unknown dimension.
At the heart of it, he detected an immense mass of green energy, and a familiar presence—or rather, a former enemy.
Back then, when testing the power of Orochi's divine finger, he had accidentally weakened the fabric of reality.
A Dimensional Demon God from the void sensed this and injected its will into a mutant on Earth.
At the time, acting as Messiah, Syd had repeatedly unleashed Sunshine, forcing the demon god to retreat and abandon Earth.
The scene came flooding back into Syd's mind, along with the parting words of the fleeing entity:
"You win this time!"
"I'll be back!"
As those words rang out, the green veil that had cloaked the sky and land vanished, and reality was restored to normal.
Back then, Syd hadn't been strong enough to deal with the demon god. Later, when he did grow powerful, the demon had disappeared without a trace—impossible to find.
But he had never forgotten it.
Now, sensing this hidden demon god cloaked in endless green energy, Syd's gaze turned ice cold.
"You got away last time... Let's see if you can run this time."
As he was about to act, deep within that dimension, the unknown Dimensional Demon God also felt something.
"Who's there?"
"Who dares to spy on me?!"
The demon roared in fury.
Syd didn't bother to respond.
He simply acted.
A flood of divine light surged outside the dimension, coalescing into his Abstract Conceptual Divine Form.
Not only that—powers from multiple universes also began to converge onto Syd.
His divine body grew larger, vaster, beyond comprehension.
Then, he raised his right hand.
Boom!
A colossal hand bathed in divine light tore through layers of space and dimensional barriers—grasping the entire dimension in its palm.
The entire dimension trembled.
Inside, the Dimensional Demon God's expression changed dramatically as he sensed the enormous hand from beyond his plane.
"What is this...?"
He quickly recognized the aura coming from that hand.
"White-robed one?!"
"I didn't provoke you, did I?!"
"Stop!!"
He shouted in terror.
Meanwhile, the sheer scale of the disturbance began attracting attention from other dimensional entities.
Across the multiverse, one after another, other Dimensional Demon Gods sensed something and turned their gaze toward the scene.
"That's..."
"The white-robed one?!"
"The Creator God?! What is he doing?!"
Mephisto, Lucifer, Dormammu—one by one, they gasped in horror.
What shocked them most was the sheer magnitude of Syd's divine form.
This guy is insane—his conceptual divine body is massive enough to grab an entire dimension?!
His power was so overwhelming that just looking at that glowing, sacred hand made them feel as though they could be crushed at any moment.
While they were panicking, Syd finally made his move.
Ignoring the demon's pleas, his glowing hand began to squeeze.
Crack! Crack! Crack!
The dimensional space twisted, contorted, and began to collapse.
"NO—Please! Have mercy!"
"I bear you no grudge! Why, Creator God?!"
The Dimensional Demon God's face twisted in terror as he begged for his life.
Outside the dimension, Syd simply looked down at it, expression calm.
He figured it was worth letting the demon die with some clarity. So, he casually said:
"Messiah."
The demon froze—its face changed instantly as memories surged.
"It's related to Messiah?"
"He's doing this because of Messiah?"
"What kind of connection do they have?!"
His mind was reeling.
And not just him—every other Dimensional Demon God who heard Syd's words was left stunned and full of confusion.
Why would the white-robed Creator God protect Messiah?
What is their relationship?
As they wrestled with these questions, Syd was already done wasting words.
His divine hand tightened.
Endless light, divine power, and laws of reality erupted in his grasp.
BOOM!!
In an instant, the entire dimension exploded!
"NO!"
"White-robed one—how can you be so heartless?!"
"I won't accept this!"
The Dimensional Demon God roared in his final moments, overwhelmed with dread and regret, desperate to scream one last curse—
But before he could finish, the flood of light and divine power consumed him completely.
There was no resistance.
Drenched in terror, his consciousness vanished into darkness.
Shockwaves of divine power rippled outward.
As the light faded, the dimension and its demon god were utterly erased.
Just to be safe, a deep crimson Chaos Magic glow lit up around Syd's right hand.
The red light swept across the region where the dimension had been—wiping out all remnants.
Once it was done, he finally stopped. His abstract divine form dissolved into countless beams of light and scattered.
Silence fell.
The surrounding Dimensional Demon Gods were shaken to their core.
A dimension and a demon god—just... gone?
And it wasn't even done in any elaborate or mystical way.
They were obliterated as easily as crushing a bug.
In their horror, fear began to rise in every onlooker's heart.
They quickly diverted their attention and began concealing their own dimensions, terrified that the white-robed god might suddenly go mad and come for them next.
Their fragile lives couldn't handle that kind of assault.
Especially Dormammu of the Dark Dimension—he was practically losing his mind, scrambling to increase his concealment magic while silently praying that the white-robed god wouldn't find him.
...
While Dormammu prayed...
Syd's attention wasn't on him at all. His entire focus was on his God Unlock Progress.
(Unlock Progress: 78%)
Feeling a nudge in his mind, he casually dumped all the energy points he had accumulated recently into the unlock.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 639
chapters.content:
Chapter 639 - 639
The next moment, Syd's God Unlock Progress shifted again.
(Unlock Progress: 79%)
He sighed and curled his lip in frustration, helplessly resuming the accumulation of energy points.
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]
As time passed, the energy points, which had been emptied before, began rising again at a terrifying pace.
Meanwhile, as Syd continued lighting up universes and collecting energy, news of his destruction of the dimension and the Dimensional Demon God had begun to attract the attention of certain cosmic beings.
In a mysterious magic dimension...
Three unspeakable entities had noticed the dimension's destruction and the demon god's death.
They were: the God of Order Hoggoth, the Goddess of White Magic Oshtur, and the Dimensional Lord Agamotto.
Together, they formed the Trinity of the Vishanti.
One had the head of a massive tiger, another the head of a middle-aged bald man, and the third the head of a long-haired woman.
They merged together, forming the great divine being known as Vishanti.
They were not only lords of the mystical dimensions, but also the source of all white magic, jointly maintaining the multiverse's order.
Now, they had sensed the dimension's collapse and the annihilation of its demon god.
In the next moment, their attention turned toward Earth in the 616 universe, focusing on the white-clad youth. All three pairs of eyes sparkled with intrigue.
From among them, Oshtur, the long-haired woman, said with curiosity, "What an interesting little fellow."
Agamotto, the bald man, added with a chuckle, "I didn't expect such a curious being to appear in the multiverse."
Finally, Hoggoth, the ancient god with the tiger head, said with growing interest, "Once we're done with our current affairs, we should go meet this little one. I'm quite curious about him."
The other two nodded in agreement.
They were very intrigued by the sixth Creator God of the 616 universe and were planning to visit Earth soon to observe and investigate him up close.
They were particularly interested in the power he possessed.
...
Elsewhere, in a dark realm...
A middle-aged man with two long horns atop his head also sensed the dimension's annihilation—and the entity responsible for it.
Instantly, Chthon—God of Black Magic and Lord of the Dead—felt a chill of recognition.
"It's him?"
"That little brat?!"
His eyes filled with malice.
Not long ago, he had sensed an unfamiliar yet potent Chaos Magic emerge.
Out of curiosity and surprise, he had tried to tempt and lure its wielder—only to be infuriated when the other party completely ignored him.
He had never been dismissed so utterly before, and he took it very personally.
Ever since, he had vowed that once he broke free from his seal, he would personally go to Earth and crush that insolent whelp.
Of course, the sudden emergence of such a powerful and unknown Chaos Magic had also shocked and intrigued him. He had been unable to resist the urge to observe it.
But now—before much time had passed—he had once again sensed that same being...
And this time, it was even stronger than before!
Chthon could hardly believe it. He almost wondered if he was sensing the wrong person.
How could such a weak creature become so strong in such a short time?
What the hell is going on?!
His mind filled with shock and greed.
His curiosity about the owner of that Chaos Magic had now grown into a ravenous obsession.
"That power belongs to me."
"Everything belongs to me!"
Chthon was now desperate to break his seal and descend upon Earth—to seize the incomprehensible power of that youth with his own hands.
"It won't be long now... I'll break this seal soon!"
"Wait for me!"
He whispered hungrily.
...
While both the Vishanti and Chthon were focusing on Earth, eager to explore or invade—
Time continued to pass.
Two days later...
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]
(Unlock Progress: 79%)
Syd stared at his system panel, eyes brimming with anticipation.
"Should be enough by now..."
"God Mimicry Progress—100%!"
Without hesitation, he funneled the energy points collected over the past two days into the God Unlock bar.
The next second, the progress bar changed once again. Syd's eyes locked on it.
But something unexpected happened.
(Unlock Progress: 99%)
"Ninety-nine percent?!" Syd froze in disbelief.
Even with two full days' worth of energy, he still couldn't reach 100%?
And the most surprising part—he hadn't heard a single system notification.
In other words, no new divine power had been unlocked yet!
"So it really has to hit 100%?"
Syd was stunned.
The leap in this new ability's threshold was outrageous.
So much time had passed—and still no new ability?
Was it really only at 100% that the next God ability would emerge?
He found it hard to believe.
At the same time, he couldn't help but feel a rising curiosity and excitement for this last ability.
"Just 1% left..."
"How many more energy points will it take to fill that last 1%?"
He wondered.
He had a hunch that the final 1% would be the hardest.
But considering the massive amount of points he had already used, it shouldn't be much longer.
With that in mind, Syd settled in to wait—eager and expectant.
The sun shone brightly.
Time marched on.
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]...
Meanwhile, across the multiverse, whispers began to ripple through the dimensions.
A massive figure, shrouded in black mist, with indescribable tentacles, had arrived in the multiverse.
It was crossing layers of space, traversing dimensions and universes.
Its destination—
The 616 Main Universe.
This was none other than the true body of the Great Old One!
"Insects..."
Its malicious, eerie whisper echoed like a curse.
Wherever it moved, dimensions and universes became twisted and deformed.
Such an apocalyptic presence naturally caught the attention of numerous incomprehensible entities across the multiverse.
Even the true forms of the multiverse's Creator Gods—like Eternity—were drawn to the terrifying figure.
Mental messages flew between them.
"What is this evil god heading toward?"
"Should we stop it?"
"Wait. Let's see what it's planning."
These multiversal beings watched the Great Old One with uncertainty.
They had no idea what it was after...
But it was clearly searching for something.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 640
chapters.content:
Chapter 640 - 640
The multiversal beings—Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion—watched in confusion as the evil Great Old One traversed across the multiverse. None of them knew what it was looking for, nor what it intended to do.
But their gaze followed it, curious and cautious.
Nearly a day passed.
Eventually, the Great Old One arrived before a particular universe and halted.
This was no ordinary universe—it was massive, far beyond the norm.
"Why is this universe so vast?"
Even the four embodiments of the multiverse, beings who had seen everything—Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion—were taken aback.
And they weren't the only ones.
Many hidden and unfathomable entities had also noticed this anomaly.
They had overlooked this universe before. But now, with the arrival of the Great Old One, it commanded their full attention.
This universe... was not normal.
Normally, no single universe could be this powerful or this enormous.
With their interest piqued, the watchers began to dig deeper. Before long, they uncovered the truth.
And just like that, all attention—even that of Eternity and the other Primordials—focused on Earth within Universe 616.
All of this unusual activity traced back to a single mutant.
Learning this, disbelief flooded their minds.
Beings like them should never be surprised by cosmic fluctuations—but this case was too far beyond reason.
They mentally reviewed the timeline of this mutant's growth, witnessing every event as if it were unfolding before them.
This mutant, through nothing more than his mutant ability, had risen from insignificance to power beyond a single universe—all in less than a year.
"How could such a terrifyingly potent mutant exist?"
As entities that defined the multiverse itself, they were naturally familiar with the concept of mutants.
But none of them had ever witnessed a mutant with potential on this level.
From the moment of awakening to now, it hadn't even been a full year—and yet this mutant had already surpassed universal level?
He was even on the cusp of reaching multiversal power!
What kind of absurd potential was this?
And what exactly was his mutant ability?
Even worse—none of them could perceive it.
Not even beings like Eternity and Oblivion could discern the nature of his mutant gene.
"That ability... is beyond comprehension."
Now, the purpose of the Great Old One became clear.
It had come... to punish this mutant boy.
Realizing this, the four Primordials shared a complex emotion.
If this mutant continued to grow, he could well become the sixth Creator God of the multiverse.
In other words, a peer—a younger brother to them.
But that future now seemed impossible.
With the Great Old One targeting him, he wouldn't even have a chance to evolve further.
Under such overwhelming power, resistance was meaningless.
Even with power beyond a single universe, how could he stand against something at the multiversal apex?
It wasn't just Eternity and the Primordials who believed this.
Other entities watching from afar—like Cyttorak, the crimson realm overlord—also concluded that the boy stood no chance.
And then it began.
The Great Old One—larger than the entire 616 universe—extended a grotesque, shadowy tentacle.
It pierced through the void, breaching into the universe's edge.
CRACK!
Reality split open.
Had the Great Old One not deliberately restrained itself, the 616 universe would've been instantly destroyed.
Even so, with just the tip of its power entering, the entire universe began to distort and decay.
Stars and planets alike crumbled.
Only the desperate resistance of the cosmic embodiments—Eternity, Infinity, Death, Oblivion, and Living Tribunal—was slowing the disintegration.
But even they were panicking.
The moment they felt it, it was already too late.
Reality had begun to collapse.
The corruptive power flooding in left them feeling hopeless.
"What... what is happening?!"
"What is that?!"
"Who is He?!"
All of the 616's cosmic gods—including Galactus—gazed toward the breach in stunned silence.
Beyond the universe, they saw an unfathomable entity—shrouded in black mist, infinite in scale—extending a tentacle into their realm.
The tentacle was pitch-black, covered in countless red eyes and mouths filled with jagged fangs. The mouths led to dark voids, their depths unknown.
The eyes twitched unnaturally.
The mouths whispered and chanted in distorted harmony.
Their movements echoed with eerie, maddening whispers that resounded across the entire 616 universe.
The void became filled with blasphemous hymns and praises, as if endless voices were hailing their dark god.
"Tiny ones, offer up your faith. Surrender body and soul to the great god..."
"O great god, your will envelops stars and all things..."
"Heehee... Foolish lives, come. Become one with the Great God..."
The whispers grew louder.
The distortions worsened.
And with them, the 616 universe began to collapse faster.
Seeing this, the cosmic beings' despair deepened.
"It's over..."
As they drowned in fear and awe, the Great Old One—outside the universe—thought disdainfully:
"These beings are pitifully fragile. I already held back, and they still can't endure."
He had restrained most of his power intentionally—so the ant who dared defy him wouldn't die prematurely.
That insolent insect needed to be punished properly.
So, he now dialed down his aura even further.
His presence, voice, and corruption receded to a level just low enough for the universe's lifeforms to endure.
The prey would not escape.
But now—it was time for the final descent.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 641
chapters.content:
Chapter 641 - 641
[300PS!!]
In the next instant, the gaze of the Old One turned toward a certain direction in the 616 main universe.
In just a moment, it found the bug who dared to offend it!
Earth.
The cosmic collapse directly affected Earth. Countless people sensed the anomaly.
Naturally, Syd—who was still on Earth, continuously lighting up the universe and gathering energy points—had long since noticed this change.
With his abstract conceptual divine body, he understood everything.
"The true body of the Old One... has appeared..."
Syd felt deeply burdened.
At that moment, as the Old One's gaze fell upon him, his material divine body began to mutate.
His fair skin gradually turned yellowed and mottled with strange spots.
Sensing this, he immediately activated the Light Avatar and dissolved his material divine body.
In the next second, the body turned into countless rays of light and disappeared.
At the same time, under the watch of beings like Eternity, an infinite brilliance burst forth within the 616 universe, coalescing into a massive form rivaling the size of the cosmos.
Within this divine body were stars, suns, neutron stars, black holes, and galaxies.
However, this towering figure that should have radiated holy brilliance now appeared grotesque.
Influenced by the mutations in the 616 universe, the pure white holy light covering his form had turned into a dusky yellow.
Like the final glow of a setting sun—it mirrored his current state.
If he couldn't stop it, it wouldn't be long before he fully mutated!
This state was all too familiar to Syd—he had experienced it multiple times before. He even possessed the power of the Old Ones within his body.
But now, even that inherited power was being assimilated by the true Old One outside the universe!
The difference in level was simply too vast. He couldn't resist at all!
Seeing this, Eternity and the other dying beings fell into despair and daze.
"Even our strongest little brother... isn't a match for this evil deity?!"
The enemy hadn't even made a serious move yet. Just the pollution radiating from its body had rendered them helpless?!
What kind of terrifying existence was this?
They couldn't believe it.
At that moment, the true body of the Old One outside the 616 universe stared intently at Syd's dusky yellow form through its crimson eye hidden in the black mist.
A moment later, its cold and bizarre voice echoed, layered and heavy.
"Worm... you dared destroy my avatar. Did you foresee this moment?"
"I told you... this wouldn't be the end!"
"Once I descend... it will be your death!"
"Becoming my puppet... is your final destiny. The power within you... will be dessert after my feast!"
Looking down upon this insignificant existence within the cosmos, the Old One's massive crimson eye was filled with disdain and greed.
"Tiny worm, little crawling insect!"
Its eerie voice reverberated.
"No matter how hard you struggle—even if you've become a Creator God in your universe—in my presence, you're still laughably insignificant!"
"You have no strength to resist my power!"
"If I didn't hold back, even a single whisper or glance from me would reduce you to nothing!"
"Such a frail and pitiful life... your only end is extinction..."
The Old One's distorted voice echoed throughout the entire 616 universe and even beyond.
The gods of the universe, like Eternity, fell into even deeper despair.
Even on Earth, the billions of humans mutating heard that bizarre voice.
Despite the Old One's tongue being incomprehensible, the moment they heard it—they all somehow understood its meaning, and even knew clearly who it was talking to.
As the twisted voice entered their ears, countless streams of knowledge and information surged into their minds.
The image of the dusky white-clothed figure in the 616 universe—glowing dimly—was etched into their minds.
"That's the Creator God?"
"The White-Clothed Hero?"
"That terrifying existence is after the White-Clothed Hero?!"
Seeing the invincible hero now grotesquely mutating before their eyes left them in disbelief and despair.
Even he couldn't resist? Was it true, as that bizarre being said—that he couldn't even withstand a glance or whisper?
And they were also witnessing the collapse of the universe itself.
Then they saw that incomprehensible Old One reaching out its massive black tentacles toward the Creator God, the White-Clothed Hero.
It looked like... it was about to kill him?!
Countless humans were stunned.
S.H.I.E.L.D.
Nick Fury, holding a right hand covered in green mucus and sprouting thin tentacles, wore a dazed expression.
Stark Tower.
"Damn it!"
Cursed Tony Stark, gazing at his heavily mutated body in frustration.
Not just him—the other Avengers, including Black Widow Natasha, were similarly shaken.
Asgard.
Thor and the others stood pale and speechless.
Outside the 616 universe.
The multiversal beings like Eternity watched what was happening in the 616 universe with increasingly conflicted feelings.
"That strange mutant... is going to die?"
In the magical dimensions—
The threefold Vishanti were also observing the scene, feeling a sense of pity.
They had been quite interested in that youth's powers, even planning to visit Earth soon to investigate him further.
But before they could, he was already about to die.
Elsewhere.
The god of black magic, the death deity Chthon, was also watching the events of the 616 universe.
His heart was full of unwilling rage.
In just a short time, he would have broken the seal and descended upon Earth.
Everything—the Creator God's powers, all of it—was supposed to be his!
But now... this was happening!
"Damn it!!"
Chthon roared in fury.
While all creation watched, as the Old One extended its black and grotesque tentacles, Syd's focus shifted elsewhere.
[Photon Energy +5157]
[Photon Energy +5157]
...
(Unlock Progress: 99%)
Looking at the energy points accumulated over the day, Syd grew tense.
There was only one way to escape his current situation—
Reach 100% in God Mimicry!
That was likely the only way to reverse this desperate situation.
However—if these accumulated energy points couldn't raise the 99% progress to a full 100%...
There was no time to think.
In the next second, Syd poured all the energy points into the God Mimicry progress bar.

chapters.title: Chapter 642
chapters.content:
Chapter 642 - 642
[400PS!!]
In just an instant, all the energy points Syd had accumulated over nearly a full day disappeared from the panel.
He stared at the display, anticipation surging in his chest.
(Unlock Progress: 99%)
(Unlock Progress: 100%)
At the same time, a prompt rang out in his mind:
[Ability: Omniscience and Omnipotence (Unlocked)]
[Ability: Omniscience and Omnipotence (0/100) Level 1]
"What... is this?"
Hearing the prompt and seeing the new ability on his panel, Syd was momentarily stunned.
[Name: Syd Castell]
[Age: 17 (Natural lifespan: ∞ days)]
[Mutant Abilities: Mimicry, Energy Absorption]
[Current Mimicked Target: God (Title: Creator, Originator, Omniscient and Omnipotent One)]
(Unlock Progress: 100%)
[Ability: Omniscience and Omnipotence (Unlocked)]
[Energy Points: 0]
The abilities Creation and Self-Existent Eternity had disappeared from the panel. What replaced them was just one ability:
Omniscience and Omnipotence.
Even Syd couldn't help being shocked by this outcome.
He hadn't expected that once God's mimicry progress reached 100%, the unlocked ability would truly be Omniscience and Omnipotence.
At first, it had only been a guess.
But now—it had actually become reality!
At the same moment that his mimicry reached 100%, and the ability Omniscience and Omnipotence appeared, Syd could feel his abstract conceptual divine body undergoing strange changes.
Some metaphysical transformations were occurring within him.
[Omniscience and Omnipotence EXP +1]
[Omniscience and Omnipotence EXP +1]
[Ability: Omniscience and Omnipotence (36/100) Level 1]
Omniscience and Omnipotence was rapidly improving at an incredible, unknown rate.
An unending stream of knowledge and information surged into his mind as he gradually began to approach true omniscience and omnipotence.
Feeling these changes, Syd was dumbfounded.
He could sense that with the mimicry progress at 100%, a fundamental metamorphosis had begun.
Logically, the transformation should've happened in an instant—but now, he felt that it still needed time.
It was the first time mimicry had ever encountered this kind of slow progress.
Though Omniscience and Omnipotence was still just at Level 1, he had already gleaned some understanding.
The changes overtaking his body were deeply linked to this ability. Only upon reaching Level 5 could he complete the final transformation.
And he could feel it—when that happened, the tremors would be immense. Both within himself... and in the world outside.
Even now, with the ability just at Level 1, Syd's abstract conceptual divine body was undergoing significant changes.
Sensing something unusual, the Old One's grotesque black tentacles paused mid-reach.
Although it felt like a long period had passed, in truth, it had all occurred in the span of a breath.
From the perspective of the other entities—and the Old One itself—just as it extended its tentacles toward the 616 Universe, the figure of the Creator within that universe began undergoing strange and profound change.
The Old One. The multiversal entities watching from outside. Eternity and the rest within the 616 Universe. Nick Fury, Tony Stark, and billions of others on Earth.
All of them—every single being—was stunned by what they saw.
A vast, cosmos-sized divine figure clad in white robes, whose body encompassed planets, stars, and galaxies...
The pollution on its surface had dimmed its radiance into a sunset-yellow hue, but now—
Now, within that dusky glow, a single strand of unimaginably pure light had begun to shine.
That light was indescribable—perfect, flawless. It had no blemish or impurity. Like the very first light before all creation.
Pure. Brilliant...
Just seeing it caused a kind of spiritual elevation in everyone who beheld it. Insight bloomed in their minds.
As if just by gazing upon that light, one could understand everything they had ever sought to know.
A single thought emerged in every being's consciousness:
"In the beginning was the Word... and the Word was God?"
Only this phrase could vaguely express what they now felt.
That pure, dazzling, flawless radiance grew stronger and stronger—until it completely engulfed the previously tainted yellow light.
And within that splendor, a formless being took shape—its appearance so indistinct, no one could describe it.
It seemed humanoid... but also not. No one could articulate its form.
Unnameable. Indescribable. Without substance, without soul, without spirit.
Looking upon it, one simply could not comprehend it.
Across the universe—and even beyond—divine hymns began to echo.
Angel-like murmurs rose in the void, as if countless beings were singing praises.
"The self-existent, who was, and is, and ever shall be..."
"The omniscient and omnipotent, the Creator of all..."
"Glory, dominion, all that is and all that ever will be, is yours..."
"Forever... and ever..."
These sacred chants rang in everyone's ears.
Gazing at that unnameable figure within the cosmos, neither the billions on Earth, nor the countless gods across the stars, nor even the multiversal powers like the Vishanti or Chthon—
None could look away.
Regardless of where they stood—on Earth or beyond the edge of space—they found the same image reflected in their eyes: that indescribable being.
Even more shocking, they realized something else...
Size no longer held meaning.
Outside the universe, the Old One's body was impossibly massive—the cosmos itself seemed like a marble in its gaze.
And yet...
Compared to the being of pure light now standing within the universe, the Old One now looked small.
The scale of perception had flipped. Big and small no longer had any meaning.
This dissonance made Tony Stark and the others feel like their brains were about to short-circuit.
They could clearly see this being, even form impressions of it—but as soon as they looked away, the memory blurred.
It was as if their level of existence simply did not permit them to truly remember this figure.
Outside the 616 Universe—
The Old One's massive crimson eye trembled.
It stared at the being of pure light and roared in disbelief:
"What has happened to you?!"
Everything before it filled it with confusion.
It swore—it had never encountered anything so incomprehensible.
The creature it once saw as an insect had suddenly become something else.
Something it could not understand.
At the same time, the multiversal entities—Eternity, the Vishanti, Chthon—all stood in stunned silence.
They too... could not comprehend what they were witnessing.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 643
chapters.content:
Chapter 643 - 643
[500PS!!]
On Earth—
The Ancient One and other beings, along with billions of humans, wore looks of confusion in their eyes.
Then—
After his initial shock, the Old One quickly regained composure, feigning calmness as he forced a grin and said coldly:
"Insignificant bug, little crawler—don't think changing your appearance will make me fear you."
"No matter how much you change, your essence remains the same!"
"All I need is a glance, and you, fragile and weak being, will perish."
"Your final end... will still be to become my puppet and dessert."
That strange, echoing voice reverberated through the entire universe—and beyond.
Upon hearing this, whether the billions on Earth or the gods like the Vishanti, everyone quickly snapped back to their senses.
"Indeed... no matter how much he's changed, it doesn't change the weakness at his core," murmured Oshtur of the Vishanti.
No matter how transformed the Creator God of the 616 Universe appeared, he could not possibly rival a multiversal—or even higher—existence like the Old One!
No matter the change, the essence remained the same.
And so would the result.
Agamotto and Hoggoth nodded in agreement.
Meanwhile, Eternity and the others from the multiverse also recovered and looked on at the radiant figure within the 616 Universe, their expressions increasingly complex.
Chthon let out a sigh of regret.
As they watched, the Old One once again extended his grotesque black tentacles toward the glowing, formless being—intent on binding and turning him into a puppet.
Many beings silently mourned the sight.
Yet just then, they noticed—
The Old One's tentacle froze in place once more.
"What's happening?!" they wondered in shock.
Then, to their surprise, the Old One's voice burst out in stunned rage:
"What have you done?!"
"Why can't I move?!"
Its massive crimson eye quivered in disbelief as it glared at the glowing figure in the universe.
Hearing that cry, Eternity and the other divine entities were taken aback.
"What's going on?"
Instinctively, all eyes turned to the radiating, indescribable being within the 616 Universe.
Syd, now under all their gazes, was quietly sensing the changes within himself.
His abstract conceptual divine body had completed its initial transformation, and even he was surprised at the current state.
Most importantly, even though Omniscience and Omnipotence hadn't completed its final evolution—it was already incomprehensibly powerful!
When the Old One extended his tentacle, a single thought crossed Syd's mind: "Stay back."
And just like that... the Old One's tentacle froze in place!
"So this is what omniscience and omnipotence means..."
Syd whispered to himself.
Anything he wished to do—he could do.
Even now, with just a Level 1 ability and an incomplete transformation, the being beyond multiversal level—the Old One—was no longer his equal?
Just then, a prompt rang in his mind:
[Omniscience and Omnipotence EXP +1]
[Ability: Omniscience and Omnipotence (0/500) Level 2]
In mere moments, the ability had reached Level 2.
Facing the Old One's rage and the countless watching eyes, Syd calmly said:
"I didn't do anything."
"I simply didn't want you to come closer."
"I didn't want you to move."
His voice, sacred and absolute—like truth itself—echoed across the entire universe and beyond.
Everyone heard him.
And yet... they were dazed and confused.
"What does he mean he didn't want the Old One to move?"
The words were clear, but no one could understand.
No—rather, they refused to understand.
Could a thought alone control a being of such magnitude?
"That kind of existence can't possibly be controlled by a mere thought!"
They simply didn't believe it.
Nor did the billions of humans on Earth. It was too absurd.
The Old One certainly wasn't going to accept such a ridiculous notion.
He let out a cold, mocking laugh:
"You think a thought can control me?"
"What a joke!"
"You must have used some kind of trick!"
Sneering, he added:
"If it's so easy, then make me disappear with a thought!"
"Heh..."
At his level of existence, it was impossible to simply vanish. He had no fear.
Hearing this, the Vishanti, Eternity, and others didn't believe Syd could do such a thing either.
But before they could scoff further, Syd's calm, sacred voice rang out once more—
"If that's what you want..."
"Then I'll grant your wish."
"You may now disappear."
That truth-like voice echoed.
And in the next second—something no one could believe happened.
"What... what did you do?!"
The crimson eye of the Old One, veiled in black mist, trembled in horror as he looked at his own body.
His once-boundless form was turning transparent—as if it were vanishing.
"Impossible!!"
The Old One screamed in disbelief.
And all who witnessed it—Eternity, the gods of the 616 Universe, the Vishanti, Chthon—were stunned beyond reason.
A single sentence—and a being beyond the multiverse... began to vanish?!
They instinctively turned to look at the radiant being in the 616 Universe, their hearts filled with awe and confusion.
In their shocked gazes, the Old One let out a final scream, his massive form becoming more and more translucent.
They could sense it clearly—
This evil being had tried to resist.
Tried to struggle, to fight back with all its might.
But none of it mattered.
He couldn't even move.
The Vishanti and the rest stood frozen.
"All because of a single sentence...?"
"What... is this power?"
Meanwhile, the rapidly fading Old One howled in despair.
His mind was filled with terror, disbelief, confusion.
Ever since coming to this multiverse, nothing had gone as expected.
The insignificant ant he thought he'd devour...
The one he believed would perish with a glance...
Now with a single sentence—he was the one vanishing.
"What are you?!"
"You're not the Creator of this universe!" he screamed as he tried to fight off the inevitable.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 644
chapters.content:
Chapter 644 - 644
"Who... are you really?!"
"You can't be this universe's Creator God!"
The Old One screamed in defiance, desperately resisting his final obliteration.
He simply couldn't believe it. This person—this so-called mutant—was allegedly the Creator of this universe?
A lowly Creator God from a single universe could never possess this kind of power!
A single sentence had rendered a multiversal-level being like him completely helpless, fading into nothing?
The Old One was certain—this figure must be hiding some mysterious, higher identity!
As the Old One shrieked in disbelief during his final moments, the same doubts began to arise in the minds of the multiversal beings watching—Eternity and the others could no longer suppress the thought.
If someone could erase a multiversal-level being—or someone beyond that—with a mere sentence, how could anyone believe he was just the Creator of one universe?
His power... had clearly surpassed even the multiverse!
A storm of speculation filled the thoughts of countless observers.
Everyone was guessing, theorizing—desperate to know this being's true identity.
But while they were speculating, Syd had already grown tired of listening to the Old One's voice.
Even though his Omniscience and Omnipotence was only Level 2, he had already shattered the logic of reality: as long as he willed it, it would happen.
Even the rebooting, annihilation, and recreation of the multiverse in front of him could be done in an instant.
He now resembled something like the original, unnerfed Beyonder from the Marvel Multiverse.
Naturally, if he wanted the Old One's body gone—it could vanish in a breath.
The only reason the Old One had lasted this long, putting up a façade of resistance, was because Syd had let him.
After all, Syd had seen his own deaths many times in his visions of divine annihilation. If he just let the Old One die instantly, it would be too merciful.
Now, listening to the Old One's screeching final questions, Syd had lost all interest in continuing the charade.
Staring at the pathetic god still futilely struggling, Syd's voice was calm and cold:
"Now that your final words are done—"
"You may truly disappear."
And with that, in the gaze of disbelief, terror, and despair—
The Old One completely vanished from the multiverse.
No trace left behind.
As if... he had never existed at all.
Instant silence.
Whether in the 616 Universe or beyond, everything fell into an eerie hush.
"Impossible..."
Eternity, the Vishanti, Chthon—every being who witnessed this moment fell into stunned silence.
They had believed that the Old One, with his unimaginable power, would at least put up some final struggle.
But in the next breath... he was gone.
His earlier resistance seemed like a joke in hindsight.
Then the truth struck them—
The Old One had only lasted this long because Syd let him.
Now that Syd had grown tired of seeing him, the Old One was erased—instantly.
There wasn't even a delay.
And that terrifying realization chilled them all to the core.
Just what level had this being reached?
On Earth—
Under the influence of Syd's power and the aftershocks of the Old One's corruption, many humans had indirectly witnessed the cosmic events unfolding above.
And they saw it:
That terrifying god who could destroy entire universes was erased by a single sentence.
"That's terrifying..."
"He really can do anything just by thinking it?"
Then they saw one final scene—
That radiant, blurry figure lifted his head, gazing at the collapsing universe above.
In the next moment, everything stopped.
The collapse paused.
And then—
All the shattered, corrupted parts of the universe began rapidly regenerating.
In less than a second, the entire cosmos was restored.
It was as if nothing had ever happened.
The humans on Earth stood frozen, eyes blank.
If they didn't still remember what had happened just moments ago... they would've thought it was all a dream.
This kind of power...
Nick Fury, Tony Stark, and everyone else felt their worldview collapse all over again.
"Where's the science now?"
"Does this thing even obey any law of reality?"
Back in the 616 Universe—
Having dealt with the Old One, Syd turned his attention outward, sweeping his gaze across the multiverse.
In that instant—
Eternity, the Vishanti, Chthon—all those beyond the stars—felt it.
A gaze unlike anything they'd known.
In that moment of contact, they all felt utterly defenseless.
As if all their secrets, all their thoughts, were laid bare.
Though hard to believe, they knew it wasn't just imagination.
In the Magical Dimensions—
The Vishanti trio—Oshtur, Hoggoth, and Agamotto—trembled under that gaze, their complexions twisted with awe and unease.
Not long ago, they had scoffed at this being—thinking his essence was weak and no transformation could change that.
They had assumed he would never defeat the Old One.
But how long had it been?
Now they stood face-to-face with undeniable truth.
Even worse—just a moment ago, they had considered probing this being further.
And now? They hadn't even had the chance.
He had looked into them first.
Under his gaze, they felt stripped bare. Every thought, every memory, laid open.
There was nothing left to hide.
It was a helplessness they hadn't felt in eons.
"When was the last time we felt like this?"
The three exchanged grim looks.
Whatever curiosity they'd held earlier was long gone.
Now, they didn't even dare to be curious.
Syd had even read those very thoughts.
He knew exactly what they had planned.
So he'd made sure to stare at them a little longer—
Just to let them fully experience what it felt like to be scrutinized by omnipotence.
Then his gaze shifted.
To the sealed realm where Chthon lay bound.
Even though Omniscience and Omnipotence was only Level 2, he could perceive everything—past and present.
Chthon's schemes, his desire to stir up chaos—Syd knew it all.
And for such a pest?
He didn't even bother with words.
As his gaze landed, Chthon felt a creeping dread.
And with wide, panicked eyes, he cried out:
"Spare me!"
And then, as if realizing it wasn't enough—
"Spare me! I'll serve you—I'll be your servant!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 645
chapters.content:
Chapter 645 - 645
As the God of Dark Magic and the God of Death, Chthon was desperately struggling to survive in the face of a fatal crisis.
But just as he opened his mouth to speak, he felt everything about himself begin to vanish.
At that moment, Chthon was filled with terror and regret, wanting to beg for mercy.
Unfortunately, before he could utter a single word, he vanished completely.
The instant Chthon disappeared, his adversaries—Vishanti and several cosmic beings including Eternity—immediately sensed it.
They knew exactly who could perform such a feat.
In that moment, all eyes turned toward Syd in Universe-616, their hearts quietly filled with awe.
At this point—
Having just dealt with Chthon, Syd gave a final glance toward Eternity and the others. After thinking for a second, he didn't take any further action.
Those entities had little to do with him—there was no need to waste time on them.
Thinking this, Syd's thoughts turned to the Time Variance Authority—an organization that had repeatedly provoked him.
Previously, due to insufficient power—his divinity not yet reaching the multiversal level, and his "God Simulation Progress" not yet at 100%—he had hesitated to act. He hadn't been confident in facing Kang the Conqueror, the mastermind behind the TVA, fearing he might stumble and fall. So he had temporarily endured.
But now...
Syd had no intention of waiting any longer.
The moment the thought arose, space rippled like liquid.
A portal to the Time Variance Authority opened instantly.
On the other side stood a group of stunned TVA agents, eyes wide with shock.
The next second, Syd's glowing white, incomprehensible, formless, soulless, shape-shifting figure began to shrink slightly—
And drifted into the TVA's headquarters.
Watching him float inward, Mobius and the others were terrified.
They had, of course, witnessed the immense disturbance in Universe-616 not long ago.
So they knew exactly who the being before them was.
"You... What are you trying to do?"
"Why aren't the magic suppression devices working?!"
They were filled with both fear and confusion as they realized even the TVA—capable of suppressing the Infinity Stones—had absolutely no effect on the glowing white figure.
He still radiated light, remained formless, and floated in midair—completely unaffected.
It was the first time they had seen something so absurd.
Outside the main universe 616, Eternity and the others who hadn't yet left, also noticed Syd's movement.
"What is he doing?"
They wondered in confusion.
Inside the TVA—
Syd paid no mind to Eternity and the others. His attention was solely on Mobius and the TVA agents.
As for these ones who had caused him trouble multiple times, he couldn't even be bothered to speak.
Under their horrified stares, he merely looked at them.
The next moment, their bodies began to turn transparent.
In a blink, they each vanished, one by one.
The entire TVA instantly fell silent. Every member had been erased with a single thought.
And just like the Old Gods—completely and utterly erased.
Not even time travel could bring them back.
After finishing off the TVA members, Syd murmured to himself, "The end of time, huh..."
He already knew where Kang was hiding.
At the end of time, in a dark and lonely citadel.
There, one could even see the manifestation of the time stream.
So how would he get there?
Syd gave it a thought, and space rippled again.
In the next moment, a new portal appeared—leading to the citadel at the end of time.
Syd slowly drifted into the space-time rift.
At that same time—
On the other side of the portal, Kang the Conqueror, the hidden manipulator behind the TVA, stared in disbelief at the approaching figure.
"The white-cloaked one...?"
"The Creator God?"
Seeing the glowing, formless entity, Kang's expression grew complex.
He knew something about this being—and knew he was unique.
At one point, Kang had even considered grooming him as a successor.
That was why he had ignored the multiple reports from the TVA regarding Syd.
He had thought he could wait for the right time to nurture him.
Who would've thought this being was far more extraordinary than he'd ever imagined?
He had become something even Kang couldn't comprehend.
Kang knew exactly why Syd had come.
Of course, he wouldn't go down without a fight.
In the next second, he activated the time device on his wrist, trying to trim Syd from the timeline.
But what happened next stunned him.
No matter how many times he activated the time control functions on his wrist, no matter what kind of temporal energy he used—Syd remained completely unaffected.
"As expected..."
"Time has no effect on you?"
Kang muttered in disbelief, "You've transcended time completely...?"
Syd gave him a glance without answering.
The next second, Kang's body began to turn transparent.
He let out a bitter smile. Already knowing the outcome, he murmured, "What a terrifying being..."
Before he could even finish the sentence, he vanished completely.
Syd observed all this with a calm expression.
The next second, his gaze turned outward—beyond the citadel.
In the cosmic expanse surrounding the citadel, a long, radiant, white time stream twisted and looped.
But this stream wasn't whole—it had splintered into countless branches.
Syd wasn't surprised.
The Sacred Timeline had already collapsed. The appearance of branches was natural.
He didn't care.
To him now, time and space no longer held any meaning.
If he willed it, he could reconstruct the splintered timeline.
He could even erase the concept of a timeline from the multiverse entirely—without the slightest effort.
Just as he was about to act and tidy up the timelines—
He paused.
A face flashed through his mind—Loki.
Come to think of it, when he helped Thor and the others grow stronger in Asgard not long ago, he had completely ignored Loki?
"Ah, fine. I'll help him too."
With a single thought—
Loki, who was still on Earth and utterly confused, suddenly vanished.
In the next instant, he appeared inside the citadel at the end of time.
Staring at the glowing, formless figure before him, Loki's heart trembled.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 646
chapters.content:
Chapter 646 - 646
[600PS!!]
Loki only saw a blur before he found himself in a strange, unfamiliar place.
He hesitated as he looked at the glowing, indistinct figure before him.
Of course, he knew exactly who this was.
His face full of hesitation, Loki wasn't sure how to begin the conversation.
At that moment, Syd spoke after a brief pause. "You're aware that Thor and the others have gotten stronger, right?"
His mysterious, almost omniscient voice echoed in the space.
Upon hearing this, Loki's hesitant expression shifted to one of jealousy and envy.
Before he could respond, Syd continued, "I can give you an opportunity."
As he spoke, he glanced at Loki—and in that instant, countless pieces of information and imagery flooded into Loki's mind.
These memories were none other than the events from the Avengers and the Loki series.
Loki's expression changed dramatically as the images played in his head.
He saw himself being strangled to death by Thanos, saw another version of himself on a different timeline.
There, he had been captured by the Time Variance Authority and went through a long series of events.
In the end, that version of him had stepped forward and chosen to sacrifice himself—saving countless timelines and becoming the God of Time, or perhaps more accurately, the God of Stories.
Sitting on a lonely throne, his body glowed with green light, connected to countless timelines.
Those timelines intertwined to form a magnificent, branching Tree of Time.
The sheer grandeur of that scene shook Loki to his core.
And as those memories continued to unfold in his mind—like he had personally experienced them—his pride and arrogance faded, replaced by a profound sense of responsibility.
That sense of responsibility... was precisely what a true king needed.
Just like Odin had once foretold—he and Thor would both eventually become kings.
But this time, it wasn't to rule Asgard, nor the frost giant realm of Jotunheim, as Odin had once envisioned.
Instead, he chose to sacrifice, to sit alone upon a throne, guarding the timelines as a solitary king.
Loki opened his eyes, his expression complicated as he gazed at the glowing, formless figure before him.
He had never expected that someone like himself—who feared loneliness, who craved love and attention—would ultimately make such a choice, to sit in solitude and guard the multiverse's time.
He was conflicted over his own fate and awestruck by the power of the brother of Balder before him.
To witness the past and future so clearly—to even experience it firsthand—was a power that left him fascinated and amazed.
But at this moment, he was also hesitant and puzzled. He subconsciously asked, "What opportunity do you want to give me?"
Hearing this, Syd's voice echoed like truth itself: "The opportunity to become a true God of Time."
"Kang the Conqueror is dead. The timelines outside need managing. I can make you the God of Time—without binding you to any one place."
Hearing such words, spoken so casually, Loki was stunned.
He could do even that?
He couldn't believe it.
While he was still reeling, Syd asked calmly, "What's your choice?"
As soon as the words fell, Loki quickly nodded.
Though it came with responsibilities, he'd be a fool to refuse such power.
Thor had already become so strong—Loki had no intention of being left behind.
Seeing Loki's nod, Syd wasn't surprised.
Since the choice had been made—
The next second, with a thought, his omniscient and omnipotent power erupted.
Inside the dark citadel, radiant light suddenly flooded the space.
Countless glowing time streams were forcibly drawn in by his immense, godlike power.
They didn't resist—because they couldn't.
In the next instant, under Loki's stunned gaze, all those time streams shot straight toward him.
"Ah—!"
Loki cried out as his body was suddenly linked to stream after stream of time.
At the same time, those streams began to glow with green light—carrying Loki's power with them.
And then, one by one, the glowing green time streams vanished as if they had never existed at all.
While Loki was still receiving the power of the timelines, Syd quietly observed him—watching his rapidly growing strength and preparing a small restriction.
Each timeline was essentially its own parallel universe, and with Loki's current power, he could destroy them with ease.
If he did so recklessly, it would lead to disaster sooner or later.
With that in mind, Syd's eyes lit up with white radiance as he began to create something.
In the next moment, as Loki continued absorbing the timelines' power—
A voice suddenly rang out in his head:
"Ding. The Timekeeper System is now at your service, Lord Loki."
Loki was momentarily dumbfounded, not understanding what had just happened.
Then, as more information poured into his mind along with the system's voice, he finally understood.
This system had been created by Balder's brother before him—to assist and supervise him.
If he destroyed too many timelines without cause, his power would be restricted and locked away for a period of time.
To lift that restriction, he'd have to behave properly and earn it back.
But if he managed the timelines well, this so-called Timekeeper System could also help him absorb energy—slowly climbing higher and higher.
Eventually, he could even become the strongest being beneath OAA.
As for who or what OAA was, Loki didn't know. The only thing he got from the information was that it was a terrifyingly powerful entity.
That thought helped calm Loki's heart a bit.
Seeing that Loki had finished receiving the timeline's power and the Timekeeper System had activated, Syd paused and said, "I'll leave this place to you. I'm heading out."
Before Loki could say anything, Syd's figure vanished instantly—without even a ripple in space.
In the blink of an eye, he reappeared within the Solar System of Universe-616.
As for Loki, after taking in the sight of the citadel for a while, he decided to return to Asgard—intent on finding Thor.
While Loki acted—
Syd stood within the solar system, gazing silently at the glowing sun in the distance.
He was deep in thought, pondering his next step.
Now that his God Template had reached 100%, and he was essentially omniscient and omnipotent, he suddenly found himself at a loss for what to do.
The former mission of lighting up and conquering universes... no longer held meaning.
In fact, he had temporarily suppressed the changes his powers would have caused upon the outside world—choosing to wait until he reached Omnipotence Level Five before releasing that pressure.
Otherwise, the resulting shockwaves would be simply too massive.
Sensing his current power, Syd murmured quietly to himself:
"My current strength has already surpassed the multiversal level... and reached far beyond the realm of an omniversal being..."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 647
chapters.content:
Chapter 647 - 647
[700PS!!]
So, what exactly is the Omnipotent Universe?
Beyond the multiverse, there exist countless other multiverses—each with infinite layers of infinite dimensions and infinite realities, stacked upon infinite axes.
Multiverses, composite universes, parallel universes, hyperverses, dimensional realms, outer universes, supreme universes—every kind of universe.
Everything known and unknown, real and abstract, all of it—
Together, they form the Omnipotent Universe.
As he contemplated this, Syd couldn't help but marvel at the power of the God template.
Or rather—the sheer strength of omniscience and omnipotence.
By now, he was fairly certain of one thing: what he had simulated was the true God—one that was omniscient and omnipotent in the most literal sense.
However, omniscient and omnipotent... was currently only—
Just then, a notification sounded.
[Omniscience & Omnipotence EXP +1]
[Ability: Omniscient & Omnipotent (0/1000) – Level 3]
Only Level 3. He had yet to complete his final transformation into true omnipotence. There was still some hesitation within him.
And speaking of the Omnipotent Universe, there were a few beings within it that he had his eye on.
The one who drew the most attention—undeniably—was OAA, the One Above All of the Marvel Universe.
A being who is, quite literally, the Creator of the Marvel Multiverse—a metaphysical being of metaphysical beings.
The strongest entity in the Marvel Universe, also considered omniscient and omnipotent, standing above all else.
Now, was Syd's Level 3 omnipotence stronger than the OAA's own? He wasn't sure.
To be honest, he didn't even want to know—because with his current level, there was a risk. Even just probing for information might attract OAA's attention.
So, for now, he avoided confrontation. He'd keep growing quietly—wait until his ability reached Level 5 Omnipotence.
By then, OAA or not—it wouldn't matter anymore.
He wasn't keen to find out whether his incomplete omnipotence could match the OAA's complete omnipotence.
Of course, there was always the possibility that OAA had already noticed him—but was simply too transcendent to care.
After all, OAA wasn't like the Living Tribunal or the Beyonders—he didn't like to step down and intervene.
Aside from OAA, there were a few other noteworthy figures.
The Living Tribunal, empowered by OAA to supervise and maintain the balance of all Marvel realities.
In name, the highest entity under OAA.
Though honestly, Syd found that title a bit exaggerated—he'd keep an eye on the Tribunal, but that was about it.
More impressive was the Pre-Retcon Beyonder, before his powers were scaled down. That guy was basically the second supreme being in Marvel, right below OAA—his will could shape reality as he saw fit.
But his mindset was that of a normal person, not transcendent like OAA. He even tried to weaken himself so the Marvel Universe could handle his presence.
Then there was the Beyonder race, or the Beyonder Gods—worth noting too...
Syd continued pondering.
Suddenly, he sensed something and turned to the side.
Five figures had appeared beside him at some point—Eternity, Infinity, Oblivion, Death, and Galactus.
Of course, these were the avatars from Universe-616. As for their true multiversal forms—they didn't dare show themselves in his presence.
Syd wasn't surprised by their arrival.
Even though he had disabled his omniscience—intentionally, to avoid boredom and unpredictability—he could still deduce that they'd come.
After all, a lot had happened recently.
As they looked at their radiant, blurry younger "brother," the expressions of the cosmic entities grew increasingly complicated.
Silence filled the space for a moment.
Galactus hesitated, then asked, "Why are you... so powerful?"
Eternity added, confused, "What is your ability, exactly?"
The others—Infinity, Death, Oblivion—all carried the same burning questions in their hearts.
Just days ago, they had been watching with curiosity, wondering what kind of power this younger brother held as a supposed creator god.
And then—barely any time later—they had witnessed that horrifying power firsthand.
It was utterly terrifying...
Suddenly, Galactus's expression shifted as a thought struck him. He couldn't help blurting out:
"Don't tell me... you're omniscient and omnipotent?"
He remembered the divine hymns and praises that echoed through the cosmos not long ago—among them, the words "omniscient and omnipotent" had clearly resounded.
Eternity, Infinity, Death, and Oblivion all thought of it too. Their hearts stirred uneasily.
Omniscient and omnipotent?
If it were true...
The cosmic entities shared a silent, bitter smile.
Just a few days ago, they had still felt smug—thinking that, while this brother was strong, his abilities weren't particularly special. Certainly not greater than theirs.
They hadn't expected this...
If it were real, then this brother's power was on a completely different scale.
Compared to him, their own cosmic roles seemed mundane and insignificant—utterly unworthy of comparison.
Still, it was just a suspicion—they didn't know for sure.
It just felt too absurd. Even if they suspected it... they struggled to believe it.
Syd, hearing their words, gave no confirmation or denial. He simply said nothing.
Then, his gaze turned toward Galactus.
"You seem to have something you'd like me to help with?"
Though he'd shut off his omniscience, his sharp perception still picked up the longing hidden within Galactus.
Startled, Galactus asked in disbelief, "How did you know that?"
When Syd didn't answer, Galactus hesitated—then slowly asked, "Can you help me... remove my hunger?"
The other cosmic entities weren't too surprised by this request. They too turned to look at their brother, wondering if he could actually do such a thing.
Syd gave Galactus a long look.
And then—something happened that stunned Galactus.
The constant hunger that had plagued him since his rebirth—
Vanished.
Just disappeared—without a trace.
Even when he focused all his senses, he couldn't perceive how it had been removed.
It was as if that hunger had never existed to begin with.
Seeing his shocked face, the others—Eternity and the rest—were taken aback.
Death asked, "What's wrong?"
Galactus, overwhelmed, said in disbelief, "My hunger... it's gone!"
"What?!"
Eternity and the others were stunned, and their eyes shot toward the glowing, indistinct being before them.
What had he done in that brief moment?
None of them had noticed even the slightest anomaly.
Could it be...
Could there truly be something called omniscience and omnipotence?
They could only wonder—shocked, confused, and increasingly awestruck.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 648
chapters.content:
Chapter 648 - 648
"How did you do it?"
Feeling the inexplicable vanishing of his endless hunger, Galactus was deeply shaken.
Without any of them noticing, the gnawing void inside him had simply... disappeared?
What kind of divine power was this?
Just as the other cosmic beings—Eternity, Infinity, Oblivion, and Death—were still reeling in shock, Syd suddenly thought of something. He glanced at Galactus and casually offered a reminder.
"That hunger of yours... the majority of it stems from your cosmic function. You're responsible for the cycle of material dissolution in the universe."
"If you stop devouring planets... you may disturb the universe's balance."
He paused, then looked deeply at the stunned Galactus.
"If you're unlucky, you might attract the judgment of the Living Tribunal—a being that stands above even the creator gods of the universe..."
Although he didn't finish his sentence, Death and the others immediately understood what he was implying—and were left astonished and unsettled.
Especially Galactus, who felt completely stifled.
Devouring planets is a sin now too?
Why?
He was furious—but powerless.
He didn't stand a chance against the Living Tribunal. It was better to hold his tongue and continue devouring planets... cautiously.
After all, he still needed life energy to mend the missing parts of himself.
As he tried to convince himself, Syd glanced his way again, seemingly sensing Galactus's inner thoughts.
"In your current state, the Living Tribunal may not interfere. But once you restore yourself and become a Herald of Life, the Tribunal will certainly come for you."
As he spoke, Syd transmitted information on the Living Tribunal and the Heralds of Life to Galactus and the others.
In an instant, Death and the rest were visibly stunned.
Galactus was completely dumbfounded—though his confusion quickly gave way to resentment and fury.
Why?
Damn that Living Tribunal!
But no matter how angry or wronged he felt, there was nothing he could do. None of them—aside from this mysterious younger brother—could possibly stand up to the Tribunal.
While Galactus was still fuming, Syd said, "If there's nothing else, I'll take my leave."
Galactus wanted to speak, perhaps even ask for help, but the words caught in his throat.
Besides, he wasn't even sure whether this younger brother could take on the Living Tribunal.
If he couldn't, then asking would only be awkward—and Syd had no obligation to help him anyway.
With that in mind, Galactus remained silent. And as for the others, knowing they had plenty of time ahead, chose not to press him to stay.
Syd nodded slightly.
In the next instant, his form vanished and reappeared on a beach on Earth.
As he stood by the sunny coastline, Syd passed the time waiting for his Omnipotence to rise to Level 4 and Level 5—while thinking about the question he'd had before the cosmic beings arrived.
"I'm kind of bored. What should I do now?"
After a brief spell of idleness, a thought suddenly piqued his interest.
"I've never examined the alternate origin of the Infinity Stones. Why not go take a look?"
In his mind, the memories of the alternate origin of the Infinity Stones surfaced.
Aside from the well-known version where six gems were formed from the remnants of the Big Bang—
There was another, far older origin.
Possibly the true origin.
In Universe-616 and beyond, before the five great cosmic entities were born, there existed an even more ancient female god.
She was the original embodiment of the Infinity Stones, the personification of multiple forces—older even than the Celestials and cosmic abstracts.
Her name was Nemesis, the Goddess of Vengeance.
Because she was born too early—when no other gods yet existed—she was overcome with loneliness and despair. Tired of the emptiness, she chose to destroy herself.
She shattered into seven parts—each becoming a Gem: Time, Space, Reality, Power, Mind, Soul, and the most unique of all—Ego.
The Ego Stone contained her slumbering will, hidden away so well it could not be found through conventional means.
Only by gathering the other six Infinity Stones could the Ego Stone be located.
Recalling this version of the Infinity Stones, Syd's eyes gleamed with curiosity.
The Nemesis version of the Stones was far stronger than the weakened movie counterparts.
"Just the thing to pass the time. Let's pay a visit to Nemesis's universe."
Syd mused with growing interest.
As for its location—he could find it in an instant.
The next moment, he selectively reactivated his omniscience, and immediately learned where in the Omnipotent Universe the Nemesis Universe was.
"Universe designation... 93060?"
Syd murmured, intrigued.
To avoid spoiling the fun, he limited what he accessed—he only looked at the universe's coordinates and designation, nothing more.
Just then, a familiar voice echoed in his mind.
"Hey! Oh glorious and majestic Syd—what are we doing next?"
Hearing the groveling and flattery-laced tone, Syd could only sigh.
The voice naturally belonged to Venom, who was often dormant to adapt to Syd's escalating divine power.
Ever since becoming essentially God, Venom's very existence had become increasingly abstract.
Originally, the divine power would have annihilated him completely—but since Syd had no such intent, Venom remained.
Instead, tainted by a trace of Syd's omnipotent aura, Venom too transformed into something utterly extraordinary.
It lost its physical form, becoming a conceptual entity—essentially a divine accessory, like a keychain on Syd's waist.
In some twisted sense, it had become a sort of angelic trinket. A "keychain angel."
Of course, despite the self-deprecating nickname, Venom—now infused with divine residue—was an unbelievably powerful being, capable of effortlessly devouring entire universes.
Having just awoken and adjusted to its new form, Venom immediately began licking boots.
It understood that everything it had now came from Syd—so naturally, it tried to flatter him in every way possible.
Knowing exactly what Venom was thinking, Syd shook his head and didn't bother correcting it.
He replied casually, "We're going to Universe 93060."
"93060?" Venom's tone turned curious. "Weird. Why do these universes even have numbers? And who came up with them?"
Its confusion was plain.
After a moment, it added with interest, "So, we're heading to that 93060 place now? Sounds fun!"
Venom couldn't help but feel excited.
(End of Chapter)
